author: akiratamai
body: ## Summary Admit a composite imported `var` as a method receiver — `lib.VS.PF()` on a struct var (value receiver, or a pointer method via auto-address). Previously the receiver was evaluated like an argument and the member read rejected the unrepresentable struct value; as a receiver it reads external state, so it is dep-free and records the imported transfer against the member. Stacked on #768. - In `_direct_import_call`, before evaluating the receiver: `_imported_member_operand(receiver)` resolving to a `var` member whose fact kind is not scalar (`integer`/`boolean`/`pointer`) → dep-free + transfer + `_pin_member_type`. Scalar member receivers (`lib.VP.PM(x)`) keep the existing member-read path. - Boundaries: an index/call-result receiver (`lib.VSS[0].PF()`) still names no member and stays closed; method expressions (`lib.S.PM(lib.VS, x)`) keep the plain argument rules (composite member args unrepresentable → closed). - 737 tests pass; ROADMAP + mumei cross-roadmap sibling PR updated. author: webtecnica
body:
Closes #186

As cinco pontas soltas que ficaram fora do #185, uma por uma. O bloqueio do #185 continua igual: desligada de fábrica, só dono e administrador, teto de custo, prazo de guarda, chamada apagada não ganha texto — com os mesmos testes de antes, todos verdes.

## O que muda para quem usa

**1. Aviso do desfecho na tela.** Ao lado do botão "Transcrever a gravação", uma linha avisa que, com o desfecho ou a análise ligados, transcrever também dispara a classificação paga da ligação. A condição mora em `apps/panel/src/ui/transcription.ts`, com teste, e a frase existe nos três dicionários (`pt-BR`, `en`, `es`). O aviso cobre os dois casos porque `summarize_call` enfileira `classify_call_outcome` quando qualquer um dos dois está ligado.

**2. Gravação longa recusada sem ser carregada.** A rota mede o arquivo com `stat` antes do `readFile`: o WAV do gravador tem 44 bytes de cabeçalho e 4 por quadro, e cada lado sai com 44 e 2 por quadro, então o tamanho basta para saber que não cabe no pedido do provedor. Recusa com 409 `transcription_too_long` sem ler o corpo. A conferência exata depois de `splitRecording` continua lá, para um WAV fora do formato canônico.

**3. Falha do provedor na linha do tempo.** `transcription_failed` entrou no vocabulário de eventos da chamada (`CALL_EVENT_KINDS`) e é gravado com o motivo, o HTTP, o motor e o modelo — sem áudio nem fala no payload. A linha do tempo mostra a frase do motivo (recusa da chave, modelo indisponível, sem crédito, região, limite de pedidos, fora do ar, resposta fora do formato) com o código e o HTTP como detalhe para quem opera. Chamada apagada a pedido do titular não ganha o evento.

**4. README.** A linha da transcrição já existia na tabela "O que ele faz hoje" desde o #187; ela agora conta o aviso do custo e a falha na linha do tempo, nos três idiomas.

**5. Ordem das falas: fora, por medição, sem meio-termo.** Fica como está — cada lado vira uma fala só — e a tela já declara isso ("sem a ordem das falas"). O motivo medido:

- `packages/voice-engine/src/engines/openai-realtime.ts` pede `response_format: "json"` e lê só `{ text }`; a referência da API diz que, para `gpt-4o-transcribe` e `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, **o único formato aceito é `json`**, e as marcações de tempo (`timestamp_granularities`, `segment`/`word`) exigem `verbose_json` — formato que esses modelos não aceitam (developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/transcriptions/methods/create, consultado em 14/11/2026).
- No Gemini a leitura é `candidates[0].content.parts[].text` (`gemini-live.ts`): texto puro, sem marcação nenhuma.
- Cada lado vai num pedido separado e independente; não há relógio comum entre os dois para intercalar a fala de um com a do outro.

Intercalar exigiria outro modelo (whisper-1, com `verbose_json`) ou uma segunda passada de detecção de fala por lado — outro custo, outra dependência e uma precisão que ainda não foi medida. Fica fora deste PR de propósito.

## Como provei

- `pnpm verify` (lint, tsc, cercas, unidade) pela lane: **rc=0**, 54 arquivos, 629 testes.
- `pnpm vitest run --project db apps/panel/src/app/api/v1/transcription.db.test.ts`: **rc=0**, 16 testes (Docker foi usado, o projeto `db` sobe o Postgres descartável).
- `pnpm release:check` com o fragmento `.changes/transcricao-aviso-e-falha.md`: rc=0.
- Teste novo do item 2: "gravação acima do limite é recusada pelo tamanho, sem o corpo ser lido". O arquivo tem 16 minutos a 8 kHz e **não** tem WAV válido dentro; a lista de leituras do processo (mock de `node:fs/promises`) prova que o caminho da gravação não foi lido.

**Sabotagem do item 2** (voltei a ler o arquivo inteiro antes de medir), rc=1 lido de arquivo:

```
× gravação acima do limite é recusada pelo tamanho, sem o corpo ser lido 73ms
AssertionError: expected [ 422, 'transcription_unreadable' ] to deeply equal [ 409, 'transcription_too_long' ]
- 409, "transcription_too_long"
+ 422, "transcription_unreadable"
Tests 1 failed | 14 passed (15)
```

Restaurado por `cp` + `cmp` (`CMP_OK`), de volta a verde: 16 testes, rc=0.

**Sabotagem do item 3** (sem emitir o evento):

```
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ [ 'transcription_failed', …(4) ] ]
- [ [ "transcription_failed", "unreachable", 500, "openai-realtime", "gpt-4o-mini-transcribe" ] ]
+ []
Tests 1 failed | 15 passed (16)
```

Restaurado por `cp` + `cmp` (`CMP_OK`), de volta a verde: 16 testes, rc=0.

**Sabotagem do item 1** (o aviso nunca aparece): `expected false to be true`, rc=1; restaurado, 2 testes verdes.

## O que não medi

- **Tela em navegador:** não subi o painel para conferir o aviso e o evento na tela. O que está provado é o teste da condição do aviso, os três dicionários e a renderização do evento no mesmo componente que o resto da linha do tempo; não há captura.
- **Provedor de verdade:** nem OpenAI nem Gemini foram chamados com chave, então o formato da falha real continua simulado, como no #185.
- **WAV com blocos extras:** a medida do tamanho assume o formato canônico do gravador; outro WAV passa por ela e é recusado na conferência exata, depois da leitura — não há teste para esse caminho.

## Sobre o escopo

A proposta é sugestiva: aprovar só parte, pedir mudança ou recusar não tem problema nenhum, e nada aqui depende de o resto entrar. O que o mantenedor pode trocar sem mexer na ideia:

- **Texto do aviso** (`transcribeAlsoClassifies` nos três dicionários): hoje cita desfecho e análise juntos; dá para separar em duas frases, ou mostrar só quando o desfecho estiver ligado, como a issue descreve.
- **Posição do aviso:** está logo abaixo do botão; pode virar nota acima da `hint`, ou um `Notice`.
- **Vocabulário do payload de `transcription_failed`:** hoje `{ reason, status, engine, model }`; cabe `side` (`user`/`agent`) se quiser dizer qual lado falhou, e o teto de 44 bytes/4 por quadro pode ir para `@deskvoice/voice-engine` se a conta for usada em outro lugar.
- **Frases de motivo:** as sete do dicionário seguem o vocabulário de `KEY_CHECK_RESULTS`; dá para encurtar ou reaproveitar as do desfecho.
- **Formato da gravação recusada:** se preferir medir pelo cabeçalho em vez do tamanho, é uma troca local na rota.
- **Item 5:** se quiser intercalar de verdade, o caminho é outro PR (outro modelo ou uma passada de detecção de fala por lado), com o custo medido antes.

author: neel2107
body:
Closes #1897 ## Problem Typing `maps` offered "Search Google Maps ⇥" only through the inline completion: history completed `maps` to `maps.google.com`, and `offeredSiteSearch` (`packages/core/src/siteSearch.ts`) matched that host. `findScope("maps")` on its own matches nothing, because the site-label rule only covers two-label hosts. The completion runs only when "When input looks like a website" is set to open it. Several onboarding presets set the bar to search first (`state/onboarding/presets.ts`), and Redo Setup… lets an existing user apply one. Also, since October Chromium has recorded only the end of a redirect chain, and `maps.google.com` redirects to `google.com/maps`, so newer history may not hold that host. In either case `maps` no longer completed and Tab offered nothing. I couldn't tie the report to one commit. The reporter's setting would confirm the search-first cause. The fix works whatever the cause. ## Change - `SiteSearch` gets an optional `keyword`. Google Maps has `keyword: "maps"`, so typing `maps` offers it with or without a completion. - Custom engine keywords and providers are checked first and still win. - The two-label rule is unchanged, so generic first labels like `open` or `apps` still don't take Tab. - `maps near me` is still a plain search. - The iPhone bundle (`ardia-core.js`) is regenerated; it changes by the same three lines. iPhone's `mobileFindScope` uses the same rule, so `maps` scopes there too. ## Verification (screenshots and videos) ![Before and after test runs for #1909](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Neel2107/arcadia/pr-media/proof-1909.png) - New test in `packages/core/src/siteSearch.test.ts`: `maps` with no completion offers Google Maps and Tab enters it; `maps` + `.google.com` still does; `open` and `maps near me` offer nothing; `google` still offers Google. It fails on main and passes here. - `pnpm -C packages/core test` passes (109 tests, bundle check included). - `pnpm -C apps/browser test` passes (2652 tests, 0 failures, conventions included), and `tsc -p apps/browser` passes. - The command bar itself wasn't exercised in the Mac app; this was run on Linux. ## Telemetry New usage counts `site_search_tab_enters` and `site_search_tab_enters_without_completion`, counted where Tab enters a site search (`components/omnibox/omniboxKeys.ts`). They live in `telemetry/siteSearchCounts.ts` and are sent with `focusFeatureCounts`. The "without completion" share shows how often the keyword is what made the offer. The parity row names both. The What's Sent list names them too. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge.

Summary

The PR makes `maps` offer Google Maps without an inline completion and adds counts for Tab-to-search use. - Typing `maps` offers Google Maps as a site search. - The browser counts Tab entries into site searches. Reviews (7) · Last reviewed commit: ["What's Sent names the site search Tab co..."](https://github.com/ardia-browser/ardia/commit/6b54621c85939a0bb7e7a7ea1be5dd67f0daa658) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=ardia-browser/ardia)

body:
## Vercel Speed Insights Installation Complete

Successfully installed and configured Vercel Speed Insights for this static HTML website project.

### Implementation Summary

**Project Type:** Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript website (no build process or package manager)

**Installation Method:** Added Vercel Speed Insights script tags directly to HTML files (as recommended by official Vercel documentation for vanilla HTML sites)

### Changes Made

**Modified Files (23 total):**
- `index.html` - Main landing page
- `lessons/*.html` (15 files) - All lesson pages (0001-0015)
- `reference/*.html` (6 files) - All reference sheet pages (01-06)
- `simulados/index.html` - Exam simulation page

**Script Tags Added:**
Each HTML file now includes the following scripts in the `<head>` section, immediately after the viewport meta tag:

```html
<!-- Vercel Speed Insights -->
<script>
  window.si = window.si || function () { (window.siq = window.siq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js"></script>
```

### Implementation Details

1. **Documentation Source:** Fetched latest installation instructions from official Vercel documentation (https://vercel.com/docs/speed-insights/quickstart)

2. **Framework-Specific Approach:** For static HTML sites, Vercel Speed Insights doesn't require npm package installation. Instead, it uses a CDN-based approach with two script tags that:
   - Initialize a tracking queue function (`window.si`)
   - Load the actual tracking code from Vercel's CDN (`/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js`)

3. **Placement:** Scripts were placed after the viewport meta tag for optimal performance, with the `defer` attribute ensuring non-blocking page load behavior.

4. **Coverage:** All 23 HTML files across the entire site now have Speed Insights enabled, ensuring comprehensive performance monitoring.

### How It Works

Once deployed to Vercel:
- Vercel automatically provides routes at `/_vercel/speed-insights/*` to collect performance events
- The tracking script loads asynchronously without blocking page rendering
- Performance metrics will be available in the Vercel dashboard under Speed Insights

After deployment to Vercel, Speed Insights will automatically begin collecting performance data. Access the metrics through:

No additional configuration is required.

author: fprochazka
body:
One Spring Boot starter per Boot minor, so a starter always means exactly one Boot minor and can pin that minor's floors.

- **Boot 3:** `typed-ids-spring-boot-30`, `-31`, `-32` (now 3.2 only) and new `-33`, `-34`, `-35`, pulling `typed-ids-hibernate-61/62/63` + `typed-ids-jackson2` + `typed-ids-openapi-swagger2`.
- **Boot 4:** `typed-ids-spring-boot-40` (now 4.0.1 – 4.0.x) and new `-41`, pulling `typed-ids-hibernate-72` + `typed-ids-jackson3` + both OpenAPI modules. `-42` is in the repository and tested against Spring Boot 4.2.0-RC2, but uses `library-internal` and is not published.
- **Floors:** each starter pins Hibernate, Jackson and Spring Framework at the higher of what its minor's first Boot release manages and what its own typed-ids modules declare. A lower pin would be untested and Maven's nearest-wins would hand it to users without the Boot BOM; this raises `-30`/`-31`/`-32` Hibernate to 6.1.7 / 6.2.46 / 6.3.2 (the module versions). Values are in `docs/spring-boot-compat-matrix.md` §5 and the README.
- **Tests:** one starter test module per minor, each on the newest patch of its own minor: 3.0.13, 3.1.12, 3.2.12, 3.3.13, 3.4.13, 3.5.16, 4.0.9, 4.1.2, 4.2.0-RC2.

author: huyhcm2k5it
body:
Fixes three Huy integration defects found by a deeper review:

- Catalog serializes Identity access updates by canonical user ID even before a projection row exists, so concurrent equal-version conflicting events cannot both commit inbox receipts.
- Clinical visit detail exposes labRequests[].sourceVersion for revisioned LAB replacements. The generated HTTP contract also includes PUBLISHED/CANCELLED terminal states.
- Diagnostic acknowledges shared Billing events owned by Appointment/Pharmacy without creating LAB retries or dead letters. Existing LAB settlement/fence checks remain; storage failures retry. SettlementDecision has no sourceType, so absent local sources are treated as foreign under the documented causal chain. Restore owned LAB orders before replaying payment history after a database restore.

Regression coverage includes a deterministic real-PostgreSQL concurrency barrier, LAB resubmit driven by public detail, and real receiver/inbox checks for duplicate foreign Billing events. Targeted Catalog/Clinical PostgreSQL tests, Diagnostic use-case tests, OpenAPI/schema checks, API matrix (86 operations) and topology checks passed locally. All Huy CI jobs passed: go test -race, go vet, go build, PostgreSQL integration suites for all three services, broker/cache integration, response-contract and architecture checks. Local full Diagnostic PostgreSQL integration also passed, including durable inbox/no-retry coverage.

No migrations, online data edits, env files, private keys or personal plans are included. CL-011 doctor-wide medical history remains intentionally blocked pending its access policy/projection; patient-owner reads are supported.

author: yuanying
body:
## 何を変えたか

サブエージェントの仕組みを、実装の前に設計として記録する。runner・backend・web の実装と `packages/contract` の型は、この PR の後の作業単位で入れる。

### ADR-0022

- サブエージェントは、runner が Pi の SDK で回す別のセッション。非同期で、起こすツールはすぐ返る。
- サブエージェントが話せる相手は本体だけ。`reply`・`reply_to_agent`・予約は本体の道具のまま（A2A の CLI は shell の道具なので子も使える）。
- 往復: サブエージェントは最後の地の文を返して止まり、本体は止まったサブエージェントに続きを送れる。走っているサブエージェントには割り込まない。状態は running / waiting / closed。
- 寿命: 本体が閉じるまで残り、夜の切り替えもまたぐ。runner の再起動で切れたサブエージェントは「中断した」と知らせ、続きを送れば再開する。
- 本体 → サブエージェントはツールで runner の中を直接渡す。サブエージェント → 本体は `self-events`。backend はサブエージェントの列を持たない。
- プロンプトの線引き（ADR-0008 の具体化）: runner の固定の文は仕組みの事実だけにする。サブエージェントの働き方は `/memory/agents/default.md` と役割のファイル `/memory/agents/<名前>.md`、本体の心得は skill `/memory/skills/subagents/SKILL.md` に書く。
- ツールは本体にだけ渡す 4 つ: `subagent_start`（名前・目的・最初の頼み・任意の役割と作業の場所）・`subagent_send`（止まって待っているものに続きを送る）・`subagent_list`（名前・状態・目的・作業の場所）・`subagent_close`（走っていれば取り消して閉じる）。名前を `subagent_*` にし、文書でも「サブエージェント」で揃えて、A2A の外のエージェント（`reply_to_agent`、`source: a2a`）と言葉を分けた。起こすと続きを 1 つのツールにまとめなかったのは、起こすときだけ効く引数（目的・役割・作業の場所）を続きのときにどう扱うかの決まりが要るためである。

### 決めた細部

| 項目 | 決めたこと | 理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| サブエージェントの名前 | 本体が付ける。英小文字・数字・`-`、63 文字まで、`main` は不可。閉じたサブエージェントとも重ねない | `/sources/self/<名前>/` と `~/agents/<名前>/` にそのまま使う。重ねないことで、場所と記録が子 1 つに対応する |
| `self-events` の `source`・`stream`・`id` | `source` は `self`、`stream` はサブエージェントの名前（backend が `agent` から付ける）、`id` は `<サブエージェントの名前>/<止まった回の番号>` | A2A の `<Task>/<番号>` と同じ形。送り直しは `id` で重複として落ちる |
| 止まった理由 | `stopped`・`failed`・`interrupted` の 3 つ。結果か問いかは runner では見分けない | Pi の実行の終わりからは見分けられない。見分けるにはサブエージェントに道具を足すことになり、本体はどちらにしても地の文を読む |
| サブエージェントのターンの終わり | `POST /v1/turns/end` を送り、`/memory` をコミットする | サブエージェントの書いたものを、本体の次のターンを待たずに残す。本体のターンの途中の変更も一緒にコミットされることは受け入れる |
| サブエージェントのターンの畳み込み（ADR-0015） | 入れない | 地の文の無いターンに畳む前の頼みを送ると、その答えが本体に返す結果を置き換えてしまう。続きは直前の結果の上に立つことが多い |
| 役割を選んだとき | `default.md` の代わりに、役割の本文を固定の文の後ろに足す | `default.md` は「役割を選ばないとき」の役割である |
| 役割のファイルが無い・壊れているとき | サブエージェントを起こさず、ツールが理由を返す | 違う役割で黙って走らせない |
| `default.md` が無い・読めないとき | 固定の文だけで起こし、そのことをツールの結果に添える | 働き方のファイルが無いことでサブエージェントを起こせなくしない |
| サブエージェントの状態を UI に出す口 | sandbox 向けに `POST /v1/agents`、UI 向けに `GET /api/agents` と流れの `agent` を足す | サブエージェントは夜をまたいで残るので、流れが覚えている最近の 1000 件からは今のサブエージェントを組み立てられない |
| サブエージェントの名前での返事・A2A の返事・予約 | `400` で断る | サブエージェントには道具が無い。取り違えを防ぐためで、守りではない |

### 記憶の種（`assets/memory-seed/`）

`agents/default.md` と `skills/subagents/SKILL.md` の文面の案を置いた。仕組みは読まず、image にも入らない。オーナーが最初のコミットで本番の記憶に入れる。

日本語で書いた。どちらも記憶のファイルで、入れた後はエージェントが自分で保守し、オーナーも読んで直す。ほかの記憶（`personality.md` など）は日本語であり、ADR-0008 は英語のプロンプトの後ろに日本語の記憶をそのまま足す形を前提にしている。runner が持つ固定の文（英語）とは別のものである。

## コミット

ツールの決定と用語の揃えは `fixup!` のコミットにしてある。マージの前に `git rebase -i --autosquash` でまとめる。

## テスト

- `npm ci` の後に `make fmt-check vet typecheck lint test tidy vuln images`: 通った
- `git status --porcelain`: 空

body: ## What This PR now carries two docs catalog fixes. The copy-button change from #7785 was squash-merged into this branch. **Link values in the preview** - Catalog pages restore variable values from the link they were opened with. A link value is now kept only when it fits its variable: a finite number, a boolean, one of an enum's options, a colour, an image address, or text with no `<` or `>`. Anything else opens at its default, and a variable's declared default always passes. - The preview player runs the composition with `sandbox-origin="opaque"`, so the composition gets an origin of its own and cannot reach the docs page. - `chatgpt-exchange` sets its editable text with `textContent` and DOM nodes instead of building `innerHTML` from it. - New `check:registry-innerhtml` (`scripts/check-registry-innerhtml.mjs`). It fails any registry file that reads composition variables and adds markup writes (`innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`). The 25 files that do this today are listed with their current counts, which may only go down. Its test runs in `test:scripts`. **Link values in the copy buttons** Catalog pages now keep values that came from a shared link out of the copied install command, render command and agent request until the reader sets them on the page. A page opened with link values says so and offers **Reset to defaults**. The install command wraps instead of scrolling sideways. ## Why **Preview:** A shared link decides what values the preview composition receives, and several registry items write variable values as markup. The type checks keep a link to values that a control could have produced, and the opaque origin keeps whatever the composition does inside the preview. The new check stops new items from adding markup writes, so the remaining items can be converted over time. **Copy buttons:** A catalog page restores tuned values from its `vars-` query string, and the copy buttons treated those values as if the reader had typed them: - The install and render commands quote values for bash and zsh only. PowerShell, cmd.exe and fish read the same quoting differently. - The agent request is pasted into a coding agent as the reader's own request, so any text in it reads as an instruction. - Values from the link were restored without any sign they came from the link, and the install command was one line that scrolled, so a long value could hide the rest of the command. ## Related work None. Converting the other 24 listed files to `textContent` is follow-up work, and the check keeps that list from growing. ## How **Preview** - `declaredValues` in `docs/snippets/catalog-detail.jsx` now takes the declared variables rather than only their ids, and checks each value with `fitsVariable`. The thresholds are 10,000 characters for text and 2,048 for an image address. Image addresses must be `http(s)` or a relative path, with no whitespace, quotes, brackets or backslashes. Colours must be hex, a name, or `rgb()`/`hsl()`. Values typed into the panel are unaffected; this only applies to what is read back from the URL. - Opaque mode was chosen because the bootstrap already drives the player only through its public API (`ready`, `seek`, `play`, `currentTime`) and receives edits via `postMessage`. Every asset under `/public/catalog/` is served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so fonts and the GSAP vendor file still load from the opaque frame. The payloads' `localStorage`/`indexedDB` uses are already behind `try`/`typeof` guards. - Catalog outputs (`docs/public/catalog/...`, the generated `.mdx`) are left to the publish automation, as source PRs require. **Copy buttons** - `catalog-detail.jsx` tracks which variables the reader set on the page (`edited`) and which ones the link opened it with. The edited list is published as `window.__hfEditedVars[]` before the existing `hf-vars-changed` event, so the separate install-command component can read it. - A new `// >>> copied values` section adds `plainLinkValue` and `copiedValues`: - **Commands** (install and render) keep a link value the reader has not set only if it is a number, a boolean, or text of at most 200 characters made of letters, digits, spaces and `. , : _ # + - / @ ( ) ?`. None of these is syntax inside the argument in bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell or cmd.exe. - **The agent request** keeps such a value only if it is a number, a boolean or one of the item's declared enum options. A link's free text never goes in. - Values the reader set on the page are kept as before. - `install-command.jsx` `varsArgument(raw, edited)` applies the same command rule. - A notice above the action bar lists the link-set values the reader has not touched yet. Its **Reset to defaults** button resets the values, the notes and the query string; the panel's Reset now does the same. - `custom.css`: `.hf-install-command code` wraps (`white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere`) in place of the `overflow-x-auto whitespace-nowrap` utilities. ## Test plan - `node --import tsx --test scripts/catalog-detail.test.ts scripts/check-registry-innerhtml.test.mjs` at the combined head: 35 pass. **Preview** - Before the copy-button change, the same two files: 33 pass. - With the old `catalog-detail.jsx` restored, the three link-value and preview tests fail. With the old `chatgpt-exchange.html` restored, the check's "passes this repository" test fails (6 writes, 4 allowed). - Headless Chrome, `chatgpt-exchange` loaded with a stubbed `getVariables`: - With default values, the `#cge-screen` DOM is byte-identical before and after. - With markup in `row1Use`, `tableHeadUse` and `prompt`, the old file created `` elements and ran their `onerror`. The new file shows the text as written and creates no elements. - Headless Chrome, the docs bootstrap served locally against the committed payloads for `chatgpt-exchange`, `aurora` and `frost-sequence-camera-orbit`, old versus new: - In both, the player reaches `ready`, `currentTime` advances, and a posted edit remounts and resumes from the current time. - With the change, the inner frame's sandbox is `allow-scripts` only, and the docs page can no longer read its document. - `aurora` renders blank in both versions because the headless browser has no GPU. Frost's "no WebGPU adapter" error appears in both versions for the same reason. - `oxfmt --check .`, `oxlint .`, `tsc -p scripts/tsconfig.json` and `lint-registry-items` are clean. **Copy buttons** - [x] On the copy-button branch, `node --import tsx --test scripts/catalog-detail.test.ts`: 30 pass. - [x] New "a link's text that a shell could read as syntax stays out of the install command": quotes, `&`, `|`, `$()`, `%VAR%`, `!x!`, newlines, curly quotes and text over 200 characters are dropped; plain text, numbers and booleans are kept; a value the reader set is kept with the existing quoting. - [x] New happy-dom test mounts the catalog page and the install command from a link whose text value carries a command and an instruction: - The notice names the link values. - The install command, render command and agent request carry the number and enum values but not the text. - After typing into the field, the typed text is in all three and the notice drops that value. - **Reset to defaults** clears the notice, the command suffix and the query string. - [x] Both new tests fail with this PR's `catalog-detail.jsx` and `install-command.jsx` reverted. - [x] `generate-catalog-pages`, `check-docs-snippet-motion` and `check-comment-citations` tests pass (188 total, together with the file above). - [x] `oxfmt --check .`, `oxlint .` and `tsc --noEmit -p scripts/tsconfig.json` are clean. - [ ] Not checked: the deployed page in a real browser with Mintlify's styles. The notice uses the panel's existing tokens and `hf-ve-action` button. - [x] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Manual testing performed - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.

## OTIO-2.4: keep media references that are not active (H4)

Plan: `docs/plans/OTIO-INTEGRATION-2026-10-24.md` (OTIO-2.4, H4; acceptance: inactive references are written back). Before this, a `Clip.2` with several `media_references` (for example a proxy and the full-resolution file) imported only the active one. The export then wrote a single `DEFAULT_MEDIA`, so the others were lost.

**Import.** CFA4 still plays the active reference (the named key, or the first one if that key is missing). The other references, and the active key when it is not `DEFAULT_MEDIA`, are kept unchanged in the clip's existing `interchange` map (OTIO-2.1) under the `cfa4` entry. That key is never a foreign metadata key, so there is no collision. No project-model change. They count against the same 16 MB kept-data budget as foreign metadata (warning past it). A clip with only its default reference keeps nothing.

**Export.** The kept references are written back under their own keys, next to the active one, with the same `active_media_reference_key`. The `cfa4` interchange entry never goes into `metadata`.

**Sample checks.** `otio_samples.expect_media` adds `other_references` (the inactive keys) for every clip, and `sample_item_problems` compares them (the `multi` sample: `["DEFAULT_MEDIA"]`, active `HIGH`).

### Tests
- `inactive_media_references_round_trip`: the active reference is the media; the proxy reference is written back byte-for-byte equal (its own metadata included); the active key stays `HIGH`; a second round trip is stable; a single default reference keeps nothing.
- Python: `test_inactive_media_references_are_expected_back`, and the updated media expectations.

### Gates run locally
- `cargo test -p cfa4-interchange` with `CFA4_OTIO_SAMPLES_DIR` (13 fresh samples, `oracle_samples` included): green.
- `cargo clippy -p cfa4-interchange --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. rustfmt on the changed files.
- `ruff check python`, `ruff format --check` on the touched files, `mypy` (strict, pinned 2.4.1) on the touched files: clean.
- `pytest python/tests` (without Qt GUI): 332 passed, 38 skipped.
- Merged with main after #1202 (the conflict in `test_otio_samples.py` resolved in main's typed style).

author: jd869
body:
Adds one entry, `entries/pets2026-euf-reidentification.yaml`, for *Access Granted, Privacy Lost: Formalizing & Quantifying the Hidden Anonymity Risks of Exclusive-Use Systems* (Ellis & Lin, PoPETs 2026(3), AEC issue 2026.3, badges available / functional / reproduced).

## What is tested

Only **Section 6.5, "Pool Re-identification (N=16)"** (p.40), which covers Figures 5 and 6. The artifact simulates 16 Teams-like users in four behaviour profiles over 10 runs. A passive observer sees only binary presence, typing and send signals. The artifact then measures how well those signals re-identify each user:
- **Figure 6:** the true user's rank in a leave-one-out posterior.
- **Figure 5:** each user's entropy loss ΔH and Bayes vulnerability V in the pool.

Per the paper (p.39), each user's top and bottom run is dropped, so 10 runs become 8 per user and 128 traces are evaluated.

Every threshold below is a number the paper prints:

| claim | paper (§6.5, p.40) | threshold | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `top1_accuracy_pct` | "Top-1 accuracy is 54.7%" (also abstract, §8) | == 54.7 | 54.7 (70/128) |
| `top3_accuracy_pct` | "top-3 accuracy reaches 89.1%" | == 89.1 | 89.1 (114/128) |
| `mean_true_rank` / `median_true_rank` | "mean rank 2.23 and median rank 1" | == 2.23 / == 1 | 2.23 / 1 |
| `mean_posterior_true` / `max_posterior_true` | "mean posterior … 0.275", "maxima approaching 0.832" | == 0.275 / == 0.832 | 0.275 / 0.832 |
| `pool_min_entropy_loss_bits` / `pool_max_entropy_loss_bits` | "approximately 0.68 to 2.44 bits" | == 0.68 / == 2.44 | 0.68 / 2.44 |
| `pool_mean_entropy_loss_bits` | "(mean 1.2 bits …)" | == 1.2 | 1.2 |
| `max_entropy_loss_is_diane_2` | "The strongest case, D2, loses 2.44 bits" | == 1 | 1 |
| `pool_min_vulnerability_pct` / `pool_max_vulnerability_pct` | "between 19% and 71%" | == 19 / == 71 | 19 / 71 |

Role `positive`, expected `REPRODUCED`. The claims, thresholds and protocols were fixed before the artifact first ran.

## Not tested

- **The §8 volume-only baseline.** The paper prints 44.5% Top-1, 72.7% Top-3 and mean rank 2.59. The artifact appendix's own output and this run both give 44.4%, 71.9% and 2.79. The paper's "+10.2 / +16.4 percentage points" therefore don't follow from the artifact. The entry records this and claims nothing about it.
- **§6.3/6.4** (pairwise indistinguishability games, Figures 3, 4 and 8) and the **PCA in Figure 7**. These are outside this subset.
- **Figures 1, 2 and 9 and the tables**, which are illustrative.

## Command shape

The command follows the README:
- It checks the pinned commit and fails if any tracked file is edited.
- It builds a Python venv with hash-pinned wheels. These are the artifact's own `requirements.txt` versions (18 packages), with cp312 sha256 values from PyPI.
- It runs the artifact's two scripts unmodified: `_run_sim_calc.sh` (simulation plus pairwise, pool and leave-one-out calculations) and `_run_plots.sh` (all plots and printed summaries), with `MPLBACKEND=Agg`.
- A short checker reads the printed True Rank and Pool Summary blocks. It requires exactly 128 traces and 16 distinct users with n=8 each, and fails on any Traceback or Error. It computes all 12 values into `amber-euf/metrics.json`; none are hardcoded.

The simulation seeds every run and user from sha256 of fixed strings, so output is deterministic. The run takes about 1.5 min including venv setup, with about 210 MB peak RSS.

## Verification

- **Two fresh clones.** The second run used the command parsed from the YAML. Both exited 0 (107 s and 94 s, 212 MB peak RSS) under a 2 GiB cap with swap off. The second run gave the same 12 metrics. The following were byte-identical between the runs:
  - all 183 generated `data/*` files
  - `versions.log`, `sim.log`, `plots.log` and `metrics.json`

  `plots.stderr.log` differs only in the absolute checkout path inside matplotlib warnings.
- **Matches the authors' run.** The printed True Rank and Pool Summary blocks are line-for-line identical to the output quoted in the artifact appendix.
- **Independent validator.** It uses only the raw `data/*.csv`, never the logs:
  - It recomputes each pool trace's H_post (−Σ p log2 p) and V (max p) from the full 16-way posterior vectors.
  - It applies the drop-min/max trim itself.
  - It checks the top-1 flags against the ranks.
  - It agrees with the checker on all 12 values: 70/128, 114/128, mean rank 2.2266, mean ΔH 1.2125 bits, extremes at Alice_2 and Diane_2.
- **Checker fixtures.** The checker rejected 25 incomplete or invalid inputs and accepted only the genuine output. The fixtures cover:
  - missing or empty logs, and a truncated run
  - a Traceback or Error in any log
  - a missing or duplicated True Rank block or line
  - a trace total other than 128
  - NaN or inf values
  - a dropped, duplicated or renamed pool user, or n ≠ 8
- **Tamper tests.** A wrong commit and an edited `calc.py` each stop the command before any output is written.
- **Measure replay.** Each claim's `measure.regex` and threshold, replayed against the fresh `metrics.json`, gives 12/12 REPRODUCED, matching the recorded baseline.

## Rerun

```
git clone https://github.com/OSUSecLab/EUF.git
cd EUF && git checkout 60212e23a04fa2398fbf32979e56343066b07620
```

Then run `run.command`. You need Python 3.12 with venv and network access to PyPI.

author: cpp-cat
body:
Seven fixes around the workspace IDE's save path and its neighbours. Nothing here changes what a pipeline, a rule, a report or a compile produces from a workspace's files.

## What changed

**Saves that check a file against the rest of the workspace.** A validator row may carry an `inWorkspace` check, given the workspace's tree as an `fs.FS` and run once the file's own validator refuses nothing (`workspace_file_validators.go`). Two rows use it:

- `.form.json`: a **warning** for each table a form's `dataTable` field draws that `table_configs/` does not hold (`workspace_form_tables.go`). A warning, since a form and its table are two saves in either order; the compile still refuses such a workspace.
- `reports/config.json`: **refuses** what `run_reports` refuses in the reports files the directives run: a file it cannot read as reports, an unclosed `{D:` date pattern, and a report with no output format where its name decides that (a name ending in a `{TOKEN}` is left to the run). Scripts and entries that are not files (report functions) are skipped. The reports-file reader and the output-format rule move from `run_reports/delegate` into `run_reports/directives` (`report_files.go`), so the run and the save share them. Checked against four workspaces' report files: 26 files, 89 reports, none refused.

**Root files save as overrides.** `SaveContent` wrote the disk, then the database refused a root file (`workspace_control.json`, `compile_workspace.sh`) for want of a first path segment as its content type, so the edit was lost at the next start. It now records a root file under content type `root`, and writes the database before the disk, so a refused database write leaves the disk untouched. (The 200-with-an-error half was already fixed by the 500 on a failed write.)

**A retired document's override is not written back.** The start-up override sync skips a `workspace_changes` row for a path in `workspace_assets.RetiredAssets` (`IsRetired`), and leaves the row in place.

**Pull Workspace with compile claims the compile before it pulls** (`claimPullCompile`), where it only checked for running tests, so a rules unit test requested during the pull raced the compile. A failed pull releases the claim through the row's `error` status.

**One test checks both copies of the IDE section contract.** A Go test reads `SERVER_SECTION_DECLARATION` and `EXPECTED_DECLARATION_CHECKSUM` from `jetsclient_ide/src/screens/sectionContract.ts` and compares them with `SectionDeclaration()`.

**One scratch-PostgreSQL fixture for `jets/datatable`'s `JETS_TEST_DSN` tests** (`scratch_postgres_test.go`: `scratchDSN`, `jetsSchemaTables`, `createTablesFromSchema`, `scratchDatabase`), replacing the suites' own copies, plus `source_period_test.go`: `InsertSourcePeriod`, and the failure row a register-key hook files under the period it returns, against the shipped tables.

This touches `jetsclient_ide/src/screens/sectionContract.ts` (comment only) and `jets/run_reports/`, outside the save path, minimally.

## Tests

- `go vet` and `go test -count=1` of `jets/datatable/...`, `jets/workspace`, `jets/workspace_assets`, `jets/run_reports/...`, `jets/cmds/install_workspace_assets` with `JETS_TEST_DSN` on a scratch PostgreSQL 16: all pass (two `jets/datatable` tests skip for their own corpus variables).
- Against the old code: the root-file test reproduced the defect (`failed to find contentType`, the disk already edited, no row); the retired-override test failed with the document written back; the pull test failed with the test queued (200) during the pull; the section test fails when the IDE copy drops a section.

## Documentation

- `developer/engine/sql-scripts.md`: a dated section on the reports-file checks at save.
- `developer/how-to/add-a-workspace-file-type.md`: the row's new `inWorkspace` field (the example row gains a fourth field).
- `developer/workspace/assets/user-flows.md`: a retired document's override is skipped at start.
- `user/screens/workspace-ide.md`: the form-table warning and the reports refusal.
- `user/screens/flows/pull-workspace-changes.md`: tests are refused from the start of a pull with compile.

No link was added; `npm run build` in `docs/` was not run here.

author: fat-git
body:
## Paperclip task

[FAT-3 — T1.1 — Vite + React + TS scaffold, CI, and GitHub Pages deploy](http://127.0.0.1:3100/issues/FAT-3)

## What changed

- React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 8 scaffold, `npm run build` → `dist/`.
- `base: '/haunted-walk/'` is defined once in `vite.config.ts` and reused for the manifest `id`, `start_url`, and `scope`; the service worker is registered explicitly at `/haunted-walk/sw.js` with scope `/haunted-walk/`.
- `vite-plugin-pwa` precaches the app shell, icons, manifest, and every `public/tours/**/*.json` file. OSM tiles are **runtime** `CacheFirst` only, `maxEntries: 250`, 7-day age — no bulk prefetch.
- CSP meta tag injected into the production HTML only: `script-src 'self'`, no `unsafe-eval`, network limited to self plus `*.tile.openstreetmap.org`, `object-src 'none'`. No analytics or third-party scripts.
- ESLint 10 (flat, typescript-eslint) + Prettier; Vitest for unit tests.
- CI on every PR: typecheck, lint, format check, unit tests, build, a post-build guard, and a separate `gitleaks` job. The gitleaks job is a hard failure, not a warning.
- Deploy workflow builds `dist/` and publishes it with the official Pages actions on push to `main`. It never pushes to `main` and assumes no merge commit.
- `scripts/check-dist-secrets.mjs` (`npm run check:dist`) fails the build on key-shaped strings in `dist/` and on a broken deployment contract (missing/wrong CSP, manifest `start_url`/`scope` not `/haunted-walk/`, missing SW precache).

## What I tested, and how

All run locally on Node 24.22.3:

- `npm ci` — clean install, 451 packages, no errors.
- `npm run typecheck` — passes.
- `npm run lint` — 0 problems, `--max-warnings=0`.
- `npm run format:check` — all matched files use Prettier style.
- `npm test` — 4/4 tests pass (base-path URL joining).
- `npm run build` — succeeds; `dist/` has `index.html`, hashed JS/CSS, `manifest.webmanifest`, `sw.js`; PWA precache 16 entries (270.74 KiB).
- `npm run check:dist` — OK, 13 files scanned.
- `npm run preview` — `GET /haunted-walk/`, `/haunted-walk/manifest.webmanifest`, `/haunted-walk/sw.js`, `/haunted-walk/favicon.svg`, `/haunted-walk/pwa-192x192.png`, `/haunted-walk/apple-touch-icon.png` all return `200`; `GET /` returns `302` to `/haunted-walk/`.
- Inspected the built output: SW registration is `/haunted-walk/sw.js` with `scope: '/haunted-walk/'`; manifest has `start_url`/`scope: '/haunted-walk/'`; CSP is present; precache list contains no OSM tile URLs; tile caching is runtime-only.
- Local `gitleaks` 8.30.1 (arm64): `gitleaks dir` and `gitleaks git` over the 2-commit history — no leaks found.

**Not tested here:** installing the PWA on a physical iOS/Android device and a real hard reload at the live URL. A feature branch cannot exercise the `main` Pages deployment; that verification belongs to the merge step.

## Decisions a reviewer would otherwise have to guess

- **CSP is injected at build time, not written in `index.html`.** Vite dev and React Fast Refresh use inline scripts that a strict `script-src 'self'` blocks. Production output — what Pages serves — is the strict policy, and `check:dist` asserts it ships.
- **TypeScript is pinned to `~5.9.3`, not 7.x.** `typescript-eslint` 8.72 declares `typescript <6.1`; TS 7 would break `npm ci` peer resolution. The rest of the toolchain (Vite 8, ESLint 10, Vitest 5) is current.
- **`gitleaks` is a separate job/check** so it can be marked required without also requiring anything else, and so a finding is visibly its own failure. Per the FAT-2 handoff note, `verify` and `gitleaks` are now required status checks on `main` (`strict` on), added only after this workflow's first green run.
- **Pages is now enabled** with `build_type: workflow` (the site 404s until the first `main` deploy, as expected). The deploy workflow also sets `enablement: true` so a re-created site does not fail the first run.
- **Lockfile is included** (`package-lock.json`); it is generated, so its size is expected.

## Checks

- [x] Branch is named `feature/FAT-3-vite-scaffold`
- [x] This PR is one task's worth of change, with no unrelated drive-by edits
- [x] **No credential, token, key or `.env` content is in this diff** — I checked the diff, not just my intent
- [x] No new network call to a keyed or paid service; the `$0`-cost and no-keys-in-the-browser constraints still hold
- [x] Any new dependency is justified above
- [x] CI is green — `verify` passed in 1m09s and `gitleaks` in 9s (run [43657456078](https://github.com/fat-git/haunted-walk/actions/runs/43657456078))

author: cucuteanu-tudor-912
body:
## Why

QA finding (Tudor's deep QA, fe-ui2, SHOULD-FIX). In the surveyor at 1440 px, clicking a takeoff row did nothing visible except tint the row. Its detail panel (settle, marks, Reject, sign-off) sits under every row of the takeoff column, 3781 px down on the sample. Only phones scrolled to it (SV-53 said a desktop must not scroll).

Repro on main: Try the sample project → Drawn plan 2 → surveyor → click "window count". Nothing shows until you scroll the column past 81 rows.

## What changed

- `frontend/src/surveyor/SurveyorScreen.tsx`: every user selection (click, Enter, a `?q=` change) now scrolls to the detail.
  - Desktop: the takeoff column has its own scroll. Only that column scrolls (`scrollTop` = the detail's offset minus the column's sticky head), so the page, the plan and the side panel stay put, and the column's head (Export CSV, Reset, progress) stays visible.
  - Phone: the page scrolls as before (`scrollIntoView`).
  - The default selection on open still does not scroll.
- `docs/specs/frontend/surveyor.md`: the desktop behaviour is added under SV-53.

## How it was verified

- Test first: SV-53 is rewritten to expect a scroll on a desktop too, and failed before the fix. A new SV-53 desktop case fakes a scrollable column and checks that the column scrolls while `scrollIntoView` (the page) does not. It fails on the old code.
- The surveyor test's `beforeEach` stubs `scrollIntoView`, which jsdom lacks.
- `./check.sh` (frontend) is green: 77 files, 1018 tests passed, plus lint, types, build and the API check.
- `npm run build` then `npx playwright test surveyor` (ports 8155/4355): 4 passed, desktop and phone.
- By hand in Chromium at 1440: after clicking "window count" and then "room count", the detail heading sits below the column's head, the page scroll stays at 0, and the screenshot shows the sign-off. At 390 the page scrolls the detail into view as before.
- Not run: the full e2e (the RAM rule allows single specs only).

## What needs a human

This reverses SV-53's "desktop does not scroll", which the orchestrator asked for when switching QA to fixing. If someone wants the detail somewhere else instead, for example above the tables, that's a design call.

## Definition of done (docs/ENGINEERING.md §7)

- [x] A test that fails without this change (bug fix) or covers the new behaviour (feature)
- [x] Lint, format check, type check and tests clean locally; CI green
- [ ] Diff reviewed by the orchestrator or a teammate
- [x] README, project guide in CLAUDE.md and decision records updated where this changes them
- [ ] Golden demo path (docs/QA.md §1) still works (not re-run in full; surveyor spec green)
- [x] No secrets, partner data, personal data or home paths in the diff

body: ## Summary Lets users edit the dock directly from the dock itself, without going through the settings window. **Right-click on the dock background** - Add a program / Add a folder - Add a separator at the clicked position - Unlock icons (reorder with the mouse) / Lock icons - Settings **Right-click on a pinned item** - Rename (display name) - Change location (.exe or folder picker, opened at the current location) - Open file location - Add a separator after - Remove from dock (not offered for the Settings item, same rule as the settings window) Right-clicking a running unpinned app also offers "Pin to dock". **Drag and drop** - While icons are unlocked, pinned items can be reordered by dragging them. A short click still launches the item; a thin border shows the unlocked state. - Programs (.exe), shortcuts (.lnk) and folders can be dropped from the desktop or Explorer onto the dock, at the drop position. MSI "advertised" shortcuts (VLC, Office...) are resolved through Windows Installer, since their target is an icon file. ## Screenshots Right-click on an icon: Right-click on the dock background: Separators in the dock: ## Implementation notes - New `DockSeparatorItemModel` with the `separatorItem` discriminator, also listed in the settings window. - New `iconsLocked` setting in config.json, defaulting to `true`, so existing configs keep their current behavior. - `DockService.InsertItem` to add an item at a given position. - `ShortcutResolver` (Infrastructure.Windows/Native) turns dropped files into launchable executables. - `LocalizationService.TextOr` returns a fallback for keys that older translations do not have yet. English and French strings are added; other languages fall back to English until translated. ## Compatibility A config.json containing a separator cannot be read by previous versions (unknown `separatorItem` type). Configs without separators are unaffected. ## Tests - 8 new tests: separator insertion and clamping, icons lock persistence, separator / lock JSON round-trip, loading a config without `iconsLocked`, shortcut resolution. - `dotnet build` with 0 warnings, all 55 tests pass. - Manually tested on Windows 11: context menus, separator placement, drag reorder, dropping an MSI shortcut from the desktop. ## Follow-ups As requested, the other changes that were in this PR are now separate PRs: the centering fix on scaled displays, the UI redesign, and dock themes.

At head `3f9db6afa47c7e1ca9bb4f4e587135947bda2b5c`, pinned Lean job https://github.com/d3lefts/d3lefts/actions/runs/43657456872 **FAILED** at `QuadraticBernoulliIdentity.lean:123:38` with an unsolved finite-sum polynomial-normalization goal. author: art-e-fish
body:
## Summary

Add `bridgeChannelApi(...).channel(id)` for the shared Bridges receiver/cache path: fixed-origin Discord Get Channel and Slack conversations.info reads, returning only a matching raw channel object. Root authenticates the bot/workspace, supplies `current()` for its connection/credential lifetime, and passes successful results to its bound `BridgeChannels` writer. Root wiring, authentication, cache validation, retry scheduling and activation remain separate.

The reader reacquires the token for every call, disables redirects, caps responses at 1 MiB and bounds holder acquisition + headers + body to one 15-second injected-clock deadline. Stale or unsuccessful reads return undefined, leaving receipt retry/expiry to the receiver. No legacy admission engine or internal service permission checks. Site-silent choice: platform refusal and transient failures both remain retryable; no message is dropped by metadata lookup.

Endpoints checked against [Discord Get Channel](https://github.com/discord/discord-api-docs/blob/main/developers/resources/channel.mdx#get-channel) and [Slack conversations.info](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.info/).

## Evidence

Before: the legacy REST readers produce legacy admission/inspection results; the shared receiver has no raw channel REST reader. Removing the new matching-id check makes three new regressions fail (Discord wrong/missing id and Slack wrong id return objects instead of undefined). Restored implementation: 74 tests pass across channel-api, receiver and normalize; targeted strict TypeScript check and diff whitespace check pass. Fake-clock regressions cover stalled holder/headers/body, shared deadline, invalidation during each async stage, no late-token HTTP and cancellation of late responses. No live network, credentials or data.

Cold review: three rounds, stopping at R3 CLEAR on frozen a9b7235b4554f65f20628880fa6669c1baf91dfd. R1 found a real delayed-timer expiry gap: folded an absolute-clock deadline at every async boundary and tests that fail when it is removed. Also folded raw kind/workspace delegation tests. R2 requested no-retry assertions and token-rotation evidence; folded both. R3 found only a test nit about success-shaped error bodies; folded after CLEAR and reran all 74 tests plus strict TypeScript. No claim that the final test-only fold was frozen-reviewed. The later public-return race described below supersedes that earlier assessment. Ledger/evidence: loom note loom/2026-11-14-bridge-channel-api-review.

Follow-up at ecb525fbff544afe03519cbc0359e7a3311db0c6: the final Promise.race await now rechecks connection lifetime and the absolute deadline before publishing its result. Four new regressions (Discord/Slack × queued lifetime/deadline changes) failed before with stale metadata and pass after. All 78 tests across channel-api, receiver and normalize pass; targeted strict TypeScript and diff checks pass. Credential follow-up cold R1 CLEAR on frozen ecb525fb, TREE b3099f8c4d16bbdcc40cba83b2c6c62709ead55156398b6a492ad2390fdf0c74, no findings. Prior three rounds reviewed the original reader; this new round reviews the follow-up patch. No known hole remains.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: additive adapter only; no registration or production root activation. Incorrect wiring could expose a token or release stale channel metadata; endpoint/lifetime/deadline tests cover this reader. Root must authenticate each configured bot/workspace and invalidate the reader and cache on connection/credential changes. No schema, site, daemon, host, installed-piece, deploy or real-data changes.

## Summary

Watchdog digest 2026-11-14: `discover — silent for 24d (window 4d)`. The timer and unit are healthy and the writer key is unchanged; discover has shed on every hourly run since the shared UW governor landed (last ok heartbeat 2026-10-21T16:00:54Z), and shed runs wrote no `discover` row, so the outage showed only as silence.

## What changed

- `scripts/utils/uw_governor.py`: `snapshot()` adds `minute_window_clears_at`, when the minute window next admits standard work (None while it has room).
- `scripts/discover.py`:
  - The admission retry waits for the later of the provider embargo and a full minute window. Before, an expired embargo with a full window computed a 0s wait and shed with no retry (2026-11-13 21:00Z ledger: scanner + flow-analysis used 45 + 51 = 96 standard admissions in the first 20s).
  - The market-wide dark-pool scoring walk is capped at `DISCOVER_MAX_SCORED_TICKERS = 25`, ranked by flow alerts and then premium. About 127 tickers could not fit 96/min in the 137s budget; the 2026-10-29 run skipped 111 of 112.
  - Shed and degraded runs write a `discover` service_health `error` row naming the reason (no provider text).
- `scripts/watchdog/check.py`: stale lines append `— market <state>` only when the service's window differs by market state. The watchdog never downgraded the severity; the suffix was copy only.
- Tests: `test_discover.py` (+5), `test_uw_governor.py` (+1), new `test_watchdog/test_stale_market_label.py`. `test_scan_service_health.py::test_error_payload_skips_heartbeat` previously asserted no row at all, which is the silent-outage shape. It now asserts no ok row and an error row.

## Test plan

- [x] Red: the 4 new discover tests, the governor test and the watchdog label test failed before the fix.
- [x] Focused local: watchdog + discover + governor + flow-refresh + scan health suites, 600 passed.
- [x] Full local `pytest scripts -n auto`: 19472 passed, 2 failed (`test_marketdesk_pdf_sim.py`). Those 2 also fail on the base commit and are in files this PR does not touch.
- [ ] CI: pending

## Risk and rollback

- A shed hour now leaves `discover` in `error` (P2 digest, red banner) until the next clean run, where before it left nothing.
- Discover scores at most 25 market-wide tickers per run.
- The options-flow wait can take up to 60s of the 137s budget, and the existing deadline still bounds the walk.
- Rollback: revert this commit.

## Operator Next Steps

None. The fix takes effect on the next RTH radon-flow-refresh fire (Mon 2026-11-16 14:00 UTC). Watch the first runs for a `discover` ok row or an error row with a reason.

- [x] Red/green TDD (failing test, then fix)
- [x] Stage only the files this change owns (no `git add -A`)

author: fyremael
body:
QFT-COND EXT-015 / 180: finite Gaussian-width independence over **compact distribution** coefficients; a new bounded mathematical source test continuing protected 177.

**New analytic lemma:** the one-sided Paley–Wiener support indicator of a nonzero compact distribution has a finite exponential rate and cannot decay like exp(−δ t²+Rt) along a positive real Laplace ray. Explicit external analytic premise: classical Paley–Wiener support-indicator theorem (Boman–Hörmander 1999, Introduction (1.1)–(1.3); source URL in primary).

**Main theorem:** Suppose a *finite* sum of Gaussian convolutions with pairwise distinct positive width ratios equals zero on a nonempty output interval. Analytic continuation and Fourier–Laplace at imaginary frequency, divided by the maximum-width Gaussian factor, would make the maximum-width compact coefficient Laplace transform decay super-Gaussianly; the support indicator forces that coefficient zero. Descending induction excludes all distinct widths. Fixed finite Hermite derivatives transfer to compact coefficients. No uniform regulator-zero estimate is used.

**Restricted 108 consequence:** For any genuine legal completed finite terminal-factorizable history of protected 177, exact equality to A=χ(x)e(x)ρ(z)κ_ε(z) requires all non-target width blocks to vanish and the width-one effective coefficient to equal χe⊗δ. author: pedropedrassolli
body:
O duelo precisa ser rápido (pedido do Pedro).

- **jemalloc** no container, pelo `LD_PRELOAD`, como no Dockerfile padrão do Rails 8: o Ruby e a engine fragmentam menos a memória e respondem um pouco mais rápido. O pacote tem uns 700 KB.
- **YJIT**: o Rails já liga sozinho (`load_defaults 8.1`) e a imagem oficial do Ruby já vem com ele. Agora o `/up/engine` responde `yjit` e `jemalloc`, e a CI recusa a imagem sem os dois.
- *Medição da engine* passa a medir também o `/up/db` (ida e volta ao banco).
- ADR 0004: a decisão e a medição de hoje, antes do jemalloc. Ação fria p50 29,9 ms e p95 47,9 ms, quente p50 1,5 ms e p95 4,6 ms. A primeira chamada depois de um tempo parado levou 4,2 s, que é o container subindo.

Depois do deploy, rodo a medição de novo para comparar.

author: christian-rogobete
body:
Before this change, the window store kept every counted total-budget row for the life of its policy, whatever its age. Each payment under a `total_budget` criterion added a row that no pruning removed. The window file grew with every payment toward its size limit, at which new operations refuse with `operation.capacity`. The store wrote authorized spend as an ordinary confirmed row, and a checked success left its rows unchanged. No row recorded that a later release could no longer change it, so no row was safe to compact. An agent that pays unattended within a signed limit needs that history compacted, and every charge must keep its full amount. The CLI warning, the CLI reference, and the rustdoc also tied a new allocation to a new signature. The store keyed each allocation by the signed policy digest.

This change:

- Adds the `final_total` record status for a total-budget charge that no supported release changes. Admitted authorized spend and the total rows of a consumption without a transaction are written with it. A transaction consumption stays pending.
- Marks a counted total row final when a retained attempt of its authorization holds a checked success, whatever status the row reached. Every writer's pruning and a reset apply this marking through `promote_final_totals`. Under the terminal-record cap and the age limit, the success record stays while a total hold or an unmarked counted row of its authorization remains.
- Promotes a confirmed row of a file below version 15 only when its origin is proved. Anonymous authorized spend without a link qualifies, and so does the retained spend of a consumption without a transaction. Linked claims, negative rows, and rows without an epoch stay individual. The first commit of such a file applies the promotion, whichever writer commits.
- Adds an optional `total_sums` list to the window file. Each `WireTotalSum` holds the settled amount of one scope, canonical asset bucket, and policy digest, with the latest folded timestamp and no row count. Durable admission and hydration count each sum at its full amount, and a reset carries every sum into its successor.
- Folds each final row strictly older than one week into its sum, and the same commit removes the row. A row whose receipt projection is still owed stays a row. The additions are checked before the working copy changes, and an overflow refuses the write with the detail `a total-budget sum overflows`. The refused write leaves the file and the commit counter unchanged.
- Makes `prune_stale` return a result that every writer propagates. The operation recorder and an exposed consumption now prune before they append audit rows, so a refused fold appends none.
- Keeps the read-only operation status on `prune_lifecycle`, which prunes without promotion or folding. The status and recovery views keep every proof and report an unrelated attempt beside a sum that cannot fold.
- Validates sums and final markers in the current and the prepared image. A sum needs a total bucket, a nonnegative amount, a canonical key no other sum shares, and exactly its known fields. A final marker needs a nonnegative total row with an epoch.
- Adds window file version 15 as `WIRE_VERSION_TOTAL_SUMS`, which a file with a final row or a sum selects. A final row or a sum in a file below version 15 refuses as invalid. The retirement threshold for earlier builds stays at version 12.
- Corrects the total-budget guidance in the CLI warning, the CLI reference, and the rustdoc of the policy limits and the state store. The warning for a signed change now reads `The changed policy digest starts a new total_budget allocation.`
- Updates existing tests to the new status and version. A ledger test and a version 12 reset test now expect final rows where they expected confirmed ones, and their other assertions stay. The destination tests expect a maximum version of 15.
- Adds two changelog fragments.

Charges keep their full amount: a fold, restart, reset, or clock change never lowers a total, and every existing release path stays as it was. A file selects version 15 only once it holds a final row or a sum, so a file without such charges keeps the version its fields need. A version 12, 13, or 14 file stays readable without retirement or a new signature. It moves to version 15 on the first commit that marks a final row or writes a sum. A file at version 15 keeps that floor, and a build capped at version 14 refuses it with `UnsupportedVersion`, as a current and as a prepared image. The `total_sums` key is absent while no sum exists, and each sum stores its amount as a decimal string. No error code is added, and a total overflow during a send reaches the CLI and MCP as `submission.record_unavailable`. In the CLI JSON output, the `warnings` text of a signed counterparty change with a total budget carries the new wording. A row without proof that its charge is final stays an individual row, so folding compacts only final charges.

On 11afc568 plus the change of #720, the core, network, CLI, and MCP suites passed in both feature states with `TMPDIR` and `STELLAR_AGENT_HOME` unset, as CI runs them: 9,938 and 10,643 tests. Clippy in both states, the network rustdoc build, the format check, the feature-discipline check, the docs-style check, and the changelog check passed too. A documentation sentence and one test name changed after that run; the format and docs-style checks and the renamed test passed again in both feature states.

author: jakechampion
body:
Refs #15268, #15563. The owner asked for one pull request that carries the repairs of main, because each repair alone still failed the tests that a different pull request repaired.

Some first repairs of this branch reached main by other pull requests in the meantime (the runtime need roots, the audio tag count, the leak census row, #15963). What this branch still changes against main:

## 1. A miscompile: `set_args` and the sole-array rule

ee090a60 lets an array stay sole after a call whose result and other arguments are scalars, because such a callee has no place to keep a reference.
`set_args` has one: its runtime keeps the array in the state of the process.
The caller then wrote the array in place, so `args()` gave the new elements, and one block leaked.

`ssasem.keeps_argument` names the builtins that keep a borrowed argument, and `ssaunits.keeps_no_loan` refuses them.
`TestSelfHostSetArgs/lent-array` fails on main on the three targets and passes here.

## 2. An allocation regression: the finalizer of `Call` is reverted

#15985 gave a parked `Call` a finalizer that reads a cell. The serve loop parks each handler one time, so the cell is one allocation for each request, and `TestSelfHostServeAllocsPerRequest` pins 0.
#15985 is mine. It had the `merge-queue-hold` label for this reason when it merged.

The two commits of #15985 are reverted. A parked `Call` has no finalizer again, and `call_cancel` ends it. The finalizer of `Task` (#15958) stays: it costs no allocation in that loop.
The finalizer of `Call` comes back when its state costs no allocation (a generation in the runtime task record, #15051).

## 3. Test repairs from other sessions

- `fix/physical-credit-helper-layout-20261114` (#15968), merged as it is.
- e0630fcd of #15986, by cherry-pick: "drivers: the credit proof controls use a box with no shape word". #15986 has other changes that are not repairs, and they are not here.

## 4. `spec/core.md`

The table gets the rows of the ops `load`, `map_file` and `scan_masks`, from `FERN_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Tests, on my machine, with this branch

Each of these fails with a compiler built from main at f90fbd19 or 9fe8639f, and passes here:

- `TestSelfHostSetArgs`, `TestSelfHostServeAllocsPerRequest`, `TestSelfHostCoreSpecMatchesTheIR`
- `TestSelfHostGuardedPhysicalReuse`, `TestSelfHostPhysicalCreditHelperBodies`, and each test with `Credit` in its name

These pass here also: `TestSelfHostOptimisationShapes`, `TestSelfHostIRVerifyStack`, `TestSelfHostIRVerifyGateChecks`, `TestSelfHostIRVerifyRc`, `TestSelfHostStaticEnumHoldsNoCount`, `TestSelfHostDecidedBranchShapeX86_64`, `TestSelfHostStdlibErrorTraits`, `TestSelfHostTaskDroppedWhileParkedIsCancelled`, `go test ./compiler/`, `TestAudioTagBounds` on each target, `TestConformanceLeakCensusX86_64`.

One test does not pass on my machine: `TestSelfHostExampleGitLogRandom`. It compares with the installed git, which is 2.52 here. #16017 made the example agree with git 2.56, which CI has.

The pre-push hook: pass.

4. "Delete my account data" left the login in place.

author: zs1l3nt
body:
## Summary

YouTube Music changed its layouts and most of the library returned wrong or empty data. This rebuilds parsing around one item reader, makes signed-in cookies work, and adds the features asked for in the open issues and PRs. Released as **6.0.0**.

```diff
 src/
 ├── YTMusic.ts            # + sign-in hash, retry, cache, timeout, search paging, ID checks
+├── RequestError.ts       # endpoint, status, reason; no session data
 ├── parsers/
-│   ├── Parser.ts         # per-page item methods, shelves read by position
+│   ├── Parser.ts         # parseFields: rows, cards and queue entries → title, segments, endpoint, thumbnails
 │   ├── Song/Video/Album/Artist/PlaylistParser.ts
-│   │                     # parseSearchResult, parseArtistSong, parseAlbumSong, parseHomeSection, …
+│   │                     # parse (whole response) + parseItem (any list item)
+│   ├── HomeSectionParser.ts
+│   └── LyricsParser.ts   # plain and timed lyrics
 └── utils/
+    └── getVideoThumbnail.ts
```

Items and shelves are now told apart by the page and video types in their endpoints, not by position or English labels.

```text
initialize({ cookies })
  mark cookies secure, site-wide     # __Secure- cookies were dropped before
constructRequest
  if cached and fresh → return
  if SAPISID cookie → Authorization: SAPISIDHASH   # cookies alone stay signed out
  retry on 429 / 5xx / no response, honour Retry-After
  on failure → RequestError (cookie and Authorization removed)
```

| Issue or PR | Result |
| --- | --- |
| #36, #40, #43 | Signed-in cookies work; `RequestError` reports YouTube's reason |
| #37 | `search*(query, { limit })` follows pages |
| #48 | `getPlaylistVideos()` returns the whole playlist, not the first 100 |
| #51 | `getAlbum()` accepts `OLAK5uy_` share IDs |
| #53, #54 | Home sections parse; unsupported items and empty shelves are dropped |
| #56 | `explicit` on songs |
| #57 | Radio playlists load with a correct `videoCount` |
| #41, #60 | README: API reference, playing songs, signing in |
| PR #52 | Undefined query values are left out |
| PR #55 | `getTimedLyrics()` |
| PR #61 | `artists[]` on songs, videos and albums; `artist` stays |
| PR #62 | 1200px Google-hosted thumbnails; `getHighresThumbnail()` for videos |
| PR #63 | Retry, optional cache, typed errors, ID checks, typed exports |

## Evidence

- **Before** (live, `main`):
  ```text
  search("Weekend")[0].artist.name      → "3:37"
  getArtist(…).topVideos[0].videoId     → ""
  getArtistAlbums(…)                    → []
  getPlaylistVideos(292-track playlist) → 100 videos
  getPlaylist(radio).videoCount         → 3   (49 songs)
  getAlbum("OLAK5uy_…")                 → 400
  initialize({ cookies })               → throws "Cookie not in this host's domain"
  bun run test:live                     → 82 pass, 1 fail
  ```
  **After:**
  ```text
  search("Weekend")[0]                  → ARTIST The Weeknd, then his songs
  getArtist(…).topVideos[0].videoId     → "waU75jdUnYw"
  getArtistAlbums(…)                    → 13 albums
  getPlaylistVideos(same playlist)      → 291 videos
  getPlaylist(radio).videoCount         → 49
  getAlbum("OLAK5uy_…")                 → "Till Next Time", 8 songs
  initialize({ cookies })               → signed in: library, liked songs, stream formats
  bun run test:live                     → 103 pass, 0 fail (anonymous and signed in)
  bun run test:coverage                 → 268 pass, 99.84% lines, 94.44% functions
  bun run lint, build, test:package     → pass
  ```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting the merge restores 5.3.0 behaviour. Publishing 6.0.0 to npm is the one-way step, and it is not part of this PR.

**Blast Radius:** consumers

Breaking changes for anyone upgrading:

- `getUpNexts()` returns `SongDetailed` (`name`, `artist`, `artists`, `album`) instead of `title` and a single `artists` object.
- Playlist IDs in results no longer start with `VL`.
- Failed requests throw `RequestError`, not an Axios error. Requests are retried up to 3 times by default and time out after 30 seconds.
- `HomeSection.contents` can now hold videos and artists.
- Thumbnail lists can end with a 1200px entry.
- `TimedLyric` uses `startTime` / `endTime`, unlike the names proposed in PR #55.
- The sign-in hash uses `crypto.subtle`, so Node 19 or newer is needed when cookies are used.

Known gaps: `getArtistAlbums()` does not page very large discographies, and `PlaylistFull.videoCount` is unverified for a header that shows views and a count but no duration.

author: julioborgesigt
body:
## Objetivo
Separar de forma explícita e sem sobreposição as **três dimensões financeiras** que antes ficavam misturadas no resumo e nas telas do mês:

1. **Pagamentos do mês (o que você efetivamente vai precisar pagar neste mês)**:
   - Soma exclusivamente a **Fatura do cartão que vence neste mês** (`faturaCents`) + **Contas previstas e pagas no Pix neste mês** (`fixedCashCents + fixedPixForecastCents + extrasPixCents`).
   - Não mistura mais custos de vida previstos no cartão para a próxima fatura (`fatura:seguinte`) dentro do que falta pagar no caixa deste mês.
   - Exibe no topo de **Resumo mensal**: **Falta pagar neste mês (fatura + Pix)**, **Pagamentos do mês**, **Já pago**, detalhamento `Fatura deste mês · Pix do mês` e **Saldo dos pagamentos do mês**.

2. **Valores lançados neste mês (para a próxima ou próximas faturas)**:
   - Substitui o antigo rótulo ambíguo `"Despesa lançada"` por uma seção dedicada **Valores lançados neste mês (p/ próximas faturas)** no Resumo mensal e um raio-X completo em **Cartões de crédito → Lançamentos do mês**.
   - Destaca quanto já foi lançado neste mês para pagar na próxima ou nas próximas faturas (dividido entre Custo de vida, Planejados e Imprevistos) e quanto ainda está previsto no Custo de vida deste mês para entrar na próxima fatura.
   - Atualiza `listCardPurchasesInMonth` (`src/db.ts`) para incluir também lançamentos vinculados por `ref:YYYY-MM` (sem data de compra explícita), evitando duplicar espelhos de categoria.

3. **Despesa prevista do mês atual e do próximo mês**:
   - Exibe lado a lado no **Resumo mensal** o card de **Despesa prevista · [Mês Atual]** (com composição `Fatura · Pix` e `Saldo previsto`) e o card clicável de **Despesa prevista · [Próximo Mês]** (somando automaticamente a fatura já lançada no próximo mês, os custos de vida deste mês previstos para entrar na próxima fatura e os Pix previstos do próximo mês, com o respectivo `Saldo previsto`).

## Validação
- `npm test` (44/44 testes passando, incluindo novo teste unitário para `monthFinancialSummary` e `previousMonthId`)
- `npm run check` (`wrangler types && tsc --noEmit && wrangler deploy --dry-run` sem erros)

author: ramtinj95
body:
## Why

The owner wants a demo that a stranger can play without help, where peace is a real choice in a war. The fifth play-through found that paying for peace is a bad buy. Idle Rome paid Carthage 1,400 gold, and Carthage declared war again the day the one-year truce ended. Carthage also opened at 1,400 when it took 700 after one refusal. This is the rules half. The panel half, #60, has landed, and this branch is rebased onto `main` at `8649b63`.

## What changed

- **A paid truce lasts longer.** A peace's truce is 365 days plus 30 for each point the terms were worth to the receiver (100 gold, or a city's points), at most 730 more (`truceLength` in `src/sim/peace/truce.ts`, applied in `makePeace`). 1,400 gold buys 785 days, and the cap is three years in all. Peace as things stand still gives one year. The length sits in the truce's existing `endsOn`, so the save shape is unchanged.
- **A winning AI opens near its floor.** It opens at the least it would take plus `OPENING_MARGIN` (5 points, 500 gold), or halfway to the most the other side would give, whichever is less. Before, it opened at that most. It breaks this cap in one case: when the other side can pay only with a city worth more. It then asks the least it would take, which is also the cheapest counter.
- **The panels say what a truce buys.** An incoming offer and its cheaper counter each say how long their truce would hold and until when (`truceText`). The war confirmation, the panel at peace and the guide state the paid-truce rule from the same constants.
- `npm run sim -- truce` (`scripts/sim/truce.ts`) plays an idle Rome that pays every offer it can, against one that refuses every offer.
- `docs/design.md` (Peace), `peace.md` and `peace-evidence.md` are updated.

## Decisions that are the owner's (taken, with the reason)

- **The truce rule.** I chose a truce scaled by the price over two other candidates measured on the same 20 seeds: a flat two-year paid truce, and an AI that needs double odds for a year after a paid truce. The scaled truce was best on every row. The odds rule still let a power declare on day 365, and it needed a new saved field. The table is in `peace-evidence.md`.
- **Should the AI open far above its floor?** No. A stranger who trusts the first price should not overpay by thousands. The panel now names the cheaper counter. The AI still keeps a small margin, so countering pays a little but is never required. On main, 88 of 177 priced offers to idle Rome asked more than 500 gold above the floor. On this branch, 0 of 159 did.
- **What I could not make true: paying does not make idle Rome live longer than on main.** Paying still beats refusing in every seed, before and after. The rise in days to the next war is large: median 437 to 1,040. But Rome's fall day when it pays moves 2,399 to 2,304, which is inside the seed-to-seed noise of about 1,500 days. The cause is measured: an idle Rome raises no men during the truce, while its enemy grows. A truce buys years for a player who uses them, and the sim cannot show that for an idle one.
- **Trade-offs for the world.** The powers fight each other about 30% less, so they turn on the minors sooner. Minors left at year 5 fall from 31 to 24, still twice the threshold of 12 that `sim:ai` checks, but below design.md's "about half". If that is too much, lower `MAX_PAID_TRUCE_DAYS` first.

## Scope

`src/sim/peace/{truce,make-peace}.ts`, `proposal()` and `thresholds.ts` in `src/sim/ai/`, `src/ui/war-room.ts` and `WarsPanel.svelte` (truce text), their tests, `scripts/sim/truce.ts`, docs. No render, e2e or dependency change.

## Blast Radius

Every peace between any two sides, the AI's included. Old saves load unchanged, because only new truces get the longer `endsOn`. AI winners collect less gold per peace.

## Review

A shepherdr reviewer found two P2 findings. I accepted both.
1. The opening cap fell through to the full range when only a city could pay. Fixed by making the exception explicit in code and in `design.md`. Breaking the cap there is the cheapest deal the other side can make, because no payment fits under it.
2. The truce sim read the AI's floor on the day after the offer. Fixed: it now reads the floor on the day the AI set the price. I reran both sides, and the opening rows below come from the fixed script.

## Captures

Publish scenarios: peace-clock

From the `peace-clock` scenario on this branch, published to `pr-assets` under `feat/paid-truce/`. That folder's `README.md` names the head the images show. I opened the image at full size when it was taken at `57021749`. The rules and panel code are unchanged since then. Carthage now asks 1,500 rather than 2,000, would take 1,000, and each set of terms says how long its truce holds.

![offer-counter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ramtinJ95/first-game/refs/heads/pr-assets/feat/paid-truce/peace-clock/offer-counter.png)

Clip: [clip.gif](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ramtinJ95/first-game/refs/heads/pr-assets/feat/paid-truce/peace-clock/clip.gif). Nexus preview: https://infra-testbench.tailc817d3.ts.net:10203/

## Verification

- `e2e/wheel.spec.ts` (zooming the map over Persia) failed browser shard 8 twice on this pull request. This change touches no render, camera or e2e file. In this pylon the test fails the same way on this branch, on `main` at `82feddfb`, and on `c40d8c7` from before #60. So it is not this change. It looks like a timing-sensitive test, which I am noting here rather than fixing, because it is outside this pull request's scope.
