author: zkaelxz
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zkaelxz"} -->
_Requested by **Kae** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011bDiZ4wPrjSyxG2FY3PPQK?thread=cmsg_011bDiZ4wPrjSyxG2FY3PPQKKNGP69gL9CgNKpWZKyczhq)_

## Roadmap step

Not a roadmap step: workflow plan decision 7 (a weekly regression pack on the two hand-corrected golden titles), step 2. Branch `claude/project-thread-3ccmbk`, base `baihe-subtitler` merged in at 20dbb2e.

## What changed

`tools/release_check.py` could not give a useful score on the golden titles:
- A transcription clip ran bare Whisper with `transcribe_for_timing`'s defaults (2000 ms minimum silence; the titles use 300, and a sweep showed 2000 drops words), with no prompt, no preset and no vocal separation. Now a clip can carry `title_settings` (a title's saved transcription columns, checked against a fixed list) and an optional `initial_prompt`, and the check runs the app's own pipeline (`transcribe_pipeline._transcribe_worker`) in a spawned child process, as the app does, then scores the lines it would have saved. Nothing is written to the library. A clip without `title_settings` runs as before.
- Whisper's default decoding moved one golden clip's CER between 0.42 and 1.30 from run to run, against a 0.02 flag margin. `--repeats N` runs each transcription clip N times and scores the median, keeping every score in the JSON. A later run is flagged only when it is worse than the worst of the previous run's scores, and the report's Previous column shows that value.
- Speaker clips can name `backend` (`nemotron` or `pyannote`; default the Speaker detection model setting, which defaults to Nemotron). Nemotron needs no Hugging Face token. A clip with `num_speakers` always runs pyannote, as the app does.
- New `transcribe_service.worker_args_for_settings`: the worker's arguments for a dict of title settings, built by the same `_check_run_request` / `_resolve_run` / `_worker_args` a real run uses, without reading the library. `_resolve_run` gained `resolved_prompt` so a prompt can be passed in without looking the title up.

Users won't notice anything in the app; this is a tool run by hand on the GPU PC.

## Testing

- Guard set plus area tests from `tools/check_change.py` (21 files), after the base merge: 1357 passed, 18 skipped. `basedpyright`: 0 errors, baseline unchanged. `ruff check` passed on the changed files.
- **Real hardware:** first commit (ec06679), on the 3080 Ti, golden titles 59 and 60, `--repeats 5`. Exit 0, 3 of 3 clips ok, 11 min 18 s, nothing downloaded. Median 1 - CER was 0.631 for 59 (runs 0.233 to 0.716) and 0.539 for 60 (0.454 to 0.631). 59's DER with Nemotron was 0.421. The later commit changes only the speaker-count backend choice, the report column and the child's daemon flag.
- New tests:
  - refusing a misspelt title setting or an unknown backend
  - title settings running the app pipeline and scoring its lines (child process faked)
  - a stopped run reported as a failure, not a zero
  - repeats taking the median
  - repeated previous runs compared by their worst score, which the Previous column shows
  - Nemotron needing no token, and a speaker count running pyannote with the hint
  - `worker_args_for_settings` passing settings and prompt through with no title in the database, its prompt fallback, and refusing hardsub OCR and Groq
- An Opus review of the diff found 1 real issue (a speaker count was ignored under Nemotron) and 2 minor ones (the Previous column, a wrong comment). All three are fixed in c11fb29.

## Docs

`docs/user-guide-operations.md`, "Release check on real hardware": `title_settings`, `initial_prompt`, `backend` and `--repeats` added.

## Exit condition

From the task: the release check can score the golden titles with each title's own settings, can repeat runs to even out Whisper's noise, and can use Nemotron. All three are met, and the real run above succeeded.

## Manual check (for the user, after merge)

None needed from Kae; the thread runs the weekly pack on the 3080 Ti.

## Anything uncertain or out of scope

- VRAM is not measured for app-pipeline clips: they run in their own process.
- Vocal separation writes its result next to the clip's audio, so keep the clip audio as copies, not the library's files.
- The spawned-child path (`_transcribe_in_child`) has no automated test: a spawn test would re-import the worker and can't use the fakes. The real run covered it.
- With a run-to-run spread as wide as title 59's, the worst-of-previous rule catches only big drops. A fixed-decoding option would sharpen it, if the temperature-0 accuracy test shows it is as accurate.
- Not built: counts of missed and invented lines (still one CER for the whole text).
- Removed tests: none.

body:
## Qué

Port vanilla del motor de texto de **Animata** (codse/animata, MIT) a la Web Animations API, sin React ni librerías nuevas, e integración en las zonas visibles.

- **Motor** (`src/lib/animata/core.ts` + `text-animator.ts`): split whole/char/word/line, fases enter/exit, stagger modes, triggers `load`/`visible` (IntersectionObserver único), `exit="leave"` con replay al re-entrar, `once` por sesión, `prefers-reduced-motion` → texto estático, re-scan en `astro:page-load` (ClientRouter).
- **Componente** `AnimataText.astro` + `src/styles/animata.css` (importado en `global.css`).
- **Presets** (solo los usados): `mask-reveal-up` (h1 hero), `blur-out-up` (descripción hero), `line-by-line-slide` (h2 newsletter, exit leave), `bottom-up-letters` (marca del header, 1 vez por sesión), `per-character-rise` y `micro-scale-fade` disponibles.
- **Micro-efectos CSS**: `underline-hover-text` en títulos de tarjetas, `shimmer-sweep` en chips, `glitch-text` (solo CSS) en el 404.
- **Accesibilidad/SEO**: el HTML sigue sirviendo el texto plano; el JS añade copia `sr-only` + unidades `aria-hidden`. Sin JS o con reduced-motion, no se trocea nada. Sin islas React.

## SSR primero

El texto viaja en el HTML generado; las unidades solo existen tras el JS. La animación no oculta contenido si algo falla.

## Verificación

- `npm run test`: 87/87 · `test:coverage`: statements 96% / branches 85% (umbral 80).
- `npm run lint`, `format:check`, `npx astro check` (0 errores), `npm run build` (949 páginas) OK.
- Smoke Playwright en dev: hero (líneas + palabras), newsletter enter/exit/re-enter, marca solo una vez por sesión, 404 glitch, navegación client-side, `prefers-reduced-motion` sin trocear.

El resto del catálogo (~35 presets) queda para PRs posteriores sobre el mismo motor.

Part of #935 (stacked on #1058).

## What

- With central stencils alone (states read from files), TENO's 3D setup computes the cell moments only to the central stencils' degree r instead of the smoothness indicators' 2r-2 (`MomentsTask<NM, D>`, same slot layout, same operations on the slots it fills, so the central tables are bitwise unchanged).
- Post commands skip the structured-block stencil-shape summary (`describe_stencil_shapes`), which they never show.

- Fixes a pre-existing GCC `-Wsign-conversion` error in `test/stencils_test.cpp`.

## Bitwise

`TENO3DSetup.CentralStencilsAloneAreTheFullSetupsBitForBit` (from the layer below, here at orders 4, 5 and 6: the degrees whose moments this layer truncates, and the pyramids' odd-degree stencils) compares every central table with the full setup's, also in a bounds-checked 3D build; `mallard diff` of `post derive` output vs origin/main on all 11 TGV snapshots: identical.

## Measurements

Apple M4 Pro, 2 threads, machine shared with other jobs (load avg 10-50). `benchmarks/post_derive/run.sh` (best of 2 in 3D, 3 in 2D; g++-16 Release with HDF5, VTKHDF snapshots):

```
mallard -i benchmarks/post_derive/tgv_3d.toml --kokkos-num-threads=2
benchmarks/post_derive/run.sh $(command -v mallard) /Applications/ParaView-6.0.1.app/Contents/bin/pvbatch benchmarks/post_derive/tgv_3d.toml 2
```

| Case | Files | `post derive` | with the run's cache | `pvbatch` 6.0.1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2D DMR, 115,200 triangles, TENO5 | 1 | 3.2 s, 0.21 GB | 1.3 s, 0.24 GB | 4.3 s, 0.21 GB |
|  | 11 | 3.3 s, 0.22 GB | 1.6 s, 0.24 GB | 5.3 s, 0.24 GB |
| 3D TGV, 64³ hexahedra, TENO5 | 1 | 47 s, 1.1 GB | 10 s, 1.2 GB | 3.8 s, 0.32 GB |
|  | 11 | 35 s, 1.1 GB | 11 s, 1.2 GB | 6.4 s, 0.37 GB |

The docs' previous rows (origin/main, idle machine): 2D 4.6 s / 1.1 GB, 3D 32 s / 9.6 GB. A/B on the same loaded machine (clang, restart input, user CPU): one file 98 s → 66 s, 2.2 → 1.1 GB for the whole stack; this layer's share is about a tenth of main's CPU time.

Reaching pvbatch needs fitting each stencil shape once instead of each cell, which is #986. Remaining memory (vertex gradient weights, staging) is #1050.

author: kodflow
body:
Fixes #1435
Fixes #1436
Fixes #1437
Refs #1439

## ADR change — ADR 0196 and ADR 0200 (for the owner)

Both by a dated amendment at the end of the file; no accepted text edited.

- **ADR 0196, Amendment 2026-11-15 (#1435, #1436, #1437):** the drain's close keeps its answers on three more paths — a lingering close keeps reading after an ENOBUFS or a cancel on io_uring, the portable peer's end waits for the queued output, a worker's HTTP/2 answer returned in the batch that fed its connection joins the batch's output.
- **ADR 0200, Amendment 2026-11-15 (#1439):** a connection refused at accept on an io_uring direct descriptor (past `MaxConns`, a stopping or drained ring, past the table) gets an `IORING_OP_SHUTDOWN` hard-linked ahead of its close. Closed alone, its file stayed held by the other connections' multishot recvs (before 6.13), and the refused peer read no end until its own deadline.

## #1435 — net/http2: a worker's answer ahead of SETTINGS, the connection closed before flush (epoll, kqueue)

`answerSlot` wrote a worker's answer and closed at once. On a connection the batch fed, it went out ahead of the SETTINGS the batch had queued (RFC 9113 §3.4 makes SETTINGS the first frame), with or without a drain, and during a drain its close refused the SETTINGS and the GOAWAY at the batch's `flush`. The answer now joins the batch's output (`pushWrite`), and the batch's end writes it, then closes (`flush`, `closeIfDone`).

`TestLoopHandler_aWorkersAnswerInTheDrainingBatchFollowsItsOutput` drives the adapter through a fake `LoopIO`, so it holds for every backend (epoll, kqueue, io_uring, portable):
```
origin/main:  loop_drain_external_test.go:175: the connection's frames [1 0], want SETTINGS first        (draining)
              loop_drain_external_test.go:175: the connection's frames [1 0 4 8 4], want SETTINGS first  (serving)
this branch:  PASS (both cases)
```

## #1436 — net/server: the portable backend closed on the peer's end without waiting for queued output

`handleEnd` finished a closing connection at the peer's EOF, so its queued output was dropped. The end now goes through the settlement (`peerDone`, `markDirty`, then `settle` and `markClosing`). Only a lingering close, its writing side already shut, ends at the peer's end.
```
origin/main:  drain_settle_portable_internal_test.go:187: the peer's end finished a closing connection with output queued: open false, peer done false
this branch:  PASS (output still queued; lingering)
```

## #1437 — net/loop: a lingering drain connection stopped reading after ENOBUFS or a cancel (io_uring)

`recvStarved`, `rearmStarved` and `recvCancelled` took a slot in the drain's linger for closed. A linger that met either path stopped reading and closed at its bound with input unread, which is a reset that discards answers the peer has not read. The three paths now share `recvBytes`'s condition (`reads`: open, or the drain's closing). Past the starved queue's bound a lingering slot stops reading and `drainLinger` ends it.
```
origin/main:  linger_uring_linux_test.go:80: 0 recvs armed for the lingering slot, want 1: it would read no more   (starved, then re-armed; cancelled)
this branch:  PASS
```
The issue's end-to-end witness on epoll and the portable backend, the slow reader of `TestDrain_aConnectionFedThroughTheDrainGetsEveryAnswer` (red on 6492b440 as the issue records: epoll `DRAIN_TIMEOUT`, portable 52 answers lost), passes on io_uring, epoll and portable over 30 runs here. The io_uring test skips on the other backends, whose receive paths have no such state.

## #1439 — net/loop: `loop_test` shard 3 of 4 at Bazel's 60 s

rules_go shards round-robin over the test list in `srcs` order. #1430's new tests reshuffled that list and put `TestConformance_closeBounded` (18.2 s) in shard 3 with `idleNoWatchdog` (6.2 s) and `drainOutOfDescriptors` (5.6 s). Measured locally under `-race` with the lane's flags (`requiredBackends=epoll`, `requiredCaps=none`, `KITSUNIUM_LOOP_SCALE=10000`, `-tags=loopdebug`), main's shards took 33 / 66 / 51 / 43 s.

The tests at the bound, and their causes:
- **`TestConformance_closeBounded` and `drainBounded` (18 s each):** 7 to 9 s of each backend's 9 went to dialing 20 000 connections. Timed by quarter, the dials took 0.3 s, 0.35 s, 1.4 s and then 5 s. `connect(2)` looks for a free ephemeral port by walking the range, even ports first. From one source to one address, past about 14 000 connections, each dial walked the half already taken, and the TIME_WAIT sockets left by earlier tests of the process made it longer. `heardConns` now spreads the dials over eight loopback sources, with the port picked at connect (`IP_BIND_ADDRESS_NO_PORT`). The dials are linear again, about 1.4 s. The tests still hold 20 000 connections and check the same things.
- **`TestConformance_drainTakesQueue` (10.2 s) and `drainTakesWhatTheQueueHolds`:** the clients stayed open until cleanup, so every subtest's drain waited out `drainLinger` (500 ms). Each client now closes by reset as soon as it has read the server's end.
- **`TestConformance_maxConns` (20.4 s, io_uring):** an engine defect, not a test wait. The refused connection's direct descriptor was closed alone, and the refused peer read nothing until its own 20 s deadline. The test took that timeout for the refusal. It is fixed in the engine (ADR 0200 amendment above), and the test now requires the end within 5 s, never a timeout:
```
origin/main engine:  conformance_native_test.go:457: a connection past MaxConns read no end in 5 s: refused, its peer was never told
this branch:         PASS (iouring 0.43 s, three runs)
```

| test (race, local) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| closeBounded | 18.2 s | 5.0 s |
| drainBounded | 18.4 s | 5.9 s |
| drainTakesQueue | 10.2 s | 4.1 s |
| maxConns | 20.4 s | 0.4 s |
| whole package | 196 s | 143 s |

The side of a TCP connection that closes first keeps a TIME_WAIT. That is normal TCP. Counted on Linux with `ss -Htan state time-wait` around single tests, the side read from which port the sockets share:

| test | TIME_WAIT left | side |
|---|---|---|
| loop `drainTakesQueue` | 4 872 | server (the drain closes first) |
| loop `drainTakesWhatTheQueueHolds` | 2 402 | server |
| server `TestDrain_arrivalsAcrossTheDrain` | 6 217 | clients (back to back since #1430) |
| server `TestDrain_graceUnderArrivals` | 2 100 | clients |
| server `TestErrorLog_handshakeFlood` | 7 785 | server (a refused handshake closes first) |

macOS has 16 384 ephemeral ports, each held 30 s, and `go test` runs these packages side by side. So the hypothesis holds for the drain tests of `net/loop`. The server's arrivals tests add their clients' own, and the handshake flood is the largest single source. Their clients now close by reset once the exchange is over or the server's end has been read (`resetClose`, now in `conformance_native_test.go`; `resetConn` in server's tests; also `buffersFollowDemand` and `cutsBatches`). Each of the tests above leaves none afterwards, and what they assert is unchanged.

author: shawnpfarmer
body:
Brings Campsites' loop up to ForgeDB's version and closes the production-QC gap behind #38. Spec and plan: `~/plans/2026-11-14-campsites-loop-update.md` on Lisa. Built by Lisa; Shawn handed every call to Lisa for this one and reviews before merge.

**Do not merge from chain mode:** this changes `ralphloop/`. After merging, rebuild the worker image (see the end).

## What changes

1. **ForgeDB's loop, merged in** (`ba8588f`). Three-way merge of each loop file, with ForgeDB `42ece62` as the base. That commit is ForgeDB's starting loop: MyGear `df0f750` + Campsites #14/#15. It brings in:
   - the gate, plus the `config.toml` refusal;
   - ratify;
   - the guard that puts back `task.md` changes outside the current task;
   - draft PRs titled `GATE FAILING`;
   - MyGear's code-fence fix (#63), which Campsites never had.

   There were 4 small conflicts. `chain.sh` keeps Campsites' schema-contract guard and its local-settings guard.
2. **The gate, for Campsites** (`1ef2a4a`). After every ticked step, the loop runs three parts and stops at the first that fails:
   - `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (Campsites' own stack);
   - `seed-dev.sh` again, because the reset empties the review app's data;
   - `ralphloop/app-check.sh` in the worker image: lint, `ng build -c production,local`, then **`console-check.mjs`**.

   The console check is headless Chromium over the public routes, then as admin and as pat (including a trip page). It fails on any console error, uncaught error or failed app request. Map tiles are stubbed. The gate's scripts run from the loop's own checkout (mounted read-only), never the worktree's.
3. **The review app serves the production build** (`2741803`). `review.sh --dev` keeps `ng serve`. `angular.json` gets a `local` configuration that only swaps in `environment.local.ts`; Vercel's build is unchanged.
4. **Ratify prompt for Campsites, worker rule 12, the image** (`bb09a43`).
   - Image: psql 17 + pg_prove, jq, and Playwright 1.64.1 with headless Chromium. It grows from 1.31 to 2.43 GB.
5. **Preflight** (`018a18b`). `doloop.sh` stops at once, with the rebuild command, if the image has no Playwright.
6. **`CLAUDE.md`** (`5388937`). Rule 6 (the gate is no longer deferred), the loop section, and the roadmap note on tests.

## Verification (Ralph)

- **Loop test suite:** 529 passed, 0 failed (`bash ralphloop/tests/run-on-ralph.sh`). It was 497 straight after the merge; the extra tests cover the seed and app-check order, retries, a seed failure, scripts coming from the loop checkout, `review.sh` modes, and the preflight.
- **Image:** built as `campsites-claude-worker:port-test`. Chromium starts as the `claude` user; psql 17, pg_prove, jq, Deno and Claude Code are all present. `:latest` was not touched.
- **Throwaway stack** (ports 553xx, `project_id` `csloopport`, since removed; the live Campsites stack was never touched):
  - database part: `db reset` + `test db` passed (31 pgTAP tests);
  - **this branch:** app check **PASSED**: lint, production build, 15 page loads, no console errors (about 40 s including `npm ci`);
  - **`3a75cce`, the commit before #38:** app check **FAILED** with `TypeError: W.markerClusterGroup is not a function` on `/favorites` (admin and camper) and `/trips/<id>`. That's the production-only crash that reached users, now caught before a PR.

## Calls I made

- **Merge, not replay:** I merged ForgeDB's ~10 loop commits in one go rather than replaying them one by one. Same end state, a fraction of the work.
- **The gate goes past ForgeDB's database-only version.** It also checks the app, because Campsites' loop never writes migrations (rule 3), so the database part alone protects little here.
- **The console check runs in the gate, every ticked step.** The alternative was a step check written into `task.md`. This way no plan changes, and the worker can't skip it. Cost: about 1–2 minutes per step.
- **It runs against the real local stack, signed in as the dev seed's users.** Only map tiles are stubbed. That's why the dev seed now re-runs after each reset.
- **Production is the review app's default; `--dev` is the opt-out.**
- **Playwright 1.64.1 (2026-10-14), not 1.65.x.** I pinned the newest release that's at least two weeks old.
- **Not ported:** ForgeDB's `ratify-proof.md` (ForgeDB-specific) and its database-rules prompt test.

## After merging (Shawn)

On Ralph, from `~/projects/Campsites` once it has pulled main:

```
docker build -t campsites-claude-worker:latest - < ralphloop/worker.Dockerfile
./ralphloop/review.sh
```

The second command restarts the review app on the production build. Then `docker rmi campsites-claude-worker:port-test`.

Esta release consolida todos os ciclos de desenvolvimento realizados na branch \dev\ desde julho de 2026, englobando grandes evoluções funcionais, arquiteturais e de design system.

body:
## 何を変えたか

モデルを探す場所を、環境変数の URL の並びにしました (docs/cache-sharing.md 7 節)。上から順に見て、失敗したら次の場所へ進みます。

```
HWNPU_MODEL_SOURCE=file:///mnt/llm/hwnpu?writeback=true
HWNPU_MODEL_SOURCE_1=https://USER:PASS@nas:5006/hwnpu          # WebDAV。書き戻しなしなら読むだけの HTTP
HWNPU_MODEL_SOURCE_2=s3://bucket/hwnpu?endpoint=http://host:9000
HWNPU_MODEL_HUGGING_FACE=false                                  # Hugging Face に出ない (既定は true)
```

- `?writeback=true` を付けた場所には、手元で作ったものや後ろの場所から取ったものを書き戻します。gated のリポジトリも書き戻します。
- `HWNPU_CACHE_LAYERS`、`HWNPU_CACHE_WRITE`、`HWNPU_OFFLINE`、`HWNPU_PREBUILT` は削除しました。互換の読み替えはありません。
- 取得元の中の並び:
  - 元のモデル: `original/OWNER/NAME/` と `hwnpu-lock.json` (コミット 1 つ、ファイルごとの sha256 と大きさ)
  - 変換後: `converted/MODEL/TARGET/EXPORT/vN/` と `entry.json`。版は models.yaml の `version` から取ります。`develop: true` のものは `vN-HASH`、版がないものは `v0-HASH` です。
- WebDAV は net/http だけで実装しました。PUT してから MOVE で置き換え、MKCOL でフォルダを作り、PROPFIND で一覧を取り、Range で途中から再開します。パスワードは URL、`~/.netrc`、`HWNPU_WEBDAV_PASSWORD` のどれかから読み、ログには伏せて出します。
- `.env` と `.env.local` を読みます (カレントディレクトリ、ユーザーとマシンの設定フォルダ)。読む変数は `HWNPU_`、`HF_`、`AWS_` で始まるものだけです。
- hwnpu-dev のコマンドを足しました:
  - `cache sources`、`ls`、`push`
  - `cache update`: lock を新しいコミットに移す
  - `cache verify`、`gc`
  - `cache migrate`: 古い `blobs/`、`upstream/`、`entries/` からハードリンクで移す

## 確かめたこと

- store、envfile、chat、hwnpu-dev の試験は通りました。WebDAV の試験には x/net/webdav の試験用サーバーを使っています。`go vet` も通っています。
- 実際のバイナリで次を確かめました: `.env` の読み込み、取得元の順番、パスワードが伏せられること、読むだけの取得元。

## 確かめていないこと

- 実際の Synology の WebDAV
- NAS (`/mnt/llm`) の中身の移し替え
- この新しい経路での Hugging Face からの実際の取得

## 次

手元のキャッシュと同梱のモデルも取得元の 1 つとして平らに並べる予定で、別の PR にします (docs/cache-sharing.md 13 節)。

body:
## 概要

Issue #120 の残りの項目の確認結果を、`docs/development/road-class-validation.md` に記録します（文書と CHANGELOG のみ。コードは変更しません）。

- **「国道の名称 `国道<番号>号` による判定」の節を追加**: 道路名が `国道<番号>号` の形のとき国道と確定できるか、盾の判定にも使えるか（Issue #120 の 3 つ目の項目。PhotoGeoExplorer #296 の案）。
- **結論の更新**: 名称による判定は採用しない（理由は下記）。
- **数値の訂正**: 鳥取市の国道の数値を、実装（#126）と同じ優先順位（`JP:E` と `JP:national` の両方を持つ道路は高速）に揃えました。前回の表は、`JP:E` を高速として扱わない分類で計算していたため、鳥取市の国道だけが食い違っていました（再現率 93% → 75%、元の OSM との比較表も 94% → 78%）。ほかの都市の数値は変わりません。

## 確認の方法と結果

OpenFreeMap の z14 タイルの `transportation_name` の線について、`name`・`name:ja` が `(?<!旧)国道\s*[0-9０-９]+\s*号` に一致するものを国道とし、PLATEAU が国道・県道・高速と明示した点だけで、精度と再現率を求めました（京都・大阪・名古屋・札幌・鳥取の 5 都市。#125 と同じ方法）。

| 都市 | 名称のみ: 国道 | 路線関係のみ: 国道 | 路線関係、無ければ名称: 国道 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 京都市 | 99% / 20% | 98% / 77% | 98% / 79% |
| 大阪市 | 94% / 62% | 96% / 89% | 96% / 94% |
| 名古屋市 | 89% / 67% | 85% / 82% | 86% / 89% |
| 札幌市 | 100% / 35% | 98% / 93% | 98% / 95% |
| 鳥取市 | 98% / 73% | 98% / 75% | 98% / 75% |

（精度 / 再現率）

- 名称による国道の精度は 89〜100% で高いが、名称だけでは再現率が 20〜73%。
- 路線関係が無い道路にだけ名称を使うと、国道の再現率は 0〜7 ポイント上がる。精度はほぼ変わらない。
- 都道府県道の名称（`県道N号`）は、道路名にほとんど入っておらず（5 都市で 1 本）、使えない。

**結論: 採用しない。** 効果が国道の再現率で最大 7 ポイントにとどまり、県道には使えない。追加するコードと、名称の付け方への依存に見合わない。必要になれば、路線関係が無い道路にだけ使う候補として `GetRouteShield` に加えられます。

これで Issue #120 の作業項目（広域の検証、対応表の修正、国道の名称の検討）がすべて済むため、`Closes #120` としています。

## 補足

- 確認に使ったスクリプトは、#125 の追記と同じく、このリポジトリには含めていません（OpenFreeMap のタイルを読み、線の中点を `lib/plateau-roads.mjs` の索引で引く、使い捨てのもの）。
- 製品コード・CI・依存への影響はありません。

## Fact-check: claims and sources
Note: WebFetch and direct downloads were blocked by this session's network policy. Every source below was read through web-search extracts only, not opened in full.

| Claim | Source |
|---|---|
| Precure plant example: 85 psi chamber, 70 psi in envelopes, 260°F, about a 3-hour cure | Overdrive, "One more round" |
| Chamber pressure about 85–105 psia | US Patent 8,632,647 |

author: jakeomega
body:
## What and why

The owner on the Monetary Union principle group: "it feels like it is net negative as the leader, very far from competitive with the other principle groups." Of three directions the owner chose "the issuer shares the currency's benefits and earns on it", and added intervention points for the leader ("up to ~3 or 4 at principle V") and investment pool benefits ("easier access to credit and more stability for private investors"). The leader's costs are unchanged.

The owner's current game (Singapore, 1 January 1957, a tier V union of 153 members) shows why it read as a loss:

- **The interest cut bought nothing.** The leader's reserve-currency cut is credit standing, and standing has a floor. Singapore's standing was already at its floor (0.05), so the 0.098 points it earned were wasted, while the 0.135 points it paid for its members were risk premium and counted in full.
- **Seigniorage was 98 pounds a week** by the script's figure (about 163 pounds once its minting bonuses multiplied it) on a weekly income of 821 million.
- Net: about −0.36M a week.

## What the leader gets now

From tier II, once at least one member has adopted its currency (the owner's ruling), the leader is the currency's issuer:

| Tier | Shares with its adopters | Seigniorage, of its own GDP a year, × reach, before minting bonuses | Risk premium, × reach | Intervention points | Common capital market (leader and adopters) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I | — | — | — | — | — |
| II | +5% export and import advantage | 0.5% | −0.5 points | +1 | capitalists put 2 points more of their profits into the investment pool |
| III | the same | 0.75% | −0.75 | +2 | 2 |
| IV | + the banking union (−25% crash chance and random momentum, 1 intervention point) | 1.0% | −1.0 | +3 (the banking union's point included) | 3 |
| V | + the reserve currency (+5% more trade advantage) | 1.5% | −1.5 | +4 | 5 |

- **Reach** is how large the economies using the leader's money are beside its own: `base ÷ (base + 15% of the leader's GDP)`. It is a half when they come to 15% of the leader's GDP and three quarters at 45%. The base is the adopters' GDP; at tier V it is every country anchored on the leader's money, treaty peggers included. Reach is zero until a member of the bloc has adopted, at tier V too (the owner's ruling on the review, below). The leader's Monetary Union row shows its reach.
- **The seigniorage figures are before the leader's minting bonuses**, which the game applies to it as to everything a country mints: +10% under Fiat Money or +25% under Digital Currency, +10% for each of the five finance technologies, −30% in the Very High inflation band and −80% in Hyperinflation. A leader on Digital Currency with every technology mints 1.75 times the figure, one on Fiat Money 1.6 times. The owner kept the bonuses and had the text say so (below). The tooltip's field is named "before Minting Bonuses" and lists them; the leader's Monetary Union row gives its seigniorage in pounds a week before the bonuses and with them.
- **The cut is risk premium, not credit standing**, so it counts for a leader already at its floor. The old standing cut is untouched.
- **Intervention points are room in the budget**, so more tools can be in force at once.
- **The capital market's bonus is the same in every phase of the cycle.** It does not grow in a downturn or a panic (the owner's ruling, below).
- The principle's tooltip prints each tier's figures under Leader, and the members' lines give theirs. Before, the leader had no line of its own and tier II's line gave no figure.

## Sizing

Singapore in the save, weekly, in millions of pounds. One point of premium is worth 2.64M a week there (0.32% of income). **Redone with the minting bonuses.** Singapore is on Digital Currency with all five technologies, so it mints 1.75 times the tier's figure. That is measured, not assumed: its minting line in the save is 526,476 a week, which is its flat minting (500, the capped GDP term's 200,000, 100,250 from currency boards and 93.18 of the old union seigniorage) times 1.75 to the pound.

| Tier | Before this PR: net | Now: reach | Seigniorage before bonuses | Minted (× 1.75) | Cut | Cost (unchanged) | Now: net | Of income |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I | −0.27 | — | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.101 points = 0.27 | −0.27 | −0.03% |
| II | −0.27 | 0.22 | 2.75 | 4.82 | 0.11 points = 0.29 | 0.27 | +4.85 | +0.59% |
| III | −0.33 | 0.22 | 4.13 | 7.23 | 0.17 = 0.44 | 0.124 = 0.33 | +7.34 | +0.89% |
| IV | −0.36 | 0.22 | 5.51 | 9.64 | 0.22 = 0.59 | 0.135 = 0.36 | +9.87 | +1.20% |
| V | −0.36 | 0.28 | 10.51 | 18.40 | 0.42 = 1.12 | 0.36 | +19.17 | +2.33% |

- As first posted this table gave the "before bonuses" column as what the leader was paid: 10.51M and a net of +11.28M (1.37%) at tier V. The independent review caught it.
- With the whole bloc adopted at tier V: reach 0.60, 39.2M minted a week (4.8% of income; 22.4M before bonuses), cut 0.9 points (2.4M), net 41.3M (5.0%). The reviewer's own estimates were 16.8M at tier V and about 36M for the whole bloc; they assumed Fiat Money's 1.6 where the save shows Digital Currency's 1.75.
- **The most any union can pay** is the tier V figure at full reach: 1.5% of the leader's GDP a year before bonuses, 2.4% on Fiat Money with every technology, 2.625% on Digital Currency. Two companies' prosperity and one production method add 5% of the figure each.
- **A rival group for the same country**, which spends 395M a week on construction goods: Construction III is worth about 36M a week (4.4% of income) and Construction V about 91M (11%). In money the union is now a gain where it was a loss: at tier V about half of Construction III as Singapore's bloc stands, a little more than Construction III if the whole bloc adopted, and still well short of Construction V. Beside the money Singapore gets +10% export and import advantage, a quarter off crash chance and random momentum, and 4 points on a budget of 8.
- **A typical AI leader** gains more beside its income because it borrows: the same save's Germany (debt 82% of GDP, members 7% of its GDP, all adopted) would net +1.9% of income at tier II and +5.9% at tier V (first posted as +1.4% and +4.3%). Germany is on Fiat Money, so 1.6 times, **if it has the five technologies**: its own minting line cannot show that (it reads 1.69 times base, so it has flat minting of its own), but none of the 17 countries whose line can be read shows fewer.

Assumptions: the "before" columns take the save's tier V costs and split them by tier (cooperation 0.101, the backstop 0.023, supervision 0.011); pounds are read from the save's budget block with a 1.14.5 token map, the interest slot was checked against principal × rate ÷ 52 on 25 debtors and the minting slot against base × multiplier on the 27 countries above the GDP term's cap (eight read exactly 1.5 times base, eight 1.6, one 1.0, ten have flat minting of their own); Construction is priced as construction Singapore need not buy.

**Why reach and not a rate on the adopters' GDP.** In three of the owner's saves a bloc's members come to 1% to 7% of the leader's GDP in five AI blocs and 35% to 57% in three large ones. A rate that paid the first kind "a few percent" of income would pay the second a second treasury, and the old share-of-world base pays a small leader nothing. Reach saturates: no union is worth more than the tier's figure (before minting bonuses).

**3 or 4 points.** Four. Under Free & Mutual Banking (4 points) the fourth is what lets Emergency Liquidity and the Deposit Guarantee run together; under Central Bank Independence (8) it fits all three 4-point crisis programs at once, where three points fit a standing guarantee and the whole leaning set exactly. The cycle simulator finds no AI-side reason against either: more points cut an AI leader's crashes by a tenth to a third and halve its months in a slump, and +4 against +3 is inside the noise.

## The owner's rulings on this PR (14 November)

"I

<!-- Adapted from akitaonrails/ai-memory; provenance and MIT notice: .github/TEMPLATES.md. -->

## What changed

Adds the Android runtime case for the optional client environment flag, `ownedSshClientEnvironmentThroughRealUi` in `NativeWorkspaceTest.kt`. Through the real host editor it saves one default host and one with "Identify lazysh to this host (LC_TERMINAL=lazysh)" ticked, reopens both editors to read the persisted flag, connects to each against an owned sshd with `AcceptEnv LANG LC_*` and prints `$LC_TERMINAL` in the remote shell. The default host shows `ENV__<nonce>`, the opted-in host `ENV_lazysh_<nonce>`; the typed command never contains its own proof.

- `SshFixture` gains `acceptEnv` (writes `AcceptEnv LANG LC_*`) and `client()` takes extra ssh options; every fixture of the ssh-parity run admits `LC_*` like a stock Debian server.
- The case joins `sshParityCases` (the `native-android-ssh-parity` job) and is excluded from the ordinary `test-android` task in `apps/client/moon.yml`.
- `tests/android-ssh-parity.test.ts` drives a real OpenSSH client and proves the fixture delivers `LC_TERMINAL` only when the client sends it and the sshd accepts it.
- `docs/reference/parity-matrix.md`: the "Optional client environment flag" row names the new case; its cell stays open until the case is green in a `main` run.

No product code changes and no default changes (the flag stays off by default). Mosh and ET do not send the variable and stay out of scope.

## Why

Issue #1642, follow-up of #988: the flag is verified on desktop by `ssh::tests::openssh_client_environment_reaches_remote_shell`, but the Android build had no case, so the checkbox, its persistence and the request sent from Android were unproven.

Refs #1642 (the acceptance also needs a green NAR run on `main` with the named case and the matrix cell promoted with the run id, so this PR does not close it).

- [x] `git diff --check` passes

Negative control with an sshd without `AcceptEnv`: the same case fails at "remote LC_TERMINAL" for the opted-in host. After the rebase onto current `main` the Bun fixture tests pass again with a real OpenSSH client (`LAZYSH_ANDROID_UI_SSH_PARITY=1 bun test tests/android-ssh-parity.test.ts`). Not verified: the case has not yet run in the `native-android-ssh-parity` CI job (API 36 AOSP emulator); the device run used an app library built from a `main`-based branch of 2026-11-14.

author: iamdarkle
body:
Part of #249.

Files too large for a message can go by link from a Nextcloud or ownCloud server. The server is connected in Settings → General under Large files, signed in to in the browser through Nextcloud's login flow, which gives the app a password of its own, or with an app password for servers without it. Files over the 25 MB limit then go up to it as they're added, and Share files by link beside Attach files sends any file that way. Each goes in a folder of its own under Mail attachments and is shared by a read-only link.

Links work for 30 days by default, which Settings can change, and less when the server limits them. A link can ask for a password, which the sender sees and the message leaves out, so it can be passed on another way. Sending waits for the uploads, a file that failed to go up holds the message back until it's removed, and removing a file before sending takes its upload and link back.

The message carries a block after what's written that lists each file by name as its link, with its size and until when the link works, in both the HTML and the plain-text part. A draft keeps each link's details in that block, so it reopens with the files as they were.

Uploads use WebDAV, in 10 MB pieces through Nextcloud's chunked upload when the server offers it, and links come from the OCS share API, version 1, which Nextcloud, ownCloud, OpenCloud and ownCloud Infinite Scale all serve. Google Drive and OneDrive follow in a second PR.

author: bryan-uipath
body:
First of two. This one: the Repos section's names, folding, one-line rows, the default folder's mark, and + to make a worktree. The second (PR state from `gh`) branches from this.

## What changed

1. **Repository name row.** Chevron at the left (always shown) folds/unfolds; the name in the normal text colour, medium weight; a quiet count of its checkouts while folded. Under the pointer, at the right: `+` (New worktree…) and a trash (stop listing it: exactly what Remove did, it changes `settings.json`, never the disk). Both built with the shared row-button helper (`words.rs`: `word` and the new `icon_word` share one `row_button`).
2. **Default marker.** No "Default" line. "Default" was never a default repository for new tasks: it marked the repository's *own folder* (its first row, vs. a linked worktree). That row now has a small accent dot in its gutter; the row's tooltip says "· the repository's own folder". No action sets a default, so nothing had to stay reachable.
3. **Folding** (`RepoFold`, core): per repository, kept in `layout.json` (`repos_folded`). A folded repository shows unfolded while a live task in one of its checkouts is Running or Needs you, and folds again when that ends; folded by the user *while* busy it stays folded until that ends.
4. **Worktree rows are one line**: branch, cut short before the task badge (the row reserves room at its end, so the branch never runs under it); click rules as #154, hover word Terminal; the path is the row's tooltip.
5. **+ makes a worktree.** A one-line field in place (`MarkInput::Worktree`, the workbook-name pattern). ↵: `check_branch` (check-ref-format rules, stricter), then `Effect::AddWorktree` → `worktree.rs` off the main thread → `WorktreeAdded` (System) reads the list again and opens a Workspace tab with a terminal there. Folder: `<worktrees_dir>/<repo>/<branch>`, `/` → `-`; `<repo>` gets `-<6 hex>` (FNV-1a of its path) when another listed repository shares its folder name. New setting `worktrees_dir`, default `worktrees` in the ottospace folder (`OTTOSPACE_HOME` honoured; a test run with no folder of its own has none).
6. **Trash asks; says what it did.** No undo exists for Remove, and the trash is one hover away: on a repository a live task works in it asks first in the shared confirm (`Unlist canvas-app?` · ↵ unlist · esc cancel; only the user answers). Every unlist then says, at info level, `Unlisted <name> · nothing on disk changed`.
7. **Keys** (list mode): a repository's name is a row (↵/space folds), ← folds the selected row's repository, → unfolds, `a` adds a worktree. In the key reference.

## git argv (`-C <repo>`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_DIR`-like vars removed, stdin null, 120 s timeout)

```
git -C <repo> rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>
git -C <repo> worktree add -- <folder> <branch>             # branch exists
git -C <repo> for-each-ref --format=%(refname) 'refs/remotes/*/<branch>'   # not local
git -C <repo> worktree add --track -b <branch> -- <folder> <remote>/<branch> # exactly one remote has it
git -C <repo> worktree add -b <branch> -- <folder> HEAD     # new branch from HEAD
```

(One runner, `child.rs`: output capped, 120 s timeout, and it does not wait on pipes a hook's background job keeps open.)

## Refused

- Any origin but the user: `WorktreeEdit`, and every edit/↵/Esc of the field (core `refusal`); `WorktreeAdded` from the socket. No socket request; the e2e drives it with `"as":"user"` clicks and keys (already test-only).
- Branch: empty, > 200 bytes, leading `-`, space/control/`~ ^ : ? * [ \`, `..`, `@{`, `@`, `HEAD`, an empty part, a part starting `.` or ending `.lock`, trailing `.`: said in the status bar, the field stays.
- Folder: not exactly two plain names under `worktrees_dir` (resolved); `<repo>` a link or a file; the worktree folder already there (even as a dangling link); a `<repo>` folder that is a checkout itself (`worktrees_dir` inside the repositories' folder). A relative `worktrees_dir` is inside the ottospace folder. On git failure its message (cleaned with `transcript::clean`, 200 chars) goes to the status bar; an empty `<repo>` folder made by this try is removed; anything git left is left and named.
- Not added: removing a worktree.

## Tests

- Core: fold rules, held fold, list-mode heading rows and selection, field origins, branch rules table, folder naming + hash disambiguation, git message cleaning, layout round trip (property test), the field closes when its repository goes.
- Shell (`worktree.rs`, real `git` on a temp repo, no network, no user git config): path inside the dir with symlinked components, existing folder, new branch, existing branch, a branch checked out elsewhere, not a repository.
- e2e `a_repository_folds_and_the_users_plus_makes_a_worktree_there`: real click fold/unfold, ←/→, a client's click/label/keys refused, new branch, existing branch, bad name, existing folder.

## Evidence

`shots.yml` on head `4c2d9304` (run 43675353857), scenarios `repos` (before/after) and `repos-fold` (after only). Looked at each.

**repos/task-badge (before: two-line rows, "Default", the long branch under the badge; after: one line, cut before the badge)**

![repos/task-badge (before: two-line rows, "Default", the long branch under the badge; after: one line, cut before the badge)](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/bryan-uipath/5ceef3ddbdde69ac9d6e729512b8cd21/raw/13bb3aad1b69c2e47b9de5b063813e69f39e300e/v3-repos-task-badge.png)

**repos/list**

![repos/list](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/bryan-uipath/5ceef3ddbdde69ac9d6e729512b8cd21/raw/13bb3aad1b69c2e47b9de5b063813e69f39e300e/v3-repos-list.png)

**repos/task-selected**

![repos/task-selected](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/bryan-uipath/5ceef3ddbdde69ac9d6e729512b8cd21/raw/13bb3aad1b69c2e47b9de5b063813e69f39e300e/v3-repos-task-selected.png)

**repos-fold/folded (two folded, with counts)**

author: lorenzowynberg
body:
## Audio-clock beat indicator with downbeat flash

A player needs to see the beat land exactly when they hear it, and see where they are in the bar. Driving the indicator from the audio clock rather than from timers keeps sight and sound locked together, which is the visual half of rock-solid timing.

Tracks https://github.com/LorenzoWynberg/metronome/issues/11

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/ui/beatIndicator.ts` exports `mountBeatIndicator(el, { store, engine })` returning a teardown function, and `src/main.ts` mounts it into `#beat-indicator` using the same engine instance as the controls (exactly one `createEngine(store)` call in `src/main.ts`)
- [ ] A happy-dom test asserts the indicator renders `getMeter(timeSignature).beatsPerBar` cells while stopped (2, 3, 4 and 6 for `2/4`, `3/4`, `4/4`, `6/8`) and re-renders when `timeSignature` changes
- [ ] A happy-dom test with a stubbed `requestAnimationFrame` asserts each frame calls `engine.beatQueue.takeDue(engine.currentTime())` and lights the cell for the last returned `BeatEvent`'s `beat`, and that a cell is not lit before `engine.currentTime()` reaches its `audioTime`
- [ ] A test asserts that when several `BeatEvent` entries are due in one frame (as after a hidden tab) only the latest is lit
- [ ] A test asserts that a due `BeatEvent` whose `beatsPerBar` differs from the rendered count re-renders the cell count before lighting
- [ ] Cells for `strong`, `medium` and `normal` accents differ in shape or size (asserted via distinct classes or data attributes per level), not colour alone, and a `strong` event triggers the downbeat flash state
- [ ] A happy-dom test asserts that when the store's `running` becomes `false` the rAF loop is cancelled via `cancelAnimationFrame` and no cell remains lit
- [ ] `src/ui/beatIndicator.ts` calls neither `setInterval` nor `setTimeout`
- [ ] Under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` the indicator's CSS defines no transition or animation, while lit and flash states remain visible
- [ ] The indicator container has `aria-hidden="true"`, its lit and accent states meet 3:1 non-text contrast in both the light and dark facets of the Ink & Amber theme, and the downbeat flash is confined to the indicator/hero area rather than the full viewport
- [ ] The six-cell `6/8` indicator causes no horizontal scrolling at 320px, 768px and 1440px viewport widths
- [ ] `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm build` exit 0 on the branch

— Trinity · Implementer · Claude Sonnet 5.5 (anthropic)

body:
Un véhicule de l'inventaire dont la fiche n'a ni version ni code (ex. « Ram 1500 EXPRESS 2027 ») apparaissait sous toutes les lignes du modèle, et la liste de codes ne proposait que ceux de la ligne affichée.

- **Version** : lue dans le titre de l'annonce quand la fiche n'en a pas. Le véhicule se range sous sa vraie ligne de programme.
- **Codes possibles** : nouvelle route `GET /api/inventory/{stock}/code-suggestions`. Version, cabine et traction viennent du décodeur public de NIV (NHTSA vPIC, résultat gardé dans `vin_decodes`), puis le référentiel `master_product_codes.json` donne les codes de cette version, classés par cabine et traction. Si la version n'est pas au référentiel (Express, Warlock), on prend les versions de la même ligne de programme.
- **Année** : la liste des codes d'un programme utilise le référentiel même s'il n'a pas l'année du programme (2027).
- **Écran** : les codes possibles s'affichent sous le véhicule sans code ; un toucher inscrit le code sur la fiche.

Vérifié en local : 117 contrôles serveur réussis ; à l'écran, un Ram 1500 Express 2027 sans code donne « Tradesman · Crew Cab · 4x4 » et les codes DT6L91, DT6L98, DT6L41 ; le toucher inscrit le code.

Si le décodeur de NIV ne répond pas, la route retombe sur le titre et la ligne de programme.

author: sihanxu
body:
## Summary

**The guides say what a report is for, not what its function takes.**

A node's `report` was introduced as "a function of the view and of what the node's program returned". In four runs in a row a model wrote one function for all its nodes, of exactly that shape: a few values of the view and the returned value. The sentence described the function's arguments, and the model filled them in. `about`, which the same page asks for as "the situation the node answers", was written differently for every node in every run.

## What changes

| | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A node's `report` | "a function of the view and of what the node's program returned ... It returns the message you want to read then" | "the message you read when you are told of this node. Write it for this node's situation: put in it what you will need at that moment to judge whether the situation is over and to decide what to do next." How it is called comes after |
| A program's `until(report=)` | "a function of the view. It returns the message you want to read whenever you are told of this program" | "the message you read whenever you are told of this program ... Write it for this program: put in it what you will need at that moment to judge how far its work is and whether it still gets there." |
| Pictures | "only the values that show the situation, or a picture of it as well" | That sentence is gone: text, data, pictures and files are listed as what a message holds, none before the others |
| The refusal of a telling node without a report | Named the function's arguments | Says the same as the guide |

No behaviour changes: only the guides `tree` and `units`, the refusal's text, the docs and a change note.

- [x] Guides, refusal text, docs (English and Chinese) updated; change note added
- [x] The tests that read these texts pass

The two tests that read the refusal and the guides, once: 2 run, 2 pass.

author: justinjohn0306
body:
R2.2. Follow-up to #1883, from CodeRabbit's review there. #1883 merged before this fix was pushed, so it lands here.

## Problem

Since #1883, a local Aider run gets its message through `--message-file`. Aider handles a non-empty `--message` first and returns, without reading `--message-file` (`aider/main.py`, 0.86.2). So a `--message` saved in the backend's extra arguments would run that saved task instead of the person's request. Before #1883 the request went in `--message` last, and argparse kept the last one, so the request won.

## Change

When the message is in a file, Aider's saved extra arguments are passed without:
- `--message`, `--msg` or `-m` and the value after it;
- the joined forms `--message=…`, `--msg=…` and `-m…`.

These are the names Aider's parser declares for the option. Other saved arguments are kept. When the message goes in argv (over SSH, or if the file couldn't be written), nothing changes: the request still comes last and wins.

## Checks

- New test `a_saved_message_cannot_replace_the_request_in_its_file`. It covers each form with a message file: the saved task is gone, `--architect` stays, and `--message-file` comes last. It also checks that the argv path still puts the request last.
- `cargo test -p craft-anything-ai --no-fail-fast` passes (589 + 16).
- Clippy `-D warnings` on Rust 1.99, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask secrets` are clean.

author: auroragpt-tim
body:
## What changed
Replaced the construction-style portal work order and registration/contact form experience with a single reusable **four-step, non-confidential** production inquiry. It follows the live Finch editorial design and the eight production services currently advertised.

- **Service → Scope → Contact → Review**, with clear progress and keyboard-friendly choices
- Service-specific hints, approximate file count, desired output, requested timing and optional non-confidential notes
- Contact details, preferred reply method, required contact/no-confidentiality acknowledgments
- Validation, error and success handling, responsive layout, no document upload or browser draft persistence
- Shared form mounted at `/portal` and `/contact`; original **two existing** Formspree destinations preserved
- Legacy prototype NewRequest TSX/JS upload forms retired; old portal paths remain redirected
- Public menu says **Request Services**; privacy notice and README now reflect actual behavior
- Technical workflow/service taxonomy module and Finch Technologies intake specification added, with secure-workspace gates

## Safeguards
This is a pre-engagement inquiry, **not** an authenticated client portal. It does not receive files, establish a legal engagement, calculate legal deadlines or determine case qualification. Source concept attribution: Inquire2Esquire playbook and criminal-defense scripts, adapted to Unbundled Finch's non-intervention policy without copying scripts.

## Verification
- Netlify deploy-preview build reported **success** for commit `102816fb7c48b521dddffc055375b695c9ce3a84`.
- Manual end-to-end form submission and visual browser smoke testing were **not** performed from this connector session.
- Both Formspree destinations predated this change, but account ownership/routing/retention have **not** been verified. No sensitive legal material should ever be sent through these forms.
- A secure document-upload service would need its own backend, access control, encryption, auditing, retention and review; it is **not** included here.

### Rollback
Revert the merge commit if the live form exposes any routing, UI or deployment regression. The previous pre-engagement registration and contact forms are superseded by this change, not migrated data.

## v3.1 正式配对判定（vs 同 sweep H1；bootstrap 10000 / 种子 20261115；权威 `campaign-mixed/aggregate-campaign.json`，评审侧 `data-v3/stats-output.json` 独立重算逐位一致）

## Purpose
Introduce a separate chronological holdout audit for the 15m/1h/4h/1d analogue engine.

## Initial implementation
- Add a fixed-parameter MTF walk-forward validation core.
- Use chronological, non-overlapping query/outcome folds.
- Keep analogue search restricted to history before each query and preserve the maximum-horizon embargo.
- Recalculate bounded candidate sampling for each fold.
- Include fee/slippage-adjusted MTF analogue decisions and always-LONG, always-SHORT, FLAT and momentum baselines.
- Report fold-level outcomes, sample counts, positive-fold frequency and drawdown diagnostics.
- Document protocol and explicitly state that the module is not yet wired to the API, desktop UI or experiment ledger.

## Important limitations
This is a validation core, not an empirical validation result. No profitability or predictive edge is claimed. CI and independent test execution are required. Next work is immutable data fingerprinting/ledger integration, API job, desktop reporting, verified full-history BTC test, then frozen cross-asset replication and an untouched final holdout.

Paper Trading only; no live exchange execution.

author: upd4ting
body:
## Why

`POST /api/builder/database/sample` handed a tenant owner up to 20 raw rows of a connected external database. The screen that used it was deleted in #11. In 0.2.0 its client method `sampleRows()` had no caller, and no MCP tool exposed it. It was dead code that could still read customer rows, so this PR removes it (ANT-2985).

## What changes

- `src/builder/routes/database.ts` no longer binds `/database/sample`, and `ROUTES.databaseSample` is gone. The API server now answers the path with its own `404 Not Found`.
- `useBuilderApi()` in `frontend-vue/builder/app/runtime/api.ts` loses `sampleRows()`, and `database-types.ts` loses `RowSample` and its private value types, which only that method used.
- `docs/8.database-connection.md` drops the route's row and now says that no route answers rows of the external database.
- The verify-dms-builder journeys expect the owner's sample request to get the API server's 404, instead of reaching the route.

Breaking: the HTTP route and the `sampleRows` client method are removed outright. No stored data stops being readable.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  O[Tenant owner] -->|POST /api/builder/database/sample| API[interface-api router]
  API -. before .-> R[DatabaseController.sample] --> S[dms SampleDatabaseRows] --> DB[(external database rows)]
  API -->|after: no handler bound| N[404 Not Found]
```

## Proof

The new test in `tests/builder/database-routes.test.cjs`, "no route answers rows of the external database: /database/sample is bound to no verb", fails on the base build and passes on this branch.

Before (base `src`, `node --test tests/builder/database-routes.test.cjs`):

```
✖ no route answers rows of the external database: /database/sample is bound to no verb (0.927925ms)
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Missing expected exception: POST
    actual: undefined,
    expected: { message: '0 routes are bound to POST /database/sample' },
ℹ tests 8
ℹ pass 7
ℹ fail 1
```

After (this branch, `node --test --test-concurrency=4 tests/builder/*.test.cjs`):

```
✔ no route answers rows of the external database: /database/sample is bound to no verb (0.622508ms)
ℹ tests 26
ℹ pass 26
ℹ fail 0
```

The `verify-dms-builder` run on a real DMS sent the signed-in owner's request and got the router's 404:

```
request:  POST http://127.0.0.1:65169/api/builder/database/sample (authenticated owner)
          {"connection":"nope","relation":"orders","columns":["id"],"limit":5}
response: {"status":404,"body":"Not Found"}
```

The `http-api` journey passed. Three other journeys failed on checks this diff does not touch: `self` in the `GET /database/project` answer (`dms` where the check expects this module), and the connection check's missing `mysql2` and `mongodb` drivers in the playground. The routes they read are unchanged here.

Local checks: `typecheck`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `lint:frontend`, `lint:rules`, `knip`, `antelopejs-suppressions`, and the builder vitest suite (58 passed).

## Other callers of `SampleDatabaseRows`

Org code search on `SampleDatabaseRows`, `RowSampleRequest` and `database/sample` found callers only in `AntelopeJS/dms` and this repo. The dms hits are the operation's implementation, its interface, its docs and its unit test. There are none in dms-database, cloud or the templates. The former `AntelopeJS/dms-builder` repo, which this module replaced, still holds its own copy of the route. The `dms` MCP server exposes no tool for the operation. Removing it from dms and `@antelopejs/interface-dms-builder` is left to a dms PR.

body:
Adopting #15 failed with "Changed since this was proposed". The cause: a refinement keeps the base from an agent's *first* proposal. The maintainer typed answers into #15 after that, and my later revision already included those answers, but it was still compared against the old base, so it could never be adopted.

- **API:** `PUT /changesets/:id/items` takes `rebase: true` for a whole new text written against the item as it is now. The item's base moves to the current text, the stale conflict is cleared, and `rebased: true` comes back.
- **MCP:** `propose` sends `rebase` whenever it gets full markdown, and tells the agent when its base moved, so the agent checks it kept what changed.
- A person's own editing is unchanged.
- **Test:** `ADOPT-13` in `api/test/api.test.mjs`. A stale revision is a conflict; the rebased one adopts and keeps the person's edit. `npm test`: 125 pass.

ADOPT-13 is proposed on #13 (refinement `2c3909e61a8f`).

author: giuseppecrj
body:
## Why

Giuseppe decided on #793 (2026-11-15) that OwnerFeed stays free of model-written text. A `review_unverifiable` entry carries no reviewer prose. It carries three things instead:

1. A fixed reason code from a closed set, with readers told to show unknown values as plain text.
2. The number of unverifiable judgments.
3. The verified URL of the review comment on GitHub, built from trusted records the same way the feed builds `questionsUrl`.

The full reason stays in the review on GitHub, in a review detail comment the controller posts. Push text stays generic.

## What changed

**Feed fields** (`src/views/feed.ts`). Each entry gets three new v1 fields. Entries not held as `review_unverifiable` get `null`, `0` and `null`.
- `unverifiableCode`: one of `evidence_missing`, `needs_execution` or `other` (`UNVERIFIABLE_CODES`, `unverifiableCode` in `src/candidate/review.ts`). The feed works it out from stored records and never emits model-written prose. When more than one code applies, the first in this order wins:
  - `evidence_missing`: the feed reruns `trustedEvidence` on the held generation's stored verdict, gate receipt and CI report, the same records review preparation used, and gets `null`.
  - `needs_execution`: an unverifiable scenario's judge text, taken from the stored suite bound by the review's acceptance digest, is one the accept validator refuses as `judge_requires_execution`. The controller deterministically classifies that model-written, digest-bound text into this closed set. It reuses `judgeOnlyRefusal` from #791, now exported, with no new keyword list.
  - `other`: everything else, including a judge that only restates a trusted gate and a suite that cannot be read.
- One code covers the whole hold. There are no per-code counts.
- `unverifiableCount`: the number of unverifiable judgments in the held review. It can be more than the 10 IDs listed in `unverifiable`.
- `unverifiableUrl`: `<issueUrl>#issuecomment-<id>` for the review detail comment, or `null`.

**Review detail comment** (`src/trust/markers.ts` `formatUnverifiableDetail`, `src/controller/effects.ts` `postUnverifiableDetail`, `src/controller/orchestrator.ts` `#publishUnverifiableDetail`, `src/candidate/review.ts` `unverifiableJudgments`)
- While a run is held as `review_unverifiable`, the controller posts a review detail comment on the issue before the blocked marker. It lists every unverifiable judgment with the reviewer's full reason.
- Each reason passes through `inert()`. It is cut only beyond 2,000 characters, with a `(truncated: <n> more characters)` note. The whole comment stays within 60 KiB, under GitHub's 65,536-character limit. A closing line counts any judgments that do not fit. Review already caps a reason at 600 characters and a suite at 30 scenarios, so in practice nothing is cut.
- The blocked marker is unchanged: at most 10 reasons, each cut to 160 characters, within the 4 KiB cap.
- The comment's last line is a key over the run, the held generation's digest and a digest of the listed judgments. Before posting, the controller looks for that key among its own comments on the issue. A restart or a later tick finds it and does not post again. Within one process, a confirmed key is also remembered per run, so ticks do not reread comments.

**Comment receipt** (`host/controller/run-files.ts`, `src/controller/claims.ts`)
- When the detail comment posts, the controller takes the comment ID from the authenticated POST response, as #774 does for the questions comment. The receipt no longer points at the marker.
- It writes that ID to the private `contracts/<runId>/unverifiable-comment.json`, with the run, repository, issue and held generation (round, number, digest). A later post replaces the file.
- The feed builds a URL only when every binding matches the entry and the current generation and the ID is 1 to 20 digits.
- A detail found by its key is not linked, because its ID did not come from a POST response. A lost or unknown POST response or a failed write (logged as `unverifiable_reference_unavailable`) records nothing new. A receipt from another generation gives `null`. The feed never takes a URL from comment text and never guesses one.

**Kept:** `unverifiable: [{scenario}]` stays. The field is already v1, and its IDs must match `S<n>`.

**Docs.** `docs/operations/owner-feed.md` now covers:
- the new fields
- where the full reasons live: the detail comment, with its per-reason cap, truncation note and overall size bound
- the closed set, its order of precedence and the rule to show unknown codes as plain text (`unverifiableCode` joins the open-vocabulary list in the change rules)
- corrected provenance wording: the controller never emits model-written prose, and it deterministically classifies digest-bound judge text into a controller-defined closed set
- the count, the key that stops duplicates and the link construction
- the Text fields table, Actions, the tap target, the new capture
- a push-rule bullet: a push for this hold says only that the owner must decide. It never includes the code, count, scenario IDs or review text.

`docs/operations/factory-cli.md` describes the detail comment, the receipt and the fallback to `null`. This repo has no code path that builds push text.

**Shep bridge: no change is required.** Every addition is v1 under the stability rule. Old readers ignore unknown fields. Nothing is removed or retyped, and no shipped bridge read #793's field. To show this hold, the bridge can render the code, count and scenario IDs as plain text and open `unverifiableUrl`, falling back to `issueUrl`.

## Review round (c81384d)

The independent review of 67034a0 found two blocking issues.
- **B1.** The link pointed at the blocked marker, whose reasons are capped at 160 characters and 10 judgments, so the full reason was nowhere on GitHub. Fixed by the review detail comment above.
- **B2.** `owner-feed.md` said the feed "never parses model text". It now says what the code does.

## Tests (red first)

- `test/src/controller/orchestrator-validation.test.ts`, `publishes every unverifiable judgment with its full reason in one detail comment, links it and never posts it twice (#795)`. It runs the real controller with 12 unverifiable judgments, each reason over 160 characters. It checks:
  - every judgment and its full reason appear in the detail comment
  - the marker still holds only the short list
  - the receipt's comment ID is the detail comment's, not the marker's
  - one more tick and two fresh-process restarts leave one detail comment and the same receipt

  Before the fix it failed with `0 !== 1`: no detail comment existed.
- `test/src/controller/orchestrator-validation.test.ts`, `hands off a unverifiable review judgment only when it is pass`. The receipt now expects the detail comment's ID. Before the fix it failed because no detail comment existed. Its marker assertions are kept.
- `test/src/trust/markers.test.ts`, 2 new cases. The first checks that all 13 judgments and their full inert reasons appear, that `@`, `#` and HTML are neutralized, that the key is the last line, and that the output is stable. The second checks that a 2,000-character reason is kept whole, that a 2,500-character reason is cut at 2,000 with the note, and that 30 reasons of 2,000 `#` characters each stay within 60 KiB and add the omitted-count line. These failed at import before the fix.
- Mutation: removing the key lookup in `postUnverifiableDetail` fails the controller test with `3 !== 1`, because each restart posts again.
- Unchanged from the first round:
  - `test/src/views/feed.test.ts`, `a review_unverifiable hold carries a controller reason code, the judgment count and a verified comment link, never reviewer text (#793)`. This covers the codes, the count, the URL and its 9 mismatch cases, and checks that real `owner-feed --json` output contains no reviewer or judge text.
  - `test/src/candidate/review.test.ts`, `owner reason code for an unverifiable-only review (#7

author: hartiganhm
body:
## What

While the scanner's two models download and warm up, the looking panel now says so instead of asking for a card it can't read yet (handoff `design/design_handoff_the99_card_scan/addendum-loading/`, READINESS 🟡 Yellow). These are the addendum's states:

- **Loading L1 · Getting the scanner ready.** The bar fills with the real model bytes against the pinned total (17.9 MB). The figure reads "7.2 of 17.9 MB", and the first-time line sits under it.
- **Loading L2 · Almost ready.** Every byte has landed. A highlight runs along the full bar while the runtime and warm-up finish.
- **Loading L4 · Starting the scanner.** Both models were cached, but the scanner still can't read 400ms after it opened. The bar is indeterminate and sits over the shipped mode line.
- **Loading L3.** This is the shipped looking panel, reached with a 150ms fade of the panel's contents (none with reduced motion).

Phone and desktop both draw these states in the shipped result panel. There's no scrim, and the camera, ✕/Stop, Auto/Normal and the light are unchanged.

## How

| READINESS item | Where it's done |
| --- | --- |
| 1 · Streamed progress, hash kept, pinned sizes | `model-cache.ts` `readCounting` reads the body as a stream and reports each chunk. The whole buffer is still hashed before use, and the cache still gets the `res.clone()` tee. `models.ts` pins `DETECTOR_BYTES` 3,185,226 and `EMBEDDER_BYTES` 14,756,557. The total is the pinned size, then `content-length`, then null (an indeterminate bar with no figures), whichever still covers the bytes read. |
| 2 · L1 or L4 from cache presence, at once | `modelBytes` reports `{from:"cache"}` as soon as a hit is found, and reports a network 0-byte event before it fetches. A cached file that fails its hash moves on to a counted download. `scanLoading` (`screen-state.ts`) counts only the files that download, and shows L2 only once every file is done or failed. |
| 3 · Shared load, not cancelled on close | Each model file's load is shared (`pipeline.ts`) and, for the scanner (`report: true`), publishes to `model-progress.ts`, a module-level store read with `useSyncExternalStore`, so a reopen shows the real progress of the one download. A scanner holds the store while open (`holdModelLoad`); a finished load nobody holds is dropped, so the next open never draws the last one's. |
| 4 · Live region never reads the MB figure | The figure is `aria-hidden` and the value lives on the `progressbar`. L1→L2 keeps the same nodes, so only the heading text changes. |
| 5 · First 400ms of a cached open | `REOPEN_AFTER_MS` timer in `CardScanner`. The shipped looking panel shows until then, and L4 shows after it. |
| 6 · A failed load | A failed file is let go at once, so the next frame's retry restarts it straight away (never the rejected promise, never waiting on the other file) as a download at 0: L1 with fresh progress, no L4 flash. `noStart` still comes after `READ_FAILURES_TOLD` failed reads (`use-card-scan.ts`, pinned by its existing test); `offlineBody` unchanged. |
| 7 · The `ready` input | `onModelsReady` sets `ready` in `CardScanner`, and `loading` is passed to `ScannerView`, whose looking panel draws L1/L2/L4. |
| 8 · #2946 | Progress is an optional `onProgress` on `pinnedBytes`, passed only by the scanner's model load (`report: true`). `webgpu.ts`'s runtime fetch and the scan lab's loads pass none, so they never feed the bar. |
| 9 · IDs | Code, comments and tests say "loading L1-L4" (`data-state="loading-download"`, `loading-almost`, `loading-reopen`). |

The highlight is a new `scan-shim` keyframe in `globals.css`. The indeterminate bar reuses `anim-search-progress` with `--sweep-end: 295%` for its 34% fill (the card search keeps its 265% default). The stream is read into one buffer of the pinned size, grown only on overrun.

## Copy

`/copy-review` (propose) ran on the six new `collectionEditCopy.scan.loading` strings. All six are frozen: they're quoted verbatim in the handoff and READINESS.

| Key | Class | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` Getting the scanner ready | Chrome | KEEP |
| `firstLine` | Teaching | KEEP. READINESS 10: it is **hidden** where Cache Storage is missing or won't open for this load (`ModelLoad.cacheless`), so no new string was coined |
| `size(done, total)` | Data | KEEP. Decimal MB, one decimal, trailing .0 dropped: the real total reads 17.9 |
| `almost` Almost ready | Chrome | KEEP |
| `reopen` Starting the scanner | Chrome + A11y (names L4's bar) | KEEP |
| `barLabel` Scanner download | A11y | KEEP |

Tally: 6 KEEP, 0 edits. No em dashes, US English.

## Design review

Handoff: `design/design_handoff_the99_card_scan/addendum-loading/` (READINESS 🟡 Yellow). I enumerated and verified this inline: the addendum is one panel, and its boards were short enough to check row by row.

| Element | Property | Phone: design → built | Desktop: design → built | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Panel | box | shipped result panel, gap 14 → `PANEL_PHONE gap-[14px]` | shipped result area, gap 12 → `PANEL_DESK` | ✅ |
| Heading | style / key | 600 16px `--fg` → `HEAD` with `loading.title`/`almost`/`reopen` | sheet's size (as shipped) → `HEAD_DESK` | ✅ |
| Load block | layout | flex column, gap 8 → `flex flex-col gap-[8px]` | same | ✅ |
| Bar track | size / color | 8px, radius 4, `#20222A` → `h-[8px] rounded-[4px] bg-[--elevated]` | same | ✅ |
| Bar fill | color / width | `--accent`, width = bytes % → inline `width: n%` | same | ✅ |
| Figure | type | mono 12.5px `--fg-muted`, done 500 `--fg` → `font-mono text-[12.5px]`, `<b font-medium>` | same | ✅ |
| Figure | total | "18" illustrative → 17.9 (READINESS 1) | same | ✅ |
| Body (L1/L2) | text | `firstLine`, `BODY` | same | ✅ |
| L1 progressbar | a11y | named `barLabel`, valuenow 0-100 | same | ✅ |
| L1 with no size | look | L4's indeterminate bar, L1's words, no figures | same | ✅ |
| L2 bar | look | full + 40% white-35% band, 1.4s ease-in-out → `anim-scan-shim` | same | ✅ |
| L2 bar | a11y | board has valuenow=100 → none (README wins, READINESS) | same | 🔸 README over board |
| L2 / L4 desktop | layout | not drawn → phone contents in `PANEL_DESK` | same | 🔸 nearest pattern: phone L2/L4 (READINESS) |
| L4 bar | a11y | named by `reopen` → `aria-labelledby` its heading (same words) | same | ✅ |
| L4 bar | motion | 34% slide, 1.3s alternate → `anim-search-progress` with `--sweep-end: 295%`, so the 34% fill leaves the track | same | 🔸 nearest pattern: card search's sweep (READINESS Codebase fit) |
| L4 body | text | shipped mode line → `mode.fastLine`/`normalLine` | same | ✅ |
| Reduced motion | bars | highlight off; indeterminate full width at 45% → `motion-reduce:hidden` / `motion-reduce:w-full opacity-45` | same | ✅ |
| Hand-off | motion | 150ms cross-fade of contents → a one-shot 150ms fade-in class (`overlay-in`) on the same box, cleared on `animationend`, motion-safe only, no timers | same | 🔸 nearest pattern: shipped opacity fade; same nodes keep the live region to the heading |
| Outline while loading | — | none → none (frames aren't read before ready) | same | ✅ |
| Cached open < 400ms | panel | shipped looking panel → same | same | ✅ |
| Focus / controls | — | ✕/Stop focus, mode, light as shipped → untouched | same | ✅ |
| Close mid-download | — | spec "from 0" → shared load kept (READINESS 3 ruling) | same | 🔸 READINESS 3 |

Verdict: 22 rows, 17 match, 5 resolved from the nearest drawn pattern or a READINESS ruling, 0 gaps.

## Copilot off

Risky by the gate: model-cache.ts deletes caches.

## Claude review

Pre-open pass: 3 Low, all fixed (the L2 band's range now leaves the bar, -66.7% to 166.7%; its comment no longer says "each way"; the L4 sweep's end is sized for its 34% fill).

/code-review medium: 10 findings, all fixed:
1. `cacheless` missed Cache Storage that exists but won't open: it now comes from whether the cache opened for this load (`keeps` on each progress event), tested.
2. A failed download froze the bar and the retry went L1→L4→L

author: randybias
body:
Two findings from sdk's rehearsal.

**D, doubled range.** A document's `groups` map is keyed by the owner part, and decode built each switch's group as `range + "." + key`. A document that keyed a group by an address (`lab.h1.l1` in range `lab`) produced four problems that read `switch "lab.lab.h1.l1"`. Decode now refuses a group key with a dot, naming the key as written: `group "lab.h1.l1": a group is keyed by its owner part only (no dots); the range is the document's, and a switch is set for an owner group, never for a single sender`. The listset validate messages are unchanged. Test: `TestDecodeGroupKeyedByAddress` (keys `lab.h1.l1` and `lab.h1`; the error has the key and `owner part`, never `lab.lab`).

**E, wrong answer.** `mash policy show` and `explain` with a legacy name or a credential that is not a list-set credential answered locally `open: owner line only, no list set in force`, also while a list set was in force. That credential cannot ask the responder, so the client cannot know. The text is now `this credential is not covered by a list set: it has the owner line only (a list set may be in force for the account's other senders; only a list-set credential can ask the policy responder)`. The JSON shape (`state: none`, reason `no_list_set`) is unchanged. The responder's own answer for an account with no list set (`policyview.NoListSetNotice`) is unchanged. The test now asserts the new text for `show`, `show --json` and `explain --json`, and that `no list set in force` is absent. `docs/install.md` and `docs/comparison.md` quote the new text.

ADR 0110 (line 47) quotes the old string as the local answer. It is accepted and not edited; this changes the wording of that answer, not the decision (a local answer for a credential that cannot ask). Lead directed `Decision: none`.

Checked: gofmt, go vet, go test for policydoc, listset, policyview, cmd/mash; changelog check.

Decision: none

author: ceckert
body:
## Problem

`docs/gke.md` cannot be followed through to the end: `down` fails on every run. Two GKE installs at 818c02c43 showed this.

- **Cloud SQL never released the connection.** After the database was deleted, Service Networking refused to delete the network's connection with `FLOW_SN_DC_RESOURCE_PREVENTING_DELETE_CONNECTION` ("Producer services (e.g. CloudSQL…) are still using this connection").
  - On the first project, the instance finished deleting at 01:00:28Z. Six reruns of `down` were refused through 02:49:13Z, at least 109 minutes, and the connection was never released.
  - On the second project, it was refused for the whole ten-minute window.
- **What `down` left:** each run waited ten minutes, then stopped. The network, its peering, the `octogee-sql` address range and the router with NAT were left behind.
- **What works:** deleting the peering from the network's own side (`gcloud compute networks peerings delete servicenetworking-googleapis-com --network=octogee`) succeeded at once on both projects. The address range, router and network then deleted cleanly, leaving only the project's defaults.

The same run found two gaps in the guide's project step:
- **Git password:** `git clone` with the issued git password is refused with `Update your password`, because Gitea wants it replaced at the first sign-in. `kind.md` says so; `gke.md` did not.
- **Agent start-up:** the project's agent appears in the channel within seconds but starts listening about two minutes later. A message sent before then is never answered.

## Change

- **`down`:** when Service Networking says the connection is still in use, `down` deletes the network's peering, then carries on with the address range, router and network. The ten-minute wait and the "run down again later" message are gone. Any other refusal still stops at once with gcloud's error. A failed peering delete also stops `down`, and the state directory is kept.
- **Guide:** `docs/gke.md` describes the new `down` behaviour. The project step now says to wait two minutes before writing to the agent, and to sign in to Gitea once and set a new password before cloning. It also no longer says the create answer names the channel; the answer carries the channel id.

## Tests

`scripts/__tests__/gke-install.spec.ts` stubs `gcloud`, so I tested the new behaviour there, red first on Linux.

- **Replaced:** the two tests that pinned the wait and the "run down again later" stop.
