body: Three-part fix round from owner reports on the live site (2026-11-15, post-PR #32). All measurements from the full-Chromium harness against real production payloads (local snapshot == main @ 3506bbc8, blob-SHA verified before editing). ## Part A — Buy Now → sign-in optimization (commit 46931f1) **Before:** card Buy on single-plan products (Netflix 4K) jumped straight to a generic login dialog with no product image/name/plan/price anywhere; grouped products reached the same context-free login from the popup's Buy button. Worse, the login dialog rendered at the **document top**: measured rect y = **−2,197px** at scrollY 2,376 (off-viewport until scrolling back up), and the page lurched on open (scroll delta **−2,283px** on Netflix Buy). **Root cause of the jump:** store-ui.css `body > * { position: relative; z-index: 1 }` — every `` is a direct child of ``, so that author rule overrides the UA `:modal` fixed positioning and the dialog centres inside a viewport-sized box anchored at the document top (isolated with a bare-dialog control test: same Chromium computes `fixed` without the rule, `absolute` with it). **Fixes:** - `theme.css` §3t: `.dialog:modal { position: fixed; }` — every modal (auth, product, payment, orders) now opens centred in the viewport at any scroll position; opening one no longer moves the page. §3n scroll save/restore untouched. - The sign-in dialog now carries the pending purchase when opened from a Buy action: `startOrder` flags the buy context, `authFrame`/`authSummaryHtml` render image (via `productVisual` — override → own image → bundled logo → emblem), name, plan label (same `planLabelFor` logic as the popup) and price as a card in the aside on wide layouts and a compact strip above the form on narrow ones (`auth.css`, token-driven, both themes). The flag clears when the dialog closes, so header Sign in shows **no** summary. Auth logic itself is unchanged. - **Post-login continuation** rides the existing mechanism (`state.pendingAction` → `resumePendingAction()` → `startOrder(productId)` → order → payment dialog; Google sign-in persists it via sessionStorage). Exercised end-to-end in the harness with the auth/order APIs stubbed at the browser edge (no production writes, no real customer account exists): stubbed sign-in as the Prime 6 Months buyer landed on the payment dialog reading "Subscription: Prime Video (6 Months) · NPR 400". **After measurements (desktop 1920×998):** Netflix Buy → login centred (centre-delta y ≈ 0.008px), scroll delta **0**, summary "Netflix 4K · 1 Month · NPR 350" with `/logos/netflix.svg`. Prime: switched popup plan to 6 Months first — page scroll stayed 2,376 through the whole chain, login summary "Prime Video · 6 Months · NPR 400" with the Prime logo. Header Sign in → no summary. Light theme: same, centred, delta 0. Mobile 400px: strip visible (aside card hidden), centred, delta 0. Prime popup geometry A/B vs the PR #32 harness record: relative geometry identical (Save pills fully inside the scrollport, footer was-price ink gap 17.6px both) — no §3r regression. Bumps: `app.js?v=119`, `auth.css?v=102`, `theme.css?v=128` on every page that loads them. ## Part C — Netflix popup banner (commit 10356ed) Owner: the Netflix card shows the red NETFLIX wordmark, but the View Details popup banner showed a wide DASHAIN SALE creative; the banner "should be shown like feature or other tags". **Investigation:** the banner image was never wrong — `detailVisual()` and `productVisual()` resolve identically, Netflix has **no** saved `image_url` in either the catalogue or detail payload, and card img src == banner img src == `/logos/netflix.svg?v=2`. The invader was the **badge lane**: the single-product popup renders `saleBadge(product.badge)` inside `.pd-badges`; Netflix's badge is `dashain`, whose variant is an `` of the transparent festive creative (964×263). card-premium.css caps that emblem at 34px in the card badge slot, but the rule is scoped to `.card-badges` — in the popup only the §3s banner caps applied. Measured with the real creative: emblem **340×93** desktop / **306×84** on a 369px phone banner. **Fix:** `theme.css` §3u gives `.pd-badges` the card lane's emblem treatment (34px/130px; 26px/105px ≤640px). **After: 125×34 desktop / 95×26 mobile** — a tag beside the −30% OFF pill, and the wordmark owns the banner. Prime/Canva/ChatGPT/Microsoft banner caps re-verified unchanged (≤216×108, zero crop). ## Part B — Favicon set (commit 24bd17c, TEXT HALF ONLY ⚠️) All 7 pages replace the single wide-wordmark icon link (`logo%20mm.png`, 512×178 squeezed into the square tab slot) with: `favicon.ico` (sizes="any"), `favicon-32.png`, `icon-192.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png` — the owner-approved D-mark-on-dark-tile set. `server/scripts/build.js` `publicFiles` gains the five icon files; local build verified (icons byte-identical in dist, links on every dist page, build skips missing files gracefully). **⚠️ The five binary icon files are NOT yet on this branch** — the snapshot push channel rejects non-UTF-8 files (`snapshot file 'favicon.ico' is not UTF-8`), and no other binary-capable channel is available in-session. **Do not merge until they are added** (repo root: `favicon.ico`, `favicon-32.png`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png`; prepared set is in the workspace at `~/workspace/favicon/` and mirrored in the local snapshot root). Parts A and C are complete and mergeable on their own if Part B needs to split out. Validation: `node --check` app.js + build.js pass; tinycss2 parses auth.css/theme.css with 0 errors (braces balanced); `node server/scripts/build.js` passes; dist spot-checks confirm new refs/rules/links.

author: charliermarsh
body:
Werkzeug turns off profiling while handling an upload. Imre already runs this code without an active profiler, but the `sys` module did not expose the call Werkzeug uses to turn it off.

Expose `sys.getprofile()` and `sys.setprofile(None)` on the normal `sys` module. Disabling the hook dispatches Python’s `sys.setprofile` audit event, including when an audit hook raises. Installing a profiler still reports the existing unsupported operation.

The original installed Werkzeug upload ran to completion on Linux and wrote the same 2,003 output bytes as CPython, with empty stderr. The 495 runtime tests also passed.

body:
## Resumo

Achado do Cursor no PR #142: `MatchAttendanceService.loadRowInputs` (caminho real de confirmação/fila) montava `isFixedList` direto do elenco, sem consultar o merge de regras efetivas da partida (`defaults` + `match.rulesOverride`). Um `rulesOverride.fixedListOnly: false` numa partida específica não tinha efeito nenhum sobre a prioridade de fila — só a regra geral da pelada funcionava.

Closes #150

## Decisão de produto

`fixedListOnly` na pelada decide se `isFixedList` *pode existir* no elenco (gate + limpeza ao desativar). O override por partida é um controle mais estreito: suspende a prioridade só numa partida pontual (ex. amistoso avulso), sem apagar o flag permanente do jogador.

## Por que não foi a correção literal do Cursor

A sugestão ingênua (`isFixedList: player.isFixedList && effective.fixedListOnly`) quebraria o teste baseline existente, que simula um estado (`isFixedList: true` com a regra da pelada no default `false`) não alcançável via API real. Ajustei o teste para configurar `fixedListOnly: true` na pelada antes — estado realista — em vez de mudar o comportamento para acomodar um teste com setup inconsistente.

## Arquivos alterados

- `apps/api/src/matches/match-attendance.service.ts`: `loadRowInputs` agora recebe o `fixedListOnly` efetivo (pelada + override da partida).
- `apps/api/test/3-4-api-attendance.integration-spec.ts`: baseline ajustado (setup realista) + novo teste de regressão para o override por partida.

## Test plan

- `RUN_DB_TESTS=1 npm run test:api` (com Postgres local real, não apenas unitário) — 20 suites unitárias (76 testes), 3 suites e2e (16 testes) e 12 suites de integração (90 testes), todos verdes, incluindo os 2 testes baseline ajustados e o novo teste de override.

author: justin13888
body:
## Summary
- JSON Schema 2019-09's `$recursiveRef` and `$recursiveAnchor` are now `E006`, the same as `$dynamicRef`/`$dynamicAnchor`. Before this change spargen read them as unknown keywords, so a property holding `$recursiveRef: '#'` became `serde_json::Value` and nothing was reported. The remedy says to use a JSON Pointer `$ref` to the recursive schema instead (`spargen/src/oas31/deserialize/schema.rs`).
- The pre-2020-12 validation keywords `additionalItems` and `dependencies` are now `W001` at the schema that carries them. Each gets its own message naming the 2020-12 replacement (`items` beside `prefixItems`, or `dependentRequired`/`dependentSchemas`), and generation still succeeds. Before this change the constraints they state were dropped and nothing was reported.
  - `spargen/src/oas31/schema.rs`: `ValidationKeywords` gains `pre_2020_12: Vec<Pre2020Keyword>`. `constrains_nothing` counts it. The new `states_no_2020_12_keyword` drives the generic validation-keyword `W001`, so a schema carrying only `additionalItems` gets one specific warning and not the generic one as well.
  - `spargen/src/oas31/deserialize/keywords.rs`: `parse_validation` records the keywords that are present.
  - `spargen/src/oas31/audit.rs`: emits the new `// W001 case: pre-2020-keyword`.
  - `spargen/src/oas31/deserialize/schema.rs`: an `additionalItems` value, and each `dependencies` entry, that has a schema's shape (an object or a boolean) is parsed into `validation_children`. The audit then checks it and resolves the references under it, like any other unlowered applicator.
- `spargen/src/diag/code.rs`: the E006 and W001 explain texts name the new cases. `spargen/src/diag/code/tests/cases.rs`: `ENUMERATED_CASES` gains W001's `pre-2020-keyword`.
- `docs/support-matrix.md`: the Schema shape row's Rejected cell names `$recursiveRef`/`$recursiveAnchor` (`E006`), and its Warned cell names `additionalItems`/`dependencies` (`W001`). `docs/errors.md` is unchanged because no code or title changes.
- `spargen/tests/frontend/schema_keywords.rs` (first commit, fixtures before the fix):
  - S1 and a bare `$recursiveAnchor` each assert `E006` at the schema, with the message and the remedy.
  - S2 and S3 each assert exactly one `W001` with its message, and that generation succeeds.
  - A `$ref` to a missing component under `additionalItems` or under `dependencies` is still reported (`E004`).
- The corpus case `openai-openapi` flips from `reject:E009` to `reject:E006`. `/components/schemas/CompoundFilter` writes `$recursiveAnchor: true`, and its `filters` items hold a `$recursiveRef: '#'` member: this is the issue's S1 in the wild. The flip changes:
  - `corpus/manifest.toml`: the expectation and its reason.
  - `corpus/README.md`: the table row and the reason. The "What a green corpus does not prove" section now says this document no longer reaches schema lowering.
  - `mise.toml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the `corpus-smoke` grep for this case. `corpus_manifest.rs` holds both to the manifest.
  - `spargen/tests/snapshot.rs` and `spargen/tests/snapshots/snapshot__openai_openapi.snap`: the comment and the histogram, now `E006: 2, W002: 1`.

## Validation
- `cargo test -p spargen --test frontend -- schema_keywords` failed 3 at the fixture commit 6e6431b1 and passed 15 after the fix.
- `cargo test -p spargen --test frontend`: passed (809).
- `cargo test -p spargen --lib diag::code`: passed (15).
- `INSTA_UPDATE=always cargo test -p spargen --test snapshot`: passed (10). The `openai_openapi` snapshot diff was reviewed as described above.
- `cargo test -p spargen --test corpus_manifest --test repo_gates`: passed.
- `mise run corpus-smoke`: passed.
- `mise run fmt-check`: passed. `mise run lint`: passed.
- `cargo test -p spargen --all-features --no-fail-fast` (at aa0035fe): passed, no test binary or doctest run reported a failure
- Deferred to CI: the rest of `cargo test --workspace --all-features` and the slow gates. Generated output for an accepted spec is unchanged, so codegen is not touched.

## Risks and rollout
- Specs that use `$recursiveRef` or `$recursiveAnchor` are now rejected where they used to generate. That is the decided behaviour. A spec using `additionalItems` or `dependencies` gets one more `W001` per keyword. Its outcome does not change.
- Corpus coverage loss: `openai-openapi` now stops at `E006` before lowering. Schema lowering is therefore no longer exercised by that document, and `/components/schemas/InputItem/oneOf/1` (the corpus's only `$ref` beside `type: object` outside Mastodon) is no longer reached. `corpus/README.md` now says so.
- The fix commit cd558253 leaves `corpus-smoke` and the `openai_openapi` snapshot failing. The next commit, aa0035fe, updates the expectation.
- Coverage gap: no test reaches a `dependencies` entry or an `additionalItems` value that is neither an object nor a boolean. Such a value is skipped silently apart from the keyword's own `W001` (decision 3).

## Issue
Closes #1446

## Decisions taken
Issue 1446 - fix(frontend): $recursiveRef is E006; additionalItems and dependencies are W001

The issue's recorded decision, which this pull request carries out: "F11: `$recursiveRef` is rejected with E006, like `$dynamicRef`, because it silently degraded to `Value`. `additionalItems` and `dependencies` get W001." (maintainer decision, 2026-11-13 audit)

1. **How the pre-2020-12 keywords reach the audit.**
   - Taken: a dedicated `ValidationKeywords::pre_2020_12` list. The audit emits one `W001` per keyword with its own message, and the generic validation-keyword `W001` keys on the 2020-12 keywords alone.
   - Rejected: setting `ValidationKeywords::other`, as the issue's suggested fix says. `other` already fires the generic "validation-only schema keywords are not enforced" `W001`, so the same site would carry two warnings, and the generic one names no keyword.
   - Reverse: add the two keywords to the `other` chain in `parse_validation` and delete the `pre_2020_12` loop in `audit_schema`.
2. **Where the `W001` points.**
   - Taken: the schema that carries the keyword, as the other `W001` cases do.
   - Rejected: the keyword's own pointer, which no other `W001` case uses.
   - Reverse: push `as_str()` onto the provenance in the audit loop.
3. **A pre-2020-12 keyword whose value does not have a schema's shape.**
   - Taken: only an object or boolean `additionalItems` value, or `dependencies` entry, is parsed as a subschema. Anything else (for example a `dependencies` property list) is skipped, and the keyword's `W001` still fires. In a 3.1 or 3.2 document these are unknown keywords, so their shape is not spargen's to police.
   - Rejected: `E011` on a malformed value. That would reject documents over keywords that 2020-12 does not define.
   - Reverse: call `parse_schema_or` without the `is_schema_shaped` filter in `parse_validation_children`.
4. **Whether `$recursiveAnchor` alone is rejected.**
   - Taken: yes, as the issue's suggested fix says, matching the existing treatment of `$dynamicAnchor`.
   - Reverse: drop the `$recursiveAnchor` arm of the check in `parse_schema_or`.
5. **E006 cases.**
   - Taken: E006 stays a prose explain body and is not added to `ENUMERATED_CASES`. It still has one emission rule per keyword pair, and the issue makes enumeration conditional.
   - Reverse: add E006 to `ENUMERATED_CASES` with `dynamic-ref` and `recursive-ref` cases and markers.
6. **The `openai-openapi` corpus flip.**
   - Taken: change the expectation to `reject:E006`, which the issue anticipates ("any corpus case that flips gets a reviewed `corpus/manifest.toml` change"). The `corpus-smoke` grep lines in `mise.toml` and `ci.yml` change with it, because `corpus_manifest.rs` holds them to the manifest.
   - Rejected: an omit profile that strips `CompoundFilter` to keep the document reaching lowering. That would add a new corpus configuration beyond this issue.
   - Reverse: revert commit aa0035fe together with the `$recursiveRef` check.

author: cyanidesayonara
body:
El Drac's arena, first piece (docs/BOSSES.md, "The arenas"): the fountain's three spouts.

- Two spouts are bronze pipes set in knobs of rock in the stair walls. The third is the serpent's head under its medallion above his plinth. Each has a trencadís pressure tile in its own colour on the paving.
- A paw or your human's shoe on a tile clicks it. For 0.8 s the spout gurgles, the tile glows and the lane is marked, filling as the warning runs out. Then the jet crosses the landing where he fights.
- In the fight, a jet that catches him takes 14 HP, dazes him for 2.2 s and pays "soaked! +6" through `award_points`. A dazed dragon is not dazed twice.
- At his last stand the serpent's jet chokes his own jet ("choked! +4") and does not daze him. A daze there would send him back through RETREAT and reset the leg tie.
- Her water never knocks her or your human. A tile fires once per step and refills in 3.5 s. The tiles do nothing while he sleeps or after he is settled.
- Until she has soaked him once, the low-priority banner between his attacks reads "STEP ON A SPOUT'S TILE TO SOAK HIM" (`mosaic.idle_status`).
- Everything is drawn through ShapeBatch. Tiles and spouts go under him, the jets over him.

Second piece, the loose trencadís (added on request after review began):

- Every hit knocks two big glazed shards off him onto the stair. His slither sheds one every 0.7 s, with at most eight on the ground, each lasting 9 s. The first shout of a fight says "LOOSE TILES! RUN ONTO ONE TO SLIDE".
- When she runs onto a shard (faster than 110 px/s), she rides it for 0.6 s at 520 px/s, steering a little, until it grinds to a stop or meets a wall. This is the new `dog.ride` in `entities/dog.gd`, which only runs while `ride_t > 0`. A knock ends a ride.
- His tail and his jet pass over a dog riding a shard, and that counts as a dodge: "slid clear! +2" through `award_points`, plus his dodge damage.

The serpentine bench is left for a follow-up PR.

Tests: `tests/test_drac.gd` grows from 55 to 93 checks (the spouts plus 11 for the shards), all passing locally on the merged tree. They cover the lane geometry, the tiles' placement, the telegraph running before any water, the hit's damage, daze and payout, the wet lane, no double daze, no refire while a tile is held, your human's shoe, tiles inert while he sleeps, and the last-stand choke. The full suite was not run locally because four sessions share this machine, so this PR's CI is the full run.

## Feel card

1. `--level=guell`: walk up to El Drac and wake him. Three tiles (blue and green low on the stair by each wall, orange up beside his plinth) breathe softly in their colours, and the banner between his attacks says "STEP ON A SPOUT'S TILE TO SOAK HIM".
2. Step the dog onto the blue tile (west wall). The spout bubbles and a blue lane fills across the landing for about a second before any water. The jet hits him and you see "SOAKED WITH HIS OWN FOUNTAIN!", "soaked! +6", crossed eyes, and a 14-point chunk off his bar.
3. Let your human drift onto the green tile (east wall). Their step fires it too. Standing on a tile after it fires does not fire it again. Step off and back on after about 3.5 s and it fires again.
4. Beat him down to his last stand on the plinth, then step on the orange serpent tile. The serpent's jet runs down over him: "CHOKED HIS JET!", "+4", no daze, and the leg tie carries on.
5. The spouts read as part of the stair (rock knobs with bronze pipes, the serpent medallion), not as lifebuoys or HUD.
6. Soak him once. Two jagged shards of his glaze skitter onto the stair and you see "LOOSE TILES! RUN ONTO ONE TO SLIDE". Run onto one and she skates on it for about half a second, grit spraying off its back edge, then slows to a stop.
7. Get behind him so he winds up the tail, then ride a shard through the swept arc. She isn't knocked, and you see "slid clear! +2" and a chunk off his bar. The same works through his jet's lane.
8. Standing still on a shard does nothing. A shard read as a broken piece of tile, not a dropped phone or card.

author: stormer78
body:
## Summary

Console (`did-hosting-ui`) safety, correctness and UX, built on the #453 foundations (`lib/query.ts`, `Dialog`, `Field`, `Button`, …). UI-only; no server or wire changes.

### #385 — destructive actions
- New `lib/feedback.ts` + `components/FeedbackHost.tsx` (mounted once in `_layout`): `confirmAction`/`confirm` open an in-app dialog (title, body, explicitly labelled action, focus on Cancel, optional type-to-confirm, optional multiple choices, queued requests); `notify` shows toasts (success/info fade, errors stay). `lib/alert.ts` (`window.confirm`/`alert`) is deleted; every call site moved over.
- Type-to-confirm: delete DID, domain "Delete now" and "Purge & delete", server "Purge now".
- ACL removal is one `RemoveEntryDialog`: lists the owned DIDs; **Remove access only** / **Remove access and delete N DIDs** (typed `delete N`) / **Cancel**; per-DID progress; on any failure the entry is kept, failures listed with their errors and a "Retry the failed ones" that only retries what is left.
- Rollback, retire generation, passkey revoke, invite revoke, unassign, owner change, and agent-name actions all use the dialog; success alerts became toasts.

### #386 — one route guard
- `lib/route-guard.ts` (`guardDecision`) + `components/AuthGate.tsx` around the navigator: splash while `!restored`; signed out → `/login?next=<path+query>` (`lib/next-path.ts` `safeNextPath`: single leading `/`, no `//`, `/\`, control chars or backslashes, never back to `/login`/`/enroll`); login returns there.
- Mid-session expiry (`webvh:unauthorized` while a token was held) sets `sessionExpired`: the screen stays mounted (and the query cache is no longer cleared on expiry — only on sign-out or a different subject), a "Session expired — sign in again" banner sits over it, and sign-in happens in a dialog (`SignInPanel`, extracted from `login.tsx`), so unsaved input survives. A sign-out in another tab still signs this tab out.
- `RequireAuth` no longer renders "Please log in"; `index.tsx`'s own redirect is gone.

### #387 — errors
- `components/QueryState.tsx`: `ErrorWithRetry`, `QueryView` (loading / error+Retry / data) and `StaleMarker` ("Last updated … · refresh failing"); `useTrustTaskQuery` now exposes `updatedAt`.
- Dashboard, DID list (no more "No DIDs yet" under an error), ACL list + invites (no longer swallowed into "no invites"), settings (config + identity generations no longer `.catch(() => [])`), domains, servers, passkeys, service overview all show failures with Retry; polled panels (service overview, servers, ACL, owner dashboard) carry the stale marker.
- DID detail: `did/info` notFound/permissionDenied → "DID not found" page with no destructive actions.
- `lib/errors.ts` maps rejection codes (`permissionDenied`, `notFound`, `unavailable`, `internalError`, `conflict`, `stepUpRequired`, `permissionDenied`+`step_up_required`, …), `NotAllowedError`/`AbortError`, fetch failures and `checkReply` refusals to plain messages, keeping the server's detail in brackets.

### #388 — document editing
- Edit is shown only when `isWalletTaskRelayAvailable()`; otherwise the card explains that updates must be signed by the DID's agent and uploaded as `did.jsonl`. "Copy to Upload" (which discarded the edit) is removed; the upload card's button is now "Load current did.jsonl into this box".
- Parameters card is read-only with **Copy parameters JSON**.

### #389 — owners
- Access nav item is `adminOnly`, and the page has a role gate.
- Owner dashboard renders per-domain cards (DIDs / resolves / updates) from their own DID list (the previously-unused fetch).

### #391 — web-only
- Decision applied: removed `android`/`ios` scripts, the `app.json` native blocks (now `"platforms": ["web"]`), `App.tsx` and the adaptive icon; `userInterfaceStyle: "dark"` and a dark splash background. No light theme (optional; skipped).
- Under 700px the nav collapses into a Menu button (links, domain switcher, Sign out); the DID list renders cards (`components/DidCards.tsx`) instead of the sideways table.

### #392 — sign-in copy
- One verb, "Sign in"/"Sign out", everywhere. Wallet section first, with the service-DID row moved inside it and a concrete hint; legacy section in plain language with a "What is this?" disclosure holding the protocol detail.
- `NotAllowedError`/`AbortError` → "Passkey prompt was cancelled or timed out."
- Wallet code: "Approve the sign-in in your wallet" (the page cannot tell a phone from the same-device plugin), and a live countdown plus a note that a backgrounded tab re-shows the code.
- Enrol page: claim-code field has a hint, auto-formats to `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` (Crockford, matching `generate_claim_code`), submits on Enter; a missing token shows "Open your enrolment link", not "Enrollment Failed".
- Step-up: the in-place ceremony that exists server-side (`auth/step-up/start` → wallet-signed `approve-response`, incl. the `webauthn` gate) is already wired for wallet sessions via `withStepUp`; the decision must be signed by the subject, which a passkey-only console cannot do, and a passkey session is `aal2` from login with no lapse (`acr_expires_at` is never set). So there is no "within N minutes" window to quote; the remaining case (a wallet without step-up support) now gets precise guidance (`STEP_UP_GUIDANCE`).
- (The flow-visualization checkbox was already removed by #445.)

### #393 — forms and missing tasks
- `lib/validation.ts` mirrors the server: `didPathError` (`validate_custom_path`, reserved first segments), `domainNameError` (`normalize_domain_name`: lowercase LDH host, optional port and path prefix, no IPs/scheme/whitespace), `aclSubjectError` (DID syntax or agent name), `quotaError`.
- New DID: inline path error; Create disabled while invalid/taken/checking/error; success toast with next steps. "Create root DID for <domain>" uses the switcher's (or default) domain and explains itself in a dialog.
- ACL add/edit: inline DID and numeric errors, scope errors inline, one-line role descriptions (`ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS`). Domain create: inline hostname validation, rewritten hint.
- `components/Term.tsx` glossary disclosure ("?") used for witness, watcher, portable, pre-rotation, TTL, alsoKnownAs, step-up passkeys, domain scope.
- "control plane" instead of "the daemon"; `did-hosting-server` instead of "webvh-server"; DIDComm/audit jargon rewritten.
- New UI for existing tasks: Suspend/Resume (`did/set-state/0.1`) in the DID danger zone; statistics detail picker (`stats/set-resolution/0.1`, 5-minute admin-only); domain label edit (`domain/update/0.1`). Type URIs added to the `T` table via generated `TYPE_URI`s.

Closes #385
Closes #386
Closes #387
Closes #388
Closes #389
Closes #391
Closes #392
Closes #393

## Tests
`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm test` (352 tests) and `expo export --platform web` pass locally. New tests:
- `components/__tests__/feedback.test.tsx` — dialog labels, focus on Cancel, type-to-confirm, multiple choices, queueing, toasts.
- `components/acl/__tests__/remove-entry.test.tsx` — the three-way removal, typed confirmation, per-DID progress, partial failure keeps the entry and retries only the rest.
- `components/__tests__/auth-gate.test.tsx` — splash, redirect with `?next=`, public pages, expiry keeps the screen's unsaved input and signs in in place.
- `components/__tests__/did-actions.test.tsx` — suspend/resume, delete behind typed name, failures as toasts not `alert()`, edit hidden without relay, read-only parameters copy, `QueryView` retry, Access hidden for owners.
- `lib/__tests__/ux-helpers.test.ts` — guard decision, `safeNextPath`, path/domain/ACL validators, error mapping, claim-code formatting.
- Updated login/enrol, DID-list and step-up message tests.

## Notes / deferred
- #394 (list paging) is deliberately not here; it lands with the server-side `did/list` filters.
- Light theme not added (optional per the decision); the app now declares dark.
- `stats/set-resolution` has no read of the current setting,

author: k2b-cloud-agents[bot]
body:
Server half of the page label (concept gustav-ui-neu v12, section 3n). The UI half is the follow-up PR on `feat/code-page-labeling`.

## What changes

- **Pill in the first paint, per viewer:** `codeRequestVersion` reads the owner's kind and, for a person, the display name in the same statement it already ran. Hosting turns that into a `CodePageLabel`: members see the person (F26) or the app by name, a resource by its type only; visitors without an account, guests and workload credentials get `anonymous`. The statement count per page request stays the same (pinned with `sql-meter` in the integration test).
- **F26:** a new, narrow visibility in `access.ts` (`isCodePageMember`, `codePageOwnerPersonName`). `readCodeOwner` is unchanged and still names a person only to that person everywhere else.
- **Opaque version value** (`codePageVersionValue`, like `codeCsrf`, keyed by the app secret) so the card can tell that a newer version runs.
- **One admission for the page and its label** (`page-admission.ts`); the page's behavior is unchanged.
- **`POST /api/code/pages/provenance`:** the card's facts per viewer (visitor, member, reader). Pages the caller may not open answer like missing ones (404); a caller budget applies before anything is read; a stale version value answers 409 `code_page_changed` after rights are checked.
- **`POST /api/code/pages/report`:** members only (F28). One open report per person and page, an idempotency key, 10 reports per person and hour. The report and its notice outbox commit together.
- **Notifications:** admins (resolved through `listApprovalAdminRecipients`) get "page reported" with links to the page and to Administration › Code; the reporting person hears back when an admin resolves it.
- **Administration › Code:** a small, separate `CodePageReports` component with "Resolved" and "Pause" at the automation, and open reports count into the sidebar hint (`preloadAdminCodeApprovals`).
- **Retention:** open until resolved, then 30 days like the automation's runs.
- **Docs:** `code-authoring/references/pages.md`, operations page "Code administration" (admins get a new notification), `platform/code-sdk.md`.

## Overlap

Lane H rebuilds the admin page at the same time (`feat/gustav-code-admin`). The report display is its own component with a minimal hook in `view.tsx` and `page.tsx`, so it moves over as one piece.

## Parity (Bauplan 9, server-owned parts)

- [x] "Automation öffnen" only for viewers who may see the automation: `viewer: "reader"` from `codePermission` (test `page-provenance.test.ts`).
- [x] The card's facts follow the 3n table per viewer: visitor gets nothing, member gets the owner, reader also gets the automation, the switch-on date and the approver (unit and integration tests).
- [x] Reports reach the admins and come back to the reporter (integration test `page-reports.integration.test.ts`, runs in CI).
- The visible rows (pill, card, dialog) are in the UI PR.

## Checks

- Locally green: typecheck for core and cloud; 80/80 rules without typecheck; Biome on changed files (exit 0); `git diff --check`; `check:docs`.
- Single test files: `hosting`, `page.render`, `page-provenance`, `access-owner`, `admin-status`, `notifications`, `CodePageReports.render`, the mandatory capability and contract files.
- The integration tests (`page-reports.integration.test.ts` and other files using `codeRequestVersion`) run in CI only.
- Reviewed by Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, high). Its findings on status codes, budget order and a report race are fixed. One remaining edge case is described in the UI PR.

body: The 911 line no longer depends on a text-to-speech fetch at the moment of the emergency, and agent audio cannot follow it. What changed: At startup the bridge synthesizes the urgent line and the wrap-up line once each and keeps the pcm_16000 bytes. `speakFixed` plays from that cache. A live fetch happens only when the cache has nothing for that line, and it logs `[bridge] WARN`. When `onTranscript` returns the urgent line, `holding` stays true for the rest of the call, so later agent audio is dropped. `finish_call` still hangs up. Files: `facetime-bridge/elevenlabs.mjs`, `facetime-bridge/elevenlabs_session.mjs`, `facetime-bridge/test_elevenlabs_session.mjs` How I checked it: - `MAC_DRY_RUN=1 VISION_FAKE=fixtures make test` is green: pytest 90 passed, 1 skipped; agent node tests 21 passed; bridge node tests 13 passed (the previous 11 plus the two new 911 cases) - Missing `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` still exits from both `elevenlabs.mjs` and `VOICE=elevenlabs node start.mjs` with `Put ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID in .env.local` - `bridge.mjs` and `agent/` are untouched Ponytail check: - New files: 0 - New dependencies: none - New abstractions/config: `speakFixed`'s optional ctx, so the bridge tests can play a warm cache without booting sox - Skipped / not checked: a live ElevenLabs synthesis and a FaceTime call. author: attacktive-gremlin[bot]
body:
## Summary
- Add Settings → Weather → Refresh on unlock, disabled by default and independent of the automatic refresh interval and appearance presets.
- Observe system USER_PRESENT events while the opt-in is enabled and the app process is alive; queue unique, network-constrained WorkManager requests.
- Force the shared weather refresh path with a five-minute process-local cooldown, preserving simulator suppression, retained weather, and existing request-order guards.
- Add English, Italian, and Korean setting text, focused JVM coverage, and the lifecycle/validation contract in docs/unlock-weather-refresh.md.

Closes #437.

## Validation
- User reports ordinary local Android instrumentation passed. Existing local connected-test XML (`app/build/outputs/androidTest-results/connected/debug/TEST-Pixel(AVD) - 17.xml`) records 272 tests, zero failures, errors, or skips. The suite was not rerun during this validation.
- Focused JVM command passed: `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*UnlockRefreshControllerTest' --tests '*UnlockRefreshSettingsTest' --tests '*DeviceUnlockReceiverTest' --tests '*UnlockWeatherRefresherTest' --console=plain` — 28 tests, zero failures/errors/skips.
- Runtime inspection found the app's USER_PRESENT receiver registered. The user subsequently reported the feature appears to work after the requested manual acceptance check. This is user-observed acceptance, not an independently captured unlock-to-fetch trace.

## Limitations
- Only observes unlocks while the Weatherd process is alive; Android/OEM restrictions may delay delivery or work.
- Five-minute cooldown resets after process death. Offline requests coalesce and wait for connectivity.
- Battery/data cost is disclosed in the setting but has not been measured.

body:
Phase 4 of v1.2 and the version bump to 1.2.0 (the release is tagged after this merges).

**Sessions** — Save / Save as / Open a `.ripper` file (Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S / Ctrl+O) holding the audio (FLAC 24-bit, + stems), chops, trims, pads, patterns, effects and settings. Recent sessions on the Library page, autosave every minute, saved sessions' tracks never expire (only unsaved scratch tracks keep the 24 h cleanup). Versioned state with migrations; v1 (bare pad program) sessions open.

**Audio settings** — output device (switches live), buffer size (new audio context, no restart), the reported latency, and *Measure pad latency*.

**Export the beat** — beat WAV, pattern/song MIDI (one note per pad from C1, velocity + swing), **per-pad stems** (one WAV per used pad, same length from bar 1, optional effects / master bus) and **chops in original position** (one WAV per chop, silence elsewhere, same length; selection or whole song). Save, → folder, or one multi-file drag. Numbered names `{track}_{bpm}bpm_{key}_{pad##|slice##}_{name}.wav`. Kits add patterns MIDI, the beat, pad stems and chops in place (subfolders).

**Polish** — `?` shortcut sheet, tooltips on every control, skippable first-run tour, Pro gates (patterns C–H, resample, effects, vintage, time-stretch / key-shift, batch and kit export).

**Docs** — README, docs/formats.md, LICENSES.md (ASIO not included: GPLv3 or a Steinberg-countersigned agreement), release notes.

Tests: per-pad stems sum to the full beat; chops in place sum to the original range; every file the same length from sample 0; MIDI + multi-file drag; session save/open round-trips every setting; autosave; an older-format session opens; latency reported + measured; buffer/device switch without restart; tour, shortcuts, tooltips, free-plan gates.

author: xiaxiazhu
body:
## 背景

Issue #2 的 11-14 复测确认：napi 上 glm-5.3-flash 丢图的根因在 sglang-proxy 的 GLM 方言（[sglang-proxy#6](https://github.com/shuzuan-org/sglang-proxy/issues/6)），不在 sub2api 的 Anthropic 透传路径。sglang-proxy 已完成止血（见「线上现状」）。

但同一份报告里指出 sub2api 自己还有一个真 bug：**Gemini 路由把 `tool_result` 里的图片拼成 Markdown 文本**，模型收到的是一长串 base64 字符而不是图片，还白占几万 token。PR #5 修的就是这个位置，但改法不对，而且只改了 antigravity 一条路径。

本 PR 把两条 Gemini 转换路径的 `tool_result` 图片都改成官方形状：`functionResponse.parts[].inlineData`。

## 改动

**`internal/pkg/antigravity/`**
- `GeminiFunctionResponse` 新增 `Parts []GeminiFunctionResponsePart`
- `parseToolResultContent` 返回值 `string` → `toolResultContent{Text, Images}`
- `buildParts` 把图片放进 `functionResponse.parts[].inlineData`
- 文本里留 `[image attached: <mime>]` 占位，让模型知道这段 tool_result 带图

**`internal/service/gemini_messages_compat_service.go`**
- 同一问题的第二份实现（Claude → Gemini `generateContent` 兼容层）
- `extractClaudeContentText` → `extractClaudeToolResultContent`，返回 `(text, parts)`

## 为什么是 `functionResponse.parts` 而不是别的形状

```
PR #5:  "![image](data:image/png;base64,iVBOR…)"        ← Gemini 收到文本
本 PR:  functionResponse.parts = [{inlineData:{…}}]      ← Gemini 收到图
```

按 `google.golang.org/genai` 的定义，`FunctionResponse.Parts []*FunctionResponsePart`，每个 part 是 `{inlineData: {mimeType, data}}` 或 `{fileData: …}` —— 图片语义上属于**这次工具调用**，不是相邻的另一条内容。首个 commit 曾做成紧随其后的顶层 `inlineData` part，第二个 commit 改成官方形状。

同文件顶层 `image` block 早就正确转成了 `inlineData`（`request_transformer.go:466-474`），不变。

## 测试

| 测试 | 覆盖 |
|---|---|
| `TestParseToolResultContent_MixedTextAndImage` | 文本顺序保留 + 图片单独返回 |
| `TestParseToolResultContent_ImageOnly` | 纯图 tool_result |
| `TestBuildParts_ToolResultImageBecomesInlineData` | 序列化后是 `functionResponse.parts[].inlineData`，且无 `![image]` 残留 |
| `TestConvertClaudeMessagesToGemini_ToolResultImage` | compat 层同一路径 |

```
go test ./internal/pkg/antigravity/ ./internal/service/   ✅
go build ./...                                            ✅
```

## 线上现状（2026-11-15 实测）

用 probe@metask-ai.com 的 key 对 `glm-5.3-flash` 跑高熵探针（480×240，左绿右橙，中央 `K9MQ7X`，每形态 3 次）：

```
A   anth user image block          HTTP 400  image input is not supported by the text-only SGLang route
B1  anth tool_result [image]       HTTP 400  同上
B2  anth tool_result [text,image]  HTTP 400  同上
D   oai user image_url             HTTP 400  同上
```

`GET /v1/models` 对 `glm-5.3-flash` 现在报 `image_input=false, pdf_input=false`。止血到位：客户端拿到明确错误，而不是静默空结果。

## 一条值得记住的排查教训

**验证多模态透传不能用颜色提问。** 模型对「什么颜色」有强先验，10-05 那次用左红右蓝图复测得到 `red, blue` 就判定「A 已修复」，而 11-14 用一张根本没送达的绿/橙图重测，模型同样答 `red, blue`。判据必须用高熵信号（随机字母串 + 不常见配色），并重复多次。

（完整复盘文档在本地 `docs/issue-2-image-passthrough-analysis.md`，该目录按仓库惯例 gitignore，未入本 PR。）

## 遗留

- GLM 方言真正支持多模态投递：sglang-proxy#6 仍未做，依赖上游多模态权重
- kimi / minimax_m3 方言是否也是纯文本渲染 → 同样的能力虚报，未排查
- 同一把 key 下 8 个模型名（含 `totally-unknown-model-xyz`）全部回同一身份，`model_mapping` 的别名能力声明问题未跟进

author: devluca999
body:
**Block:** follow-on to D2 (real world files) · **Milestone:** M2 · **Flag:** none (new layers appear in the layer panel)

⚠️ **Contract change (rule 2):** CONTRACTS.md §1 gains optional layers (the views below and `passable.u8`). Nothing renamed or removed. Needs every owner's approval.

### Why
An 8 m cell's slope averages away what stops a person on foot. On our Gale slice (from the 1 m HiRISE terrain):
- 35% of the cells that look walkable at 8 m hide a stretch steeper than 25° at 2 m scale;
- half of all cells have a ≥ 0.5 m jump between neighbouring 1 m points;
- boxwork ridge/hollow relief inside a cell: median 0.8 m, 90th percentile 1.7 m.
JETT3 (RESEARCH.md) had 1 m maps and still hit impassable drop-offs. Passability belongs to the **crossing between two cells**, not to a cell.

### What's in it
`data/pipeline/terrain_1m.py` → `data/worlds/gale/`:

| View | Shows | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `terrain` | 1 m hillshade at 8 m | context |
| `fine_steep` | % of cell steeper than the limit at 2 m scale | hidden steepness |
| `dropoff` | largest 1 m height jump (m) | ledges (JETT3) |
| `crevice` | deepest trough narrower than ~5 m (m) | fractures, sand-filled troughs |
| `landform` | flat / slope / ridge / hollow | boxwork structure (ridge vs hollow drill sites) |
| `open_dirs` | passable neighbours, 0–8 | how open the ground is |
| `reach` | reachable from base | islands you can't get to |
| `chokepoint` | how much of the map funnels through here (log 0–1) | the gaps routes must use |
| `unsure` | share of crossings near a limit | where the scout helicopter should look (feeds #83 step 2) |

`passable.u8`: bit k = you can step to neighbour k (same order as `app/src/plan.js` `NB`). Checked along the 1 m profile between cell centres in three lanes (centre, ±2 m). Blocked by:
- a **ledge**: height change over 1 m or 2 m above the suited step limit plus what the slope limit allows over that length. Step limit **0.3 m: NASA ICES-2025-294** recommended maximum step height for a suited crew member (xEMU);
- a **steep run**: slope over `max_slope_deg` **up, down or across** (Artemis xEVA spec says "up/down/across") for ≥ 3 m (estimate, knob).

Result on Gale: 82% of crossings passable, 90% of cells reachable from base (8 m rule: 85% "walkable", but 307 of those cells are actually cut off and ~4,500 "too steep" cells have a walkable lane). **The current planned route crosses 7 blocked crossings.**

### Not in this PR
Nothing reads `passable.u8` yet. Next PR: `cost_to_go` (pipeline) and the app planner use crossings instead of cell slope, together with the energy-model fix from #83 (gravity factor, sand), so `cost_to_go` changes once and gets reviewed once.

Also worth a team decision: our `max_slope_deg` is 25°; NASA's Artemis xEVA suit capability is slopes **up to 20°**.

### Tested
`pytest` (33 passed; new `tests/test_terrain_1m.py`: flat ground open, a wall cuts the map, crossings symmetric, a 0.25 m step passes and a 1.5 m ledge blocks), `ruff`, `check_world.py`, hygiene, `npm test` (31 pass), `npm run build`; world 3.7 MB (< 5 MB). Headless Chrome `?world=gale`: all nine views in the layer panel with sources, no console errors. **A real-phone check is still to do.**

author: wtadler
body:
## What

`getMgaSession` reads a session file whose body is blank after trimming (a bare line break, an empty body, whitespace) as an empty file, as it already reads a `null` body. A body that is neither JSON nor blank still fails closed.

## Why

MGA serves the 2027 regular session's `legislation.json` with status 200, a JSON content type, and a body of one CRLF, regenerated every few minutes, while the session has no prefiled bills. `JSON.parse` rejects a blank string, so every hourly pass of that session failed closed with "the session file isn't JSON" and the pass alert fired for about 40 hours. The other sessions kept syncing, since one session's failure doesn't stop the rest.

## Evidence

- Red: `central/test/providers/mga/client.test.ts`, four blank-body cases rejected with `MGA 2027RS: the session file isn't JSON`; the null, empty-list, and HTML cases passed before and after as the oracle.
- Green: full central suite 173 files, 3,688 tests; `tsc --noEmit` and lint clean.
- Live: `curl -i https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2027RS/misc/billsmasterlist/legislation.json` answers 200, `application/json`, `content-length: 2`, body `0d0a`.

## Notes

No migration. The central that owns the Maryland sessions stops alerting on its next pass after deploy.

author: bool-
body:
Lets somebody other than the requester pay for a build.

## What changes for users

- **Requests are always filed.** A requester with no build credentials is no longer refused at `/request new`. Their approval card says **Paid by: Nobody yet - this needs a sponsor** and carries a **Sponsor** button.
- **Sponsor.** Anyone with a stored credential clicks it to pay from their own environment. That includes the requester, after running `/credentials set`. The same button reads **Withdraw sponsorship** for the current sponsor.
- **Approve** is refused while nobody can pay, and the sponsor cannot approve the build they pay for (unless `allowSelfApproval`).
- **Each build is sponsored once.** A retry, a revision, or an expired request put back loses its sponsor. The requester pays if they were the payer and still can; otherwise the new card asks for a sponsor again.
- The Building card shows who is paying.

## How

- At dispatch the payer is `sponsor ?? requester`. That environment name is what the approval MAC already signs, so the workflow and `verify_approval.py` are unchanged.
- Builder migration `0007_sponsors.sql`: `sponsor_id`, `needs_sponsor`, and the approval card's content (sanitised), so a Sponsor click can redraw the card.
- `canPay` in `payer.ts`. `setSponsor` / `markNeedsSponsor` are compare-and-set on the version, with a fresh card nonce in the same statement.
- With `requireOwnCredentials: false` the server pays, there is nothing to sponsor, and the Sponsor action refuses.

## Review

An independent adversarial review found no way to charge somebody who never clicked Sponsor, and no path to `ai-agent` with `requireOwnCredentials` on. It did find these, all fixed in the second commit:
- Sponsor/Withdraw clicks reset the expiry clock.
- A requester who stored a credential after filing could be charged by an approval.
- A retry of a sponsored build re-dispatched onto the requester.
- A sponsor whose credential vanished blocked the request.
- A dispatch pass could spend a stale snapshot.
- A missing test pin on clearing the sponsor for revisions, now caught by mutation.

Remaining low-severity items are in `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`.

## Testing

- `npm run check`: 1213 pass, 0 fail; lint unchanged (4 pre-existing).
- New `sponsor.test.ts` (22 cases): consent, withdraw, superseded cards, Approve rules, payer and MAC at dispatch, credential loss, each re-arm path, the expiry clock, the stale dispatch pass, and the switch off.
- The front-door tests that pinned "refused without credentials" are rewritten to the new rule.

## Operator action required

1. **Behaviour change:** requesters without credentials are now filed (with a Sponsor button) instead of refused, so cards that need a sponsor may appear in request channels.
2. Builder migration `0007_sponsors.sql` runs at boot. Back up the database first as usual.
3. No new permission, secret, environment variable, intent or dependency. Ships as 2.2.0 after a release PR.

author: josephwylie
body:
## Why
Ferrite's everyday journeys must work completely and feel polished, including recovery. Unit 03 (panel-tools-001 and the concurrent-edit finding): a failed file save was silent, and closing a Files tab dropped the edited buffer; a late save from an old buffer could overwrite an external edit. Audit: `docs/audits/2026-11-13-t3-parity/remediation.md` (Unit 03).

## What changed
- New `SaveState` machine (`Idle | Saving(revision) | Saved | Failed | Conflict`) in `tools/save.rs`; the editor tracks an edit revision and the fingerprint of the file as last read.
- Writes run off the UI thread, replace the file atomically, and are refused if the disk differs from what the buffer was read from. A result applies only to the write in flight, so a late success cannot mark newer edits saved.
- Failed shows the error with Retry and Discard under the lines. Conflict shows "This file changed on disk" with Reload and Overwrite.
- Closing a dirty tab writes first and closes on success; on failure or conflict the tab stays with its bar.
- Fix round after review: saving follows a symlink (stages beside and renames over the real file, so `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` stays a link and the target gets the text); if no staging file can be created (writable file in a read-only directory) the file is written in place, as on main; staging names are unique per write; the status bar's buttons are a typed `BarAction` enum (no fallback can discard); a failed Reload says "Could not reload" and offers Reload/Overwrite instead of Discard; unused `Editor` re-export gated `#[cfg(test)]`.
- Tests now click the rendered editor and type through the production key table (`bind_production_keys`, `simulate_input`, Enter), and the late-write test dispatches cmd-s without waiting so the write is genuinely in flight.

## Evidence
Headless real app (`fv`), clicking the editor and typing with real keys, scratch repo only. Before = origin/main, after = this branch.

Refused write (before: read-only file; after: read-only directory, since this branch replaces the file atomically).
Before: no error shown, edit looks fine, file on disk unchanged; clicking the tab's x then silently drops the edit.
![before refused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/josephwylie/ferrite/evidence/repair-u03-file-save/before-refused.png)
![before close drops it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/josephwylie/ferrite/evidence/repair-u03-file-save/before-close.png)
After: "Could not save: Permission denied" with Retry and Discard; closing keeps the tab; after restoring access, Retry writes the same text.
![after refused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/josephwylie/ferrite/evidence/repair-u03-file-save/after-refused.png)
![after close keeps tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/josephwylie/ferrite/evidence/repair-u03-file-save/after-close-keeps.png)

Changed on disk. Before: an agent's edit made after opening was overwritten by the buffer's save (file ended as the buffer text only).
![before external](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/josephwylie/ferrite/evidence/repair-u03-file-save/before-external.png)
After: the agent's text stays on disk and the bar offers Reload or Overwrite.
![after changed on disk](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/josephwylie/ferrite/evidence/repair-u03-file-save/after-changed-on-disk.png)

Save through a symlink (after the fix round): `linked.rs -> real.rs` opened and edited in the Files editor, cmd-s; afterwards `linked.rs` is still a symlink and `real.rs` holds the new first line.
![after symlink saved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/josephwylie/ferrite/evidence/repair-u03-file-save/after-symlink-saved.png)

Tests: `cargo nextest run -p ferrite-cockpit -E 'test(/cockpit::tests::files::/) | test(cockpit::tests::link_clicks)'` -> 32 passed (before the fix round). Fix round: `cargo nextest run -p ferrite-cockpit -E 'test(/cockpit::tests::files::/) | test(cockpit::tests::link_clicks) | test(key_ownership) | test(/tools::save::/)'` -> 42 passed (new: symlink, read-only directory, read-only file, failed reload); `cargo check -p ferrite-cockpit` -> only the 2 pre-existing dead-code warnings.

## Limits
- No "Save elsewhere"; conflict check is read-then-write, not a lock. Clean buffers are not refreshed on external change.
- Saving/Saved indicator motion and CEF/IME input are not exercised. The write-refusal test hook (`refuse_writes`) injects the failure in unit tests; the app shots use filesystem permissions.


- Not done, left as polish: pending-close indicator, lingering "Saved" label. The symlink and read-only-directory fallback tests are unix-only.

author: buildthehomelab
body:
## Why

Some profession recipes of the original game are still in the Forever client, and nothing says who teaches them: no trainer, quest or obtainable item on the realm, no live recording, and the players' site only says "trainer" or "quest". The realm's own data names no quest for any of them. The original game's database does name the teacher.

## What this adds

A new source, asked last and only about profession recipes nobody can learn: cmangos' [classic-db](https://github.com/cmangos/classic-db) (GPL-3.0), the content database of the 1.12 game.

- **`tools/classicdb_pack.py`** makes a pack (about 150 kB) from the project's full dump: trainer lines, quests whose turn-in shows or casts a spell, and spells a line of a creature's conversation casts. The dump is only read as text.
- **Imports page**: send the `.cdbpack`, or *Read the pack again* after an analysis. The tracker never downloads the database.
- **The card**:
  - a trainer line becomes a `trainer_spell` row at the trainer the server has for that creature, with Classic's cost, skill and level;
  - a quest of the server that casts nothing at its turn-in gets the spell Classic cast (`quest_template.RewardSpell`). It is a fill: a quest that already casts a spell is left alone and counted;
  - a recipe Classic teaches through a line of a creature's conversation needs a script, not a row: counted, never written.
- Classic names the spell that teaches (10843 teaches Heavy Mageweave Bandage, 10841); the server's own learn effects say which recipe that is.
- The source is the last in `[sources] trust`.

## What it finds

On the client tables of build 70938, for the 538 profession recipes that were incomplete:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Trainer lines | 7: Goldthorn Tea (Henry Stern), Heavy Mageweave, Runecloth and Heavy Runecloth Bandage (both Triage doctors) |
| Quests to fill | 2: Badlands Reagent Run II, both sides (Restorative Potion) |
| Taught in a conversation | 18: Gordok Ogre Suit (2), Dimensional Ripper, Ultrasafe Transporter, Smelt Dark Iron, 13 Naxxramas frost resistance recipes |
| Classic names nobody | 515 (new in Forever, or learned from an item) |

Whether the rows are written depends on the server: a creature that is no trainer there is left out and counted.

## Tests

`python -m unittest discover -s tools/tests`: 484 tests pass (13 new: the pack tool on a small dump, the evidence). PHP tests pass (10 new checks).

## Summary

Fixes for what the 2026-11-14 live checks and the DeepSeek review of PR 99 turned up. One commit per fix, each with a test that failed first.

- **The eval's attribution check had two gaps** (DeepSeek on PR 99):
  - a sentence saying "medians" was never checked;
  - "the median of its peers" was read as the company's own median, so correct prose could fail.

  Both are read now. A new test also checks that the rubric finds every comparison `research_derived` writes, so rewording a formula can't silently switch the check off.
- **The R&D lens index listed AMZN.** Amazon tags no R&D (checked against SEC), and the lens page already leaves it out. A `LensSpec` now names the companies that never tag its metric, and the index leaves them out.
- **Lens points capped citations at four.** The lens reused the analyst view's four-chip limit, so a point quoting five facts lost a chip, and the lens prompt asked for "1–3 ids".
  - `resolve_points` now takes the limit as a parameter; the analyst view keeps 4, and the lens keeps every fact a point quotes. It already drops cited facts the point doesn't quote.
  - The prompt now asks for the id of every fact quoted.
- **DIS insider card read "0.00% of market value".** A share that rounds to zero at two decimals now reads "<0.01%".
- **Yahoo's `info` sometimes comes back cut short.** A KO report showed dashes for P/S, EV/EBITDA and gross margin until it was regenerated.
  - Price-to-sales marks it: every company with revenue has one, banks and loss-makers included. So a market cap without a P/S means the answer was cut short.
  - `yahoo_info.read_info` then reads `info` once more and fills the gaps. Fields the first answer had keep its values.
  - It's a new module so `fundamentals.py` (541 lines) doesn't grow.
- **Docs:** `tasks/todo.md` catches up with everything merged through #106, including the demo tickers rebuilt at version 8 (done before this PR) and the call-log item fixed by #105. Changelog and test counts updated.
- **No `REPORT_VERSION` bump.** A report from a healthy Yahoo is unchanged; the retry changes only a cut-short answer.

## Test Plan

- [x] New tests, each failing first:
  - rubric: plural medians; peers named after the median; every `research_derived` comparison found;
  - lens: index without AMZN; five quoted facts keep five chips; prompt wording;
  - insider: "<0.01%";
  - Yahoo: a partial `info` is read again; a second partial keeps the first's fields; a complete one is read once (a bank without gross margin isn't retried); the retry fills only the gaps.
- [x] `uv run ruff check app tests` clean. Touched backend suites pass: evals, lens, thesis, fundamentals. 1113 tests collected; CI runs the full suite with Postgres.
- [x] Frontend: `vitest` 680 passed, `tsc -b` and ESLint clean.
- [x] Live golden eval on this branch, covering the rubric change and the Yahoo retry ([run 43670716260](https://github.com/xuanbai01/Market-Analysis-Agent/actions/runs/43670716260)): **7 passed**, factuality 1.000 on all seven (AAPL, NVDA, RIVN, JPM, KO, XOM, DIS), no attribution errors.
- [ ] After deploy:
  - `/lens` shows six tickers on the R&D card;
  - DIS insider card reads "<0.01%";
  - Fly logs show a `yahoo info … reading it again` line whenever the retry fires.

## DeepSeek review (on 9a2dd8c)

| # | Point | Response |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No `REPORT_VERSION` bump, so a report cached with dashes is served unchanged | Not bumped, on purpose. A bump would rebuild every cached report for a failure seen once. The six demo reports all have a P/S (checked on the live API), the KO case from 11-13 has been rebuilt since, and any cached report expires after 7 days (`RESEARCH_CACHE_MAX_AGE_HOURS=168`) or on Regenerate |
| 2 | The live eval box was unchecked | It had been started with the PR; it passed 7 of 7 at factuality 1.000 (above) |
| 3 | A cut-short answer that also lost the market cap isn't retried | Kept. An answer without a market cap is usually a fund (SPY), and retrying those would cost every such build a second read. One that lost the market cap too is broken past what this retry is for |

author: chadgian
body:
## Issue
Torn Hunting sessions (commonly log type 6020) expose a cash `cost` and `income` in the same record. v0.5.11 handled `cost` but not `income`, making profitable hunts appear as losses.

## Fixes
- Hunting: classify both `cost` and `income` as independent exact-dollar movements, with net result income minus cost. Explicit zero income is a valid outcome, not an error; unrelated skill, session type, and "Easter egg hunt" events are excluded.
- Flag missing or invalid hunting `cost` or `income` as partially unclassified **even when the other cash component was recorded**. Data Quality now explains that parts of an event can be recognized without implying complete financial classification.
- Generalized cash handling: a strict, currency-aware parser recognizes explicit fields such as `money_received`, `money_spent`, `cash_gained`, `cash_paid` for **unrecognized activity titles**. One inflow and one outflow per source log at most, with aliases deduplicated and safe nested objects supported. Generic `cost`, `income`, `balance`, `amount`, `value`, points and credits are **not guessed as dollars**.
- Domain-specific rules for cash vs capital transfers, racing points, mission credits, bank interest/principal, property and item purchases always run first. Generalized parser cannot override specialized logic.
- Broaden selected `/torn/logtypes` discovery with directional payment titles and explicit financial-category descriptors while limiting known high-volume noncash activity.
- Add deterministic `:in`/`:out` component IDs to log resync replacement so historical generic rows cannot double count.
- Upgrade `ACCOUNTING_VERSION` to `0.5.12`; historical hunting proceeds and newly supported log types require a **Full Resync**. No changes to API-key permissions or automatic sync timing.

## Coverage safeguards
The Torn API has over 1,000 log types, without a universal schema for each payload; the new rule engine is broader but not a promise of exhaustive account-lifetime financial history. The trusted hunting `{cost,income}` example is documented by another published Torn cash-flow userscript, not independently verified against an authenticated TCFA user's account.

## Tests
16 new simulated hunting/general cash tests plus existing tests. GitHub Actions validates `npm test` and `npm run check`.

## Release
Review only. **Do not merge or deploy without approval.** Recommend backing up data and Full Resync after installation; pre-existing hunting payouts cannot be recovered from cost-only stored rows.

author: misterbisson
body:
The window's **Drain** sat beside a chart of every host this Mac's gateway sends work to, but it drained only this Mac's own models. The gateway kept taking new requests from clients and sending them to peers, so a drained Mac never got idle, and **Stop** still cut off whatever was running on peers.

Now Drain drains the gateway too:

- The gateway finishes the requests clients already sent it, waiting or running, on any host, and answers new ones `503` with `error.code` `draining` and a `Retry-After` of 30 seconds. A retry that carries the `Idempotency-Key` of a request it already has still gets that request's answer.
- Requests other devices' gateways send this Mac's hosts aren't affected by the gateway's drain. The hosts' own Draining state still governs those, as before.
- The headline shows Draining, and how many client requests are left, until the gateway and this Mac's models are both done. After that it shows Paused, drained, and Stop has nothing left to cut off.
- Pause stays local to this Mac's models: the gateway keeps sending clients' work to peers. Resume, or Stop, opens the gateway again.
- The scheduler's snapshot carries `draining` and `clientRequests`, the turned-away requests count toward the gateway's `unavailable` answers, and docs/running.md, design.md and clients.md describe all of this.

Tested:
- `swift test`, and `swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing`. New tests check that a draining gateway finishes what it has and turns new requests away; that it still answers keys it already has; that it leaves its hosts to peers' requests; that the gateway answers `503 draining` with `Retry-After`; and that a node's Drain drains the gateway but Pause doesn't, and that Stop resets it.
- `tools/ci/build-app.sh`, after regenerating the project, and `tools/ci/build-ipad.sh`, both clean. `tools/ci/check-public.sh` passes.

Not tested: draining by hand in the running app with peers in the mesh, so the headline's Draining-to-drained change hasn't been seen on screen.

author: lourencovp
body:
Sublayers, as asked ("We need to add sublayers to curva then"); spec `docs/specs/sublayers.md`, written from Rhino 8's `commands/layer.htm`. Stacked on #122 (Make2D).

**Rules (as Rhino):**
- A layer can sit under another layer, at any depth. Full names are joined with `::` (`Make2D::Hidden::Curves`).
- A layer shows only when all its parents are on, and it is locked when any of them is locked. A sublayer keeps its own setting, but can't be turned on or unlocked while a parent rules it; the panel greys its box.
- Any layer can be current. Making one current turns its parents on and unlocks them, and the current layer's parents can't be turned off or locked.
- Deleting a layer deletes its sublayers too. Nothing is deleted if any of them is current or has objects.
- Names must differ under the same parent. A layer can't be moved under itself or its own sublayers.

**Layers panel:**
- The tree is indented, with painted triangles to fold sublayers away. Whether a layer is folded is saved.
- Drag a layer's grip onto another layer to nest it, or onto the header to bring it to the top.
- New sublayer button. The layer menu adds New sublayer, Move up one parent, Select objects, and Select sublayer objects.

**Elsewhere:**
- The viewport's per-object cache now keys on the object's whole layer chain, so turning a parent off redraws its children's objects.
- Selection, printing and per-detail hiding follow parents.
- `.3dm` import builds the real tree from Rhino's parent ids, instead of flattening it to `A::B` names. Export writes the tree from full names, so older flat names still export as a tree.
- `ChangeLayer` takes a full name, or a plain name when only one layer has it.
- The assistant's layer list gives each layer's `full_name` and `parent`.
- Make2D puts its drawing under `Make2D` > `Visible`/`Hidden` > `Curves`/`Silhouettes`.

**Tests:**
- full names and lookup by name;
- parents turning their sublayers off or locking them;
- the current layer's parents staying on and unlocked;
- no loops, and unique names under a parent;
- deleting a tree;
- finding or making a layer by path;
- the `.3dm` round trip with a sublayer;
- Make2D's tree and its dashed hidden layer.

**Checked in the app:**
- Make2D on two boxes created the tree, shown nested.
- Folding `Hidden` hid its rows.
- Turning `Make2D` off greyed its sublayers' boxes and hid the whole drawing.

author: cdoughty08
body:
## What

A distinct list, row identities, a diff and a search now read a packed result **fused**, without unpacking it whole first. This follows #480's pattern and reuses `PageRooms`. Each worker unpacks the pages it reads into rooms reserved from the result budget.

- **Diff** (either or both results packed): Compare reads the first result in the second result's order through a small per-run LRU of unpacked pages (`RoomReader`, `LeftSlots`/`RightSlots`). The unified result is written on one thread, so each side's pages are unpacked ahead on the workers (`PageAhead`): two batches of rooms, taken only from spare budget, otherwise the writer unpacks them itself. `ResultDiffer.Local` counts the unpacks the first result's order would cost. Past four a page, that result is unpacked in place as before (refused: `TOO_LARGE`, same sentence).
- **Distinct**: built through the fused `PageSource`. The snapshot now keeps its result's pages, not their bytes (`KeptPages`). Later window reads and value searches go in row order through one `ReadRoom`, each page unpacked once. This also fixes a latent leak: the old snapshot held raw page arrays alive, uncharged, after the policy packed the result again. Pivot's Distinct Count was already fused by #480 (`FusedReadChecks.Spec` covers it).
- **Row identities**: every candidate pass and the probe read through rooms.
- **Search**: base order and near-order views are fused, two rooms a run. A sorted view (`ResultSearcher.Local` false) still unpacks first in `SqlService`. A direct call through a far view reads through the accessor, as before.
- Rooms now ask the system's memory load once for every `WorkCheckBytes` they take together.
- Refusals stay values with the existing sentences, pinned by a check.

### Still rehydrating, and why
- Search through a sorted view: its runs visit pages at random.
- A diff whose first result is read far from its pages' order: in place, the second result stays packed.
- #480's fallbacks: `PageSource.Rehydrate` (refused extract) and `RowAccess.Hold` (refused pivot hold).
- Transposed Copy/Save keep their rows' pages together (`BodiesTogether`). This is bounded, not a whole rehydrate.

The rehydrate path (`TryUnpackAll`/`SqlService.Unpack`) cannot be removed while these use it; it is now the exception.

## Numbers
`--page-compression-bench <GiB> orders --fused --whole`, 16 workers, median of 3, seconds; budget = most charged above the result. Full tables are in docs/page-compression-findings.md.

| 1 GiB | raw | rehydrate | fused | budget, rehydrate | budget, fused |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Distinct, low cardinality | 0.16 | 0.11 | 0.12 | 525 MiB | 4 MiB |
| Distinct, 3.7M values + value search | 2.53 | 2.47 | 2.83 | 639 MiB | 118 MiB |
| Row identities | 0.06 | 0.09 | 0.08 | 525 MiB | 4 MiB |
| Search | 0.12 | 0.20 | 0.15 | 525 MiB | 4 MiB |
| Diff, same order | 0.32 | 0.38 | 0.49 | 1,067 MiB | 35 MiB |
| Diff, shuffled (first result unpacked in place) | 0.67 | 0.76 | 0.84 | 1,060 MiB | 562 MiB |

| 4 GiB | raw | rehydrate | fused | budget, rehydrate | budget, fused |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Distinct, low cardinality | 0.19 | 0.41 | 0.42 | 2,108 MiB | 4 MiB |
| Distinct, high cardinality + value search | 13.86 | 17.76 | 15.87 | 2,563 MiB | 459 MiB |
| Row identities | 0.11 | 0.38 | 0.30 | 2,108 MiB | 4 MiB |
| Search | 0.49 | 0.71 | 0.62 | 2,108 MiB | 4 MiB |
| Diff, same order | 1.16 | 1.83 | 2.06 | 4,283 MiB | 89 MiB |
| Diff, shuffled | 2.99 | 3.50 | 3.97 | 4,248 MiB | 2,244 MiB |

Unpacked inputs: the same bench built on `main` gave raw times within noise of this branch at 1 GiB.

## Checks
- New offline suite **FusedWhole** (`FusedReadChecks.Whole.cs`). It compares packed against raw for:
  - diff: packed/packed, packed/raw and raw/packed; key and whole-row matching; in order, shuffled and interleaved; model plus the unified result's pages;
  - distinct over four columns, with and without views (windows, searches, ticks, Freeze, Digest);
  - identities (auto, column, row);
  - search (base order, filtered view, sorted view, and the service);
  - a partly packed pair.

  It also checks bounded unpack counts, the writer unpacking ahead, cancellation mid-operation (budget back, results stay packed), refused rooms with the exact sentences, the diff fallback refused, a write with no spare budget, the load check, and the snapshot holding no page bytes (in Store's isolated lane).
- Updated `PackingChecks`/`PackerChecks`: a base-order search no longer unpacks; a sorted-view search does. Updated `DiffChecks.Refusals` (cut-short budget, run raw) and the working-memory lint table.
- Mutation proofs: 15 of 16 caught. The miss: RowIdentity's per-pass reader not disposed. All rooms still go back when the operation ends, so there is nothing observable. Each review fix below also has a check, proven to fail with the fix reverted (6 of 6).
- `npm run check` passes. 3,823 offline .NET checks pass, also with `DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=4` (CI's runners).

## Review rounds
Six independent read-only rounds; the sixth found nothing significant. Fixed along the way:
- A fused reader now parses the array `ResultSetBuffer.Read` returns, so a page another operation unpacks in place mid-read is never read from a stale room (`RoomReader`, `PageAhead.Fill`).
- Distinct, identity and search refusals inside the operation answer the low-memory sentence when the machine is short of memory (`LowMemoryAware`), as their up-front refusals did.
- The unified diff writer gives its rooms unpacked ahead back once the budget reaches the eighth spare memory leaves free, or once the result is unpacked in place (`YieldAhead`). A batch that holds every page reserves one half, not two.
- The writer's pages-ahead list stayed in step with the reader only within a batch: a diff read alternately from two pages stopped reading ahead after the first batch. It now looks back over the whole batch, as the reader does.
- `ResultSearcher.Local` is counted once, and it can be cancelled.
- A check sized from the machine's worker count failed on CI's 4-core runners; it now runs on four workers.
- Stale docs: status-bar-memory.md, ipc.md (store and search sections, distinct figures), architecture.md.

Follow-ups (speed only, output unaffected): `RowReader.Ahead` builds its list without checking cancellation; `ResultSearcher.Local` assumes two slots where a very wide result on many runs gets one; a distinct read in the moment after its result's release can unpack a page a value before answering `RESULT_RELEASED`.

## Not verified
- Live SQL groups: not run, since `VARIA_TEST_SQL_SERVER` is not set on this machine.

author: xss3cut10n3r
body:
Works on #181. Third step of decision 0057. Builds on #186 (the switch to the database); review that one first.

## Why
With history in a database, nothing forces the app to read a whole conversation any more, but it still did: the chat list and every open conversation were given every message. That is the start-up and per-message cost #181 is about.

## What changed
- **A conversation is given its newest 200 messages.** That is what the chat list needs for the last message and the unread count, and what a conversation shows when opened.
- **Scrolling back loads the next 200**, each time the oldest shown message is neared. In 1:1 chats and groups.
- **Jumping to an old message loads up to it**: a search result, a quoted message, a pinned message. A pinned message older than the loaded part still shows in the pin bar.
- **Search reads whole histories only when a search is made.**
- **A long conversation is no longer kept in memory** once nothing is showing it.

No screen changes, so no previews.

## What people will notice
- The app opens in time that no longer depends on how long the chats are.
- Scrolling far back in a long conversation loads older messages as you go.
- The unread count looks at the newest 200 messages of a chat. More than 99 already shows as "99+".

## What this does not do yet
"Seen" is still a list of message ids (#180). The read flag in the database replaces it in the next step.

## How it was checked
- [x] `test/db/history_window_test.dart`: the newest messages, more on request, a jump to an old message, a late-arriving old message does not appear at the window's start, a removed message lets an older one in, two watchers of one chat, and 12 random runs of 300 changes each checking that what a window shows is always the true end of the conversation.
- [x] `scripts/check.sh` passes.
- [ ] **Not covered by a test: the scrolling itself.** The screen tests use an in-memory store that has no windows, so "scroll to the top loads more" and "jump to an unloaded quote" are tested at the store, not through the screen.
- [ ] Not run on a device.

## AI assistance
Claude Code made this change, directed by the owner.

## Privacy and safety
- [x] No data leaves the device.
- [x] No secrets, keys or real user data in the diff.

body:
## Changes

### Unpaid sessions say "Meeting room pending" forever
- The backend already marks unpaid sessions for students with `meeting_status: 'payment_required'`; the clients ignored it.
- **Web** (`frontend/src/pages/Sessions.jsx`): shows "Payment required to join" and a **Pay for session** button linking to `/payments`.
- **Mobile** (`mobile/src/app/(app)/session/[id].tsx`): says payment is required and points to the existing **Pay securely** button.
- Payment and meeting-access rules are unchanged. While Stripe isn't live, students still can't pay; they now see why.

### Admin access via `ADMIN_EMAILS` didn't require a verified email
- `requireAdmin` only auto-grants admin membership when the email is in `ADMIN_EMAILS` **and** the account's email is verified. Before, anyone could register an unverified account under an admin address and get in.
- Accounts that already have an `admin_memberships` row are unaffected.
- The `isAdmin` flag on login follows the same rule; on signup it is now always `false`, since a new account is never verified. `security-flow.test.js` was updated for this.

### Google OAuth state token worked as a login token
- The state token was signed with `JWT_SECRET` and had a `userId` but no `sessionVersion`, so `authenticateToken` accepted it for any user whose session version is 0.
- Access tokens now carry `type: 'access'`, and `authenticateToken` rejects any JWT with a different `type`.
- Access tokens issued before this deploy have no `type` and are still accepted until they expire (15 minutes), so nobody is signed out.

### `/users/tutors` loaded everything with a query per tutor
- Availability is now loaded for all tutors in one query (chunked at 500 ids), with the legacy JSON parsed from the row already loaded. The legacy parser was moved to `parseLegacyAvailability` in `utils/availability.js`.
- Optional paging: `?limit=` (1–100, default 24) and/or `?offset=` return `{ tutors, total, limit, offset, nextOffset }`. Without either, the response is still the full array, so shipped mobile builds keep working. Results are now ordered by tutor id so pages are stable.
- Web and mobile still request the full list; switching them to paging is a follow-up.

## Tests
New `backend/test/admin-tokens-tutors.test.js` (SQLite by default, `TEST_DATABASE_URL` for Postgres):
1. An unverified account in `ADMIN_EMAILS` gets 403 and no membership; after verification it gets admin access. An ordinary verified user is still refused.
2. A real access token works; the `state` from `/google/auth-url` gets 401 when used as a bearer token.
3. The tutor list returns table slots and legacy JSON availability correctly, and two pages together equal the unpaged list.

All three fail on the previous code.

## Checks run
- `backend`: `npm test`, 24/24 passing.
- New tests and the earlier scheduling tests on a local PostgreSQL 16: all passing.
- `frontend`: `npm run lint && npm run build`, clean.
- `mobile`: `npm run lint && npm run typecheck`, clean.

## Before merging
- **Admin lockout check:** if the production owner account's email isn't verified **and** it has no `admin_memberships` row yet, it loses admin access until the email is verified. Email delivery (Resend) isn't set up yet, so check this first.
- Not run on a real device or browser: the payment-required UI was only checked by lint, typecheck and build.

author: mahach666
body:
## Problem

`TestFiles.Scratch(name)` returned a fixed path under `%TEMP%\rvtio-tests`. `dotnet test` runs the net8.0 and net10.0 test hosts at the same time, and other checkouts may run the suite on the same machine, so they overwrote each other's scratch files. `ContainerRewriterSampleTests` failed with `IOException: ... being used by another process` or a JSON mismatch of the copy, and passed when only one target framework ran.

## Change

- `TestFiles.Scratch` now returns a path under `%TEMP%\rvtio-tests\<process id>-<guid>\`, created once per process. When the tests have left the folder empty it is removed at process exit; a folder that still holds diagnostic dumps stays.
- Every scratch user (including both `Fresh(...)` helpers) goes through `Scratch`, so no test changed and each keeps its own cleanup. All other temp paths in `tests/` already carry a GUID or use `GetTempFileName`.
- `docs/test-fixtures.md` describes the new layout.
- No production code changes.

## Testing

`dotnet test tests/RvtIO.Tests -c Release` with both target frameworks together and the private fixtures available:

| | passed | failed | skipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| net10.0 | 10911 | 7 | 110 |
| net8.0 | 10907 | 7 | 110 |

The two hosts ran concurrently in separate scratch folders; `ContainerRewriterSampleTests` passed on both and no file-in-use error occurred. The 7 failures are the same on both frameworks, and none uses scratch files. The bounding-box ones are known to fail on main; the pinned count was not rerun on main but reads no temp file: `Proxy289128_*` (3), `Wall263597_BBox`, `FamilyInstance289128_BBox`, `ElementHeaderBoundingBox` (2022) and `CompactPropertySourcesTests.Test2022_PropertyCountsAreStable` (pinned count 47742, measured 47754).
