body:
## Summary

Adds the community files a public repository needs, plus a Markdown link check in the gate.

- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`**:
  - setup and how to run the gate (`pnpm verify`, `pnpm verify:full`);
  - the code rules the gate enforces;
  - Conventional Commits; the pull request title becomes the squash commit, and CI checks it;
  - the Checks section of the template;
  - CodeRabbit comments on each pull request; its comments are suggestions, and the maintainer decides which to apply.
- **Issue forms** in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`:
  - `bug.yml` and `idea.yml` (labelled `enhancement`, an existing label);
  - `config.yml` turns off blank issues and links private vulnerability reporting.
- **`.github/pull_request_template.md`**: Summary, plus a Checks section listing what was run and what was not.
- **README**:
  - a short Status section (in development, playable at the link, version in the game's top bar and in `package.json`; nothing hard-coded);
  - the `pnpm quality` line now mentions link rules;
  - gameplay text unchanged.
- **Link check**:
  - `pnpm check:links` runs `remark` with `remark-validate-links` (configured in `.remarkrc.json`) on README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY and the Markdown under `.github`;
  - it checks relative links and heading anchors, offline, and is part of `pnpm quality` (so of `verify` and CI);
  - both packages are pinned exactly: remark-cli 12.0.1, remark-validate-links 13.1.0.
  - Tool choice: lychee is the more active project (release 2026-05), but it is a native binary outside pnpm. remark-validate-links is part of the unified collective, stable with 1 open issue; its last release was 2025-02. It runs from the lockfile on every platform, which decided it.
- **`check-conventions`**: `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `pull_request_template.md` join the tool-mandated file names (GitHub looks for those names).
- **`pnpm-workspace.yaml`**: `trustPolicyExclude: undici-types@6.21.0`.
  - It is types only, reached through remark-cli and `@types/node` 22. `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` reports it as a downgrade, because it was published after a provenance-attested 7.x release.
  - It does nothing until `trustPolicy` is set (#35). Whichever of the two PRs merges second has a small conflict in that file.

## Checks run

- `pnpm check:links`: passes. Against a scratch file with a missing file and a missing heading, it fails (exit 1) with 3 findings.
- The lockfile was resolved under the 3-day release age and `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` from #35. Publication dates of all locked packages: no new version younger than 3 days (only the 2 already excluded in #35).
- `pnpm verify`: passes (exit 0, 155 tests), also after the review fix.
- Review fix (CodeRabbit): `.remarkrc.json` names the repository URL, so the check no longer depends on a remote called `origin`. Checked with `GIT_DIR` pointing nowhere: it failed before and passes now.

## Not run

- Browser journeys locally (CI runs them).
- How the issue forms render on GitHub: visible only after merge.

body:
## 概要

- **新增 5 种语言**：JavaScript（Node.js）、Go、Ruby、PHP、Java。加上 C、C++、Python、Rust，共 9 种，均自带 SDK。
- **程序间互相调用**：插件按 ID 调用其他插件的方法（等待结果或单向通知），也可发布/订阅消息。路由由核心新增的 `ProgramBus` 在 IO 线程完成。
- **统一改名为 TranForLanguage（不兼容变更）**：移除所有旧名称和兼容别名。
- **版本号改为 2.2.0**，CI 中的发布标记同步改为 `[release-v2.2.0]`。

## 互相调用

- 每个带 `id` 的调用只会收到一次回复：成功、远端报错、目标未运行或队列已满、目标在回复前停止、超时（默认 30 秒，`-Dtranforlanguage.call-timeout-ms`）、管理器关闭。
- 转发给目标的调用 ID 由核心改写，只有被调用的那个进程能回复；其他程序伪造的回复和超时后迟到的回复会被丢弃。
- SDK 等待回复时会继续处理收到的调用，所以 A → B → A 不会死锁。期间到达的游戏事件暂存，按顺序处理。
- C 和 C++ 共用新的事件循环运行时 `rpc.c`，取代原来的 `runtime.c`。
- 协议说明在 `docs/protocol.md`；示例在 `examples/interop`：Go 记账、Python 商店、JavaScript 欢迎程序。

## 不兼容变更（旧名称已全部移除）

| 项目 | 旧 | 新 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spigot 程序目录 | `plugins/C++ Plugins/` | `plugins/TranForLanguage/programs/` |
| 模组程序目录 / mod ID | `config/tranforcpp/programs/` / `tranforcpp` | `config/tranforlanguage/programs/` / `tranforlanguage` |
| 命令 / 权限 | `/tranforcpp`、`/cpp`，`tranforcpp.*` | 只有 `/tranforlanguage`，`tranforlanguage.*` |
| Java 包 / 主类 / Bukkit 事件 | `com.github.tranforcpp.TranforCPlusPlus`，`GenericTranforCEvent` | `com.github.tranforlanguage.TranForLanguage`，`TranForLanguageEvent` |
| JVM 参数 / 环境变量 / 缓存目录 | `-Dtranforcpp.*`，`TRANFORCPP_PROGRAM_ID`，`.tranforcpp/` | `-Dtranforlanguage.*`（C++ 编译器参数改为 `tranforlanguage.cpp.compiler`），`TRANFORLANGUAGE_PROGRAM_ID`，`.tranforlanguage/` |
| SDK | `tranforcpp` 模块，`Tranfor` 类，`tranforcpp_api.h` | `tranforlanguage` 模块，`TranForLanguage` 类，`tranforlanguage.h` / `tranforlanguage.hpp` |

README 新增「从 2.1 及更早版本升级」一节，写明迁移步骤。协议动作别名（`dispatchCommand`、`sync` 字段）和 SDK 函数别名（`sendMsg` 等）没有动，它们不属于旧名称。

## 测试

- 核心测试共 37 个，在本地（只用 Maven Central 的临时 POM）连续跑了多次，全部通过：
  - `ProgramBusTest`：调用路由、改写 ID、伪造回复、超时、目标停止、单向通知、发布、关闭；
  - `BuiltinLanguagesTest`：每种新语言收发中文和转义字符；
  - `InteropTest`：9 种语言同时运行，测试环形调用、A→B→A 回调、错误传递、发布/订阅，以及停止某个插件后调用立即失败。
- `examples/interop` 在本地实际跑过。
- **未在本地验证**：Spigot API 仓库在当前环境无法访问，所以 Spigot 插件模块（含 `PluginDescriptorTest`）和 Fabric/Forge/NeoForge 适配器都没有编译，真实服务端冒烟测试也没跑，需要靠本 PR 的 CI。
- CI 测试会用到 Node.js、Go、Ruby、PHP、JDK，已在工具链检查步骤中加入版本输出；GitHub `ubuntu-latest` 自带这些工具。

## 发布

合并时请把合并提交标题以 `[release-v2.2.0]` 开头（例如 `[release-v2.2.0] Merge PR: TranForLanguage 2.2.0`），这样 CI 才会在完整构建通过后创建 `v2.2.0` 标签并发布。

## What
- New engine safety net beside NEWS2: clinical-limits.json + clinicalLimits.ts with per-measure absolute limits, each cited (AHA BP categories, AHA resting HR, ATS/BTS SpO2, Cleveland/AMBOSS temperature, StatPearls respiration, ADA glucose, NHLBI sleep). Adults, non-pregnant, sex-independent; humanVerified: false pending human check.
- deviation(): personal band is a change detector, not a clinical validator - absolute breach overrides a collapsed [200,200] baseline and alerts without history (fixes systolic 200 -> normal).

Locked, non-overridable `ALG-04` excludes affected matches, prevents item approval/staging, and blocks gateway quote/commit rechecks even after manager approval. Preserve claim semantics and the separate missing-declaration/D35 behavior. No catalogue data or staged UI changes.

- Eight related API suites: 134 tests passed, including 16 new deterministic safety regressions for SKU462678/AN, all declaration states, family expansion, older Product shapes, claims, request staging, unrestricted ordering and post-approval commit recheck. Synthetic supplier fixtures; no live calls.
- After the final integration merge: 76 tests passed across safety, item-review, menu fixed totals, proposal outlet scope and static SPA suites; API typecheck and production build passed again.

author: stanleycm
body:
Descripción

Se implementa el primer módulo de análisis científico de PyroGravity, utilizando los datos de la investigación BASS-II (PSI-25) de NASA.

El módulo permite analizar los cambios en la concentración de CO₂ entre las lecturas iniciales y finales de cada ensayo, conservando la precisión numérica, la procedencia de los datos y sus limitaciones científicas.

Cambios realizados

  • Implementación de data/src/analysis/bass_ii_co2.py.

  • Incorporación de data/tests/test_bass_ii_co2.py.

  • Análisis reproducible desde Parquet y PostgreSQL.

  • Cálculo de diferencias de CO₂ mediante Decimal.

  • Validación de lecturas exactas dentro del rango de 0 a 5 % vol.

  • Filtros por investigador (PI) y material.

  • Identificación de muestras repetidas y exclusiones.

  • Estadísticas descriptivas y resultados estructurados para backend e IA.

  • Conservación de la trazabilidad hacia los registros originales NASA.

Resultados científicos

Indicador | Resultado -- | -- Ensayos registrados | 129 Pares válidos | 121 Ensayos excluidos | 8 Mediana del cambio de CO₂ | +0,24 pp Primer cuartil | +0,04 pp Tercer cuartil | +0,62 pp Mínimo | −0,01 pp Máximo | +2,78 pp Cambios positivos | 113 Cambios nulos | 6 Cambios negativos | 2

Se identificaron 48 cambios inferiores a 0,1 puntos porcentuales, resolución publicada del sensor, por lo que se incluyen advertencias para evitar interpretaciones científicas incorrectas.

Validaciones realizadas

  • 40/40 pruebas automatizadas aprobadas.

  • Comparación completa entre Parquet y PostgreSQL 18 local: PASS.

  • Comparaciones con filtros por PI y material: PASS.

  • Verificación de estadísticas, exclusiones, registros individuales y procedencia.

  • Conservación de los archivos originales y sus hashes SHA-256.

  • Consultas PostgreSQL parametrizadas y de solo lectura.

  • Sin modificaciones a los datos existentes en Supabase.

Próximos pasos

  • Integrar los resultados científicos con el backend.

  • Preparar las visualizaciones de CO₂.

  • Continuar con los análisis de FLEX, Flame Design, CFI-G y SPICE.

Este PR incorpora el análisis científico BASS-II y sus pruebas, sin modificar el esquema de la base de datos ni los datos originales NASA.

body:
The Preview rewrite test treated a hidden parent popover as proof that the child iframe had restored its original document. Restoration is processed by a later message handler, so WebKit could read the edited text before that handler ran. Await the iframe's exact original text and removal of contenteditable after Save and Escape, retaining every existing assertion, timeout and test.

Only the browser-command fixture changes (10 added lines); Preview runtime behavior is unchanged. Local Chromium and Firefox each passed, and WebKit passed five fresh invocations. Blocking the restoration message made the test fail at its unchanged30-second limit, confirming that a real restoration failure remains detectable. Full validate:static and the trusted-main boundary check pass. Documents the waves list as `ROADMAP.md` — the arc from the current engine to the practical capabilities of a Chromium-class browser, in priority (dependency) order: 40 phases across seven waves (rendering & text, JavaScript as a platform, layout & CSS, the network, DOM everywhere, hardening, measurement), each with a rough size, plus an honest baseline, explicit non-goals, and the internal dependency order.

**Priority, not policy:** the file says so up front, and AGENTS.md gains a \"Reading the queue\" note pointing at it — no item is compulsory, agents claim freely from either place, and if the two disagree the task table wins.

## What it does not do

No code, no scoreboard changes, no claims recorded against any phase. The open-tasks table in AGENTS.md is untouched apart from the pointer.

author: tixxin
body:
## 改了什么

### 下载 Node（`src-tauri/crates/plugin-base`）
- 新增 `prepare_node`：电脑上没有能用的 Node 时，下载写死版本（Node 26.13.1，当前 LTS）的官方发布包到 `<数据目录>/runtime/node-v26.13.1/`，边下边核对写死的 SHA-256，解压后整个目录原子地改名到位；中途失败清理干净，下次能重试；已经核对过的一份直接用，不联网。
- 下载地址按顺序试：nodejs.org → npmmirror → 腾讯镜像（两个镜像的 `SHASUMS256.txt` 和官方逐字节相同）。进度回调给出地址、已下载和总字节；失败时列出每个地址和原因。
- 新增 `node_for_host`：先找电脑上的 Node，不行再下载，返回用的是哪一份（`System` / `Downloaded`）。还没接进 `plugin_kernel`，接线方法写在文档里。
- 新依赖都是 `src-tauri` 已经在用的：`reqwest`（多开 `blocking`）、`sha2`、`zip`。macOS 的 `.tar.xz` 用系统自带的 `tar` 解压。

### 正式版带上宿主脚本
- 新增 `scripts/plugins-v3/bundle-host.mjs`：用 Vite 自带的 esbuild 把宿主打成 `src-tauri/target/plugins-v3/host/` 下的一个文件夹（6 个 ESM 文件，776 KB）。是文件夹而不是单个文件，因为内核在运行时按地址加载插件接口、`include`、`hmr`，它们要和宿主共用同一份 Cordis。
- 新增 `docs/architecture/plugins/v3-node-runtime.md`：设计、实测、怎么接线、正式版怎么带上资源。构建流程这次没改。

## 为什么
插件平台第 3 版第 1 阶段第 4b 步。方案的决定 16：安装包不带 Node，先用电脑上的，没有才下载；宿主脚本要随正式版发布。

## 验证
- `cargo test`（工作区 596 条，plugin-base 9 + 8 + 6 条）通过；`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` 在 macOS 和 `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` 上都通过。
- 下载的测试用本地 HTTP 服务：哈希不对时拒绝且不留文件、下载中途断开后清理并能重试、第一个地址失败时用镜像、已经下载过的不再下、损坏的一份被换掉、`.tar.xz` 解压后 `bin/node` 还能执行。
- 手动跑了一次真实下载（`#[ignore]` 的测试）：nodejs.org 10 秒、npmmirror 4 秒、腾讯 20 秒，三份都打印 `v26.13.1`。
- `pnpm check`：类型、lint、行数、颜色、任务都通过；854 条测试，833 通过、15 跳过、1 失败（`agent-harness-gate` 在 Mac 上本来就失败，和这次无关）。新的打包测试把宿主打到仓库外面，用 `node --disallow-code-generation-from-strings` 跑起来，插件能 `import "@fuyu/plugin-base"`，发出 `ready`，`stop` 后退出码 0。
- 用资源叠加配置打了一个 debug 版 `.app`：`Contents/Resources/plugins-v3/host/` 在，macOS 原有的资源没被冲掉，宿主能从里面跑起来。

## 注意
- `tauri-build` 每次 cargo 构建都会拷 `bundle.resources`，路径不存在就失败，所以宿主资源要加在发版用的叠加配置里，不能直接加进 `tauri.conf.json`。具体改法在文档里，等宿主要随正式版发布时和 Rust 找资源目录的代码一起做。
- Windows 上没有跑真实下载和打包实测。

## 关联
任务 E36.1 · issue #291

body:
## Why
The Drone website and silent vision film were created outside this repository and were not committed to either existing branch. The user requires this repository to preserve the complete website, specifications, reusable package, traceability data, and media; they should not have to save and re-upload generated files.

## Saved now
This branch inherits the original PR #1 documents unchanged from `07fee9310b2f20167501e57b4d75a10205c639ff` and adds five files:

- `AGENTS.md`: repository-first preservation and evidence-backed delivery rules.
- `docs/project-package-requirements.md`: the agreed complete reusable package scope.
- `docs/asset-recovery-status.md`: audited inventory, known original locations, missing assets, and remaining recovery work.
- `media/vision/transcript-recovered.md`: seven chapter passages recovered from the earlier browser inspection in the project conversation.
- `media/vision/storyboard-recovered.json`: the same text with chapter timings and existing plan references.

Commit: `0cfeea74a9c205381a33504cc45c44b7cfdea965`.

## Important limitations
This is a preservation/recovery checkpoint, NOT the finished narration or website migration. The original MP4, full website source, original caption file, complete backlog/evidence data, and reusable package implementation have not been recovered. No narration audio has been generated and no deployed update is claimed. Do not close the recovery work on the basis of the transcript alone.

The current unauthenticated fetch of the recorded hosted video and reusable-package pages returns HTTP 401. The original authenticated site/editor or its source export is needed. Earlier working files are not available in the current session. This does not establish that the original hosted assets are lost.

## Remaining acceptance checklist
- [ ] Recover original website source and complete structured project records.
- [ ] Recover original 72-second silent MP4 and its visual/rendering inputs.
- [ ] Recover original captions, preserving chapter navigation.
- [ ] Add actual timed voice-over narration and validate audio/non-silence, sync, seeking, and mobile playback.
- [ ] Save final media in Git or versioned Git-linked release/LFS storage; record hashes and reproducible commands.
- [ ] Recover or explicitly reconstruct the reusable package and prove it on a second project.
- [ ] Publish from a recorded commit and verify the actual live site and narrated video.

PR #1 is left untouched and unmerged. No simulator capability or acceptance result is asserted by these documentation changes.

author: johnarleyburns
body:
## Summary
- The periodic time observer let a remote `AVPlayerItem`'s own duration estimate unconditionally override the library's known duration every 0.5s. That estimate (e.g. for a Jamendo VBR MP3 served with no exact `Content-Length` up front) can be wildly wrong and keeps changing as more of the file loads — the crossfade code already reached this exact conclusion for its own `fadeStart` math and preferred the library value there. Plausible direct mechanism for the reported "nonsensical elapsed/remaining times".
- Added `PlaybackDisplayPolicy.effectiveDuration(libraryKnown:itemEstimate:)` (pure, directly testable) and used it in the tick: the library's known duration is authoritative once set, falling back to the item's estimate only when the library has none.
- Clamped `seek(to:)` to the known duration (and zero): a scrub computed against an inflated/stale duration could otherwise seek past the item's real end, ending it and silently triggering `next()`.

Step 5 of the stabilization plan (steps 1–4: #420, #421, #422, #423).

## Test plan
- [x] `Tests/PlaybackDisplayPolicyDurationTests.swift` — pure-function tests for the new duration-choice policy.
- [x] `Tests/AudioPlayerSeekClampTests.swift` — seek clamps past-end/negative, leaves in-bounds seeks and the "no known duration" case alone.
- [ ] Could not run `swift test` locally — no macOS SDK, and `parso-audio-engine`'s C/C++ deps don't build on Linux. Relying on CI.

- [v1.7.0](https://github.com/vi/websocat/releases/tag/v1.7.0)
- [v1.8.0](https://github.com/vi/websocat/releases/tag/v1.8.0)

Each of these comes out differently from what the registry holds, so this replaces a file the registry is already serving. A version whose file was unchanged isn't here.

What CI checks is that the new file describes the release it says it does: the assets download, the checksums match, the archives open and `files[].src` is inside them, and every signature the entry claims verifies. What it can't check is whether replacing the old file was right, so auto-merge is off and this needs reading. The old file is in the default branch's history.

## Merging this

This changes files the registry already serves, which a lock file may hold the checksums of. It is labelled `replaces-published` and ar2 doesn't set it to merge itself. Merging it, or turning auto-merge on for it, is what says the change was read and is meant.

Before merging, read the diff of each file: what changed should be what the definition was fixed for. An asset whose checksum changed is a release rewritten after it was published, which is what a lock file is there to catch, so decide whether to serve the new one rather than taking it because it verifies.

For: Prince (backend owner). Draft by AskAr for review; please don't merge without your OK.

## Why
The operator should open the Command Center and see the building camera with **nothing pasted**. Today the tile only shows a stream after someone pastes its URL into each browser. With this, the camera says where its view is when it registers, and the dashboard (Hillary's PR) reads it from `state.cameras`.

## What changes (simulation adapter only, `shared/` untouched)
- `CameraRegistration.stream_url` is optional: plain `http(s)://`, no `user:pass@`, at most 500 chars. Anything else returns 422.
- `CameraRecord.stream_url` (default `null`) appears in `state.cameras`.
- **The mapping stays immutable.** The same mapping with a different `stream_url` updates only the URL (`duplicate: false`) and emits `simulation.camera_registered` again with the new record, so the WebSocket pushes it. A restarted camera on a new address stays on the dashboard. A different mapping still returns 409.
- No new event type, and no change to observations, tracks, freshness, routing or proposals (`impact cause` is `None`, so no replan).
- README section updated.

## Tests
- `backend/tests/test_simulation_cameras.py`: 30 passed, including the new `test_stream_url_is_listed_and_follows_the_latest_registration` and four new 422 cases (`javascript:`, `file:`, credentials, too long).
- Full backend run (without the EMS tests): 493 passed. One failure, `test_neural_shadow.py::test_independent_validator_and_zero_committed_violations`, **also fails on main**. It asserts `comparison.available` but the weights aren't provisioned on this laptop, so it should probably skip like its neighbours.

## Rollout
Additive and optional. Old cameras and dashboards are unaffected. Companion PRs: the dashboard tile (Hillary) and the CV registration (AskAr).

author: coreyphillips
body:
Closes #2083

A final-hop onion message whose encrypted recipient data fails to decrypt or fails the strict reader is now dropped instead of being handed to application handlers.

At the final hop, `processOnionMessage` wrapped `decryptBlindedData` and `decodeBlindedHopData` in a catch and returned `delivery` anyway, just without a `path_id`. So a message whose encrypted data set an `allowed_features` bit, carried an unknown even type, or failed authentication still reached registered TLV handlers. BOLT 4 says to ignore such a message at every hop. The strict reader from #2047 was only enforced at relay hops.

## What changed

- `processOnionMessage` final hop: errors from decrypting or decoding `encrypted_recipient_data` now propagate. `OnionMessageManager` then emits `message:error`, and neither `message:received` nor any TLV handler fires.
- `processOnionMessage` final hop: `encrypted_recipient_data` with no blinding point now throws instead of being delivered. The wire form always carries a path key, so only direct callers can hit this.
- A final payload with no `encrypted_recipient_data` at all (the legacy unblinded form from `constructSimpleOnionMessage`) is still delivered without a `path_id`.
- New `readRecipientData` helper in `process.ts` does the decrypt and strict decode for both the final hop and `resolveNextHop`.

## How to test

- `npx mocha --exit --timeout 20000 -r ts-node/register tests/lightning/blinded-spec-rules.test.ts`: 24 passing. The new "onion message final node (#2083)" block sends through `OnionMessageManager.handleMessage`. It covers a valid `path_id` (delivered), `allowed_features` 0x02, an unknown even type 16, and a tampered ciphertext (all three dropped), plus final-hop data with no blinding point.
- With `process.ts` swapped back to HEAD, four of those five cases fail: the handler runs for all three bad inputs, and the no-blinding-point case does not throw.
- Onion message, large packet, BOLT 4 blinded onion message conformance, bolt4-low-hardening, bolt12-interop-fixes, blinded-path-key-override and bolt12-path-id files together: 135 passing.
- `npm run tsc:check`, `npm run build`, `npm run tsc:check:tests` and `npm run test:api` (8) all pass. eslint and prettier are clean on the touched files.
- `npm run test:lightning` at load average up to 31: 10594 passing, 13 failing in 23 minutes. Nine are this machine's usual load failures. The other four are direct-funding sender and receiver timeouts ("funding negotiation did not complete in time").
- All nine failing files pass when rerun alone: 345 passing for bolt12-path-id, the three direct-funding files and blinded-relay-correctness, and 176 for the rest together with the onion files.

## Notes

I left one case unchanged: a final payload with no encrypted recipient data at all is still delivered. A strict reading of BOLT 4 would drop that too. But it is the legacy unblinded form that `constructSimpleOnionMessage` and the raw-key fallback produce, and many tests rely on it. The issue only covers data that is present and fails.

author: cairnwright[bot]
body:
## Proof

Owner ask (mon X): quick replies show up slowly after a Coordinator reply.

| Answer end → quick-reply request | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live turn 04:30:54Z (Langfuse `chat` spans) | 3.23 s: mirror ~0.7 s, then input replay ~2.5 s | re-measured after deploy |
| Server test world, `afterMirror` held until the request starts | request waits for the mirror, times out at 2 s | request starts while the mirror runs |

The new `turn.test.ts` case fails on origin/main.

```text
Live: Langfuse chat spans 04:31:00.430 (answer end) and 04:31:03.656 (suggestion start); coordinator_conversation.updatedAt 04:31:01.144 marks the mirror end.
Replay cost: a copy of the live server.db rewrites 223 transcript rows, one transaction each, in ~1.0 s on a quiet disk (4.6 ms/row fsync); 44 ms in one transaction.
Not covered: live timing after deploy.
```

## What

The quick-reply request starts as soon as the answer settles and runs alongside the transcript mirror and input replay. The chips are still written after the answer row, and the existing gate is checked again at write time.

<details><summary>Review and risk</summary>

## Review

No review ran (code review is off). Local: lint, typecheck, spec:parse, prepush; `apps/server/test/coordinator/` passes (225 tests).

| Path | Before | After | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| User turn, answer with text | suggestion after mirror and replay | suggestion starts at settle, awaited before `done` | `turn.test.ts` "asks for quick replies while the transcript is still being mirrored" |
| Stop during the turn or the suggestion | stop poll aborts the suggestion | unchanged; also skipped when a stop is already pending at settle | "aborts prediction on stop without publishing stale chips" |
| Mirror, replay or answer lookup throws | no suggestion started | suggestion aborted in `finally` | covered by abort signal |
| Event triggers, empty or non-stop answers | no suggestion | unchanged | "predicts after cold and warm ordinary replies but skips every event trigger" |
| Unusable or failing suggestion | answer succeeds, usage counted | unchanged | "keeps the answer successful and counts usage when prediction is unusable" |

## Risk

Two-way door. Replay and mirror writes are synchronous SQLite work, so the suggestion response is read only after they finish; the gain is the model's think time overlapping them. Replay rewriting every row since the first consumed input on each turn is the larger cost and is left for a separate change. Auto-merge route.

</details>

author: rajvardhanpatil07
body:
Fixes from a full read-through of the Python and Rust gateways.

## Consent
- **Rust: default approval mode is now manual.** Before, any new tool that set `readOnlyHint: true` and avoided five verbs was approved and sent to the model with no review, including tools a server added later. Annotations are server-supplied and the MCP spec says not to trust them.
- Automatic modes now apply only to tools in a server's first catalog (`onboarding_tools` table). Tools added later always go to review.
- Definitions with zero-width, bidi or tag characters are never auto-approved.
- Users who explicitly chose an automatic mode keep it.

## Python store and sessions
- The shared SQLite store uses WAL, and `dispatch` commits the authorization before calling the upstream tool. Before, the write lock was held for the whole call (up to 300 s); any call over 5 s made the desktop app and other gateways fail.
- A busy store skips one heartbeat instead of also stopping the catalog watcher.
- Upstream RPC errors and withheld results (private keys, credentials, non-text content, `outputSchema` mismatches) fail that call only. Before, one such result closed the gateway and revoked every approval.
- The stdio CLI exits once its upstream connection is gone instead of answering every request with an error.
- After a restart, a changed tool is compared with the last approved definition, so the diff, scoring and auto-quarantine still work. That earlier approval is evidence only; calls still need a fresh approval for the current session.

## Harness discovery
- Fetch refuses servers from a repository's own `.mcp.json` or `.codex/config.toml` unless Claude Code approved them (`enabledMcpjsonServers` / `enableAllProjectMcpServers`) or Codex trusts the project. A cloned repo could otherwise run a command or send `${GITHUB_TOKEN}` in a URL with one click.
- Scan shows the command or URL that would be used, with secret-looking arguments redacted and no variable expansion.

## Rust sessions
- A JSON-RPC error from an HTTP upstream no longer closes the session.
- Late stdio replies to timed-out requests are discarded instead of breaking the next exchange.

## Smaller
- `git` subprocesses in history mining have a 300 s timeout.
- Static string concatenation in the source extractor is capped at 64 KiB (`a = a + a` repeated 40 times exhausted memory).

## Testing
- Python: 394 passed, 4 skipped; ruff clean.
- Rust: all tests pass; `clippy -D warnings` and `fmt --check` clean.
- Desktop: 15/15 node tests, production build OK. Browser checks not run locally.
- New regression tests cover each fix. The store-lock test fails on the previous code.

author: inquiredu
body:
## Why
GitHub Pages can't put a login in front of a page, so `inquiredu.org/settings.html` is loadable by anyone. The private catalog stays behind a fine-grained token (unauthenticated API calls to `site-catalog` return 404), but the page also had a "Remember on this device" option that saved the publishing key in `localStorage`, which every page on inquiredu.org shares, and it had no Content-Security-Policy.

## What this changes
- Deletes `settings.html` and the `admin.html` redirect to it.
- Removes the gear link (and its CSS) from the home page.
- Removes the now-dead "Site settings" link from `lighttable.html`.
- README: says Settings now runs only on the owner's computer; drops the stale "If you ticked Remember there" line in the light table steps.

Settings itself isn't lost. It lives in a local copy of this repo (`settings.html` and `assets/settings.*`, listed in `.git/info/exclude`, never committed) and starts from a local launcher beside the repo at `http://127.0.0.1:8787/settings.html`. The local copy has a strict CSP (no inline script or style) and keeps the key in tab memory only; Remember is removed.

## After merging
- GitHub Pages redeploys in about a minute, with up to ~10 minutes of cache. `inquiredu.org/settings.html` should then return 404.
- If the publishing key was ever remembered in a browser on inquiredu.org, that copy stays in that site's localStorage. Delete `gh-token` there or rotate the token on GitHub.

## Not changed
`lighttable.html` still takes the same publishing key and stores it under the same `gh-token` localStorage key, so it has the same exposure. Left alone because it is in active development.

## Tested
Served the branch locally: the settings page loads with no CSP errors and the page's injected-script and off-site-request probes are blocked. The home page and light table contain no links to `settings.html`, and none of `settings.html`, `admin.html` or `assets/settings.*` are tracked. A real publish with a live key was not tested.

author: mikhail-yaskou
body:
## Summary

A fork can use the same branch name as the sync branch. Sync now requires the pull request's head repository to match the configured repository before adopting it, so a same-organization fork's pull request keeps its title, description and state.

## User-Facing Changes

- Sync opens or reuses the pull request from its own repository, even when a fork uses the same branch name.
- Pull requests with missing head repository identity are ignored.

## Why This Matters

Branch names alone do not identify the source of a pull request. Checking the source repository keeps sync actions attached to the intended changes.

Validation: Typecheck, build and 15 focused API and sync regression tests passed. The serial test suite is running; its result will be supplied before merge. Tests use local Git and fake GitHub and Linear APIs; no live service check is needed for this lookup change.

author: samikaperera
body:
Closes #474. `web/` is mine, so this stays in `web/main.py` and leaves the loaders in `analysis/` alone.

## What changed

- `web/main.py:2043` adds `_refusal_without_temp_path(message, temp_path, display_name)`. It replaces every spelling of this upload's temp path in a loader's refusal with the quoted name of the file the user uploaded: as written, as `repr()` quotes it (an OSError doubles every backslash), and with forward slashes. Every other word of the message is kept.
- `web/main.py:2156` (`/api/policy`) and `:2405` (`/api/business-context`) use it in place of `detail=str(error)`.

## Before and after

Measured with the real app and `TEMP` and `TMP` pointed at an empty folder. The temp path is written as `<temp path>`.

| endpoint | bad file | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| /api/policy | invalid JSON | `<temp path> is not valid JSON: line 1, column 25: Expecting value` | `'mine.json' is not valid JSON: line 1, column 25: Expecting value` |
| /api/policy | a 5,000-digit integer | `<temp path> holds a value that cannot be read: ...` | `'mine.json' holds a value that cannot be read: ...` |
| /api/policy | nested 100,000 deep | `<temp path> is nested too deeply to be a policy` | `'mine.json' is nested too deeply to be a policy` |
| /api/policy | not UTF-8 | `<temp path> is not UTF-8 text: byte 23 cannot be decoded. ...` | `'mine.json' is not UTF-8 text: byte 23 cannot be decoded. ...` |
| /api/business-context | the same four | `<temp path> ...` | `'ctx.json' ...`, same words |
| either | duplicate key, unknown section, unknown tier | no path | unchanged |

## Why the exact path and not a pattern

Three options were measured:

1. **Replace the exact temp path. Chosen.** It touches only text the web layer itself introduced.
2. **A regex for any path. Rejected.** The loaders echo the user's own values back. Uploading a context with tier `D:\shares\gold` gives `unknown tier 'D:\\shares\\gold'`, and a drive-path regex rewrote that, swallowing the closing `'.` too.
3. **Change what the loader is given. Rejected.**
   - A file named after the upload still sits in a temp folder, so the folder still shows.
   - A relative path needs `os.chdir`, which is process-wide and unsafe with concurrent requests.
   - Parsing the bytes in `web/` would duplicate the loaders' messages, which the comment above the policy upload explicitly avoids.

## Tests, red then green on purpose

`tests/test_upload_refusal_hides_temp_path.py`, 14 tests:

- the four bad files on both endpoints: no temp folder, no `AppData`, no `Users`, no drive-letter path, and the detail keeps the uploaded name and the loader's reason
- a refusal quoting the path with doubled backslashes, on both endpoints
- a refusal naming the path twice
- controls: a refusal that never had a path keeps its exact words, and a good upload of each kind is unchanged

The temp folder is a canary whose name contains a backslash, so the doubled spelling differs from the plain one on Linux as well as on Windows.

The commits are in order on purpose:
1. **Tests only.** 10 fail on `main` (the temp folder is in the refusal), and the 3 controls pass.
2. **The fix.** All pass.
3. **One more test, from mutation testing (below).**

## Mutation check

Each mutant ran in a scratch copy, one at a time:

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| remove the replacement | killed, 11 fail |
| replace only the first occurrence | **survived the first 13 tests**; killed by the third commit's test |
| apply on `/api/policy` only | killed, the 5 business-context cases fail |
| do not handle doubled backslashes | killed, the 2 doubled-backslash cases fail |

## Counts

```
tests/test_upload_refusal_hides_temp_path.py     14 passed
full suite, Batfish running                      2340 passed, 13 skipped
ruff check --select E4,E7,E9,F (changed files)   All checks passed
merges cleanly with #470 (e7c3a69): its tests and the upload tests, 147 passed
merges cleanly with #467 (5087466): the loader and upload tests, 206 passed
```

## What this does not change

- The loaders in `analysis/`: the command line still names the real file it was given.
- `/api/upload`: it already names the uploaded file and never showed a path.
- A different spelling of the same location, such as a resolved or 8.3 short path, or the temp folder quoted without the file name. Neither appears in any refusal today.
- `/api/ask` and `/api/policy/draft`, which pass `describe_error()` text that can name the session's config folder. That is not reached by a bad upload and is noted on the issue for a separate look.

author: usmannsiddiqui
body:
A real mail said the AI Guides report was due "tonight at 11:59 PM". The stored commitment had no dueAt, so no nudge, draft or "started for you" offer followed. The model was never told the current time or the user's zone, and assemblePreparation dropped any dueAt with an offset.

- The model input gets a trusted `now` block beside the evidence: the UTC instant, the owner's IANA zone from attentionSettings, and the local date, weekday and time (preparationClock, Intl only). Each evidence item already carried occurredAt.
- INSTRUCTIONS get dueAt rules: set it only for a stated or clearly implied deadline, resolve relative words against the item's occurredAt in the user's zone, a bare day or "tonight" means 23:59 local, output a UTC Z instant, otherwise null. The deadline never changes who is responsible.
- assemblePreparation keeps Z and offset ISO datetimes, stores them as UTC Z, and drops garbage and absurd dates (more than 2 years after, or more than a day before, the cited evidence).
- No stored zone: the now block says so and no dueAt is stored, whatever the model returns.
- Due in under an hour: nudge row, no past due-1h job, the started offer opens at once. Already past: the time is stored, with no nudge, no draft and no offer (this was existing behaviour, now covered by tests).

No schema change. Tests: unit 309, integration 234 (`pnpm verify` clean).

body:
Follow-up to the linked Android saves stack, based on [Export linked Android saves to their source with conflict recovery](https://github.com/woahitsraj/PKSX/pull/488). Moves emulator folder linking from Settings to Saves as two choices, Import file and Link folder, and removes the long explanatory text.

Refs [Link Dolphin save folders on Android](https://github.com/woahitsraj/PKSX/issues/379), [Discover saves from common Android emulators](https://github.com/woahitsraj/PKSX/issues/381), [Refresh and explicitly write back linked Save Files](https://github.com/woahitsraj/PKSX/issues/380). No closing keyword: the parent PRs close those issues.

## Summary

```diff
 <Settings>
-  <LinkedSaveFolders>   # folder list, scan reports, source paragraphs
 <SavesGrid>
-  [Import a Save File]
+  [Add saves] -> <AddSavesMenu>
+     Import file
+     Link folder   (emulator detected from the folder path)
+     Linked: Scan again · Unlink <folder>
   <SaveCard>
-    xd.gci
+    Dolphin · xd.gci            [Updated] when the emulator changed it
 <SaveFileMenu>
+  Load from Dolphin | Restore file in Dolphin   (only when needed)
 <BoxMenu> (linked Save File)
-  Export
+  Export to Dolphin -> "Overwrite xd.gci?" Overwrite / Cancel
   Export a copy
```

- PKSX detects the emulator from the linked folder path and stores it on each discovered Save File (`emulator`), so cards, menus and later grouping can use it.
- Scan results and errors are short toasts (`Found 2 new saves`, `Couldn't read GC`, `Folder not linked`). Background rescans stay silent unless they find saves.
- A Save File whose folder was unlinked is just a Save File. No warning text.

## Evidence

- Unit and browser tests: 727 passed. New test opens Add saves on Android and checks the `Dolphin · xd.gci` card label. Box Menu test checks `Export to Dolphin` and `Export a copy`.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` pass. Svelte autofixer clean.
- Retroid Pocket 6, build `cbcabe15`: Add saves menu, `Dolphin ·` labels, `Export to Dolphin` and the Overwrite / Cancel prompt all work. Screenshots are in the PR comments. Cancel froze the page in the first build because two queued focus calls kept taking turns. Fixed; 137 Boxes end-to-end tests pass.
- Not run on device: Overwrite itself, Load from Dolphin, and linking a new folder through the picker.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

UI and message changes. Adds an optional `emulator` field to stored Save Files; older records without it just show no emulator label.

**Blast Radius:** Android Saves and Box Menu

Web keeps the original Import a Save File cell.

author: jbakertt
body:
## What

`actions/vault-secrets`: a composite action that gets an ephemeral GitHub token and/or Vault secrets from OSPO Vault. It replaces the ~30 lines that each job copies today (Confluence: "How to get Vault secrets and ephemeral GitHub tokens").

```yaml
      - id: vault
        uses: tenstorrent/.github/actions/vault-secrets@<full-commit-sha>
        with:
          role: tenstorrent--example-app
          github-token: tenstorrent--example-app--lib-read
          secrets: |
            kv/data/tenstorrent/example-app/upload api_key | UPLOAD_API_KEY
      - env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.vault.outputs.token }}
          KEY: ${{ fromJSON(steps.vault.outputs.secrets).UPLOAD_API_KEY }}
```

Steps: pre-checks (id-token permission, `pull_request_target`, inputs) → Tailscale join (skipped with `join-tailnet: auto` when the runner is already on the tailnet) → wait for Vault → `hashicorp/vault-action` jwt login with `exportEnv: false`.

- Inputs: `role` (required), `github-token`, `secrets`, `vault-url`, `join-tailnet` (`auto`|`true`|`false`), `tailscale-client-id`, `tailscale-audience`, `tailscale-tags`.
- Outputs: `token`, and `secrets` (JSON; also holds the key `VAULT_SECRETS_GITHUB_TOKEN` when `github-token` is set).
- Inputs reach shell only through `env:`. Third-party actions are pinned by SHA (tailscale v4.4.0, vault-action v4.0.0, checkout v7.0.1).
- Follows the `actions/<name>/action.yml` layout of #13. Does not depend on #13 or #14.

## For the reviewer: Tailscale defaults

A composite action cannot read `vars`. `TS_VAULT_OSPO_CLIENT_ID` and `TS_VAULT_OSPO_AUDIENCE` have the same values in all six orgs (tenstorrent, automationTT, tenstorrent-digital, tenstorrent-forks, tenstorrent-metal, tenstorrent-riscv-software; read 2026-11-15). So the action uses them as input defaults. They are OIDC federation identifiers, not secrets. If an org variable changes, the action default must change too, or callers pass `${{ vars.TS_VAULT_OSPO_CLIENT_ID }}` / `${{ vars.TS_VAULT_OSPO_AUDIENCE }}`. Please confirm this is acceptable.

## Masking

vault-action calls `core.setSecret` for each value and for each line of a multi-line value. The runner masks a registered value everywhere in the job log, also after it goes through a composite output, `toJSON` or `fromJSON` (the runner also masks the JSON-escaped form). Not yet verified live: the test jobs print only lengths and key names, never values. In the first live run, read the `token-and-kv` and `two-calls` logs and confirm nothing unmasked appears.

## Tests: `.github/workflows/vault-secrets-test.yml`

Uses `./actions/vault-secrets` from the PR checkout. Triggers: `pull_request` (action and workflow paths) and `workflow_dispatch`. Fork PRs are skipped.

- Run now (no grant needed): pre-check failures (no inputs, empty role, bad token name, bad `join-tailnet`, http URL, reserved output name, no `id-token: write`) and network failures (unreachable `vault-url`, `join-tailnet: false`).
- Gated on repo variable `VAULT_SECRETS_TEST_ENABLED == 'true'`: token only, token + KV, two calls in one job, Vault refusals (wrong role, wrong token, wrong KV path, wrong KV field), and no `environment:`. They use `environment: vault-action-test`. The gate stops a run from creating that environment before it is set up.

Each failure job runs the action with `continue-on-error: true` and then asserts that the action failed and both outputs are empty. The job fails if the action succeeds.

Grant expected (github-vault-iac PR 31, not applied yet): role `tenstorrent--.github--vault-action-test`, environment `vault-action-test`, events `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch`, token `tenstorrent--.github--contents-read` (contents read, metadata read, this repo only), KV `kv/data/_roles/tenstorrent--.github--vault-action-test/test` field `value`.

To enable: apply the grant, create environment `vault-action-test`, store the KV test value, set the repo variable.

## Prerequisite for wide use

This repo has no CODEOWNERS, and ruleset 8193855 lets the maintain role bypass review (`always`). Proposal P3 of the 2026-11-14 `.github` review (bypass only via pull request, plus CODEOWNERS on `/actions/`) should land before other repos use this action widely, because the action runs inside their jobs with their OIDC identity.

Until then, a consumer must:
- pin by full commit SHA, never a branch or tag;
- check that the SHA is on `main` of `tenstorrent/.github` (GitHub also resolves SHAs from forks);
- review the diff when bumping the SHA.

Lint: `actionlint` and `shellcheck` pass locally.

author: daviddef
body:
## What

The visitor's own tree opens first on the Tree Canvas, and each person has a **Where to from here** panel built from the Atlas: the order of work (death, marriage, birth, moves), sources cheapest first with links, who ruled each place in that year and where its books were filed, neighbouring places, the wars and displacement the life spans, the surname in the tree, and a research sheet to copy.

## How

- `scripts/roots/tree-canvas.template.html`: a vendored, corpus-less build of the Tree Canvas. `build-roots-data.py` gains a `canvas` step that writes `site/public/roots/canvas.html` (gitignored and generated, like `viewer.html`) with its own CSP.
- The canvas reads `window.parent.RR.{tree,atlas}`, the same data the viewer draws, through a one-archive port of the corpus transform. A redacted living person is drawn as living: no dates, no places.
- `roots/index.astro`: "Tree canvas" is the first tab; the old Tree tab is "Tree views". `app.js` mounts the frame the first time its tab is shown for a file, and again for a new file.

## Privacy

- The file never leaves the browser. The canvas stores nothing (no localStorage), so the start screen's "kept only if you tick" rule still decides what is remembered.
- The panel asks this site for `/p/<place id>.json`, `/regions.json`, `/providers.json`, `/index.json`, `/pi/<cell>.json`, only when the tab is opened for a person. Only Atlas place ids are in any request: no name, date or relationship. Frame CSP: `connect-src 'self'` (viewer.html's is `'none'`), `font-src data:`, nothing else.
- Living people never get a plan.

## Checked

- Canvas self-test 161 passed, 0 failed (research engine against real Atlas records; 12 for the tree-to-corpus port).
- In a browser, with the invented sample family: canvas first, frame mounts, a person with three events gets a three-step plan with the regime for each year (Austria-Hungary, then Italy's Istria province for the 1922 marriage, then Yugoslavia), links, neighbours, WW1/WW2/displacement layers, and Copy works. Phone width checked on the standalone canvas.
- Not run: the full `npm run data` / site build (a clean clone lacks `data/fs-volumes-world.json.gz`), so this was tested through `astro dev` with the generated roots data copied from the working tree and place JSON read from recordatlas.org.

## Decisions for David

1. The per-click place-id reads are visible to the Atlas server's logs (which places a visitor looks up). Nothing else is. Is that acceptable beside "your file never leaves this computer"? The roots page's own text should probably say so in one line; I have not changed the promise copy.
2. The Tree Canvas source is not in git. This vendors its built output; the next change needs a rebuild and a re-vendor. Suggest putting the source in its own repo.

Draft: not for merge until David says.

author: tsavo
body:
Part of #7757. Step 5 (construct: the temporal rewrite), with one field read at step 6 (reduce).

## Cause

Try.substitute held a second rewrite for except*, behind a type check. It substituted the body, the else, every handler and the finally against the scope standing before the try, and exported nothing. So:

- a name the statement bound was read after it as the binding standing before it. A function local first bound inside a try* (the deferred finally's y in test_finally_holds_every_pending_return.py) is unbound at function entry, so the return after the statement read an unbound local: after discharge the only exit was a NameError halt and no completed record held the return;
- the else did not read what the body bound, a handler did not read what the body bound before it halted, and the finally read the pre-try state on every path.

The reduce side was already one (TryStarSugar runs try_sugar._and_finally_with_raise_context and _try_outcome). The copy was in the tree's rewrite.

## Change

- Try.substitute: the except* branch is deleted. TryStar.substitute is Try.substitute, and TryStar borrows the steps it takes (the way Match borrows the route merge).
- What except* does differently is stated on TryStar, by name, as three overrides of steps the one rewrite asks for:
  - _handler_matches: every arm may receive every body halt. except* matches the leaves of a group, so a raised class other than the arm's is not a miss. A decided match still stops an edge.
  - _arm_halt_point: none. An arm that falls through still leaves by the raise of the rest no arm matched, after every store it made, so no one statement's state is that raise's state; every name the arm changed is unknown under it (the existing arm_halt_state).
  - _arm_entry_state: the arms of an except* run in turn on one group. The rewrite states one arm per halt, which is an except* exactly where no arm but the last changes a binding. An arm that begins after an earlier arm changed one (a store, an object its calls may have changed, an as name the later arm does not bind itself) is refused by name (SugarNotWritten, owner TryStar.substitute). It is not begun from the body's halt as if the earlier arm had not run.
- TryStarSugar takes finalbody_halted and hands it to the one finally, as TrySugar does: a halted arm runs the copy substituted for the halted faces.
- Try: the one-statement halt point and the arm entry state are named steps (_arm_halt_point, _arm_entry_state); for a try they answer what the inline code answered.

## Deleted returns, raises and guards

- Try.substitute: the guard on type(self) is not Try, and its early return of the keyed node (the whole except* branch).
- Inside that branch: the guard that recorded handlers only when a handler changed or was keyed, and the guard that recorded body, orelse and finalbody only when changed. Both are subsumed by the same guards of the one path.
- Moved, not deleted: the guard that an arm has exactly one halting statement is now Try._arm_halt_point (same condition, same answer for a try).

Added exits: one raise (the named refusal above), TryStar._handler_matches returns True, TryStar._arm_halt_point returns None.

## Tests

Not run locally; CI measures.

Expected to move to green:
- test_finally_holds_every_pending_return.py::test_a_deferred_try_star_finally_resolves_with_the_callers_actual

New, test_try_star_one_temporal_rewrite.py: a name the body binds is read after the statement (and its lying twin: not the binding before it), a finally reads what the body bound, an earlier arm that binds is refused by name (twin: arms that change nothing run in turn), an earlier arm's as name a later arm does not bind is refused (twin: the same as name on both arms runs).

Expected to stay red, for a different reason than today: test_exception_group_nesting.py::test_nested_handler_preserves_temporal_bindings_across_inner_try_star. Today its return after the try reads an unbound local. With this change the first arm's store before a second arm is refused by name. Its law (the value on one completed arm) needs each arm threaded from the state the arms before it left, and TryStarSugar deciding the route slots on each face. Not written here.

## Not removed here

- The route and edge slots the rewrite mints are not grounded by TryStarSugar: a binding joined over one is read under both of its arms (undecided, never one arm's value).
- Module threading for readers still declares every name a try* binds undecided (_module_uncarried_names, the as name apart). That is pinned by test_module_global_evaluation_reference.py and is left as it is.

second ways removed: the except* branch of Try.substitute (a second temporal rewrite of a try statement); second ways added: none

part of #3436, the metric half. The span half is a separate PR.

**What changes.** An owed metric kind was re-read on every turn while the store refused it. Each kind now gets the log exporter's counted window, **per kind**. After `k` refused reads of a kind in a row, the next `2^k − 1` turns that touch that kind skip its read, with `k` capped at 6. A skipped turn fails exactly as a refused read does: that kind's updates go to `Partial.uncounted`, its turn counts in `failed`, and nothing of it is applied or written. A read that lands resets that kind's `k`. `recover()` always reads every kind. A turn that does not touch a kind spends none of its window. A batch refused for overflow does spend one, because it would have read the kind; it still counts no turn. No API change.

**Concurrency and cancellation.** Skips are spent last in the turn: after its reads and after `ensureActive`, under `lock`, with an identity compare (`if (owedReads[kind] === seen)`). So a caller cancelled in a later read of the same batch spends no skip.

**Sharing.** The window is a small internal `RefusedReadBackoff`, so the span half can reuse it. I left `WarpLogRecordExporter.kt` alone (#3444 is in flight), so its copy of the same few lines stays.

**Tests.** `WarpMetricExporterRefusedReadBackoffTest` (6) was red 6/6 on main (`955f0ab62`). Thirteen `WarpMetricExporterRefusedRecoveryTest` arms now step through the window: each spends the skip before the turn it measures.

**Mutations**, final suite, `--no-watch-fs --no-build-cache`, `compileKotlinJvm` EXECUTED every row (new class / RefusedRecoveryTest):

| Mutation | New class | RefusedRecovery |
|---|---|---|
| no skip | tests=6 skipped=0 failures=6 | 20/0/13 |
| skip runs the turn | 6/0/6 | 20/0/12 |
| `k` not reset on heal | 6/0/1 (heal arm) | 20/0/0 |
| uncapped (`k` to 30) | 6/0/2 (long outage, per kind) | 20/0/0 |
| one window shared across kinds | 6/0/2 | 20/0/2 |
| a turn without the kind spends its skip | 6/0/1 (sums' schedule) | 20/0/1 |
| skip skips `ensureActive` | 6/0/1 (cancellation) | 20/0/0 |
| skips spent before the reads | 6/0/1 (sums' skip spent) | 20/0/0 |

**Gate.** `:kuilt-otel:build :kuilt-otel-sdk:build --max-workers=2 --no-watch-fs` is green. The cached test tasks were re-run with `--rerun --no-build-cache`: jvm 519/0, android debug and release 493/0. The new class is 6/0/0 on jvm, both android variants, `macosArm64`, `iosSimulatorArm64` and `wasmJsBrowser`, and each test passes run alone. One SDK rig count changed (`KuiltMetricExporterBatchTest`): the bridge's retry after an overflow now skips the gauges' read, so the store refuses one read, not two.

**Unpinned on.** The window is only as good as "a skipped kind is in `refused`". Mutation row 2 reds 18 tests when that breaks.

author: mohammadchehab
body:
## The problem

`commandInvariants.ts` is the guard chain every project, bot, delegation, MCP server, group and thread command passes. Twenty of its twenty-two throws carried no refusal code, and each one interpolates an internal id into a sentence. Web has routed these failures through `commandFailureMessage` since #231, so acting on a view another device already moved on rendered the server's sentence verbatim — `Thread 'abc-123' does not exist for command 'thread.archive'.` — in the toast the user reads. That is the ordinary multi-device case, not the exceptional one.

## The codes

Four new literals and one reuse, per the architect's ruling on TASK-288 (comment #3). Each keeps `detail`, so the log line and the unknown-code fallback stay exact.

| Code | Sites | Sentence |
|---|---|---|
| `stale-view` | 9 | Something here has changed. Refresh to see the latest. |
| `already-exists` | 6 | It already exists. Refresh to see it. |
| `entity-archived` | 3 | It is archived. Restore it first, then try again. |
| `workspace-root-in-use` | 1 | Another project already uses that folder. Choose a different one. |
| `bot-not-a-group-member` | 1 (reuse) | already shipped, no new copy |

## Every call site, enumerated

The card's count was disputed (21 in the sweep, 20 verified, 22 in the architect's scan). Settled by reading the file: **22 `invariantError` call sites, 20 of them uncoded.** Two already carried a code before this card (`actor-not-a-group-member`, `environment-rights`) and are untouched.

| Function | Line | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `requireProject` | 99 | `stale-view` |
| `requireProjectAbsent` | 117 | `already-exists` |
| `requireProjectWorkspaceRootAbsent` | 144 | `workspace-root-in-use` |
| `requireBot` | 162 | `stale-view` |
| `requireBotAbsent` | 177 | `already-exists` |
| `requireDelegation` | 196 | `stale-view` |
| `requireDelegationAbsent` | 211 | `already-exists` |
| `requireBotArchived` | 230 | `stale-view` |
| `requireMcpServer` | 252 | `stale-view` |
| `requireBotNotArchived` | 270 | `entity-archived` |
| `requireMcpServerAbsent` | 290 | `already-exists` |
| `requireGroup` | 308 | `stale-view` |
| `requireMutationActorAuthorized` | 334 | `actor-not-a-group-member` (already coded) |
| `requireEnvironmentManageRights` | 360 | `environment-rights` (already coded) |
| `requireGroupOwnedThreadMutationAuthorized` | 395 | `stale-view` |
| `requireGroupAbsent` | 413 | `already-exists` |
| `requireGroupMember` | 436 | `bot-not-a-group-member` (reuse) |
| `requireActiveGroupMember` | 458 | `entity-archived` |
| `requireThread` | 480 | `stale-view` |
| `requireThreadArchived` | 498 | `stale-view` |
| `requireThreadNotArchived` | 518 | `entity-archived` |
| `requireThreadAbsent` | 543 | `already-exists` |

## Why the stale-view sentence says "something here has changed"

The architect's first draft was "This no longer exists", and this PR originally had "It has already been removed". Both are false at two of the nine sites: `requireBotArchived` and `requireThreadArchived` fire when the entity **exists and is not archived** — the client asked to unarchive something already unarchived. The architect adopted the corrected sentence and recorded the rule: *a code's sentence must describe the client's situation, not the server's object.* The same test was applied to the other two families and they hold at every site — `already-exists` is true at all six creates, `entity-archived` at all three archived states.

`detail` still carries `Bot 'B' is not archived for command 'X'` with the id, so the log and the fallback lose nothing.

## Ordering

The thread guard chain (`requireThread`, `requireThreadArchived`, `requireThreadNotArchived`) is the chokepoint every thread command passes and is already live on web, so it was coded and tested first; the rest of the family follows. This is one PR because the whole slice is written and green now — splitting it would not land the thread trio any sooner.

## Tests — 38 new, red-checked

After the rebase the three touched files run **43** tests; the five extra arrive from #241, #244 and #247 sharing `commandFailure.test.ts` with this card. The 38 below are the ones this card adds.

- **20 server** (`commandInvariants.refusals.test.ts`, `it.effect`): one per site coded by this card, asserting `refusal` is the literal **and** `detail` still contains the id. Reverting the three thread throws turns exactly its three tests red. A 21st test reads `commandInvariants.ts` and fails if a new `invariantError` call site arrives without a code.

  That guard originally matched `invariantError(` only when it ended the line, so a one-line `Effect.fail(invariantError(command.type, detail))` slipped past it with no code at all — the security-architect caught it. It now brace-matches **each** call and requires that call's own arguments to carry a `CommandRefusalCodes` member. Per call rather than a file-wide tally, because a tally can be offset by a stray code literal elsewhere and hide exactly the throw it exists to find. The counts ride in the failure message instead of being asserted, so a legitimate new coded site does not break it.

  Parens are matched against a mask that blanks comments and string literals to spaces while preserving length, so offsets still line up. Without it an unbalanced `(` in a detail string ran a call's scan past its own `)` and let it swallow the next call's code literal. Comments are masked in the same pass because an apostrophe in one (`// thread's rows`) would otherwise open a "string" that blanks real code.

  Red-checked five ways: a legitimate **coded** one-line site passes; an **uncoded** one-line site fails; an **uncoded** site *plus* a stray `"stale-view"` literal still fails, where the global tally computes `calls=23, literals=23, difference 0` and would have passed; an **uncoded call whose detail string holds an unbalanced `(`**, followed by a coded call, fails — it was 21/21 green before the mask; and the restored file is 21 green with lint at 0.

  The test is marked **TEMPORARY** in a comment: TASK-304 makes the invariant failure a discriminated union so an uncoded throw cannot compile, and deletes this test when it lands.
- **14 client-runtime** (`commandFailure.test.ts`): `classifyCommandFailure` returns each of the four literals rather than `unknown`; each renders in en, ar and zh-CN pairwise different, with no `Bot '`, `Group '`, `Thread '`, `Project '`, `MCP server '`, `Delegation '`, uuid or filesystem path in the rendered string; an unknown code still falls back to the server sentence.
- **3 web surface** (`useChatActions.threadGuards.test.ts`): archiving a chat another device removed, archiving one already archived, and restoring one already restored — each drives the real action and asserts the toast description, the line the user reads. Reverting the helper call at `useChatActions.ts` turns all three red.

## Guard scope — why it stays file-scoped here

The architect asked whether the guard test should cover `OrchestrationCommandInvariantError` construction repo-wide, with an allowlist of registered exclusions, instead of reading only `commandInvariants.ts`.

Measured on this branch before the rebase onto `5ff9bd84e`: **93 direct construction sites across 17 files, 15 carrying a `refusal` and 78 not.** A hard-fail repo-wide guard therefore needs a 78-entry allowlist across 15 files — and that allowlist is exactly the register TASK-298 (11 exclusions) and TASK-303 (7 sites in `groups.ts`) are writing by hand right now. Building it here would duplicate both registers, in the wrong PR, and go red on 78 sites the moment it lands.

So it is too big for this PR, and it is not left implicit: **the repo-wide guard belongs to TASK-303**, which owns the `groups.ts` register and lands last of the three cards. Its allowlist should be the union of TASK-298's and TASK-303's registers; once that exists, this file-scoped guard folds into it.

author: danielaskdd
body:
## Description

The native DOCX table extractor (`TableExtractor.extract_with_metadata`) started every row at grid column 0 and ignored `w:gridBefore`. A row that starts late (its first grid columns have no cell) therefore had its cells shifted left:

- its text and paraIds landed under the wrong column headers;
- a vertical merge restarted in such a row was cached at the wrong column, so the continuation cell in the next row found no merge and the merged text was lost.

Example: a 3-column table whose first row has `gridBefore=1` and a merged "Total" in its last column extracted as `[["r0c1", "Total", ""], ["r1c0", "r1c1", ""]]`. It now extracts as `[["", "r0c1", "Total"], ["r1c0", "r1c1", "Total"]]`.

The legacy extractor already handles this (`_docx_table_grid_rows`), and its docstring states that it shares the native extractor's merge rules, so the two parsers disagreed on the same document.

## Related Issues

Follow-up to #4413, found while reviewing it.

## Changes Made

- Start each row at its `w:gridBefore` offset. `w:gridAfter` needs no handling: rows are pre-filled to the grid width.
- End a vertical merge in every column that has no restart or continuation cell in the current row, whether a normal cell or no cell at all (`gridBefore` / `gridAfter`) occupies it. A continuation therefore repeats only the row directly above, as in the legacy extractor. This end-of-row rule replaces the per-normal-cell `pop` added in #4413 and covers it.
- Walk rows and cells through `w:sdt` / `w:sdtContent` / `w:customXml` (same wrapper set as the legacy extractor's `_iter_docx_row_cells`). Before, a row inside a content control or custom XML element (a repeating section) was dropped, and a wrapped cell was skipped without advancing the grid column, so the cells after it shifted left. Together with the end-of-row merge expiry, a skipped wrapped continuation cell would also have ended its merge (Codex finding on 6af248b).
- A cell inside a placeholder or table-of-contents content control keeps its grid columns and paraIds but nothing else: no text is extracted from it, so its images are not exported (they would count against the shared image budget) and its list items are not counted, and its title-block features stay blank; a row inside one is left out. Same rule as the legacy extractor; without it, walking wrapped cells exposed placeholder text such as "Click or tap here to enter text." (Codex findings on 9af4c0032 and 5ee500881).
- A continuation that no merge reaches any more (orphaned) keeps its own first and last paraIds and no text. Before, its paraId scan ran only inside the active-merge branch, so it got `None` and a table ending in it gave `parse_document` a `uuid_end` that stopped at an earlier cell (already the case on `main` for a merge broken by a normal cell; Codex finding on a2d7700c1).
- Docstring of `extract_with_metadata` states these rules.

## How it works / what could break

- Tables without `gridBefore` and with well-formed merges extract exactly as before; the 1080 existing DOCX parser tests pass unchanged.
- Changed output only for: rows with `gridBefore` (now aligned), wrapped rows and cells (now extracted in place), and a continuation cell whose row above has no cell in that column (now empty instead of repeating an older merge). The second case follows the OOXML rule that a merge continues from the cell directly above, and matches the legacy extractor.

**Verified in Word** with a probe document (four tables, LightRAG's output printed under each):
- a `gridBefore=1` row is drawn with a gap in its first column, and a `gridAfter=2` row with only its first cell: matches the new output;
- a merge restarted in a late-starting row spans its own grid column in both rows: matches the new output (`main` put the text one column left and lost it in the second row);
- a continuation below a row with **no cell** in that column, and one below a **normal empty cell**, are both drawn as separate empty cells, without the merge's text or shading: matches the new output (`""`). The docstring records this rule.
- Edit targeting: paraIds in such rows now sit in the right grid columns, so `uuid` / `uuid_end` are unaffected for normal tables and correct for late-starting rows.

## Checklist

- [x] Changes tested locally
- [x] Code reviewed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if necessary): not needed, the rules live in the docstring
- [x] Unit tests added (if applicable)

## Additional Notes

Tests: `./scripts/test.sh tests/parser/docx` → 1111 passed. The new tests (`test_grid_before_row_keeps_cells_in_their_columns`, `test_vertical_merge_below_grid_before_row`, `test_column_without_cell_ends_vertical_merge`, `test_wrapped_continuation_cell_keeps_vertical_merge`, `test_wrapped_row_counts_like_a_direct_row`, `test_orphaned_continuation_keeps_its_own_para_ids`, `test_placeholder_cell_keeps_its_column_without_text`, `test_placeholder_row_is_left_out`, `test_placeholder_cell_content_is_not_extracted`) fail against `main`'s `lightrag/` package and pass with this change.

Differential check against the legacy extractor's `_docx_table_grid_rows` over 19 constructed tables (grid skips, spans, intact and broken vertical merges, wrapped rows / cells / continuations, placeholder controls): 11 differ on `main`, 2 with this PR.

Not in scope (both also differ on `main`): the native paragraph walk keeps the text of inline placeholder controls, in tables and in the body; and the native body walk (`parse_document`) and cell paragraph walk read direct children only, so block-level content controls outside or inside tables are not read. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.

body:
Part of #7757. Step 5 (construct: build or refuse by name).

## The wrong answer

`test_construction_testimony_conservation` (2 failing): `Node.sugar()` on a module-level `Constant` whose constructed value cannot be canonicalized returned green under a testimony reporter. It was a dropped loud gap, not a patch that missed the node.

Cause: `Backend.materialize_module` built the sugar of a module-level constant (`x = 1`, a provider member) itself. It called `_construct_sugar`, testified `present_fact` alone and seated the memo row by hand: a second way to make a node's sugar row. That row holds no `present_construction`. Memo rows are shared across reporters and replay their testimony (#7838), so a testimony reporter that asked later was served that row and never saw the constructed value. The coordinate was present with no testimony (`testimony_for` answered None for a constructed node), and a value the reporter could not content-address stayed green.

## The change

The provider value's sugar is `node.value.sugar()`, the one door: constructed once at its coordinate, with the testimony every construction gives stored in its row, a refusal remembered and reported by name (#8438). A testimony reporter served the row now hears `present_construction` and refuses a value it cannot content-address through its one typed door (`_testimony_gap`).

## Deleted returns, raises, guards

- `except BaseException: abandon_row(computation); raise` around the hand-seated row's `_construct_sugar` call. `Node.sugar` holds that path: a refusal by name is remembered, reported and re-raised; anything else abandons the row and re-raises.
- `assert node.value.sugar() is value_sugar`: the value is that call's result now.

## Tests

- `test_construction_testimony_conservation`: the fixture opens the file under a roll of its own, so the collector hears the testimony roll alone (the open constructs the constant under a reporter that builds no testimony, and that roll hears it present). New truthful test: a module constant's testimony reaches a testimony reporter that asks after the open. The patched, uncanonicalizable constant is the lying half: loud, one gap, no present answer beside it.
- `test_constructed_module_backend_door::test_source_file_constructs_and_seals_inside_one_reporter_event` pinned exactly one `present_construction` at the open (the receipt), which is the missing testimony. It now reads: the receipt is presented once, last, after one presentation per provider member.

Not run locally; CI measures.

## Not finished here

`test_repeated_sugar_reraises_the_memoized_panic_without_new_roll_mass` still needs the next PR: a reporter that refuses a served row's testimony is marked as having heard it, so its second ask is green.

second ways removed: the backend's hand-seated sugar row for a provider value (`_construct_sugar` + `present_fact` + `close_row` outside `Node.sugar`); second ways added: none

The config is already applied, and the old classic branch protection was removed in favor of the rulesets. Copilot reviews keep running from the existing hand-made ruleset, which Terraform no longer manages. The `.gitignore` now also ignores local Terraform files.

body:
## Summary

Local review runs save their notes and saved repro tests in a `review-artifacts/` folder at the repo root. Git showed every one of those files as a new, untracked file, so `git status` was noisy and it was easy to commit them by mistake. This PR tells git to ignore everything inside that folder. Nothing in the product changes.

## Repo impact map (mandatory)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    GI["Repo git settings (.gitignore)"] -->|"new: ignore review-artifacts/*"| WT["Local working tree (git status)"]

    classDef touched fill:#ffd54f,stroke:#f57f17,color:#000;
    class GI touched
```

## What changed

- `.gitignore`: adds `review-artifacts/*`, so files written there by local review runs stay out of `git status` and out of commits.

## How to review

Trivial tier (pr-review.md §A.5): one line in `.gitignore`, no code and no change to how the product behaves.

### ✅ Quick start (≈ 2 min)

| # | Commit | What it does (plain words) | Review with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `362bd4f09` | Git ignores the files inside `review-artifacts/` | Part 3 · Step 1 |

### Part 0: The change in one picture

On my machine `review-artifacts/` holds 98 files (1.2 MB) from earlier review runs. With the old `.gitignore`, 66 of them showed as untracked in `git status` (the other 32 were already hidden by older rules). With this change, 0 show.

### Part 3: Review steps

**Step 1: git ignores the review-artifacts folder ⭐ ⏱ 2 min**
- **Open:** `.gitignore`, find the line `review-artifacts/*`
- **What it does:** before, every file a local review run wrote into `review-artifacts/` showed in `git status` as untracked, and `git add .` would stage it. Now git ignores them.
- **Check:**
  1. Is the rule anchored to the repo root (`review-artifacts/*`), so it can't hide a folder with the same name deeper in the tree?
  2. Does `git ls-files review-artifacts` on `main` print nothing, so the rule hides no file that is already tracked?
- **Example:** `git check-ignore -v review-artifacts/saved-repro-tests` printed nothing before. Now it prints `.gitignore:128:review-artifacts/*`.
- **Test:** no test: verified only by `git check-ignore` and the before/after `git ls-files -o` count in Part 0.

### Part 6: Red flags

- ❌ If `git ls-files review-artifacts` lists any file on `main`: those tracked files would keep being tracked, but new files next to them would be hidden by mistake.
- ❌ If the diff touches anything other than `.gitignore`: this PR must not change any code, docs or CI.

## Code-path diagram

N/A - `.gitignore`-only change. No runtime code path changes.

## Safety axes

### Sandbox boot impact

N/A - no work added to sandbox boot path.

### Idempotency

N/A - no API surface changed.

### Failure-path consistency

N/A - no multi-step write path changed.

### L4 / host-port-pool changes

N/A - neither touched.

### Cluster correctness

N/A - no cluster path changed.

### Mount inputs

N/A - mount inputs unchanged.

- [x] `git check-ignore -v review-artifacts/saved-repro-tests` → `.gitignore:128:review-artifacts/*`
- [x] `git ls-files review-artifacts` on `main` → empty (no tracked file is hidden)

- [ ] CI (DCO + gate)

Blast radius: only what local `git status` shows for contributors who have a `review-artifacts/` folder. No product, SDK, schema or CI change. Rollback: `git revert` this commit.

body:
After #443, GL's Frame/Extrusions stayed about 1% above the `main` before it. Part of that was per-frame work #443 added on GL, which this removes:

- A storage buffer rewritten each frame was uploaded with `glBufferData`, so the driver allocated and cleared new storage every time. Same-size rewrites now go through `glBufferSubData`, as the old GL backend did.
- Each draw made the context current through an `Rc` clone; the open pass now holds it current.
- The clip masks rebuilt their tile map (a `Vec` per tile) and their projection bytes every frame; they keep both. The frame's clip tiles are sorted only when they aren't already.

Instructions, millions a frame, GL (radeonsi):

| | `main` (`3a66b13a`) → this PR | before #443 (`f68eb512`) → this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Still/chicago | 3.545 → 3.540 (−0.1%) | 3.978 → 3.540 (−11.0%) |
| Still/sanfrancisco | 1.890 → 1.884 (−0.3%) | 2.160 → 1.884 (−12.8%) |
| Still/norway | 0.734 → 0.732 (−0.3%) | 0.848 → 0.731 (−13.8%) |
| Still/CollidingIcons/1024-overlap | 25.88 → 25.84 (−0.2%) | 46.17 → 25.83 (−44.0%) |
| Frame/Extrusions | 0.802 → 0.798 (−0.5%) | 0.791 → 0.798 (+0.9%) |
| Frame/Extrusions/DataDriven | 0.819 → 0.815 (−0.5%) | 0.808 → 0.815 (+0.9%) |

Method: `mln-bench run --json`, LTO release builds, 6 processes a side in ABBA order, the median of each process's median; user-space instructions from `perf_event_open`.

What stays above the old backend on Extrusions, about 7 k instructions a frame over its ~56 draws, is the interface's own per-draw cost, which the old GL drawable didn't have because it called GL directly. By callgrind, per frame: the draw's O(1) checks (`check_draw`, 3.5 k), the three id lookups (1.5 k), comparing and recording what the open pass has bound (4.6 k), the renderer's check that a drawable's bindings still hold (2.4 k), and building the `Draw` and the `dyn Gpu` call (2.1 k). Each is constant per draw; other GL work that #443 made cheaper offsets part of it.

Validation CI doesn't run: the render suite is byte-identical to `main` on WebGPU, Vulkan, GLES and desktop GL, and `just test` passes on GL (llvmpipe).

author: quolu
body:
a149 (Trony's row, split confirmed): the production members exchange to ccb49250 failed twice at 13:37 JST 11/15. It hit MEMBERS_DRAIN_TIMEOUT, then MEMBERS_NOT_ACCEPTING on the retry (the retry half is Belota's #1547).

## Cause
- The members exchange drains every members lease (60 s).
- `conversation-assembly.mjs` invoke registered each conversation root's members lease on `result.completion`. For `user.turn` that is the whole turn, so any running Owner turn held a members lease for minutes and every exchange timed out.
- The lab passed because it has no long turns. The new test hangs on the old code and passes on the new.
- This contradicts the existing design note in members-admission.md: "acceptedが返った後のAI/job完走はこのcompletionへ含めない".

## Change
- `conversation-assembly.mjs`: the members lease tracks `result.accepted ?? result` (a turn's acceptance, or a root's reply). The conversation lease still tracks `completion`.
- `conversation-execution-effects.mjs`: a room root (`room.post` / `room.reply`) returns once its deliveries are issued, not accepted. Its `execution.notify` fan-out therefore re-enters members with a fresh `withLease`, like the fork answer relay and reports. N102 found this; it is the only conversation-side case.
- Kiro checked the execution side: lease assertions happen only before acceptance, and wake, restart and configure are their own roots. N102 checked the conversation side: finishing a user turn, callbacks and durable receipts never read members under the root lease after acceptance.

## Impact (function map / DFD)
- execution `members-admission.md`: new row 「会話rootのmembers lease（a149）」 (lease lifetime = acceptance; room fan-out fresh).
- Carrier: BODY.

## Tests
- New `test/a149-members-lease-acceptance.test.mjs`: a members drain completes after the turn's acceptance while the turn still runs. It hangs (cancelled) without the fix.
- `conversation-execution-effects`: 12/12, including the new room.post / room.reply fresh-lease cases.
- `conversation-execution-lifetime`: 1 pass / 7 fail on both main and this branch (an identical baseline; AitermGenerationClient reference assertions).
- `execution-conversation-joint`, `execution-assembly`, `conversation-preservation`: hang past 200 s on both main and this branch (baseline), not compared further.
