author: divyuuu
olety
body:
L2-37 PR-1 of 3 (ARCH-0067 #idle-fold-policy, RESEARCH-1333 E+; plan lanes/post-untangle/plans/PLAN-L2-37.md). It records the data that the keep, fold or expire decision will read. No code acts on it yet.

- `IDLE_FOLD_WAITS`: one row per parked canonical wait. It is written in the commit that parks the attempt under its trap (`park_and_bind_wait_trap`). The row holds the session kind from the dispatch's caller origin (connected, hosted or unknown), the wait class from the trap (user = human or consent; tool = peer; budget traps are not recorded) and the wall-clock park time.
- The return time is written in the delivering commit (`deliver_in_txn`) at the delivery's time. A run that resumes with no delivery closes its row when its wait rows retire, at the vault clock. A reply already delivered at the park closes the row at once, with gap 0.
- `coach.idle_return_tables`: a nightly Coach maintenance job. Once a week it rebuilds `IDLE_FOLD_RETURN_CELLS` from the last eight weeks of rows. Each cell is one session kind, wait class, four-hour band and weekend flag (the owner's zone from the reminder route, else UTC). It holds the sorted return gaps and the count of waits that never returned (open for a day, or back after more than a day). Rows older than the window are deleted. It is closed form: no model call, no proposal.
- Recording never refuses a delivery: the row read is lenient. The facet constant has its own module because coach.rs is at 791 lines.
- Test doors: `test_doors::idle_fold` (cfg `oneiron_test_support`). Tests: `crates/oneiron/tests/idle_wait_returns.rs` (5 tests).

Stored rows (STORED-CHANGE-RULE): keep. The change is additive: two new side tables, and no existing row changes meaning.
No verb is added, no grant is read, nothing is spent.

author: huayc09
body:
## Summary

- Support standard-agent TypeScript and Python handlers on Linux using the existing Node permission model and Python audit hook, while retaining the macOS Seatbelt launch path.
- Close a Linux read-scope bypass in which ESM named imports could retain unwrapped Node filesystem functions and follow a Study symlink to sibling evidence.
- Replace macOS-only sandbox and network claims in the hosted-action runtime contract with per-platform, per-binding facts.

## Implementation

The Node bridge now synchronizes builtin ESM exports after installing its realpath filesystem wrappers. Default imports and named imports therefore encounter the same read-scope checks.

The runtime contract now records:

- macOS as `macos_sandbox_exec`, with OS sandbox enforcement and network denial.
- Linux as `linux_runtime_guard_only`, without OS sandbox enforcement or Seatbelt equivalence.
- Linux TypeScript networking as unblocked by the Node permission model.
- Linux Python networking as denied by the Python audit hook.

The macOS `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` command, profile handling, and `macos_sandbox_exec` receipt kind remain unchanged.

## Regression coverage

A new test places sibling Study evidence behind a symlink inside the declared Study read root and reads it through an ESM named `readFileSync` import. Before the fix, the handler returned the sibling secret. After the fix, execution fails closed with the realpath scope violation.

A contract conformance test also prevents restoration of the misleading scalar `current_sandbox_kind` and `network_allowed` claims.

## Verification

- Focused sandbox and contract tests: **17 passed, 0 failed**.
- `npm run typecheck`: passed for the root project and both workspaces.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.

## Scope and limitations

- This is focused verification, not a full-suite or production-readiness claim.
- macOS runtime behavior was not exercised in the Linux verification environment.
- No real network exfiltration test was performed.
- Linux remains reduced runtime-guard isolation and must not be described as Seatbelt-equivalent.

author: watany-dev
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"watany-dev"} -->
_Requested by **watany** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U73kMa9N8Th4xMXXCFTB2g?thread=cmsg_01U73kMa9N8Th4xMXXCFTB2g3AZKtsQneUcH4HbrSxzKZR)_

## What and why

A bug hunt over the Phase 1 code (#7) with generated inputs instead of hand-picked cases. Each fix is one commit with the test that found it.

| Bug | Found by | Effect before |
|---|---|---|
| `parseRemoteUrl` threw `URIError` on a broken %-escape | fast-check over remote URLs | every command in that clone died, even with `--repo` |
| `--region` naming another region still counted as "in the clone" | exhaustive check of `resolveContext` against the spec (7,680 combinations) | `pr create --region eu-west-1` in a us-east-1 clone drafted from local commits, pushed to the us-east-1 origin, and opened the PR in eu-west-1 |
| `git log` parsed on `\x1e`/`\x1f` | fast-check against a real temp repository, with git itself as the oracle | a message containing either byte split into a wrong title/body |
| Other people's titles, descriptions and rule names printed raw; `pr list` padded by UTF-16 length | fast-check over the formatters | escape sequences (screen clear, OSC 52 clipboard write) reached the terminal; Japanese titles pushed columns out of line |

## Decisions

- **Tool choice.** fast-check is the only new dev dependency (it depends only on `pure-rand`). I didn't add TLA+/Alloy: the state that matters is small and finite, so it is enumerated in TypeScript inside Vitest (`context.model.test.ts`, under 0.2 s). That keeps CI free of a JVM or extra toolchain.
- **`--region` mismatch** follows the rule `--repo` already had: same name, different region means a different repository. One existing test expected the old behaviour by accident (its point was flag precedence), so its flag region now matches the remote. The spec says so explicitly now.
- **Control characters** are shown in caret notation (`^[`), like gh does, rather than dropped, so the user can see something odd is in the title. Descriptions keep `\n` and `\t`, and CRLF becomes LF. Dry-run output echoes the user's own input and stays as it is.
- **Width** is a small East Asian wide range table, not a dependency. Combining marks and ZWJ emoji are approximated.
- **Regression guards that found nothing:** `pr create` safety rules over 3,000 random flag/state combinations (no push on `--dry-run`/`--no-push`, edit before push, no prompt without a TTY, never an empty title, branch on origin before the PR); I confirmed they catch a mutation (deleting the `--no-push` guard fails in about 600 runs). Also pagination against a mock service that picks its own page sizes, `mapLimit` order and concurrency, and `loadConfig` on arbitrary JSON.

## Run against the built CLI

Both `dist/` builds (main and this branch) ran against a local fake CodeCommit endpoint (`AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`) in temporary git repositories:

- origin `.../repos/a%zz`, `pr list --repo demo`: main exits 1 with `URIError: URI malformed`; this branch lists the PRs and exits 0.
- A PR title with `ESC]52;…BEL ESC[2J`: main writes 2 ESC bytes to stdout; this branch writes 0 and shows `^[]52;…^G^[[2J`. The Japanese title row lines up.
- A single commit `Fix\x1ethe parser` + body, `pr create --fill --dry-run --json`: main gives title `Topic` with two bullets; this branch gives the commit's subject and body.
- us-east-1 clone, `pr create --fill --dry-run --region eu-west-1`: main plans the PR from local commits after 4 API calls; this branch exits 2 (`--head is required outside a clone`) with no API calls.

`bun run ci` passes locally, except `lint:workflows`. There, zizmor's online audit gets a 401 from GitHub in my sandbox. The offline run reports no findings, and no workflow changed.

## Found, not fixed

- With a region mismatch, the message says "--head is required outside a clone of the repository", which is confusing when you are standing in a clone. It should say why the clone was not used.
- `consoleUrl` builds `https://us-gov-west-1.console.aws.amazon.com/…` for GovCloud (the real console is `console.amazonaws-us-gov.com`). `cn-*` URLs are also unverified. I couldn't check either without AWS.
- `pr list -L N` takes the first N ids in ListPullRequests order, then sorts them by last activity. So it shows the N most recently created PRs, not the N most recently active.
- `pr view`/`pr status` with no id scans up to 1,000 open PRs with one GetPullRequest each.
- A config file saved with a UTF-8 BOM fails as "invalid JSON".
- `pr create --title` with a newline, combined with the editor, loses everything after the newline (the editor buffer's first line is the title).

author: ruibinray
body:
## What this is

A whole Pilot mission was played from start to rescue by a script, through the game's own controls (E and Q, the panels, the Power Board, the Control Center), paying walking time for every trip and taking REGO's recommended answer on every emergency card. This fixes what it found.

**Result of the run:** rescued on Day 8, 08:01. Survivor, 3,823 points, 12 emergencies, 6 of 6 questions right. Health 100 throughout, no power cut, no frost, no script errors, but only 0.7 L of water left. Seed 1920914870, main at pull request 48.

## What it found, now fixed

| Problem | Now |
|---|---|
| When a meteoroid holed the Water Room, REGO said to lock the door. That froze the room and ended water recycling; it nearly lost the mission. | The Water Room and Oxygen Room are patched on a thinner margin of oxygen (0.3 kg left, against 1 kg for other rooms). Every leak card's "lock" choice says what is lost and what the rebuild costs. |
| REGO said nothing while water was on course to run out two days before rescue. | REGO and a yellow alert speak as soon as oxygen, water or food will not last until the rescue ship. |
| REGO said "turn the Water Recycler up" with the recycler's room sealed, and never mentioned a leaking pipe. | REGO names the dead recycler or the pipe first, and says when the repair needs more materials than you have. |
| The elevator took you up into a solar storm without a word. | Its prompt reads "Ride the elevator up INTO THE SOLAR STORM (radiation!)" while a storm is on. |
| "The battery is full" at 92%. | "nearly full". |

## What the run confirmed

REGO was never inside a wall or a machine at the twelve points checked, including beside the rover and after elevator rides. REGO's Battery Store advice appeared in normal play. The night-cold rule cost nothing with the heaters at the needed level. The pipe repair is logged. At night the meteor card recommended leaving the panel.

## How the fixes were checked

- In the browser: the same leak as in the run (Water Room, 2.0 kg of oxygen, from the Bunk Room) now recommends patching, and the lock choice names the Water Recycler and 5 materials; the water advice with a sealed room (with and without enough materials), with a leaking pipe, and when water will not last; the oxygen advice; the three "before rescue" alerts; the elevator's label in and out of a storm.
- `sim_test`, `frost_test`, `life_test`, `jobfx_test`, `radio_test`, `moonmap_test`, `follow_test`, `build_teachers --check`, `comment_scan` and `node --check` on every module pass.

## Limits

- Two earlier attempts at the run were thrown away because of the test tooling, not the game. In the final run a steering loop cost about eight game hours on Day 4.
- Not covered by the run: rescuing an astronaut, the Polar Ice Mine, the Water Plant, the hopper, the robot-arm builder, the job games, sound.
- Seen and not changed: five rooms were holed in one mission, which may be too harsh once materials run out.
- The mission has not been replayed whole with these fixes in.

body:
## Summary

- SD-13: PluginKit gains schema-taking overloads of the table DDL generators (add, modify and drop column, index, foreign key, check constraint, primary key, create table). Their defaults forward to the schema-less requirements, so a kit-44 plugin keeps working. Kit 44 -> 45, minimum unchanged.
- SD-13: PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Snowflake, DuckDB, Dameng, Trino and BigQuery qualify with the caller's schema and use the session schema only as the fallback. PostgreSQL's and Oracle's session schema now sits behind a lock.
- SD-13: Structure saves, Create Table, Compare & Sync and Object Copy pass their scope's schema. Compare & Sync names the target's schema, never the source snapshot's.
- SD-13: Oracle's column reorder plan, SQL Server's check constraint read, and Oracle's and DuckDB's DROP INDEX now name the requested schema. Dameng's CREATE TABLE goes out one statement per call. SQL Server's column rename brackets each part of the name `sp_rename` parses.
- AR-07: no `as? PluginDriverAdapter` left in `TablePro/`. `DatabaseDriver` gains `plugin`, `sessionQueryTimeoutSeconds`, `truncateTableStatements`, `dropObjectStatement`, `streamRows` and `streamExportRows`. `tableOperationEligibility` moves onto the protocol. The adapter's pure PluginKit forwards are gone. A SwiftLint rule refuses a new cast.
- UI-13: the Parts pane reads a new PluginKit capability, `PluginStorageParts`. The ClickHouse plugin owns the `system.parts` read and the OPTIMIZE, DROP and DETACH PARTITION statements. The pane shows for any driver that answers it, not for a type check.
- Not in this PR: AR-05, AR-06, IO-09, and the rest of DL-10 (the schema-less adapter overloads and the iOS `DatabaseDriver`).

## Test plan

- `PostgreSQLDDLSchemaQualificationTests`: every generator names the given schema; nil falls back to the session's.
- `MSSQLSchemaQueriesTests`: a schema named `[dbo]` or a table with a quote stays inside its own bracketed part.
- `PluginSchemaDDLDefaultsTests`: a driver with only the schema-less generators answers the new overloads.
- `SchemaSyncTargetSchemaTests`: Compare & Sync and a Structure save name the target schema.
- `DatabaseDriverPluginSurfaceTests`: the adapter witnesses each lifted member through the protocol; a double answers none.
- `StructureServerSupportTests`, `StructureAvailabilityTests`, `StoragePartsGridTests`, `ClickHousePartStatementsTests`: the Parts pane follows the capability.
- `verify.sh plugins`, `abi` (changed, kit 45, minimum 19), `ios ConnectionCoordinatorCatalogTests` and `lint`.

body:
Closes #232

## 変えたこと
- ブラウザのタブを出している間、ページの上の端に URL バー（`app/src/browser/UrlBar.tsx`）を出す。今のページの URL を出し、中継しているタブは中継前の元の URL（`o y` でコピーするものと同じ。タブが持つ `url` をそのまま出す）。戻る・進む・読み込み直すのボタンも並べた（`o h` `o l` `o r` と同じ `navTab`）。
- URL バーを押すか `o u` で、キーがバーに移って書き換えられる。`Enter` で開き、`Esc`（またはキーがほかへ移ったとき）は元の URL に戻す。`Esc` はキーをページに戻す。`o u` の入力の窓はなくした（`UrlDialog` は `o n`・`o N` だけ）。
- 打ったものが URL ならそれを開き、そうでなければ Google で検索する（`tabs.ts` の `urlOrSearch`）。
- ページの場所は、URL バーの高さだけ上の端を下げる（`overlay.ts` の `pageBounds` に `top` を足し、`BrowserArea` が `[data-overlay-top]` の高さを測る）。シークレットのタブでも同じに動く。
- `docs/keys.md`・`docs/key-design.md`・`README.md`・`README.ja.md` を直した。

## 決めたこと（作業役が決めてよいとされたもの）
- 見た目は、ページ内検索の欄に合わせた細い帯。ボタンは並べた（理由：普通のブラウザと同じで、`o h` `o l` `o r` と同じ動きなので増える決まりがない）。
- URL と検索語の分け方：`://` 付きは URL（http と https 以外は開けないので、バーの枠を赤くして開かない）。scheme を省いたものは、空白が無く、host が「.」で区切った名前（`example.com`）か `localhost`・`127.0.0.1`・`[::1]` のときだけ URL。それ以外（空白を含む・`foo` のような「.」の無い一語・`hello.` のように「.」で終わるもの・`user@example.com`）は検索。`javascript:` のような `//` の無い scheme は、検索語にせず開けないものとして断る。
- 新しいタブの入力の窓（`o n`・`o N`）は、Issue が「今の入力の窓と同じ決め方に足す」のはバーの話なので、これまでのまま（検索しない）。
- バーの中のキーは `FindBar` に合わせた（`Esc`・`Enter`、かな漢字変換中は無視）。ブラウザ側の Cmd+L のような近道は足していない（Issue の範囲外。`o u` で足りる）。

## 確かめたこと
- `npm test`（`urlOrSearch` と `pageBounds` の `top` のテストを足した）・`go test ./...`・`tsc` が通る。`nix fmt` の差分なし。
- 実機の画面では確かめていない（キーの移り方とページの下がり方は、ページ内検索の欄と同じ仕組みを使っている）。

body:
## Why

The trial-nurture worker selected `plan_status=trial` nurture accounts with `LIMIT 50` and no `ORDER BY`. There are now 54 such rows, so the 4 newest `signup_verify_reminder` accounts never entered a run. The 48h cap recorded 8 `verify_reminder_too_old` skips at 08:40 GMT on 15 Nov, but the 9th too-old skip and one still-eligible reminder (due window ends about 13:09 GMT today) were left unprocessed. No nurture email of any kind has gone out today.

## Change

Selection still keeps a batch size of 50, but:

1. **Exclude non-pending rows before the limit.** A row is pending when `decide()` would `send` or `skip` on this run (including `verify_reminder_too_old`), or when a verify-reminder contact has already verified and must be promoted to `signup_finish_setup`. Complete sequences and not-yet-due / 24h-throttled waits are not pending. Pending is decided with the same `dueAt()` / `decide()` / softphone remapping the worker already uses, so other products are unchanged.
2. **Deterministic due-first order:** earliest next-step due time, then `enrolled_at`, then `id`.

The worker loads trial-status nurture rows plus their steps, runs `selectPendingTrialNurtureBatch()`, and only then processes the 50. No copy or template changes.

## Test

Regression in `tests/pendingBatch.test.ts`: 50 complete or not-yet-due rows, then later pending rows including a verify-reminder `too_old` skip, an eligible verify-reminder send, and a due `generic_softphone` send. Asserts those later rows are selected and that `decide()` records the expected skip/send.

author: spy4x
body:
<!-- agent -->
Closes https://github.com/spy4x/seed/issues/993

## In short

Offline, the palette now searches the notes saved on the device with `@spy4x/search`, the engine the commands already use: a typo (`notse`) or the other keyboard layout (`тщеу`) finds a note called "note", the best match comes first, and a note whose body matched shows the text around the match. Every command the server must run stays listed offline, dimmed, with "Needs a connection". A failed note search for typed text now shows as a dimmed row under Notes, is said to a screen reader, and the commands stay; before, the whole list was replaced by the error line.

## Why

Seed promises that data lives on the device, so offline search must be as forgiving as online search, and an offline command that silently does nothing looks broken. Seed is the base of Financy.

## What changed

- `apps/spa/src/state/search.ts`: `notesOnDevice` builds a `@spy4x/search` index (label = title, text = body), searches it with `limit: NOTE_SEARCH_LIMIT`, and uses the hit's snippet (its text parts joined) when the body matched, else `trimNoteSnippet(body)` as before.
  - **Order: best score first, newest first among equal scores.** The server ranks `ORDER BY rank DESC, updated_at DESC` (`libs/server/notes/note-search.ts:101`), so this matches it. The index breaks score ties by input order, and the input is sorted newest first.
  - **The index is kept between queries** and rebuilt only when a note's id, group, date, title or body changes (the key is those fields as JSON). Building it per query cost 30 to 57 ms on 1,000 notes (see below), above the ~50 ms line on a loaded machine and more on a phone; searching the kept index costs 1 to 5 ms. I did not tie the cache to an open palette: a content key needs no palette lifecycle and can never serve stale notes.
  - **Only the first `NOTE_SEARCH_MAX_LENGTH` (200) characters of the query are searched**, the most the server accepts, so pasted text cannot stall the page (see the cost below).
- `deno.jsonc`: `@spy4x/search` added to the import map at 1.126.0, the version preact-components 14.8.0 already imports and the lock already held; `deno.lock` gained only the workspace dependency line.
- `libs/ui/search-palette.tsx`: a rejected `searchNotes` no longer fails the whole palette search. It shows `Search.error` ("Could not search. Change your search to try again.") as a dimmed row under the Notes heading, and the groups, commands, quick-create rows and records still list. No new translation key. A stale answer needs no special case: the palette drops it.
  - **The failure is announced.** The palette's own status line stays empty, since the rest of the list is still answered, so `SearchPalette` adds its own `role="status"` line (`sr-only`, `data-e2e="search-notes-status"`) that holds `Search.error` after a failed search for typed text and is emptied by the next search that works. It is drawn **inside** the palette's `<dialog>` with a Preact portal (`preact/compat`'s `createPortal`): the dialog is opened with `showModal()`, which makes the rest of the page inert, and a screen reader does not hear a live region there, so a line next to `CommandPalette` (outside the dialog) would never be heard.
  - **For the empty query nothing shows and nothing is said**: the recent notes are left out and the commands list as usual. The props JSDoc now says so.
- `libs/ui/palette-commands.ts`: one `SERVER_ONLY` list and one `needsServer` helper replace the two inline `disabledReason` expressions. `paletteCommands` applies the helper to every listed command whose id is in the list; `quickCreateRows` uses it for the group row. JSDoc lists the commands.

### Commands offline

| Command | Server-only offline | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| This page commands | no | The page provides them; out of scope here. |
| Go to: Overview, Notes, Tags, Activity, Groups, Notifications, Profile, Open benchmark | no | Navigation to pages that render from the device or show their own offline state. |
| New note, New tag (and their quick-create rows) | no | Queued offline (`offlineTags`, the notes offline layer). |
| New group (and its quick-create row) | **yes** | The group is made on the server (unchanged). |
| Theme | no | Stored on the device. |
| Settings sections (Account, Sign-in and security, Language and region, Appearance, Notifications, API tokens, Delete account section) | no | Navigation to a profile section; each section's own forms handle being offline. |
| Download my data | **yes** | `/api/account/data-export` (`apps/spa/src/state/data-export.ts`). |
| Change profile picture | **yes** | An upload; `profile-picture.ts` answers `ProfilePicture.offline` without the server. |
| Keyboard shortcuts | no | A local dialog. |
| Keep your account (guest) | **yes** | Signs the guest in with an address or provider on the server. |
| Install app | no | The browser's install prompt. |
| Delete my account | **yes** | Its confirmation calls the server. |
| Turn off two-factor sign-in | **yes** | Checks the current code on the server. |
| Sign out of all other devices | **yes** | Ends sessions on the server. |
| Sign out | no | `signOut` (`apps/spa/src/state/auth.ts:548`) signs the page out at once and owes the server's sign-out until it is back. |

### Admin and the website

The admin palette (`libs/ui/admin-palette*.ts*`) has no note search and no offline mode, so it has no counterpart to change. The website's claims (`i18n/site/en.ts:648`, `:1094`-`:1103`) are about forgiving search in general and stay true; `docs/` has no statement this makes untrue.

## Timing (1,000 synthetic notes, title of three words, body of 60 words)

A one-off script on this machine (16 cores, load average 22 to 37 during the runs), median of 10 runs:

| Query | Index built per query | Kept index (shipped) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `budget` | 40 to 57 ms | 3 to 5 ms |
| `budgte` (typo pass) | 35 to 50 ms | 1.4 ms |
| `икуфв` (layout pass) | 33 to 50 ms | 3 to 4 ms |
| no match | 30 to 51 ms | 1 to 2 ms |

**A 10,000-character query** of real words cost 860 ms (median) per query before the 200-character cap, with the index built per query. With the cap it costs 57 to 85 ms with a fresh index and 18 to 24 ms with the kept index. The query is the person's own text, so the cost falls only on their own tab.

## Branches and the tests that cover them

| Branch | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Server reachable | `asks the server, and answers its notes as not from the device` (existing) |
| Server unreachable / no call possible / proxy answer | `searches the device when the server cannot be reached…`, `searches the device without asking when no call can be made…`, `searches the device when a proxy answers for the server` (existing) |
| Server refusal rejects | `passes on a refusal of the server, such as the rate limit` (existing) |
| Empty query | `answers the selected group's newest notes first for the empty query` (existing) |
| Typo and wrong layout offline | `finds saved notes offline despite a typo or the other keyboard layout` |
| Score order, newest among equals | `ranks the best match first offline, the newest first among equal matches` |
| Hit with body snippet / title-only hit | `shows the text around a match in the body offline, else the body's start` |
| Limit | `answers at most 20 notes offline` |
| Query cap | `searches the device for the first 200 characters of a longer query only` |
| Kept index rebuilt on change | `finds a saved note by the text it was changed to since the last search offline` |
| Failed note search under Notes, commands kept | `shows a failed note search under Notes, in a dimmed row, and still lists the commands` (replaces `shows the error line when the search fails`, whose behaviour this changes) |
| Failure said in a live region inside the dialog, cleared on success, silent for the empty query | `says a failed note search for typed text in a live region inside the palette, and clears it once a searc

author: stiffjobs
body:
## Problem

The component keeps the runtime options (`apiKey`, `testMode`, retry settings, `onEmailEvent`) in one `lastOptions` row, and every `lib.sendEmail` call replaces it when its options differ. `makeBatch` and the webhook callback both read that row, so options are last-writer-wins across every caller of one mounted component.

This shows up with Convex Auth v2 (`@convex-dev/auth` 2.0.0). Its documented setup passes `components.resend.lib.sendEmail` to `setupEmailPassword`, and it calls that mutation directly with `{ apiKey, testMode: false, initialBackoffMs: 30000, retryAttempts: 5 }` and no `onEmailEvent`. In an app that also has `new Resend(components.resend, { onEmailEvent })`:

- after any auth email, webhook events for the app's emails no longer reach `onEmailEvent`, until the app sends another email;
- if the two callers use different API keys or retry settings, a batch is sent with whichever was written last.

Two `Resend` instances with different options on one component have the same problem.

Minimal repro against `main`: call `lib.sendEmail` with `onEmailEvent: { fnHandle }`, then again with other options and no `onEmailEvent`. `lastOptions` holds only the second caller's options.

## Change

- New `emailOptions` table (indexed by `options.apiKey`), and an optional `optionsId` on `emails`. `sendEmail` finds or creates the row for its options and stores the id on the email.
- `makeBatch` splits a batch by `optionsId` and enqueues one Resend batch call per options set, each with its own API key, retry settings and rate-limit slot.
- The webhook callback uses the options of the email the event is for.
- `lastOptions` is still written, and is the fallback for emails enqueued before this change (no `optionsId`) and for `sendEmailManually` emails. The behaviour described in #124 is unchanged.
- `get` leaves `optionsId` out of its validator and return value, so the component API is the same.

## Behaviour to be aware of

- An email keeps the options it was enqueued with. Events for emails sent before an app changes its `onEmailEvent` function go to the old handle.
- `emailOptions` rows are not cleaned up: one row per distinct options set, each holding an API key as `lastOptions` already does.
- A mixed batch makes one Resend call per options set.

## Testing

`npm run check` passes (38 tests, 5 new). The new tests cover: one row per distinct options set, a mixed batch sent with each caller's key, the `lastOptions` fallback, and an end-to-end case with two clients where only the app's email runs the app's callback. Four of the five new tests fail without the `lib.ts` change; the fifth guards the manual-email behaviour.

Not run: `npm run build:codegen` and `npm run test:e2e`, which need a Convex deployment. No file in `_generated` should change, since `dataModel.ts` derives from `schema.ts` and the `get` return type is the same.

This overlaps with the batching rewrite in #117; happy to rebase onto it.

## Phase 5d — returns, damaged products, contact and the support inbox (SRV-02, SRV-03, SRV-05)

Last sub-phase of Phase 5 (decision 82). Spec: `2026-11-12-phase-5-orders-accounts-design.md` §7.

### API (`apps/api/src/support/`)
- `POST /api/support/returns`, `POST /api/support/damaged` (multipart, 1–5 photos, ≤10 MB, JPEG/PNG/WebP checked by content), `POST /api/support/contact`. Storefront origin only, throttled per IP (`THROTTLE_SUPPORT_LIMIT`) and per order (`THROTTLE_SUPPORT_ORDER_LIMIT`), hidden honeypot field.
- The order is matched by the customer session, or by order number + phone exactly like the order-status lookup (same normalization, constant-time compare, one identical 404). A signed-in customer can also report on an order placed as a guest by giving the phone; the guest order is never linked to the account (decision 77).
- Returns and exchanges: delivered orders only, until the end of the Israel day of delivery + `returnWindowDays` (default 14, editable in the admin). Damaged reports: delivered orders, no day limit.
- Damaged photos: processed (upright, metadata such as GPS removed, one WebP ≤1600 px), stored only under the private storage folder, served only to the admin.
- Each ticket (numbers from 5001) queues two outbox e-mails: a confirmation to the customer ("קיבלנו את פנייתך, מספר פנייה …", never echoing text the customer typed) and an alert to `SUPPORT_EMAIL` without customer details.
- A delivery change request from the SMS link now also opens a `delivery_change` ticket.
- Additive change to the order view: `orderItemId` on each line, `deliveredAt`, `returnUntil`.
- Migration `support`: `support_tickets` (sequence from 5001), `ticket_notes`, `ticket_attachments`, `store_settings` (row 1, 14 days).

### Admin
- "פניות" inbox (`support.manage`, added to the customer-service template): filters by type and status in the URL, new-ticket badge in the menu, ticket page with contact, order link (refunds stay on the order page), lines, photos (full size in a new tab), internal notes with author and time, and an explicit "עדכון סטטוס" button. Every change is audited (notes without their text).
- "ימי החזרה" setting (1–60), for Super Admin / `orders.manage`.
- Separate commit: order status buttons now read "העברה לסטטוס: …" instead of "קדם לבהכנה".

### Storefront
- `/returns`, `/returns/damaged`, `/contact` (noindex, not in the sitemap). Order step by number + phone (the lookup token stays in memory only) or from the account; photo picker with previews and limits checked before upload; inline error mapping; focus and live regions for keyboard and screen-reader users.
- Links "החזרה או החלפה" (until the deadline) and "דיווח על מוצר פגום" on delivered orders (order page and account), carrying only `?order=<number>`; footer links.

### Checks
- API unit 376, API e2e 379/379 (24 files, clean full run), storefront 531, admin 130 (also with `TZ=UTC`); `tsc`, lint clean.
- Browser check (dev, mock providers): contact, return and damaged forms signed out and signed in, delivery change → ticket, private photos (401 without an admin session, 404 under another ticket, not under `/media`), admin inbox, notes, status, settings — with the test admin signed in by the owner.

### For the owner
- **Interim:** customer-service phone, e-mail and WhatsApp in `core/support-contact.ts` are placeholders until the business sends the real numbers.
- **Kept until you decide:** damaged-product photos have no retention period yet (spec §9.5).
- **Return window:** 14 days to the end of that Israel day — please check against the legal returns wording.
- **New Hebrew copy to review:** ticket e-mails, ticket type and status labels, form field and error messages, the signed-in intro texts, the admin inbox, ticket page and "ימי החזרה" texts, and the new order status buttons. The full list is in the 5d task reports (`task-15/16/17-report.md`, `final-fixes-5d-report.md`).
- **Known, deferred:** contact-form order numbers are linked unverified (the admin page says so); uploads are buffered in memory (≤50 MB per request, set the proxy body limit in production); a repeated identical lookup error is not re-announced to screen readers.
- **Windows dev only:** the random worker crash (exit 3221226505) is most likely a libuv bug in Node 24.15 on Windows, fixed in Node 24.16+; Linux is not affected.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Overnight integration branch for the **artificial scientist swarm** This is the one integration line: PRs #28, #30–#37 and #39–#42, plus the eval-swarm, held-out and Ig Nobel committee work, are merged here in sequence. Ariel authorized merging once this wrap-up landed.

### What changed (high level)
- **Swarm / orchestration (`swarm.py`)**: `--resume` with heartbeat and checkpoints, detached attempts, per-round commits. Rounds are synchronous: workers take turns and results are recorded at round close.
- **Fair evaluation (`held_out.py`)**: BixBench mini is split 10 dev / 7 held-out test, and the swarm only sees dev scores. Playworld mini uses disjoint test seeds `300_000–300_199`. The final best is graded once on the test split.
  - The cached `held_out_test.json` is reused only if `baseline_commit`, `best_commit` and `grader_sha256` (a hash of the task's grader files) all match. Otherwise the held-out score is recomputed.
- **Contamination guard**: BixBench forces Exa/literature off, and `answer_literal_qids` rejects candidates that hard-code a gold value. Statistical constants and tolerances are exempt.
- **Ig Nobel consolidated into the swarm** (`testcases/ignobel/`): preregistration, a real public dataset, one registered Spearman test, p<0.005, |ρ|≥0.1, split-half consistency, citation verification and an Exa prior-work check. Confirmed studies are then scored by two non-Kimi committee judges (`committee.py`; defaults gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3.5 on Tinker; `IGNOBEL_JUDGE_BASE_URL` / `IGNOBEL_JUDGE_API_KEY_ENV` / `IGNOBEL_JUDGE_{A,B}_MODEL` point it at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint):
  - `score = 0.25 + 0.75*min_judge(min(laugh, think))`
  - The committee fails loudly on HTTP 402 or a missing key, and retries transient HTTP errors and read timeouts.
- **Lab / Pages**:
  - Replay-only static site in `docs/`, built from the real `out-ignobel` recording.
  - Progressive first load, proximity bubbles, status strip, run finale with Wilson CI, orchestration swimlane, "How it's judged" explainer.
  - **Visual-first redesign** after hostile desktop + phone UX reviews (40 and 39 issues): opens straight into the 3D Lab with a grow-in loader and autoplay; satire badge, joke headline and the intro text wall removed; swarm framed and centred on phone; tap a scientist / status tile to focus it and open its bubble; short highlight replay by default; results as charts (test funnel, tools-used counts computed from the recording: 119 Exa searches, 357 source cards, 157 past.dev recalls, 123 writes).
  - Results show `Committee verdict: no award` with a ranked score chart and the judge model names when every committee score is < 0.5; `Finalists — awaiting committee judging` only for unjudged recordings; the podium only for real awards.
  - `scripts/export_pages.py`: a run whose in-run losses were gate-only keeps the `split-half consistency loss` label (in manifest, event text and frame messages; recorded LLM calls stay verbatim) even after post-run `award.issued` events are added, and its proxy note names the judges and best score from those events.
  - Mobile fixes: overflow, coach mark, collapsed dock, "Loss" label.
- **Video (`video/`, Remotion)**: 2-minute demo with real Lab footage replayed at a measured 7.10× (269.7 s real capture in 38 s), shown on screen as "7.10× speed · replay of a real run (Kimi + Exa + past.dev)". The MP4 is not committed. It was captured before the Lab redesign and needs a footage-first re-cut.

### Results (all real runs)
| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| BixBench mini v2 (real Kimi, research off) | Dev loss 0.10. **Held-out 6/7 vs baseline 1/7** (n=7, Wilson 95% ≈ 0.49–0.97). |
| Playworld mini (synthetic proxy, not PlayWorld/Genie 3) | Held-out over 200 episodes: loss 0.872 → 0.253. |
| hadamard19 | Reaches the known optimum (loss 0), a ceiling, not a record. |
| Track 3: boredom swarm (B) vs meter off (A) vs single agent (S) on 18 held-out bixbench_numeric Qs | **Exploratory; neither ordering is significant.** See the breakdown below. |
| Ig Nobel run (Kimi + Exa + past.dev), stopped at round 13/15 when Tinker credit ran out | **21 registered, 13 run, 11 passed the preregistered gates, 10 also pass the \|ρ\|≥0.1 floor added after the run.** Known relationships in public teaching datasets, not discoveries. The ρ≈0.07 coordinate study is the failure case; it shows as a second confirmed row only because the critic re-ran it. The Pima bmi~skin hypothesis was re-run on a second split after failing; one Exa paper appears as six source cards. Largest confirmed p ≈ 3.4e-7. **Post-run committee (gpt-oss-20b + MiniMax M3.1 Flash on NVIDIA NIM, Exa prior-work lookups): no award.** 11 confirmed studies scored; top 7 tied at 0.2/1, the other 4 at 0.1. Both judges gave THINK 2–3/10: correct but textbook. |
| past.dev vs local TF-IDF memory | 419 real memories, 40 hand-written probes. See the breakdown below. |

**Track 3 breakdown.** Each set is 3 runs per arm. The seed controls orchestration only; Kimi's sampling is not seeded.
- **Preregistered primary (guard2, stopped early, guarded):** B 0.26 > S 0.24 > A 0.11. B leads S on mean only because a known guard false positive (integer loop bound) zeroed S on run 3001; S beats B on the other two runs. Smallest observed sign-flip p = 0.5.

Parity TC-CLH-3 / TC-CODE-AUTH-12 / TC-CLO-1 (TeamCode `TeamCode-On-Behalf-Of`, docs/cloud-sessions.md "Principals and the effective member" and "Attribution and audit"; domain/cloud/CloudSessionService.kt `actor()`, presentation/CloudRoutes.kt `onBehalfOf()`).

## Contract (planned, `runners.cloud.onbehalf.v1`)
- Header parameter `Ostrom-On-Behalf-Of` (member id or login, `A-Za-z0-9._-`, 1-64) on `createCloudSession`, `stopCloudSession`, `pauseCloudSession`, `resumeCloudSession`, `setCloudSessionGithubAccess`, `setCloudPermissionBypass`.
- Only an owner/admin signed in (USER credential) or an administrator's `cloud:admin` service key may name another member; otherwise 403 `on_behalf_forbidden`. Target not an active member: 422 `invalid_effective_member`. Several or malformed values: 400 `invalid_on_behalf`.
- Create on behalf: effective member = owner, `githubAccess: none`, 422 `github_owner_consent` on a profile requiring GitHub; remote sessions never on behalf (403). GitHub access and bypass stay owner-only (403 `github_owner_only` / `bypass_owner_only`).
- `CloudSession.createdBy` = `CloudAttribution {initiatorId, credentialId?, effectiveMemberId}`.
- `AuditEvent` gains optional `effectiveMemberId`, `credentialId` (journaled `cloud.session.created/paused/resumed/deleted`).
- Capability key `runners.cloud.onbehalf.v1` (no hyphen: the capability regex forbids it; TeamCode has no key for it, but an Ostrom server without it would silently ignore the header, so clients gate on it).

## Kotlin
- `run.ostrom.core.api.OnBehalfOf` (header, error keys, pattern), `CloudAttribution` + `CloudSession.createdBy`.
- Client: `cloudSessions.create/pause/resume/stop(..., onBehalfOf)`; malformed reference -> `IllegalArgumentException` before any request. Tests in `CloudSessionCreateTest`.

author: heidari-dev
body:
Closes #88

Adds the opt-in kill switch on Windows. `--kill-switch` and the desktop toggle work there now; both stay off by default.

With it on, Windows Filtering Platform filters (one sublayer, ALE connect and receive-accept, IPv4 and IPv6) block everything except loopback, the `kite0` adapter, Kite's own connection to the relay (by program and address), DHCP and IPv6 link discovery. They go up before the tunnel's routes and come off after them, so a dropped phone or a missing adapter never leaks, DNS included. The session redials with the existing backoff.

The filters belong to no engine session and are not persistent: they survive a Kite crash (as the Linux blackhole route does) until `kite restore`, `kite disconnect` or the next connect without `--kill-switch`; a reboot or a restart of the firewall engine clears them. The service does not lift them when it starts again after a crash. `kite restore` and the uninstaller lift them too.

Deliberate differences from the issue text: the permit for the local network is not there (only the relay's address), and the filters are volatile rather than persistent so a reboot cannot leave the machine offline.

Tests: unit tests for the filter set, the condition encoding and the relay address handling; `scripts/tun-smoke.ps1` takes the tunnel's routes away and checks that a connection to 1.1.1.1 and a DNS query to 8.8.8.8 work without the kill switch, fail with it on and the relay dead, work after disconnect, and (after killing the daemon or service) fail until `kite restore`. I could not run the WFP calls locally (no admin), so CI is the first real run.

No new dependencies; `kite-win` only gets two more `windows-sys` features (WindowsFilteringPlatform, Rpc). The new `unsafe` is in `kite-win/src/firewall.rs`, each block with a SAFETY comment. Reviewed with rust-review and security-review; findings fixed except two documented gaps (hard-block flag, interface permit under weak host mode).

author: shd-isac
body:
## Runtime issue reproduced by user

The Apple Silicon ad-hoc test app at `/Applications/PlayCover-SecurityTest.app` starts successfully, but still prompts to move to Applications. Clicking Move renames/relocates it to `/Applications/PlayCover.app`.

## Root cause
`AppIntegrity.swift` hardcodes the expected URL `/Applications/PlayCover.app`, checks containment by substring, and performs a best-effort delete of that destination before copying the running bundle. An alternate app filename incorrectly triggers the dialog and may replace a preexisting production installation.

## Fix
- Determine installation by checking whether the resolved **parent directory** of the running bundle is `/Applications`, regardless of its `.app` name.
- Preserve the source bundle's filename when moving from another location.
- **Never delete or overwrite an existing destination**; report file errors instead.
- Reuse the actual `Bundle.main.bundleURL` rather than deriving it from Resources.
- Preserve the existing Xcode-development launch exemption.

## Validation
CI should compile and lint this change. Manual checks: named test build in `/Applications` must show no move prompt; a standard PlayCover build in `/Applications` should be unchanged; launching from Downloads must not overwrite an existing destination; confirm macOS 27.2.1 runtime. No change to signing, SIP, AMFI, Gatekeeper or official release workflow.

This is a separate issue from Sparkle dynamic-library signing in PR #4.

author: farhanaliraza
body:
An HTTP server removes the spaces and tabs around a header value (RFC 9110 section 5.5). `TestClient`, `AsyncTestClient` and `WebSocketTestClient` gave the value to the request pipeline as the test wrote it. Thus a test and `runbolt` gave different answers. An earlier mutation testing session reported it for API keys. Base `master`, no stack.

## Reproduction

A route with `APIKeyAuthentication(api_keys={"key1", " lead"})`. The server column is a real `runbolt` on TCP, with a raw socket that sends `X-API-Key:<value>`.

| header value | `runbolt` | `TestClient` before | `TestClient` after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"key1"` | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| `" key1"` | 200 | 401 | 200 |
| `"key1 "` | 200 | 401 | 200 |
| `"\tkey1"` | 200 | 401 | 200 |
| `" lead"` | 401 | 200 | 401 |
| `"lead"` | 401 | 401 | 401 |

So the test client differed from the server in the two directions. A key that starts with a space authenticated only in a test.

The test `test_a_header_value_loses_its_outer_spaces_and_tabs` failed before the fix: the handler got `' \t a  b\t '` and not `'a  b'`. It checks `TestClient`, `AsyncTestClient` and `WebSocketTestClient`. It is not a case of `parity_cases`, because httpx (h11) refuses to send such a value to a real server (`Illegal header value`).

## The change

Three lines: the two `handle_request` transports in `testing/client.py` and the header list in `testing/websocket.py` apply `.strip(" \t")` to each value. The spaces inside a value stay.

**For the merge decision:**
- A test that sent a header value with outer spaces or tabs, and read them in the handler, now reads the value without them. This is what the server gives.
- Library code outside `django_bolt/testing` does not change.
- The CHANGELOG entry is at the end of the "### Fixed" list, so a conflict with other pull requests on that line is expected.

## How was this tested?

- [x] `uv run ruff check python/django_bolt python/tests/test_testclient_production_parity.py`: "All checks passed!"
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check` on the three changed Python files: no file listed
- [x] `uv run pytest python/tests -n 4 -q -p no:cacheprovider`: 5158 passed, 43 skipped
- [x] bolt-mcp, which uses the same test clients: `uv run pytest tests -q` in `python/bolt-mcp`: 235 passed
- [x] Manual run: a `runbolt` server on a port and a raw socket for the server column of the table, and the same values through `TestClient` before and after
- [ ] No `server_integration` test added (httpx cannot send the value)
- [ ] No Rust change, so no Rust tests

## Performance consideration

Test clients only. The server does not run this code.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01LwJUCVqhN9d9uKz16g2H5U

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01LwJUCVqhN9d9uKz16g2H5U)_

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

**Did the PR touch the hot request path?** No. The PR changes only test-client code. The diff touches four files: `CHANGELOG.md`, `python/django_bolt/testing/client.py`, `python/django_bolt/testing/websocket.py`, and `python/tests/test_testclient_production_parity.py`. No server, router, middleware, or Rust file changed. The `strip` search found no changed call in the server modules. The only new `strip(" \t")` calls are in the three testing-client paths.

**Is the added work wasteful?** No. The work is small and required for the stated fix.

- `BoltTestTransport` and `AsyncBoltTestTransport` (`client.py`, lines 132 and 200): each header value now gets one `.strip(" \t")` call. The loop that builds `headers` already existed. The cost added is one string operation per header per test request.
- `WebSocketTestClient._find_handler_via_rust` (`websocket.py`, line 196): `list(self.headers.items())` became a list comprehension that strips each value. The cost is the same order: one string operation per header per connection setup.

The change matches the PR goal. Test clients must send header values that the server would send. Without the strip, a test could pass or fail for a value that the real server would handle differently. The cost is in test code only, so it does not affect production request latency.

**Limits of this review.** I confirmed what the diff changes and where the change sits. I did not read the Rust or server-side header parsing, so I did not verify that the server trims values exactly as `" \t"`. That is a correctness question for the parity claim, not a hot-path question.

# [meroctl] every help says instance

## Description

#5074 (in 1.0.0-rc.26) renamed `meroctl context` to `meroctl instance` and `--context`/`-c` to `--instance`/`-i`, but missed the help text:
- `meroctl --help`'s examples still read `context create` and `call --context`;
- `instance alias add` showed `<CONTEXT>`;
- many subcommand descriptions said "the context".

I found this while walking the docs quickstart on the rc.26 build. This PR changes the doc comments to say instance. The restore path now matches what the node actually uses, `{backup-dir}/{app}/`.

  meroctl --node local context create --package com.example.kv --name notes

body:
## Parallel component (independent of G3 writer integration)
Adds an offline research utility to inventory evidence for a *bounded* Linux document-writer security review. It does NOT participate in authorization or mint a certificate.

## Function
- Requires ten explicit categories: signed effects, separate UID bypass checks, revocation, restart, crash recovery, resource limits, rights/consent, original-six X3 correspondence, independent review, and rollback.
- Rejects missing/extra categories, stale commit labels, duplicate/unsafe paths, symlinked files and mismatched SHA-256 bytes.
- Even on passing structural inventory, always returns `certified_for_production:false` and `universal_physical_protection_proved:false`.
- Seven adversarial unit tests and dedicated non-deploying CI workflow.

## Verification boundary
Packet/reviewer metadata are user-supplied and *unauthenticated*. Matching file hashes do not establish evidence truth, external review, consent or physical X3 proof. `ready_for_independent_review` denotes only a complete *self-described* inventory, never a security certificate. Require actual independent authentication, threat-model review and runtime acceptance tests elsewhere.

## Coordination
Separate draft branch off current `main`; no changes to #463 writer or its recovery/authorization integration, no Lean source edits, no live system and no secrets. Please keep unmerged until reviewed as a distinct auxiliary audit-preparation tool.

author: kapji
body:
An excess reportable income (ERI) figure of 0 was never compared with another figure for the same holding and period. So cgt-calc silently used the non-zero one, whichever file it came from, and never told the user that their `--eri-raw-file` disagreed with its own data.

A nil figure is now compared like any other: an equal one is skipped with a warning and a different one stops the run, as #1466 describes for other figures. The error for any such conflict is also clearer: it names both figures and says where the other one is.

## Example

A made-up holding of the HSBC ETF `IE00B64PTF05`, under the ticker HSBX:

1. 1 June 2022: buy 100 units at GBP 10.00, with GBP 5.00 fees.
2. 1 August 2023: sell the 100 units at GBP 11.00, with GBP 5.00 fees.
3. The `--eri-raw-file` has one row: `IE00B64PTF05,31/12/2022,GBP,0`.

- cgt-calc's bundled HSBC data gives GBP 0.06330 a unit for the year to 31 December 2022: 100 x 0.0633 = GBP 6.33, added to the cost.
- Allowable costs with the bundled figure: 1,000.00 + 5.00 + 5.00 + 6.33 = GBP 1,016.33.
- Gain: 1,100.00 - 1,016.33 = GBP 83.67.
- Before: the user's 0 was dropped without a word, and the run reported this gain.
- After: the run stops with:

```
ERROR: Two different excess reported income figures for HSBX for the period ending 2022-12-31: 0 GBP a unit on the row below, and 0.06330 GBP a unit in cgt-calc's bundled data. cgt-calc cannot tell which is right. Check the fund's report, then correct or remove the row below.
2022-12-31 Excess reported income, price 0 GBP
  N/A (ISIN IE00B64PTF05), read from row 2 of eri.csv
```

The reverse case stops the same way. Before, a user figure for a period where the bundled figure is 0 was used without a word.

## What changes

- A nil figure is compared with an earlier figure for the same holding and period. Figures less than 0.0001 apart are skipped with the existing "Skipping duplicated ERI transaction" warning, and different ones stop the run.
- The conflict error is reworded for every conflict, including two different non-zero figures. It names both figures, says which one is on the row printed below it, and says whether the other is in cgt-calc's bundled data or on row N of the user's `--eri-raw-file`. It replaces the message that began "A conflicting ERI report", which #1466's description quotes.
- A nil report still stays out of the calculation, so the text report and the PDF are unchanged. It is kept only for the comparison, in a new `eri_reports` map beside `eris`, with the row it was read from.
- A nil figure is compared with one in another currency as stated, without an exchange rate, since nil is nil in any currency. Two nil figures were never compared before, so they never needed a rate, and they still do not.

The message can tell the two sources apart because of the order the rows are read in. The bundled files are read before the single `--eri-raw-file`. No fund and period appears twice among the 14,931 bundled rows, and cgt-calc refuses a ticker that two ISINs claim. So bundled figures never conflict with each other: the row printed below the message is always the user's, and an earlier row from another file is cgt-calc's bundled data.

## Who is affected

- A run stops only when its `--eri-raw-file` has a row for a share class the portfolio holds, for a period that the bundled data or an earlier row of the same file also covers, with 0 on one side and 0.0001 or more on the other. Before, the non-zero figure won silently in each such case.
- Each user row equal to a bundled nil figure, and each repeated nil row in the file, now prints one duplicate warning.
- Rows for funds the portfolio does not hold, and rows with no other figure for their period, are unaffected.

The likely trigger is figures typed by hand for HSBC, SPDR or JPMorgan ETFs before cgt-calc bundled them (#1464, #1466, #1469). The bundled data holds 4,703 nil figures among its 14,931.

## Limits

- A row whose fund distribution date falls in a period of non-residence is left out before the comparison, as before.
- A user row can no longer replace a bundled nil figure, as it silently did before, and still cannot replace a non-zero one. If the bundled figure is wrong, it has to be corrected in cgt-calc's data.

## Tests

The calculator tests cover a nil figure before and after a non-zero one, two nil figures (skipped, and kept out of the calculation), and, for a period with no published exchange rate, a nil figure in pounds against a nil one in dollars, and against a dollar figure in either order. A CLI test runs the example above against the bundled HSBC figure and checks the whole error. The error's two sources are each checked: cgt-calc's bundled data in the CLI test and a calculator test, and a row of the user's own file in another calculator test.

author: olety
body:
FIX 2230 (OF-067 A, #2120): "a restore leaves a withheld file as the checkout holds it; if the file is gone, the restore's post-check fails rather than recreating it."

## What changes
- `restore_repo_snapshot` (crates/oneiron/src/repo_mutation/snapshot.rs) skipped every withheld entry, so a committed secret file that the checkout no longer held stayed gone. The checkout then no longer recaptured as the snapshot, and a crash-recovery post-check on that row reported divergence.
- The vault keeps no byte of a withheld file. The restore now reads the bytes the snapshot head commits at each gone withheld path, from the repository's own object store (`commit_files`, shared with the secret remediation). When custody still withholds those bytes, it writes them anew. The checkout then recaptures as the snapshot's own entry.
- The file is created owner-only from its first byte (0600, or 0700 when the entry is executable). It is never written over an existing file (`create_new`) or through a symlink (`O_NOFOLLOW`).
- What stays as before:
  - A gone withheld file that the head does not track (a T2 file) stays gone. It re-materializes from the vault alone, never from a snapshot (ARCH-0069 S4).
  - A withheld file the checkout still holds keeps its bytes and its permissions. The restore never runs `set_executable` on it, because that would widen an owner-only file to 0644.
  - A withheld path at or inside a linked checkout is left as it is.
  - Lift-marked entries take the same rule, because the restore treats them as withheld.

## Tests
`cargo test --locked -p oneiron --all-features --test repo_snapshot_withheld_restore` (crates/oneiron/tests/repo_snapshot_withheld_restore.rs):
- `a_restore_recreates_a_committed_withheld_file_the_checkout_lost`: red on main, green on the head.
- `a_restore_leaves_a_gone_untracked_withheld_file_gone`: a guard, green on both.
- `a_restore_keeps_a_held_withheld_file_and_its_owner_only_mode`: a guard, green on both.
- `a_restore_leaves_a_gone_declared_file_gone_however_its_declaration_is_spelled` (review round 2): red at b14c61e89e5 (round 1's head plus this test file, `opus-fix-custody/withheld-restore-r2-red` 2979f4df80e), green on the head. Main never recreates a file, so the test passes there.
- `a_restore_goes_on_when_a_gone_withheld_files_committed_bytes_are_lost` (second review, P3-1): red at 48911c59975 (round 2's head plus this test, `opus-fix-custody/withheld-restore-lost-blob-red` 396d423b732), green on the head. Main never reads a commit for the restore, so the test passes there too.
The recreation test and the held-file guard run on unix only, where the restore recreates a withheld file.

Stored change: keep (no stored row or encoding changes; the fork hash is unchanged).


### Review round 1 (Sol xhigh; fixed at b14c61e89e5)
- #1 A path custody declares is vault-resident: a T2 file there comes back from the vault under its lease, never from a commit, so a lease that expired stays torn down (`SnapshotExclusionSet::declares`, `SnapshotCustody::declares`).
- #2 Off unix no file is owner-only from its first byte, so the restore recreates no withheld file there.
- #3 The file is created through its directory's held descriptor, as a T2 file is (`secret_lease::written::Target`: O_NOFOLLOW walk, O_EXCL 0600 create, the post-open re-walk). An ancestor that moved since the walk writes nothing and removes the empty file again; an executable is set 0700 through the handle before its first byte.
- #4 The snapshot head's commit is read through a ref pinned at that head, not at the caller's revision.
- #5 A path at or inside a linked checkout is skipped before any blob is read.
- #6 The test file carries the clippy allow for its own git subprocesses.
Not tested: #1 needs a served repository's secret manifest to declare a path; covered by code read.

### Review round 2 (Sol xhigh; fixed at 48911c59975)
- #1 A declaration with a `.` component or a doubled `/` (`<root>/config/./secret.env`, `<root>//secret.env`) is admitted by the T2 writer, whose walk reads the path by components. The snapshot matcher compared literal strings, so the restore did not see such a file as declared and recreated it from the commit after its lease expired. A declaration and the snapshot root now match by their `/`-separated components (`secret_snapshot::lexical_path`). `..` stays as spelled, because the T2 writer refuses it. Snapshot ingest reads declarations the same way, so it excludes such a path too (it only withholds more). Tested, as above.
- #2 A refusal by the re-walk (a symlinked ancestor) returned before cleanup, and `Links::Sole` left the empty file in place when it had a second name. Every failure after the create (the re-walk refusing or reporting a move, the chmod, the write) now removes the file this restore created, through the held directory, with `Links::Any`, as the T2 guard does for a fresh file. No empty or partial file is left to stand in for the committed one.
- #3 The created file's handle stays open through that identity-checked removal, so its inode cannot be reused by an unrelated file.
- #4 The recreation test is `#[cfg(unix)]`.
- Also: `std::io::Write` is imported on unix only (an unused import off unix).
Not tested: #2 and #3 are races between the create and the re-walk, and no test hook reaches that window. Covered by code read.

### Second review (OPUS-REVIEW2-MONEY, Opus; lanes/kimi/OPUS-REVIEW2-MONEY/reviews/8290.md, read at 48911c59975): P1 0, P2 0, P3 1. Fixed at 0f387dfde6e.
- P3-1: `withheld_files_to_recreate` propagated every Git error (`GitWire::new`, `open_repo`, `resolve_commit`, `commit_files`) before the restore's write loop. A snapshot whose head commit, or one gone withheld file's blob, the object store had lost (a gc after a reset, a shallow or partial clone) then failed the whole restore, where main writes every other entry. Now a head that does not read recreates nothing. Each gone path reads its committed bytes on its own, so a lost blob keeps only its own file gone. Both cases log a warning without the path. The restore goes on, and the post-check reports the file as before. Custody's own read (`SnapshotCustody::of`) still propagates its error. Tested, as above.

author: zui-0000
body:
### 対応内容

- `schema/` に TypeSpec で API を定義し、`schema/dist/openapi.yaml`（OpenAPI 3.2）を出力する
  - 書き方（構成・命名・エラー・レスポンス）は [typespec-schema-template](https://github.com/zui-0000/typespec-schema-template) の規約に合わせた。リソースは `schema/contexts/{resource}/`
  - サンプルとして Todo の API（一覧・取得・作成・更新・削除）を置いた
- orval で `src/generated/api/` に fetch クライアントを生成する（`vp run gen:api`。Vite Task なのでキャッシュが効く）
  - 生成物は `.gitignore` し、`package.json` の `prepare` で `vp install` のときに生成する
  - ベース URL などの共通処理は mutator の `customFetch` に置く
- README をセットアップと vp のコマンドだけにした
- `docs/09` に手順と理由を記録した

### 対応背景

フロントエンドのテンプレートとして、API の型とクライアントをスキーマから生成できるようにするため。間に OpenAPI を挟むので、バックエンドの言語を問わずに同じ契約を共有できる。

### 確認

- [x] `vp check` と `vp test` が通る
- [x] `schema/` を変えた場合、`vp run gen:api` を実行し、`schema/` の差分（`schema/dist/openapi.yaml` を含む）をコミットした

### 特記事項

- `schema/dist/openapi.yaml` はコミットし、`src/generated/` はコミットしない。契約の変化は PR の差分で `openapi.yaml` として見え、生成コードの差分は PR に混ざらない
- OpenAPI 3.2.0 は、同じスキーマを 3.1.0 と 3.2.0 で出力して orval の生成結果を比べ、完全に一致することを確かめた
- clone 直後の `vp install` だけで `src/generated/` ができることを、node_modules も生成物もないコピーで確かめた
- この PR の上に #8（TanStack Query・Router・MSW・Zustand）を重ねている

### 参照

- `docs/09-TypeSpec と Orval による API クライアント生成.md`
- https://github.com/zui-0000/typespec-schema-template

author: rozievkomiljon
body:
## What

S4 (STEP 3 of the plan): practice mode.

**Start from the catalogue.** A section button on a catalogue card opens a start choice:
- **Exam rules**: the whole section, official time, one play of the audio, no help. Nothing about the exam rules changes.
- **Practice**: all parts or a single part, with no timer, the section's time, or the part's share of the section time. The server keeps the deadline, so the clock is not client-side.

**Backend** (`apps/core/practice_mode.py`):
- `POST mock/exams/<id>/start` accepts `groupIds` (≤10, unique, must belong to the section) and `timer` (`none|section|part`; `part` requires a part). These are allowed only for `mode=practice` with exactly one skill.
- The attempt's question scope is narrowed to the chosen part(s). The part timer is `max(60 s, ceil(share/60)·60)`, where the share is the part's question count over the section's.
- A timed start no longer resumes a practice attempt for the same explicit skill, and vice versa. A start with different practice options also does not resume. A mode-only resume still keeps the owned practice attempt, as the readiness contract requires.
- `POST mock/attempts/<id>/reveal {questionId}`: practice, in progress, a Listening/Reading question in scope. It returns the key and the evidence, and records the reveal on the attempt. Exam attempts get `403 PRACTICE_ONLY`.
- The attempt detail returns the Listening `audioScript` only for an in-progress practice attempt, and marks revealed questions.

**Exam window, practice only:**
- Listening player: speed (0.75–1.5×) and ±10 s.
- An audioscript toggle for the part.
- **Show answer** on each Listening/Reading question.

None of these render under exam rules; the single-play player is unchanged.

**Results:** a practice attempt is always raw (correct / asked, %), never a band, whatever its length. The result table marks questions whose answer was shown.

No migration in this PR: the reveal list lives in the attempt's existing `mediaState`.

## Checks

- pytest: full suite green, plus `tests/test_practice_mode.py`.
- `scripts/verify_practice_mode_postgres.py`: 16 PASS. `verify_review_evidence_postgres.py`: 22 PASS.
- tsc: clean. eslint: 0 errors. vitest: 781/781. next build: OK.
- New E2E `scripts/e2e-local/practice-mode.mjs`: 5/5.
  - One part with its clock: Passage 2, questions 14–26, 19:59.
  - Show answer.
  - Raw result, with the shown answer marked.
  - Listening tools: 1.25×, ±10 s, audioscript.
  - The same section under exam rules: single-play player and no tools.

Research-only review of **13 additional source groups** using publicly readable sample book/catalogue/chapter pages, official EPUB documentation and published source terms.

**Best technical candidate for Chinese cultivation fiction:** WuxiaClick. Public title, complete ordered chapter index (e.g. 2,276 Martial World entries) and readable chapter pages. Still needs automated archiving permission and runner metadata validation; no source enabled.

**Best direct EPUB candidate for fanfiction:** AO3, which has an official per-work EPUB download flow. Verify permitted automated usage and rate limits before implementation.

body:
Closes #168. Closes #167. Part of #155.

## Summary

The Visitor switches Locale from the Command palette or with `lang` at the prompt, and the Session ships Spanish at `/es`.

```diff
 <SessionTerminal>
   useSession()
+    lang | lang <code>  → setLocale → navigates / ↔ /es
   <SessionPromptBar v-model:theme
+                    v-model:locale>
     <SessionCommandPalette>
       theme   light / dark / system
+      lang    English / Español
```

One page key for every Locale keeps the Session mounted across the navigation, so nothing in `useSession` had to be reshaped:

```ts
// app/pages/index.vue
definePageMeta({ key: 'session', scrollToTop: false })
```

```diff
 i18n/locales/
   en.json
+  es.json                 # every key en.json has
 app/data/
   en/ profile.ts experience.ts
+  es/ profile.ts experience.ts
 routeRules
   '/':   prerender
+  '/es': prerender
```

Job titles, company, people and technology names stay as written; Recommendations stay verbatim in English with a Spanish provenance line.

Also on this branch: `pnpm look --path /es` (look opens any Locale and reports where the page ends up and what it fetched), and the banner's missing space in "ppadron.page— Pavel Padron".

## Evidence

- **Before:** a switch remounted the page and the Session started over.
  ```
  ✗ keeps the Transcript, with each echoed Command where it was
  ✗ reprints an echoed Output in the new Locale
  ✗ keeps the prompt history        expected ['lang es','help'], got ['','']
  ✗ keeps the Enquiry draft         expected 'Dagny Vole', got ''
  ```
  **After:** all four pass (`test/nuxt/app.test.ts`, the whole app with its router).

- **Before:** `/es` rendered per request only. **After:** `public/es/index.html` is in the build, with `lang="es"`, Spanish head, `hreflang` for both Locales, and the Spanish Profile and Roles in their blocks (`test/e2e/ssr.test.ts`). Messages ship as static files under `_i18n/`.

- Output tests read each component in both Locales and compare one `{ en, es }` object: plurals at 0, 1 and 2, the complaint limit (`5,000` / `5000`), Role periods (`Feb 2011 – now` / `feb 2011 – actualidad`), and the word order of Help, Unknown and Role detail.

- In a browser: a switch keeps the scroll position, fetches nothing after load, and the console stays empty; the production build hydrates `/` and `/es` cleanly under a German locale in Tokyo. `pnpm look` at 390px showed `responder a:` wrapping in the Contact form, so it is `responder:`.

- `pnpm test`: 788 passed, coverage 100%. Lint and typecheck clean.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The Spanish is a draft and this does not merge until I have read it: `tú` throughout, and the headline is translated to "Ingeniero frontend" while Role titles stay in English.

**Blast Radius:** sitewide

`/` is unchanged apart from the banner's space and the palette's new language row. `/es` becomes a public, indexable page with `hreflang` from `/` pointing to it, so whatever Spanish ships is what search engines pick up.

## Purpose

Keep bookmark editor fields editable and preserve their focus during typing. When both Title and URL were invalid, the validation effect ran after each edit and moved focus to the other invalid field, sending subsequent characters into the wrong input.

## Solution

- Focus the first invalid field only when Save is submitted, and let normal pointer focus handle title, URL, and icon-search inputs.
- Use stable modal ref callbacks for settings, the bookmark editor, trash, and confirmation dialogs. Preserve initial editor focus and existing dismissal/focus restoration.
- Add `homepage/stable-dialog-ref` and `homepage/no-invalid-focus-effect` as ESLint errors, with positive and negative rule tests.
- Add GitHub PR checks for lint, unit tests, and Chromium focus scenarios on desktop and mobile. Browser coverage includes immediate click-to-type, saving/reopening both bookmark fields, validation recovery, folder names, icon search, and Quick Launch search/dismissal.

## Verification

- `bun run lint` and the commit's formatting/lint hooks pass.
- `bun test`: 94 passing tests, including 14 lint-rule cases.
- Chromium: all eight desktop/mobile scenarios pass against the production build; the six bookmark/folder scenarios also pass with the development server.

author: alexfelker12
body:
## Spielerprofil

Closes #14

Jedes Konto hat ein Profil mit seiner persönlichen Statistik, gesamt und pro Gruppe, nach dem abgenommenen Design (`docs/design/issues/14-spielerprofil.md`, `decisions.md` › Statistik). Die Rangliste (#13) und die Spielerliste (#4) verlinken jetzt darauf.

### Server-Befehl (`src/server/player-profile.ts`)

- **`getPlayerProfile`** liefert Name, Bild, die 7 Kennzahlen gesamt (Teilnahmen zuerst, dann die übrigen in ihrer Reihenfolge) und pro Gruppe Spiele, Siege und Winrate für einen Zeitraum. Dazu kommen „seit wann“ und die Jahre mit Spielen für die Zeitraum-Auswahl.
- **Was zählt:** Die Gesamtwerte zählen alle eigenen beendeten Spiele, auch aus Gruppen, die man verlassen hat (Entscheidung vom 15.11.). Die Gruppen-Karten zeigen nur Gruppen, in denen man aktuell spielt.
- **Sichtbarkeit:**
  - Das eigene Profil sieht man immer.
  - Fremde Profile sieht nur, wer mit dem Konto mindestens eine Gruppe teilt, in der beide aktuell Spieler sind. Die Aufteilung zeigt dann nur die gemeinsamen Gruppen.
  - Alle anderen bekommen `playerNotFound`.
- **„Spielt in N Gruppen“** (`groupCount`) bekommt nur das Konto selbst.
- **Geteilt mit der Rangliste:** `src/server/stats.ts` bündelt Zeitraum-Prüfung, Starttag in deutscher Zeit, „nur beendete Spiele“, die Zählung aller Kennzahlen und die Zeitraum-Auswahl. `getLeaderboard` nutzt das jetzt auch.

### Tests (`src/server/player-profile.test.ts`, 5 Tests)

- eigenes Profil gesamt und pro Gruppe
- Mitspieler: Gesamtwerte über alle, Aufteilung nur über gemeinsame Gruppen
- Sichtbarkeit: ohne gemeinsame Gruppe, ehemalige Spieler in beide Richtungen, unbekanntes Konto, ohne Sitzung
- abgebrochene Spiele zählen nicht, Spiele aus verlassenen Gruppen schon
- Zeitraum und Jahre

Die Rangliste und die Spielerliste liefern jetzt die `userId` (Gäste `null`), die Tests sind ergänzt.

### Oberfläche
