author: rodrigopavezi
body:
## O que muda e por quê

Fecha as sobras do app listadas em #356.

- **Avisos da página com curtidas e republicações (#334):** o serviço de conta lê os avisos da página por `varanda/notices/3` e confere cada curtida e republicação como já confere respostas e menções: bloco assinado pelo autor, alvo numa publicação da página, regra do futuro, bloqueio, e o tipo informado pelo semeador nunca é aceito sem conferir. Com um semeador sem o canal v3, a leitura cai para o v2 e mostra as quatro linhas de antes.
- **Links nos Avisos (#304):** o trecho da publicação numa linha de aviso passa a ter links http, https e www, com a mesma regra das publicações, que fecha em caso de dúvida. Um trecho cortado em 90 caracteres continua texto simples, porque o corte pode cair no meio de um endereço.
- **Desfazer durante um recarregamento (#328):** a proteção já existia em A Rua e virou a função pura `countAnswerApplies` (`apps/app/src/engagement.js`), com teste.

Já resolvidos na `main` e conferidos no código, sem mudança aqui:

- Sair com uma troca de inscrição em andamento (#239): `offHere` em `apps/app/src/push-offer.js` espera até 3 s e desliga de novo um "Permitir" tardio (testes em `apps/app/test/push-offer.test.js`). A seção do `docs/verification.md` foi atualizada.
- `useFollowSet` com `follow.list` falhando (#309): `readFollowKeys` devolve null e o conjunto anterior fica.
- Pessoas relê os seguidos depois de seguir (#309): `onFollowsChanged` e `loadFollows`.
- Aviso local de A Rua: `TOAST_MS` já é 4 s, igual ao aviso com ação.
- Fontes Feather e Ionicons: cada uma no seu `try` (`Icon.js`).
- Toque duplo com republicar pendente: `doubleTapPlan` em `doubleTap.js`.

Sem mudança de RPC nem dos Termos. `docs/protocol.md` (seção 12) e `docs/app.md` descrevem o v3 nos avisos da página, e `docs/verification.md` perde os limites resolvidos.

## Issue

Closes #356

## Como verificar

- `node apps/cli/test/pages-notices.test.js`: curtida e republicação de uma publicação da página entram; curtida em publicação de outra pessoa, bloco forjado e autor desconhecido ficam de fora.
- `node apps/app/test/notices.test.js` e `node apps/app/test/engagement.test.js`.
- Conferido no emulador Android (build de debug), no simulador iOS e na web: Avisos com um endereço no trecho de uma publicação.
- Não conferido aqui: os passos com contas na página (curtida e republicação vistas pelo dono e por um administrador, limite de 8 por minuto, página encerrada) precisam de contas no serviço de produção e entraram no checklist de #224.

Limite conhecido: a queda do v3 para o v2 não tem teste automático, porque o semeador do teste sempre abre os dois canais (registrado no `docs/verification.md`).

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run lint`, `npm test` (ou `npm test -- --affected=origin/main`) e `npm run demo` passam
- [x] docs/protocol.md ou docs/rpc.md atualizados, se um formato mudou
- [x] Textos para o usuário estão em pt-BR
- [x] Conferido no Android (emulador ou aparelho) e no simulador iOS antes da web/PWA, ou explicado por que não se aplica
- [x] Nenhum segredo, chave ou dado pessoal no diff

author: nrjdalal
body:
## TL;DR

- A session can now delete its own stray scratch file, such as `scratch/<its name>-probe.txt` or `scratch/<its name>.tmp`, with `playground rm`. Before, the delete was refused and the file stayed until the nightly clean took it.
- A script's delete exception can no longer follow a link out of its own folder into a protected folder. Before, only the page exception checked this.
- `playground page --remove` now says "too big" when the page index is only too big, and writes MiB.

## Summary

```diff
 isProtected(path, session)
   exempt: scratch/<session>/, scratchpad/<session>/
+  exempt: scratch/<session>-* or scratch/<session>.*, a regular file directly in scratch/ (or nothing there, for a restore),
+          only while scratch/ is a real folder reached through no symlink from HOME
+          a symlink, a folder, scratch/<session>x.txt and scratch/sub/<session>-* stay refused

 carveOutAt(path, carve)
-  if carve.noLink and folder is a link: refuse   # page alone
+  if folder is a link or sits behind one: refuse # every carve-out
+    "<folder>, the <name> carve-out's folder, goes through the symlink <link> and leads to <real path>, ..."
```

The `noLink` field is gone from `CarveOut`; the check is now the rule for all five carve-outs.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the red commit `1c98c37b8` at canary: 13 fail in `tests/packages/safe-delete/src/index.test.ts` (both owned loose files refused; four carve-outs move the target's file through a linked folder; page refuses with the old message; the linked-parent row).
  **After:** head `2185c4d30` (canary `fa9e31ab5` merged in): 570 pass, 0 fail over safe-delete, page, plan, cli, verbs, rm, jobs, trash-build, supervisor, the new-worker, stop and brief-rush brief tests, trace-count AGENTS and no-raw-delete; check-types exit 0.
- A/B: the same script run against canary's `packages/safe-delete/src/index.ts` and the head's, on a fake data folder under the temp folder, measured:

  | Row | canary | head |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `scratch/<session>-probe.txt` (own) | refused | moved |
  | `scratch/<session>.tmp` (own) | refused | moved |
  | another session's `scratch/a4b5c6-worker-probe.txt` | refused | refused |
  | a symlink `scratch/<session>-link.txt` | refused | refused |
  | a folder `scratch/<session>-dir` | refused | refused |
  | `scratch/<session>x.txt` | refused | refused |
  | `scratch/sub/<session>-probe.txt` | refused | refused |
  | dashboard-supervisor: folder a link into `~/.ssh` | moved | refused |
  | jobs: folder a link into `~/.ssh` | moved | refused |
  | jobs-installed: folder a link into `~/.ssh` | moved | refused |
  | jobs-units: folder a link into `~/.ssh` | moved | refused |
  | page: folder a link into `~/.ssh` | refused | refused |
  | `scratch/` a link into `~/.ssh`, `scratch/<session>-key` | refused | refused |
  | `scratch/` a link into `~/.ssh`, `~/.ssh/<session>-key` | refused | refused |

- Round 1's finding: `scratch/` itself a symlink into `~/.ssh` or another protected folder, with `<session>-key` there. Canary refused, `cfcf736` allowed it, the head refuses it again. Red at `54d90e849` (2 fail: `refuses the caller's own loose file name through a scratch/ linked into .ssh` and `.playground/elsewhere`, by either path), green at `84c7eee9b`.

- Link message row: `the jobs-units carve-out names the link and its real path behind a linked parent, and a link to an unprotected folder still moves` (dotfiles shape: `~/.config/systemd` a link). Into a protected folder it is refused and the message names the folder, the link and the real path; into a folder nothing protects, the unit still moves.
- Carve-outs' own tests pass unchanged at the head: `tests/scripts/ops/dashboard/supervisor.test.ts`, `tests/packages/scripts/src/trash-build.test.ts`, `tests/packages/scripts/src/playground/jobs.test.ts`, `tests/packages/scripts/src/playground/page.test.ts` (one string updated, `over 20 MB` to `over 20 MiB`, plus a new row for the index size message).
- Measured on this Mac: `~/.playground/ops`, `ops/dashboard/builds`, `ops/launch-agents`, `~/Library/LaunchAgents` are real folders, so each carve-out still removes what it removes today.
- Checks: `bun run check-types` 0, `bun run test:skills` all 13 passed, `bun run format`, `bun run hooks:bundle` (the guard bundles import safe-delete).
- Hook differential at head `2185c4d30` against canary `fa9e31ab5`, over `guards` and the hooks whose bundles this PR rebuilt (the bundles carry only the `CARVE_OUTS` literal, with `noLink` gone), measured:
  - `bun run hooks:differential sweep --forms ~/.playground/scratch/9cxf2j-worker/forms.ts --canary fa9e31ab550e456f6411fac7e66679c1f252a8ba --hook guards --hook no-extension-repo-write --hook no-extensions-write --hook no-playground-leak --hook no-public-leak --hook writing-first --all` (2,565 forms: the refused-forms fixture's rows for these hooks plus 8 `playground rm` / `page --remove` forms): each of the six hooks 7,695 cases, newly allowed 0, newly refused 0.
  - `bun run hooks:differential replay --canary fa9e31ab550e456f6411fac7e66679c1f252a8ba --hook guards --hook no-extension-repo-write --hook no-extensions-write --hook no-playground-leak --hook no-public-leak --hook writing-first --role session --all`: each of the five single hooks 18,183 calls, newly allowed 0, newly refused 0. `guards`: newly allowed 0, newly refused 49. Each of the 49 calls ran in the main checkout or ran `bun install` in a worktree. That is the documented effect of `--hook guards` passing no main checkout (`scripts/README.md`, hooks:differential). So both hooks it names were replayed alone:
  - `bun run hooks:differential replay --canary fa9e31ab550e456f6411fac7e66679c1f252a8ba --hook no-main-checkout --hook no-unslotted-run --role session --all`: each 18,060 calls, newly allowed 0, newly refused 0.
  - The one refused-to-allowed move is the own loose scratch file inside `playground rm`, shown in the table above.
- Docs touched, each read by writing-for-agents and doc-sync: `web/next/content/docs/cli.mdx` (own loose file in the refused list; the link rule for every carve-out, page's own line trimmed; 20 MiB), `packages/scripts/src/playground/plan.ts` (`playground rm` help names the own loose file; page help says 20 MiB), `scripts/hooks/README.md` (no-raw-delete: three kinds of path), `extensions/core/skills/playbook/SESSIONS.md` (lines 66, 287, 290), `scripts/briefs/new-worker.md` (lines 21 and 22), `scripts/briefs/new-research-worker.md`, `scripts/briefs/brief-rush.md` (its pinning test `tests/scripts/briefs/brief-rush.test.ts` updated).
- Changed-term greps over the whole repo, 0 hits each at the head: `carve\.noLink|noLink\?: true|noLink: true` (outside bundles), `clears only (your|its) folders|never loose in|<session>-x\.log|only the folders named after`, ``only while `previews` is a real folder|carve-out does not follow``, `page.bytes / 1024 \*\* 2\} MB`. No list member added; no text moved.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The own loose file is a refused-to-allowed move: a session named `X` now owns every loose `scratch/X-*` and `scratch/X.*` regular file. A session whose name is a prefix of another's, followed by `-`, could take the other's loose file. Session names are a random id plus a role, or a fixed lead name, so this is unlikely, and every move restores from the trash for 7 days.

**Blast Radius:** carve-outs

A carve-out folder that is a link into a protected folder is now refused for every script. The Linux folders (`~/.config/systemd/user`) were not measured; a dotfiles link into a folder nothing protects still moves, as the row above shows.

## Links

Closes #2229
Closes #2238
Follows #2237's review nits.

author: incipienstation
body:
Daemon-backed installations now serve historical tool-detail expansion through the Rust Task read use case. The existing `/api/tasks/:id/history/details` endpoint keeps authentication, task/range validation, response shape and `no-store` in TypeScript; composition selects the native reader through an outbound port. Source and legacy configurations keep local reads.

The application contract separates activity reads from SQLite and HTTP. A read-only adapter captures cursor and ordered tool events in one committed snapshot, and the use case preserves inclusive ranges and cursor clamping. Opaque provider JSON retains JavaScript wire behavior for duplicate keys, overflow, primitives and Unicode. Activities remain complete even above the control transport's default 16 MiB limit; that opt-in applies only to this reader, while two native admission slots bound read/serialization concurrency. Corrupt payloads and runtime/database failures return 503 without fallback.

Startup requires the additive `taskActivityDetails: 1` capability. Event/schema writes, Task execution, queue admission, transcript pages, step details and content chunks remain in TypeScript. There is no schema migration; rollback uses the existing local reader. JSON parsing and public response encoding remain in the API process, and no performance improvement is claimed.

Verification:
- Focused native/TypeScript parity and HTTP checks passed, along with TypeScript checking, Clippy and the combined architecture gate.
- Extended the existing native read fixture instead of adding another process fixture: complete ranges beyond 200 events, cursor edges, payload semantics, external writes, uncommitted snapshots, rollback, restart, deletion, corrupt data, database errors and unavailable runtime.
- The single large payload is just over 16 MiB to catch accidental truncation; the same test verifies the default transport limit still applies to other callers.
- Extended the existing activity HTTP scenario for async reader selection, authentication and input rejection before reads, no-store, and native failure responses. No browser scenario or new timed fixture was added.
- All 16 CI checks passed on exact head `1ad2f33cf83dc67d0426b5193a135b02fbf3417f`, including both server lanes, browser checks, native builds and packaging. The local verifier passed source, type and tooling checks; its still-running combined server contract suite was stopped after CI completed, so the full local run is not counted as a pass.

## Laporan rilis

Batch ini berisi dua laporan klinik (15 Nov 2026). Keduanya **selesai penuh**. ID checklist: — (laporan langsung dari klinik).

### 1. Kas Keluar ke akun induk gagal ("Jurnal gagal tersimpan")
**Akar masalah**
- `730000 Beban Marketing` adalah akun induk (`is_header = true`, lihat `20261105010000_coa_bagan_baru.sql`).
- Pemilih akun di Kas Masuk/Keluar menampilkan akun induk.
- `postJournal` menolak akun induk tanpa mengirim pesan galat apa pun, lalu bukti kas dihapus lagi, dan pengguna hanya melihat pesan galat umum. Tidak ada data setengah jadi.

**Perubahan**
- `kas/KasEntryScreen.tsx`: pemilih akun dan form koreksi kas sekarang hanya menampilkan akun rincian. Nama akun di daftar riwayat tetap diambil dari semua akun.
- `kas/actions.ts`: sebelum nomor bukti diambil, server memeriksa bahwa akun tujuan ada, aktif, dan bukan akun induk. Kalau gagal, pesannya: "Akun 730000 · Beban Marketing adalah akun induk — pilih salah satu akun rinciannya."

### 2. Jurnal Umum: memilih akun harus scroll daftar panjang
**Perubahan**
- `keuangan/jurnal/JurnalForm.tsx` dan `JurnalCorrectionForm.tsx`: `<select>` akun diganti dengan `SearchableItemPicker`, yaitu kolom yang bisa diketik dan dicari berdasarkan kode atau nama. Komponen ini sama dengan yang dipakai di Kas Keluar. Nilai yang dikirim tetap `account_id`, jadi server action tidak berubah.
- `keuangan/jurnal/page.tsx`: akun induk tidak lagi ditawarkan (`.eq("is_header", false)`). `create_manual_journal_atomic` dan `revise_manual_journal` memang sudah menolak akun induk, jadi sekarang pilihan di layar konsisten dengan aturan server.

### Hasil tes
- Tes baru `src/lib/__tests__/kas-akun-induk.test.tsx` (3 kasus): akun induk tidak ditampilkan, ditolak sebelum ada penomoran atau penyimpanan, dan akun rincian tetap diproses. Sudah dicek bahwa tes ini **gagal** tanpa perbaikan.
- Tes baru `src/app/(app)/keuangan/jurnal/jurnal-cari-akun.test.tsx` (2 kasus): cari akun berdasarkan nama atau kode di form jurnal baru dan form koreksi, lalu `account_id` yang benar terkirim.
- `finance-transaction-forms.test.tsx` disesuaikan: akun sekarang dipilih lewat pencarian, bukan dropdown. Assertion selisih satu sen tidak berubah.
- Regresi penuh `vitest run`: 973 file lulus, 4 dilewati. 9116 tes lulus, 16 dilewati.
- Typecheck `tsc --noEmit` bersih. `eslint` pada file yang diubah bersih.
- `Technical checks` di head final `827eb20`: **success** ([run](https://github.com/rezanje/Kamo-Vet-OS/actions/runs/43707368490/job/132791236188)).

body:
Roadmap: FreeGroupsAndLimitGroups
<!--redteam:v1 {"owner":"AI-DOOM-b743906b-281a-4ba5-939c-d5913cc9d39b","findings":["RT-20261029-884e37"],"patterns":["hypothesis-stronger-than-needed"],"severity":"MINOR"}-->

Quality pass:
- Q1 Mathlib duplicates: checked - Mathlib has no countable-support retraction of a free group onto a free factor (searched `Mathlib/GroupTheory/FreeGroup` for `retract`, `Countable` and left inverses of `FreeGroup.map`; nothing there bounds the support), and no equational Noetherianity or algebraic sets over groups (no `Equationally` anywhere in Mathlib at the pin), so `exists_seq_of_forall_finite_V_ne` and `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_isFreeGroup` have no counterpart either.
- Q2 Tau Ceti duplicates, on main and in open PRs: checked - on main the retraction argument was written out inline in `FreeGroup.exists_monoidHom_fin_two_forall_ne_one`, which now uses `FreeGroup.exists_countable_retraction`. `EquationallyNoetherian.lean` has only the converse direction (`exists_forall_ge_V_eq`, `exists_forall_ge_Rad_eq`), and no other lemma builds a chain from a system with no equivalent finite subsystem. No theorem on main derives equational Noetherianity from `IsFreeGroup`. None of the 18 open PRs touching `GroupTheory/FreeGroup/`, `GroupTheory/GroupAlgGeom/` or `GroupTheory/LimitGroup/` adds such a lemma (searched their added lines for these names, retractions, finite supports and `IsFreeGroup` with `IsEquationallyNoetherian`). #40684 calls `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_freeGroupBasis` and will need `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_isFreeGroup` with `FreeGroupBasis.isFreeGroup` once this lands.
- Q3 Hypotheses: changed - dropped `[Countable α]` from `isEquationallyNoetherian_freeGroup`, `isDiscriminatedBy_id_iff_forall_realize_iff_of_freeGroupBasis` and `isDiscriminatedBy_freeGroup_iff_forall_realize_iff`, and replaced `{κ} [Countable κ] (b : FreeGroupBasis κ H)` by `[IsFreeGroup H]` (`isEquationallyNoetherian_of_freeGroupBasis` becomes `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_isFreeGroup`). Kept, each with a counterexample: `[IsFreeGroup H]` (without it the statement says every group is equationally Noetherian, refuted by `not_isEquationallyNoetherian_restrictedProduct_freeGroup`); `[Countable κ]` of `exists_countable_retraction` (for `u = FreeGroup.of` on an uncountable `ι` every admissible `β` is all of `ι`); `hS` of `exists_seq_of_forall_finite_V_ne` (for `S = ∅` no `s k ∈ T (k + 1) ⊆ S` exists); `hs` of `exists_monoidHom_fin_two_forall_ne_one` (`s = {1}`); `[Finite X]` and `hπ` of the two Remeslennikov theorems (a nonprincipal ultrapower `K` of `F(α)` is universally equivalent to `F(α)` with constants by Łoś, but `(a ^ k!)ₖ` has roots of every order, so every homomorphism to `F(α)` kills it; take `X = K`, or `X = ∅` with the non-surjective diagonal map). `b` of `isDiscriminatedBy_id_iff_forall_realize_iff_of_freeGroupBasis` is needed to state it (the constants name the basis). The group instances are needed to state the theorems. `exists_finset_mem_closure` and `exists_finset_forall_mem_closure` are moved unchanged and have no hypotheses.
- Q4 Section variables: checked - `#check` shows each added or changed theorem takes only binders it uses. `unusedArguments` reports 0 on all five changed modules.
- Q5 Proofs of at most 50 lines: checked - the longest proof added or changed is that of `isEquationallyNoetherian_freeGroup`, at 22 lines (the moved `exists_finset_mem_closure` is 21).

This completes #40011, which bors merged at an earlier commit: accepted head `bd7508a7`, the docstring-only version. That version recorded on `main` that countability is a proof artefact but did not prove the general case. The two later commits on that PR, which prove it and answer its api-design, placement and reuse findings, never reached `main`. This PR re-applies them on current `main`, together with the fixes asked for by this PR's own review.

Improvement of existing code. The roadmap's own sources (`Suggested.lean`, `README.md`) name only `isEquationallyNoetherian_freeGroup` (finite-rank target `isEquationallyNoetherian_freeGroup (n : ℕ)` in `Suggested.lean`); it keeps its name, module and namespace and only loses `[Countable α]`, so it still covers that target. `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_freeGroupBasis` appears in the roadmap only in the generated `STATUS.md` (line 20) and `PROGRESS.md` (line 30); at the generality review's request it is replaced by `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_isFreeGroup`, so those generated links will point at the new name once regenerated.

## What was wrong
`RT-20261029-884e37`, `TauCeti/GroupTheory/GroupAlgGeom/Linear.lean`: `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_freeGroupBasis` and `isEquationallyNoetherian_freeGroup` assume a countable basis. The assumption is only there because the proof goes through the embedding into `SL(2, ℤ)`. Free groups of every rank are equationally Noetherian.

## The fix
- `GroupAlgGeom/Linear.lean`:
  - `isEquationallyNoetherian_freeGroup` is proved for any `α`. A system over `F(α)` with no equivalent finite subsystem gives finite subsystems `T k`, solutions `v k` and failing equations `s k ∈ T (k + 1)`. The countably many values `s k (v k) ≠ 1` survive the retraction onto a free factor `F(β)` of countable rank. So the algebraic sets of the `T k` over `F(β)` never stabilize, which contradicts the countable case (through `SL(2, ℤ)`).
  - `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_freeGroupBasis {κ} [Countable κ] (ι : G →* H) (b : FreeGroupBasis κ H)` is replaced by `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_isFreeGroup [IsFreeGroup H] (ι : G →* H)`, which follows from the previous item through `IsFreeGroup.toFreeGroup H`. A caller with a basis `b` passes `b.isFreeGroup` (Mathlib's `FreeGroupBasis.isFreeGroup`, any universe). No alias is kept.
  - The module docstring, which on `main` says the argument is not formalised, now describes the proof, and Sanov's paper, which it cites, is in the references. The private import of `FreeGroup.Discrimination` becomes one of `FreeGroup.Basic`.
- `GroupAlgGeom/UniversalTheory.lean`: both forms of Remeslennikov's theorem drop `[Countable α]`, and their docstrings and the module docstring now say any rank. The basis form uses `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_isFreeGroup` through `b.isFreeGroup`.
- `FreeGroup/Basic.lean`: new public `FreeGroup.exists_countable_retraction`, which says countably many elements of `FreeGroup ι` lie in a free factor `FreeGroup β` with `β` countable, through a retraction `r` with `r.comp (map (↑)) = MonoidHom.id _`. `FreeGroup.exists_finset_mem_closure` and `FreeGroup.exists_finset_forall_mem_closure` move here unchanged from `FreeGroup/Discrimination.lean`, so the finite-support API sits with the other elementary free-group lemmas rather than behind the linearity and discrimination imports. The module title and summary now cover them.
- `FreeGroup/Discrimination.lean`: keeps only `FreeGroup.exists_monoidHom_fin_two_forall_ne_one`, which reuses `exists_countable_retraction` instead of repeating the argument; it imports `FreeGroup.Basic` privately.
- `GroupAlgGeom/EquationallyNoetherian.lean`: new public `TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.exists_seq_of_forall_finite_V_ne`, the chain step above.

The two new lemmas were private helpers in `Linear.lean`; the api-design, placement and reuse reviews of #40011 asked for them to be exported. This PR's review then asked for: `isEquationallyNoetherian_of_isFreeGroup` in place of the basis form (generality), the retraction and its finite-support prerequisites in `FreeGroup/Basic.lean` (placement), and a docstring of `exists_countable_retraction` that no longer promises the retraction kills the other basis elements, which its statement does not say (documentation). All three are done.

author: tonyhopland
body:
## Summary

The backend suite now starts from a clean environment, so `ILD_*`, `AGENT_*` and proxy variables exported in an agent pod no longer cause false failures. The module initializer in `TestEnvironmentBaseline` clears them from the test host and points `ILD_AGENT_READ_ROOT` at a writable per-run temp directory. Only the test host is cleaned, so `dotnet restore` still uses the outer proxy.

```
ModuleInitializer Apply():
  for each env var in process:
      if name starts with ILD_ or AGENT_, or is a proxy var (HTTP(S)_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY, ...):
          unset it
  ILD_AGENT_READ_ROOT = <tmp>/ild-tests-private-<guid>   # writable; removed on process exit
```

```
ILD.Tests/TestEnvironmentBaseline.cs       clears ambient vars, pins per-run read root
ILD.Tests/TestEnvironmentBaselineTests.cs  guard tests (new)
ILD.Tests/OpenCodeAdapterTests.cs          joins ProcessGlobalStateCollection
.github/workflows/ci.yml                   second test step with a polluted environment
AGENTS.md                                  one-line note on the rule
```

## Evidence

- **Guard tests** in `TestEnvironmentBaselineTests`:
  - `NoAmbientIldAgentOrProxyVariableSurvivesIntoTheTestHost`
  - `AgentReadRootIsAWritablePerRunDirectory`
  - `LogLevelAndSecretListAreNotInherited`
- **New CI step**, "Backend tests with a polluted environment", runs the whole suite with:
  - an unwritable `ILD_AGENT_READ_ROOT` and `ILD_AGENT_SCRATCH_ROOT`
  - `ILD_LOG_LEVEL=Warning`, `ILD_AGENT_USER` and an `AGENT_*` variable
  - dead-port `HTTP(S)_PROXY` and `ALL_PROXY`, with `NO_PROXY` empty

  A test that starts reading any of these again fails that step.
- I did not run the suite for this description, so I have no before/after counts. The pod-shell check (`dotnet test` showing 0 failures from read-root ownership, log level or proxy) has not been done.
- `OpenCodeAdapterTests` now runs in the process-global-state collection. Both it and the guard tests touch environment state, so they must not run in parallel with other tests.

## Merge Danger

- **Door:** two-way door. It changes only test setup, CI and one docs line, so it reverts cleanly.
- **Blast radius:** test suite and CI.
  - A test that relied on an inherited variable now fails and has to set the variable itself.
  - CI time grows by one extra full test run.
- Before merging, run `dotnet test` in an agent shell in the pod, with the pod's variables still exported, to confirm 0 failures from these causes.

body:
## Why

Backlog `56d2430b` had two parts. The embedding half was merged in #868. The other half: `routes/policies.rs` broke CLAUDE.md's rule "All SQL stays in `crates/epigraph-db/src/repos/`", including a raw `INSERT INTO claims`. Its suggested fix: "move the policies INSERT into a repository".

## What changes

- New `crates/epigraph-db/src/repos/policy.rs` with `PolicyRepository` (no repo owned these tables before), exported like its siblings.
- Five of the route file's nine production statements move into it, unchanged in SQL, binds and `ON CONFLICT`:
  - `list_active_network` and `get_challenge` take an executor and still run on the raw pool;
  - `lock_challenge_create`, `find_challenge_by_hash` and `insert_challenge` (the `INSERT` the finding names) take `&mut PgConnection` and still run on the viewer-stamped transaction from `begin_claim_write`.
- Repo functions return `sqlx::Error`, so the handlers' error messages are byte-identical.
- Registers:
  - `visibility_lint` registers the three viewer-less challenge functions with reasons;
  - the `policies.rs` route-layer reads row in `viewer_route_table_lint` goes from 2 to 0;
  - `viewer_spend_lint` names the repo calls;
  - the inline-SQL ratchet's `policies.rs` entry goes from 9 to 4, and `HIGH_WATER` from 120 to 115.

### Not moved, deliberately

Four statements stay in the route: `UPDATE claims` in the admin-scoped handlers `record_outcome`, `resolve_challenge` (two) and `decay_sweep`. They run on the raw pool with no viewer.
- Moving them as they are would add ungated repo writes, which `write_gate_lint` forbids ("Never add one").
- Gating them means deciding how an admin writes to system-owned policy claims, for example through the audited admin path `patch_claim` uses. That is a behaviour change, not a move.
- They remain counted in `ROUTE_LAYER_WRITES` (4) and in the ratchet, and are filed as a separate backlog item.

## Verification

On the branch merged with current `main`, on a fresh database migrated to 209:
- `policies_auth_test` 21, `conventions_policies_embed` 3 and `--lib policies` 7 passed; the agent also ran them before the change.
- `no_inline_sql_in_routes` 4, `viewer_route_table_lint` 15, `viewer_spend_lint` 6, and epigraph-db `visibility_lint` 13, `no_unscoped_pool` 5, `pool_read_lint` 3, `write_gate_lint` 9 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; clippy `-D warnings` clean on `epigraph-db` and `epigraph-api` locally, with an allow for an existing `epigraph-engine` lint from the older local toolchain that CI's lint job does not report.

author: domonic18
body:
## 背景

#242 合入 develop 后,测试环境自动发布(develop push)失败:

```
✗ soap-mock:挂载源类型(dir)与容器内目标类型(OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed:
  unable to start container process: current working directory is outside of container
  mount namespace root -- possible container breakout detected)不一致
✗ 挂载源预检失败(见上):容器将起不来,已中止发布(旧版本继续服务)
```

## 根因

新增的类型比对用 `docker exec` 进运行中的容器探目标路径类型。两个坑:

1. **exec 失败**:容器自身的 `WORKDIR` 失效(如 `/app` 已被换成别的 bind 源)时,
   exec 直接报 OCI 错误——该容器正是如此(`working_dir: /app` + `scripts/dev → /app`)。
2. **报错文本被当成类型**:exec 的错误输出落进捕获变量,于是「目标类型」= 一句报错文本,
   与源类型对不上 ⇒ 误判错配 ⇒ 把发布拦下(发布在换容器前中止,站点无损失)。

## 改动

- `scripts/deploy.sh`
  - `docker exec` 加 `-w /`(绕开容器自身失效的 WORKDIR)。
  - 类型只认 `dir` / `file`,其余(空串、报错文本)一律当「类型未知」⇒ 不比对、不误伤;
    同一收紧也加进纯函数 `mount_source_verdict`(白名单在纯函数侧,单测可覆盖)。
- `tests/unit/deploy-mount-check.test.ts`:补一例「非法类型取值 ⇒ 放行」。

## 验证

- `make check` 绿(见下)。
- 测试环境自动发布(develop push)即为本次修复的实测场——合入 develop 后重跑验证。

author: steelotter1242
body:
## Summary

- Add Perl 5 as a supported language: `.pl`, `.pm`, `.t` and perl-shebang scripts parsed with `tree-sitter-perl` from `tree-sitter-language-pack` (no new dependency).
- Symbols: named subs and Perl 5.38 `method`s, each owned by its package (`package X;` to the end of its block, or `package X { .. }`), so `A::run` and `B::run` in one file are two symbols. `sub B::f` defines `f` in `B` wherever it sits, and a named sub declared inside another sub is still package-global (`my sub` / `state sub` stay lexical). Subs in `main` stay top-level.
- Imports: `use Foo::Bar` / `require` resolved `@INC`-style by whole-segment path suffix; pragmas dropped. An import binds in the package it appears in: `use Foo qw(a b)` imports those subs, `use Foo;` its default exports (read as all of them), and `require Foo` / `use Foo ()` nothing, except that `require` of a package-less `.pl` library makes its subs callable from `main`. When two imports bind one name, the last wins, even when the later one is from a module outside the repo; a later default `use` of an outside module (`use Carp;`) may export any name, so it leaves the call unresolved. An import binds only from a file that declares the imported package. A package no file declares binds nothing, and a wildcard import binds only the module's own package subs. A bare name never binds by repo-wide uniqueness. A recursive call binds the sub itself, through the shared recursion check other languages use.
- Calls: a bare `foo()` resolves in the caller's own package, never falling back to `main`; `main::foo()` names a package-less sub in the caller's file or a library it `require`s; `Pkg::sub()` binds to that package only; `Pkg->m()` and the indirect `new Pkg(..)`, `$self->m()` (also `$class`, `$this`, `shift`, `__PACKAGE__`, `ref($self)`), `$self->SUPER::m()` and constructor-typed locals (`my $o = Pkg->new` / `new Pkg`) dispatch through `@ISA` in Perl's default depth-first order. `main` scripts inherit too (`use parent 'Base'` then `__PACKAGE__->m()`). `@ISA = (..)` replaces the parents, `unshift` prepends, `push` and `use parent` / `use base` append. Parents are read off the syntax tree of the analysed revision, so POD and heredocs are ignored.
- Tests: a `.t` file is a test wherever it sits (`xt/author.t`, `basic.t`), through a new `test_extensions` field on `LanguageSpec`, and any Perl file under `t/` is test material. Only `.t` files are runnable tests: a `.pm` / `.pl` in a test tree is support code (`LanguageSpec.test_extensions` makes the others `test_support_extensions`), so test reach walks `t/basic.t -> t/lib/Helper.pm -> lib/App.pm` to the test, and test selection collects `.t` files and treats the helpers as code.
- Health: a Perl complexity dialect (if/unless/elsif, ternary, statement modifiers, loops, try, `&&`/`||`/`and`/`or`).

## Related Issues

None.

## Known limits

- `use mro 'c3'` is read as the default depth-first order.
- `use Foo;` is read as importing all of Foo's subs; its `@EXPORT` list is not read.
- A receiver is typed only by a constructor assignment, keyed by variable name within the calling sub: a later non-constructor reassignment of `$obj`, or an inner `my $o` shadowing an outer one, is not told apart.
- An imported sub is reached only by its bare name, not as `App::helper()` or as a method of the importing package.
- A package's own sub wins over an import of the same name, wherever the two sit in the file.
- When two files declare the same package, nothing binds unless the caller is in one of them.
- Perl 5.38 `class` blocks own their methods like packages, but `:isa(Parent)` is not read as inheritance.
- `AUTOLOAD` and subs installed through the symbol table (`*foo = sub {..}`) are not seen.
- `repowise update` rebuilds the graph after a Perl edit rather than patching it: Perl is not in `PATCHABLE_LANGUAGES`, since its packages, parents and imports are cross-file facts the patch-parity fixtures do not cover yet.
- Two subs of one name, or a call and a different sub, on a single source line: the shared parser keys symbols and call sites by line, so such one-line files resolve coarsely. Package regions themselves are byte ranges.

## Test Plan

- [x] Tests pass (`uv run pytest tests/providers/ tests/unit/`): 45,719 passed in a parallel local run. Rerun serially, every failure from that run passes except `test_blast_radius_change_requests::test_a_managed_checkout_fetches_the_published_ref`, which fails locally on a `git fetch` of a merge-request ref and passes in upstream CI; the rest were timing budgets under parallel load.
- [x] Lint passes (`uv run ruff check .`, `npm run lint`)
- [x] `npm run type-check` passes
- [x] `repowise doc-drift --check --baseline .github/doc-drift-baseline.json` passes
- [x] `repowise health check origin/main...HEAD` passes (medium warnings only)
- New tests: `test_perl_extractors`, `test_perl_resolver`, `test_perl_inheritance`, `test_perl_package_calls`, `test_perl_complexity`, a Perl parser golden, and a Perl sample in the health-engine golden. Covered cases include same-named subs in two packages of one file, bare calls that must not fall back to `main`, `main::` calls, imports scoped to their package, `require`d package-less libraries, block packages inside a `package X;` region, `@ISA` read as a value, `@ISA` set/unshift/push/clear, duplicate package declarations, import lists, methods named like builtins, and package facts read from the analysed revision rather than the working tree.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's code style
- [x] I have added tests for new functionality
- [x] All existing tests still pass; the test-path corpus's `t/basic.pl` "another language" example moved to `t/basic.rb`, since Perl now claims `t/`
- [x] I have updated documentation (LANGUAGE_SUPPORT.md, architecture/language-support.md, README and the language counts)

body:
Phase B05 continued 4 (FR-INV-003, FR-INV-007, FR-INV-008, FR-INV-015, FR-INV-016, FR-INV-019; A-128, A-136). This is the last part of B5. The report is `docs/sessions/B05e-inventory-cold-chain-opening.md`.

**Needs the owner's approval:** ADR-0050 (proposed). MDM's `EntitySheet` becomes a port, and a higher module registers a sheet with `MdmImports.registerSheet`. The first is INV's `OPENING_STOCK` sheet. **No new dependency.**

## What changed
- **Temperature readings** (`listTemperatureReadings`, `recordTemperatureReading`):
  - A reading is judged against the location's range. The range comes from MDM and is copied onto the reading, and the database checks the reading against that copy.
  - An excursion, in the same transaction:
    - places a `QUARANTINE` hold on every lot and animal in the room;
    - raises a `TEMPERATURE_EXCURSION` exception for each stock line there;
    - publishes `inv.TemperatureExcursionRecorded`.
- **Reorder rules** (`listReorderRules`, `createReorderRule`, `updateReorderRule`) and **`listStockAlerts`:**
  - A rule raises one alert per crossing, judged in every movement, reservation and hold transaction.
  - The published view `inv.pub_reorder_level` serves B05x's low stock tile.
- **Expiry:** the daily `stock-alerts` job raises the expiry alerts, and the database refuses the sale of an expired lot (`STOCK_UNIT_EXPIRED`).
- **Scheduled jobs:** `stock-balance-recompute` (02:00) and `stock-alerts` (06:30), both through `ScheduledJob` (ADR-0049).
- **Opening stock:**
  - The `OPENING_STOCK` import is applied by the Owner only, once per product and branch, as `OPENING` goods receipts.
  - `createGoodsReceipt` with kind `OPENING` stays refused. That decides A-136 (a), recorded in A-148.
- **Contract 1.20.0, additive.** `StockAlert.suggestedQty` is new; three error codes are new; `OPENING_STOCK` now works on the import operations. CR-012 (the blind count example) is fixed.

## Gate
The B5 gate is passed in full:
- on hand derived from the movements matches the hand count of the seeded farm;
- negative stock is refused outside the allowed movement types;
- a lot traces in both directions over the API;
- all 24 INV writes refuse the Accountant, Cashier, Sales, Driver and Farm hand.

## Security review (hakorem-security-review)
Boundaries crossed: TB2 back office, and the database. I ran SECURE_CODING_STANDARDS.md item by item on the opening stock import and on temperature quarantine.

Passed:
- **Authorisation** is checked in the application layer, deny by default. Readings and rules are scoped to their location or branch. Opening stock is authorised at each location the file writes, on top of `mdm.import.apply`.
- **Maker-checker:** the person who recorded an excursion cannot release its quarantine (`RELEASED_BY_PLACER`, proved). Opening stock is the Owner's alone; a Manager's apply is refused and writes nothing.
- **Database:**
  - the excursion check is a constraint;
  - readings are append-only;
  - one alert stays open per rule or lot;
  - an expired lot's sale is refused for every role.
- **Input:** strict schemas; parameterised SQL only.

Not applicable, with reason: payments, webhooks, uploads and personal data are untouched.

Abuse cases 25 and 26 are added to the threat model. Their items on the daily exception report are B12's, as for cases 7 and 20 to 24.

author: jakobnunnendorf
body:
## What

Implements **WP-3B** from `docs/design/ICE-HUNTERS-VISION.md` §3.3 B. The real launch now plays a seven-shot ascent, cut like a broadcast, instead of the 11 s fairing ride:

| # | T (s) | Shot | Rig as built (spec ±20%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | -10→-3 | Pad at dusk | static, 600 m, 1.5 m up, FOV 28°, rocket on the left third |
| 2 | -3→+2 | Engine bells, ignition | 12 m from the base, looking up 20°, shake ramping |
| 3 | +2→+8 | Tower clearance | 80 m, FOV 35°, tilts up with the nose |
| 4 | +8→+20 | Long-lens tracking | 3 km, FOV 4°→2°, spring-lagged follow, heat shimmer |
| 5 | +20→+26 | Stage-2 down-cam | looking aft, stage 1 separates at +21 and falls away over Earth |
| 6 | +26→+34 | Inside the fairing | halves open, **the player's CubeSat with its packed parts** springs out of the deployer |
| 7 | +34→+42 | Deploy | slow orbit, wings unfold (+35), "hello" beep + Reyes line (+37), then cut to the flight view |

- Cuts, not drifts: every shot boundary is a hard cut with its own sound accent (tested: the pose jumps at every boundary).
- The rocket on the pad is the player's own stack from the Launch Hangar (`layoutRocket`), so shot 5 separates their real stage 1.
- **Skippable after the first viewing** (Skip button + Esc appear from the second run; under reduced motion always). Count kept in `localStorage`.

## The Liftoff bug

`launchTimeline.ts` no longer exists on `feat/ih-wp0`, but the bug survived in two places:
- `assets/cues.ts` played `sfx.ignition`, `voice.countdown` and `voice.liftoff` the instant the sim reported launch, i.e. ~10 s before T-0 of the ascent. Removed (the departure music cue stays).
- `FairingRide` said "liftoff" at deployment (t = 9.15). It now says it at ignition, and only in the Rocket-screen preview.

In the ascent, liftoff text and sound fire only at T-0 (measured in the browser: `sfx.ignition @ T0.02`, `voice.liftoff @ T0.02`, the LIFTOFF word appears at T-0).

## Entry point / hand-off (WP-3A unchanged)

Same trigger as before: `FlightStage`'s effect when the sim reports liftoff. It now calls `playAscent({ onEnd: endLaunch })` instead of `insideStore.play('fairing-ride')`. Whatever WP-3A does to start the flight (it ends in `startSimulation()`), the ascent follows without changes.

## Public API (for WP-4A)

- `playAscent({ onEnd?(skipped) })` and `useAscentStore` (`playing`, `startedAt`, `timesWatched`, `end`) in `src/scene/launch/ascentStore.ts`.
- `onEnd` fires once at the cut out of shot 7 (T+42) or on Skip; today it calls `useUiStore.endLaunch()`, which switches to the space flight view. WP-4A hooks its first flight moment there.
- Pure timing in `src/scene/launch/ascentShots.ts`: `ASCENT_SHOTS`, `ASCENT_BEATS`, `ASCENT_DURATION_S` (52), `ascentPose(T, rocketHeightM, aspect)`, `beatsBetween`, `countdownText`.
- Generic cut-list helpers in `src/world/camera/rig.ts`: `TimedShot`, `activeShot`, `cutsBetween`, `isContiguous`.

## Files

Mine: `src/scene/launch/{Ascent.tsx, ascentShots.ts(+test), ascentStore.ts, FairingRide.tsx}`, `src/world/camera/rig.ts(+test)`, `scripts/e2e/ih-qa-ascent.mjs` (films the ascent, logs every sound with its T, checks Skip gating).

**Shared files touched (small, please review):**
- `src/ui/flight/FlightStage.tsx`: `<Ascent/>` instead of `<FairingRide/>`, `playAscent` instead of `insideStore.play` (~10 lines)
- `src/state/uiStore.ts`: `LAUNCH = { ignitionS: 10, durationS: 52 }` (drives the non-WebGL island countdown and the safety timer)
- `src/assets/cues.ts` (+test): launch cue keeps only the music

Not changed: `LaunchPad.tsx`. Its camera is the pointer-sway camera of the classic Ride step's departure board, not a launch camera; replacing it would break that step. The launch camera that played lived in `FairingRide`, which this PR replaces. No edits to `src/sim`, `src/data`, `src/minigames/launchDirector`, `rooms/registry.ts`, `src/ui/report`.

## Checks

- `pnpm typecheck` ✅ · `pnpm test` ✅ 87 files / 975 tests (18 new for the shot list, 4 for rig) · `pnpm build` ✅
- `pnpm lint`: only the known error at `src/ui/report/ReportScreen.tsx:182`; new files add only the repo's usual three.js mutation warnings.
- Watched in headless Chrome (`node scripts/e2e/ih-qa-ascent.mjs <dir>`): all seven shots, LIFTOFF at T-0, Skip absent on first viewing and present on the second, no page errors. Screenshots of shots 1, 2 (T-0), 4, 5, 6, 7 are in the side-session notes folder `wp3b-ascent-shots/`.

## Known limits

- 52 s is long; the table's timings were kept as specified. Skip from the second viewing.
- Only the core stage gets a plume; boosters have none yet.
- In shot 7 the craft keeps its tumble from the spring-out, so late in the shot you see its back.

# P14 M57-FIX (s21): wieżowiec Andersa 38 — ściany i dach opisane z obrazu

Poprawka do **#56** (gałąź `research/mistral-p14-office-tower`). Nowa gałąź `research/mistral-p14-office-tower-fix-s21` wychodzi z `502d574e9` (głowa #56). Historii nie przepisywano. Zmiany są tylko w `research/mistral/p14-office-tower/`.
Podstawa: `docs/owner/MISTRAL-FIXES-12.md` § M57-FIX oraz `docs/reports/REVIEW-2026-11-14-s20-mistral-m57.md`.

## Metoda
- Pobrałem ponownie (2026-11-15): 3 kadry Commons z wieżą (miniatury 3840 px, bo oryginał 4608 px daje 429), 2 kadry kontekstowe Commons, 7 klatek KartaView, ortofoto WMS 80 m, OSM (zbiornik, kominy) i plik UKE xlsx.
- **Każdy kadr obejrzałem osobno**, razem z wycinkami 1:1 / 2,5–4×. Opisy w manifeście przepisałem z obrazu, bez szablonów.
- Pliki są w gałęzi (polecenie właściciela s21): `files/` ma 16 JPG, ok. 2,9 MB, ≤ 1600 px, sha256 w README i STATUS. Główny `.gitignore` (linia 69 `research/mistral/*/files/`) je ignoruje, więc dodałem je przez `git add -f`. Lokalny `.gitignore` pakietu usunąłem. Ortofoto jest JPG, bo `*.png` idzie do LFS.
- Liczby: manifest ma **19 wierszy** (dodany P14-019). Obejrzałem 14 plików źródłowych i ok. 15 wycinków. Audyt s21: seed **20261115**, 6/19 = 31,6 %, w tym 5 kadrów z wieżą. Wynik: **4 PASS / 2 FIX** (poprawione).

## Pozycje recenzji / M57-FIX

**Poprawione (12/12 punktów bloku, z zastrzeżeniem pkt 11):**
1. Oglądanie: każdy kadr obejrzałem osobno. P14-002…006 mają teraz osobne opisy klatek.
2. Reguła strony ściany jest w README razem z tabelą φ dla każdego kadru.
3. 073045 = szczyt SW (po prawej) + **NW** (po lewej). Kamera stoi na φ≈224°, ≈125 m (ESTIMATED, metoda w README). P14-007 opisuje teraz NW, a po prawej jest niebo. Usunąłem drabinę. Klimatyzatory wiszą pod oknami kolumny (2/1/2). Kolumna ma 10 okien + pas szklenia parteru. Ramy to białe skrzydła w ciemnoszarym obramieniu. Pierwszy plan to płot z graffiti, nie bariera.
4. NW: **6 grup pasmowych na kondygnację, 5–6 świateł w grupie** (±1). Ułamki zmierzyłem sam na 115626. Status: SOURCED z 3 kadrów, ułamki ESTIMATED. Wycinki zrobiłem z 3840 px, nie z 4608 (429).
5. Ortofoto: usunąłem tezy o NW-siatce, ciemnych pasach SE, cieniach NE i nadbudówce. Opisałem: cienie na NW, 4 podstawy X (N, E, środek SE, W z odciągami), ok. 10–14 niebieskich elementów, korytka, przybudówek SE (nowy wiersz P14-019).
6. KV 993062122 i 1326673613: wieża jest **w kadrze**, widać ścianę SE. Krótka grupa przy S, przerwa, dłuższe pasmo. Odcień SE taki sam jak szczytu. Dach: 2 maszty kratowe i panele. Status SOURCED (ref. BY-SA). Usunąłem „hFoV 70° — poza kadrem”.
7. KV 14055: kierunek **123° z toru**, heading API 357° odrzucony. Zbiornik = **OSM way/279896715** (`man_made=gasometer`), na pewno nie stacja paliw. Usunąłem „zasłonę drzew/słupów”.
8. Maszty: środkowy w 0,49, przy SW w 0,88, 3–4 krótkie przy NE. Wysokości policzone (podziałka + poprawka na attykę): ≈11–12 m i ≈11 m (115626), ≈9–10 m (073045). Zakres do gry: 9–12 m.
9. P14-012: parter wieży NW zasłonięty → UNVERIFIED. „Witryny” należą do hali giełdy.
10. Audyt: stary (seed 14) unieważniony, opisy „zaobserwowano” usunięte. Nowy seed, każdy kadr obejrzany ponownie.
11. Pliki: 110412 (1280×2276) wypadł z pakietu (był tylko kontekstem). KV 2769366/3686129 opisane jako 1280×720. 110808 i 131224 obejrzane (wieży brak) i dopisane do sources.md. **ZIP-a nie ma**, bo pliki są w gałęzi.
12. Luki w README zaktualizowane: NE nadal UNVERIFIED (tylko poszlaka). Układ SE nie jest już luką. Kolor SE = konflikt źródeł.

Dodatkowo: P14-016 (UKE) sprawdziłem ponownie i w audycie zacytowałem wiersze xlsx „stan na 2026-02-25”.

**UNVERIFIED (zostaje):** ściana NE; kolor SE (KV kontra Mapillary 2020 / ortofoto); parter NW i wejścia; funkcja i wymiar przybudówki SE (ortofoto ok. 5×8 m kontra BDOT 6,3×1,8 m); szarobrązowe dolne 2 kondygnacje przy końcu SW ściany NW; który maszt widać w 073045; funkcja zbiornika (akumulator ciepła?); który z dwóch kominów EC widać w 7119872; data nalotu WMS; pozycje kamer Commons (ESTIMATED, EXIF GPS jest sprzeczny z obrazem).

**Nie dało się:** pobrać oryginałów 4608 px (Commons 429 dla oryginału; użyłem standardowej miniatury 3840 px). Kadrów kontekstowych 065632…20191211 nie oglądałem ponownie (przegląd s20 potwierdził „wieży brak”, plików nie commitowałem).

body:
## Why

`parse_decision` was 249 lines and carried `#[expect(clippy::too_many_lines)]`: a `match` over the directives of the decision block, then the checks of the settings against each other, the URL, and the selection of the backend (#120).

This is the second of four PRs for #120, one for each parser. Stacked on #163 (with #162 down to #151 under it): until those are merged, this PR shows their commits too. The change itself is the last commit.

## What

The same shape as `parse_rule` in #163:

- `DecisionDraft` holds the settings read so far and the directives that the errors point at (`backend_line`, `token_line` and `model_line`, which stay at the `decision` directive when the block has no such line).
- `DecisionDraft::apply` reads one directive into the draft. Every directive may appear once, except `redact_header` and `redact_field`, whose lines add up, and `max_body`, which is always refused.
- `DecisionDraft::finish` runs, in the order they had: `check_timeouts`, `per_client_limit`, `endpoint_url`, `select_backend`. The backend selection, which the issue names as the first thing to pull out, is one function for each backend: `http_backend`, `clef_backend`, `strands_backend`, `jev_backend`. The model check that strands and jev both made is `model_id`.

`parse_decision` is 14 lines now, the longest function is `apply` with 56, and the `#[expect]` is gone.

Behaviour is unchanged:

- Every message is the same text and points at the same directive.
- The checks run in the same order: the block, each directive as written (unknown name, then the duplicate check, then its value), the timeouts, the concurrency limits, the URL, the backend.
- The token variable is read in the same cases, with the same name, after the URL and the model have passed.
- `DecisionConfig` and `BackendConfig` get the same values and defaults.

Only `src/config/decision.rs` changes.

## Tests

New tests, for behaviour that had none:

- each of the nine other single-use directives written twice (only `redact_file_parts` had a test);
- `redact_header` lines add up, and `redact_header` with no name is refused (`redact_field` had both tests);
- an unknown directive in the block; a `queue_timeout` equal to the `timeout`; a `url` that is not an absolute http(s) URI, with its line;
- the lines that two errors point at: a missing `url` at the `backend` line, and a `model` with backend http at the `model` line.

Not pinned by any test, before or after: which error is reported when the block has two.

## Checks

- `cargo test --workspace --locked`: 2119 passed (2103 before, plus the 16 new tests).
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items` with `-D warnings`, `jscpd` (14 clones, the same as before) and the eval tests.
- `cargo mutants --file src/config/decision.rs -- --lib`: 47 mutants, 39 caught, 8 that do not compile, none missed, none timed out. Before the new tests, one was missed (`>` for `>=` in the `queue_timeout` check), in an expression that the old code had too.

author: remydegenne
body:
This PR adds `LMLExplore/EValues/Numeraire.lean` (346 lines, one new file, no existing file changed). It proves the verification criteria that identify Statlib's numeraire e-variable through the effective null, for EValues Layer 1, item 2, **Identifying numeraires** [LRR25, Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.2; RW, Theorem 6.15], together with the likelihood-ratio corollaries that item lists [RW, Theorem 3.20; LRR25, Corollary 3.15].

Roadmap: EValues

Milestone: EValues Layer 1.2, "Identifying numeraires". Covered here:
- the first bullet's main statement: for `Q ≪ S` and a `Q`-a.s. positive e-variable `X*` with `P* = Q.withDensity X*⁻¹`, `X*` is the numeraire exactly when `P* ∈ effectiveSet S` (`isNumeraire_iff_withDensity_inv_mem_effectiveSet`); `P*` is then Statlib's `ripr Q S` (`IsNumeraire.ripr_eq`) and is equivalent to `Q` (`absolutelyContinuous_ripr`, plus `withDensity_absolutelyContinuous`); and `P*` is maximal (`IsNumeraire.eq_withDensity_inv_of_le`).
- RW Theorem 6.15: the numeraire is the only e-variable that is a likelihood ratio against an equivalent member of the effective null (`isNumeraire_iff_exists_ae_eq_rnDeriv`; the sufficient direction `isNumeraire_of_ae_eq_rnDeriv` needs no `Q ≪ S`).
- the generating-family criterion [LRR25, Corollary 4.2], in the "⊃" form noted after it (`isNumeraire_of_lintegral_div_le_one`, `ripr_mem_of_lintegral_div_le_one`).
- the likelihood-ratio corollary: `IsNumeraire (Q.rnDeriv P) {P} Q` for `Q ≪ P` [RW, Theorem 3.20] (`isNumeraire_rnDeriv`). Its value `klDiv Q P` is already Statlib's `maxUtility_singleton_eq_klDiv`, so it is cited rather than restated. Without absolute continuity: `∞` on a `P`-null set `N` off which `Q ≪ P`, and `(Q[|Nᶜ]).rnDeriv P` on `Nᶜ` [LRR25, Corollary 3.15] (`isNumeraire_piecewise_rnDeriv_cond`). As the roadmap's "derive as corollaries" asks, `isNumeraire_rnDeriv` is the case `N = ∅` of it.

All of these come from one statement that holds for every finite `Q` and every null: `isNumeraire_iff_smul_withDensity_inv_mem_effectiveSet` says that `X` is the numeraire iff `(Q X.fsupport)⁻¹ • Q.withDensity X⁻¹ ∈ effectiveSet S` (the normalisation of [LRR25, Theorem 3.13]). "`Q ≪ S`" is stated inline as `∀ s, MeasurableSet s → (∀ P ∈ S, P s = 0) → Q s = 0`, and `IsEVar.ae_ne_top_of_forall_measure_eq_zero` records its consequence that e-variables are `Q`-a.s. finite.

What remains in Layer 1.2 after this PR: the dominated criterion [LRR25, Theorem 4.7] and the `L¹` convergence of [LRR25, Corollary 4.11], which both need the bipolar theorem of Layer 1.1 [BS99]; the σ-algebra and stopping-time corollaries [RW, Proposition 3.22, Corollary 3.23, Theorem 7.11; KG22, Theorem 5], which need an `∫ᵉ`/`trim` lemma that does not exist yet; the monotone-likelihood-ratio families [RW, Proposition 2.18]; and the GROW corollaries [GdHK24; LGH24].

Correction to the source: LRR25's Corollary 3.15 also says the RIPr is `P₀ᵃ`. With Statlib's `ripr Q S = Q.withDensity (numeraire Q S)⁻¹`, the RIPr is `Q(Nᶜ) • P₀ᵃ` (example: `P₀ = ½δ_a + ½δ_b`, `Q = ½δ_b + ½δ_c` gives `ripr = ¼δ_b`). So only the numeraire part of that corollary is stated.

Reuse: built on Statlib's `isNumeraire_iff`, `IsNumeraire.ae_unique`, `isNumeraire_numeraire`, `ripr`, `ripr_mem_effectiveSet`, `rnDeriv_ripr`, `absolutelyContinuous_ripr_of_ae_ne_top`, `effectiveSet`, on LMLExplore's `mem_effectiveSet_of_le` and `subset_effectiveSet` (`EValues/EffectiveSet.lean`), and on Mathlib's `Measure.inv_rnDeriv`, `Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_le`, `cond_mul_eq_inter'` and `withDensity_indicator`. Before writing each declaration I grepped Mathlib, Statlib, TauCeti, LML and `LMLExplore/` for it (e.g. `ripr_eq`, `isNumeraire_rnDeriv`, `ae_ne_top_of`, `withDensity_inv`), as well as the open EValues PRs (#401, #402, #404, #405, #409); none overlaps. No Mathlib infrastructure is vendored.

Local checks (not CI): `scope: scoped: against a890e2a`, whole-library `lake build --iofail` green, `local-axioms: checked 1 changed module(s), 20 declaration(s); 0 violation(s)`, module-system, header style and environment lint passing.

author: starkchristian
body:
## Why

The owner wants StarkLLM to be an international product: English first, German second, nothing that assumes the user lives in Germany. This PR starts from an audit of where the app assumed Germany or German, fixes what can be fixed safely, and lists what is left.

## Audit: what was found

| Area | Found on `main` | Status |
|---|---|---|
| UI language and fallback | English was already the source and fallback; German was found by hard-coded `startsWith('de')`; a new language needed edits in `i18n/index.js`, `utils/languages.js` (with flag and region by hand) and `check-i18n.mjs`. | **Fixed**: one file per language, found automatically |
| Date/number locale | `en-GB` or `de-DE` only; `formatUsd` wrote `74.291,00 $` for German only | **Fixed**: system region wins when it speaks the UI language (en-US, en-AU, de-AT ...); money by `Intl` with the real currency |
| Answer language | Detector knew 8 languages; short questions got "language of the message"; prompt said "For German, use correct Hochdeutsch"; dates in the prompt were `dd.mm.yyyy` | **Fixed**: UI language is the fallback for short questions, Portuguese and Russian added, ISO dates in prompts, neutral wording |
| Inbox: kinds of letters | German and English words only | **Fixed**: fr, es, it, tr added |
| Inbox: sender / "not a name" | German/English markers; `[A-Za-zÄÖÜäöüß]` letter classes | **Fixed**: any letters, fr/es/it/tr markers |
| Inbox: references | German/English labels | **Fixed**: fr, es, it, tr, US/UK (case, claim, tracking, ...) |
| Dates | `dd.mm.yyyy`, ISO, German/English month names | **Fixed**: `15/12/2026` and `12/15/2026` (order read from the letter), `15-12-2026`, `2026/12/15`, `15 de diciembre de 2026`, `1er décembre`, `15th December`, Turkish month names (also `ARALIK`), months without accents (scans), 12-hour times, `14h30`, `a las 10:30`, `alle ore 9`, `saat 10:30`; "Paris, le 3 novembre 2026" is the letter date; `Due date:` is no longer taken for the date of the letter |
| Deadline words | Frist, bis zum, due, by ... | **Fixed**: fr (avant le, au plus tard, échéance), es (antes del, hasta el, vencimiento), it (entro il, scadenza), tr (son ödeme tarihi, tarihine kadar) |
| Amounts and currency | Always printed `EUR`, even for `$1,234.56`; no integer amounts; no `£`, `CHF`, `TL` | **Fixed**: EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, TRY, PLN, CZK, INR, JPY ...; `1.234,56`, `1,234.56`, `1 234,56`, `1'234.50`, `412,-`; fact carries the number as written, `number` and ISO `currency` |
| Bank formats | IBAN only | **Fixed**: US routing (check digit) and account, UK sort code and account, Australian BSB, BIC/SWIFT, all label-based |
| Scam warnings | German authority list; "foreign account" = not `DE`; German words | **Fixed**: authorities by country (DE/AT/CH, FR, ES, IT, TR, GB, US), words in six languages, a US authority asking for an IBAN, prompt injection in six languages; genuine Austrian/French/... authority letters are not flagged |
| OCR | Tesseract with `deu+eng` fixed in config | **Fixed**: user-chosen languages (Settings), packs downloaded only on request, bundled data untouched; default `eng+deu` |
| First start / Settings / errors | German-free; UI strings go through `t()` | Checked, no hard-coded German found in the frontend |
| TTS | Voice chosen by a German word list, two voices fixed | **Fixed**: voice by detected language (6 languages), extra Piper voices by file, `/voice/voices` |
| STT | Whisper autodetect, no way to give a hint | **Fixed**: optional `language` hint |
| Studio | Language names and headings only for `de`/`en`; browser podcast voice = system language | **Fixed**: any ISO code, headings per language table, utterance language from the text |
| Retrieval | Stop words English + German only | **Fixed**: French, Spanish, Italian, Turkish, Portuguese, Dutch added |
| Tests | German fixtures (+ English) only | **Fixed**: fixtures and tests for en-US, en-GB, de-CH, fr, es, it, tr; generated benchmark extended |
| Desktop app dialogs, installer, diagnostics page | English only (no German either) | **Left**, see below |

## What changed

* `backend/app/services/locale_rules.py` (new): all words and formats per language in one place. `dates_service.py`, `facts_service.py`, `document_checks.py` read from it.
* Extraction (rule-based, no model): dates, deadlines, appointments, fees, old amounts, price changes, kinds of letters, references, amounts with currency, bank accounts, scam signs. **Every fact still carries page and line text** (tests check that each fact's text is a line of the document).
* `ocr_languages.py`, `api/ocr.py`, `OcrSettings.jsx`: choose OCR languages; install a pack on request (the only network access, one file from the Tesseract project's `tessdata_fast`, nothing about the user is sent); bundled English and German keep working (tested).
* UI: `frontend/src/i18n/<code>.json` files are discovered; `locales.js` (pure helpers, tested with `node --test`); Settings language cards are built from the files; `check-i18n.mjs` checks every language file.
* Speech: `utils/speech.js`, `voice_service.py` (voices from `STARKLLM_VOICES_DIR`).
* Chat: `language` (UI language) is sent with each message and used only when the question is too short to tell.
* `docs/adding-a-language.md`: how to add an interface language, letter rules, OCR language, voice, studio headings.
* CI: `npm test` added to the frontend check.

## Tests

* Backend (`starkllm-backend` image): **412 passed** (236 before). Frontend `npm test`: 12 passed. New: `test_international_letters.py`, `test_international_scams.py`, `test_ocr_languages.py`, `test_international_prompts_and_voice.py`, extended benchmark (300 generated letters: recall, precision, kind and amount accuracy 100 %; 600 letters of other countries >= 99 %).
* Desktop `npm test`: 56 passed (unchanged). Frontend: `npm run i18n:check` clean, `npm test` 11 passed, `npm run build` ok, `scripts/check-languages.py` clean.
* **Not done**: the LLM scenarios (`backend/scenarios/run.py`, class A) were not run before/after because no model was used; no manual run of the app in a browser (the new Settings page is built and linted, not looked at); a real download of a language pack was only tested with a fake download.

## What was left, and why

* **Desktop app texts** (update dialogs, diagnostics page, installer) are English only. Fine as the fallback; translating them needs a decision on the languages (owner).
* **UI translations**: the owner chose French as the third language after this PR was opened; `frontend/src/i18n/fr.json` (863 texts, checked by `npm run i18n:check`) and French Studio headings were added. Nothing else was added; the fr texts were written by Claude and should be read by a French speaker before a release.
* **API error messages** (`detail` strings of the backend) are English; the UI shows some of them as they are.
* Known limits of the rules (also in the docs): `03/04/2026` is read day first unless the letter shows month first or looks American; `$` means USD; two-digit years are 20xx; the Turkish "replaces the letter of ..." has no rule; account numbers need their label (routing number / sort code); the "missing words in the documents" check in the chat (`_GENERIC_NOUNS`, synonyms) is still German.
* Backup (`/system/backup`) zips the whole data folder; downloaded OCR packs (a few MB each) are inside it.
* docs/RULES.md R2 says the project languages are English and German; the UI now also has French (owner's choice). The extraction rules now contain French, Spanish, Italian and Turkish *words* (Latin script, with fixtures); the UI is still English and German only. The owner may want to reword R2.
* Overlap with the open draft #95 (B5 deadlines): it also edits `dates_service.py`, `facts_service.py`, `Inbox.jsx` and `de.json`. I kept the lines it changes (`FoundDate`, `_fact`, `dates()`) as they are; expect a small merge conflict in `dates_service.py`.

## Update: owner decisions (relayed by the coordinator session

author: ihsankabir
body:
## Before merging: run the migration on production

This PR adds a column. Run `supabase/migrations/0025_preorder_express.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor **first**. Every preorder screen reads the new column, so merging without it breaks the request form and the admin preorders page. It is one line and safe to run twice:

```sql
alter table preorder_requests add column if not exists express_fee_bdt integer;
```

## What changes for customers

- **Flower product pages:** "Estimated delivery · 1 to 3 days, usually the same day" and "Need it today? Same-day express +৳200, order by 2 PM", in English and Bangla.
- **Flower request form:** a same-day express box. Ticking it clears the date (it means today) and asks for the address. After 2 PM Dhaka time it says when to order instead.
- **FAQ, shipping and terms pages:** flowers within 3 days, usually the same day, plus how express works. The homepage delivery line for flowers says the same.
- **Stock orders:** unchanged, still 48 hours inside Dhaka.

## What changes for you (admin)

- An express request shows a red "Same-day express · Deliver {date}" line in the preorder drawer.
- **Quote:** the ৳200 is added to the deposit, so it is paid in advance.
- **Totals:** the quote email, the WhatsApp quote, the account page and the "collect ..." amounts all include it.
- **Converting the order:** the fee becomes the order's delivery charge. The chosen day and card message now carry onto the order (they were dropped before, for every preorder).
- **Booking the courier:** express orders book Pathao **on-demand** (`delivery_type 12`) instead of the 48-hour service.

## Settings

The fee (`EXPRESS_FEE_BDT = 200`) and the cutoff (`EXPRESS_CUTOFF_HOUR = 14`) are in `src/lib/delivery.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] Type-check and lint pass. No em dashes.
- [x] `npx tsx scripts/check-express.ts`:
  - cutoff before and after 2 PM Dhaka time, flowers only, address required
  - customer notes cannot trigger on-demand booking
  - the WhatsApp balance equals what the courier collects
- [x] English and Bangla message keys match.
- [x] Local screenshots: the lily page in both languages, and the form before and after the cutoff.
- [ ] After the migration and deploy: place one express request before 2 PM, quote it, check the WhatsApp text and the deposit.
- [ ] Book one express order on Pathao and confirm on-demand is accepted for that zone. On-demand availability and price depend on the zone; the API value comes from Pathao's merchant docs and could not be tested here.

## Known limits

- Express is not offered on the weekly holiday or public holidays any differently. If the shop closes on Fridays, say so and I'll switch it off then.
- If a quote or deposit arrives after the day has passed, nothing blocks the order. The drawer shows the date in red so you can see it.

body:
## Summary

The axe sweep now runs the whole `best-practice` tag next to WCAG 2.1 A and AA, instead of only `page-has-heading-one` and `heading-order`. This is the last part of WEB-301; the heading migration landed with #814.

Closes WEB-301

## Changes

- `apps/web/e2e/support/axe.ts`: `AXE_TAGS` adds `best-practice` to the WCAG tags and the scan uses `withTags`. `BEST_PRACTICE_RULES` and the `rules` override are gone. The experimental rules stay out.
- `apps/web/e2e/specs/navigation.spec.ts`: the comment no longer claims the sweep skips `landmark-unique`; the spec still holds the landmark names in place.
- Docs: the axe section of `apps/web/AGENTS.md` and the summary in the root `AGENTS.md`.

## Motivation

`best-practice` reports no conformance failure but the structure a screen reader moves through: one `h1`, no skipped heading level, landmarks it can tell apart, content inside a landmark, no empty heading. Once #814 cleared the last violation, the whole set passed everywhere, so there is no reason to guard only two of its rules. A rule a later axe release adds to the set shows up in that release's Renovate PR, which fixes it or lists it in the baseline.

## Testing

- The accessibility specs, the hovered volunteer card and the landmark-name spec ran in the pinned Playwright container (both projects, including the forms submitted empty and the open search panel): 61 passed, 3 skipped by design, no violation. axe 4.14 has 30 `best-practice` rules, two of them experimental.
- The three skips are project-specific on purpose: the 24 px target sizes are checked on the phone only, the heading anchor on keyboard focus in Chromium only (WebKit leaves links out of the Tab order), the hovered reason card on the desktop only.

## Breaking Changes

None.

author: sacss-dev
body:
## Étape 5 (partie bilans) – Nettoyage des bilans et calcul des ratios (Olivier)

Cette PR couvre la moitié « bilans » de l'étape 5. La moitié « BODACC »
(type et date du premier jugement) est faite par Lucas dans une PR séparée.

### Ce que fait cette PR
- `src/nettoyage/ratios.py` : à partir de l'extrait de l'étape 3, enchaîne
  1. la conversion des postes en décimaux (float64) ;
  2. les filtres (types de bilan, un bilan par entreprise et par année) ;
  3. le statut des comptes (`statut_comptes` : `public` / `confidentiel`, pour la partie 5) ;
  4. le remplacement par 0 de certains postes absents ;
  5. l'harmonisation des postes C et S en colonnes communes (`chiffre_affaires`, `resultat_net`,
     `capitaux_propres`, `total_bilan`, `dettes_totales`, `emprunts`, `disponibilites`...) ;
  6. le calcul de 6 ratios ;
  7. la winsorisation à 1 % et 99 %.
- `config.py` : `CHEMIN_S3_BILANS_RATIOS`, `TYPES_BILAN_GARDES`, `STATUTS_COMPTES`,
  `CODES_ABSENTS_A_ZERO`, `CORRESPONDANCE_POSTES`.
- Résultat sur S3, lisible sans clé :
  `ocaffier/diffusion/faillites-signaux/bilans_ratios/bilans_ratios.parquet` (6 280 227 bilans, 884 Mo).
  Une ligne par SIREN et par année de clôture ; les colonnes brutes `poste_<code>` sont conservées.
- Lancement, sur le SSP Cloud : `python -m src.nettoyage.ratios`

### Choix de nettoyage (à justifier dans le rapport)
| Choix | Règle appliquée |
|---|---|
| Types de bilan | C et S gardés ; K exclu (bilan consolidé d'un groupe : risque de double compte) |
| Plusieurs bilans la même année | On garde le plus complet (`nombre_postes`), puis le plus récent |
| Postes absents | 0 seulement pour les postes de détail (emprunts, disponibilités, dotations, charges de personnel, composantes du CA en S) **et** seulement dans les comptes publics ; les totaux et tous les postes des comptes confidentiels restent NULL (inconnus) |
| Dénominateur nul ou négatif | Ratio NULL |
| Winsorisation | Quantiles 1 % et 99 % de chaque ratio, calculés sur toutes les années ensemble |

### Ratios calculés
| Ratio | Définition | Famille |
|---|---|---|
| `rentabilite_nette` | résultat net / chiffre d'affaires | Rentabilité |
| `marge_exploitation` | résultat d'exploitation / chiffre d'affaires | Rentabilité |
| `autonomie_financiere` | capitaux propres / total du bilan | Solvabilité |
| `taux_endettement` | dettes totales / total du bilan | Endettement |
| `liquidite` | disponibilités / total du bilan (**bilans C seulement**) | Liquidité |
| `croissance_ca` | CA de l'année / CA de l'année précédente − 1 (NULL si l'année précédente manque) | Croissance |

### Validation
Bilans bruts : 6 323 425 → après filtres : 6 280 227.

| Ratio | Valeurs connues (C) | Médiane (C) | Valeurs connues (S) | Médiane (S) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rentabilité nette | 2 911 478 | 3,7 % | 1 152 332 | 3,9 % |
| Marge d'exploitation | 2 915 200 | 3,7 % | 1 154 530 | 4,2 % |
| Autonomie financière | 4 751 182 | 41,6 % | 1 522 153 | 37,3 % |
| Taux d'endettement | 4 737 919 | 57,6 % | 1 503 023 | 63,2 % |
| Liquidité | 4 739 762 | 11,9 % | 0 | — |
| Croissance du CA | 1 981 331 | 2,4 % | 693 871 | 2,4 % |

Contrôles faits sur un extrait : aucun doublon SIREN-année ; en S, CA = 210 + 214 + 218 ; en C, CA = FL ;
aucun zéro ajouté dans un compte confidentiel.

### Constats utiles pour la suite
1. **La rentabilité n'est connue que pour environ 60 % des bilans C**, contre environ 100 % pour
   l'autonomie financière : les comptes confidentiels cachent leur compte de résultat, pas leur bilan.
   À garder en tête pour la partie 3 (biais de sélection) et la partie 5.
2. **Pas de ratio de liquidité pour les bilans S** (actif non détaillé) : limite à écrire dans le rapport.
3. **4 bilans S affichent plus de 2,1 milliards d'euros de CA**, ce qui est très suspect pour un bilan
   simplifié (probables erreurs de saisie). Leurs ratios sont ramenés dans les bornes par la winsorisation.
4. **Correctif technique** : les postes sont convertis en float64 dès la lecture. Avec pandas 3, mélanger
   des Int32 et des Int64 faisait planter l'harmonisation (déclenché par ces 4 bilans).

### ⚠ À l'attention de Lucas et Claudia
- **Claudia (étape 6)** : lis le fichier avec
  `lire_parquet_s3(config.CHEMIN_S3_BILANS_RATIOS + "/bilans_ratios.parquet")`. La colonne
  `annee_cloture` et la date `date_cloture_exercice` servent à calculer N-1 à N-4 par rapport au jugement.
- **Lucas (étape 8)** : les ratios sont winsorisés ; pour les rangs sectoriels, il faudra joindre la
  section NAF depuis SIRENE (`section_naf`).
- **Tous** : deuxième panne due aux versions non fixées (pandas 3 après DuckDB) : figer
  `requirements.txt` sans attendre l'étape 13.

author: kartamyshev-dev
body:
LAB-1680. `python-module-v1`: члены модулей проверяются по списку разрешённых имён, а не только по deny-list.

**Причина.** На `origin/v040` политика пропускала `np.fromregex("/etc/passwd", …)` и `pd.ExcelFile("/srv/secret.xlsx").parse(0)`: обе функции читают файлы сервера.

**Правка**
- `python-source-policy.mjs`: `PYTHON_MODULE_NAMES` — разрешённые имена верхнего уровня для каждого модуля из `PYTHON_ALLOWED_MODULES`, плюс подмодули (`numpy.random/linalg/ma/fft`, `pandas.api.types`, `pandas.offsets`, `pandas.tseries.*`, `collections.abc`). `inspectModuleMembers` разбирает импорты по всему скелету, включая скобки и `\`-продолжения: `import m.sub as a`, `from m import (x as y)`. Затем проверяет каждую цепочку `псевдоним.имя[.имя…]`; переносы и пробелы вокруг точки её не разрывают. Отказы:
  - `attribute:<модуль>.<имя>` — имя не из списка;
  - `attribute:<модуль>.*` — импорт со звёздочкой;
  - `module_value:<модуль>` — модуль используется как значение (`f = np`);
  - `alias:<имя>` — одно имя импортировано и как модуль, и как другое значение.

  Deny-list остаётся первым слоем и по-прежнему проверяет члены объектов. Поэтому прежние причины отказов не изменились.
- `python-parameters.mjs`: в текст отказа добавлена подсказка: какое имя запрещено и чем его заменить.

author: derekadams
body:
## Summary

An authenticated GraphQL request whose access token the server rejects with HTTP 401 (for example a token revoked or expired early, or a clock that runs behind) used to fail outright, even though the session's refresh token could still mint a new one. `@devicechain/client` now offers opt-in recovery: one forced refresh, one replay of the same operation, and then the host's `onEnd` if recovery fails or the replay is refused again.

- `setUnauthorizedHandler({ refresh, onEnd })` and the `UnauthorizedHandler` type are new exports. Without a handler the SDK behaves exactly as before and throws `GraphQLRequestError` with status 401.
- `SessionTokens.forceRefresh(rejectedToken)` refreshes regardless of the token's expiry, shares an in-flight refresh with any concurrent caller, returns the sibling's fresh token when a 401 arrives after another request already refreshed, returns null for a token from a replaced session, and ends the session rather than handing back the rejected token. This adds a member to the `SessionTokens` interface, which the SDK returns from `createSessionTokens`; the API report records it as an additive member.
- Recovery is bounded: at most one refresh and one replay per request, never for anonymous requests, and the refresh call itself is anonymous so it cannot recurse. Replaying is safe for mutations too, since the server answers 401 at the authentication middleware before any operation runs.
- The console and the dashboard viewer register the handler. Identity tokens have no refresh path, so a 401 on that lane ends the identity session. `onEnd` only clears the session that still owns the rejected token.
- `frontend/api/client.api.md`, the package README and the GraphQL API reference (with the `es` and `zh-CN` translations) describe the behaviour.

## Testing

- `npm ci`, `npm run codegen`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` in `frontend`.
- `@devicechain/client`: 123 tests, including refresh sharing, the one-replay bound, anonymous requests, a late 401 from a replaced session, and a replay that is refused again. Dashboard: 288 tests. Console auth: 36 tests.
- `hack/check-npm-api.sh`: reports match, 0 breaking changes against the baseline.
- `node docs/scripts/check-structure-parity.mjs` and `hack/check-docs-adr-refs.sh`.
- Negative control: with recovery disabled, the new regression test fails.

author: akshaychugh-xyz
body:
## What this adds

`--judge llm` (or `Policy(judge="llm")`, or `PAUSE_JUDGE=llm` for the MCP server) lets a model make the judgment calls that were fixed thresholds: whether a rating is good enough given the review count, whether a return window suits this item and price, whether slow shipping matters, and whether a saving is worth a switch. The buyer's thresholds become a sentence in `--preferences`.

The fixed thresholds stay as the default judge and as the fallback.

## What the model is not trusted with

- **Hard stops** (`rubric.hard_stops`): a failed search, a store with no Google profile, a lookalike domain, an unknown store with an absurd price. These are decided before the model is asked, and it is never called for them.
- **Choosing a seller it wasn't given.** It may only pick from offers the code already filtered (new, same product, store checked). The alternative's price comes from the data.
- **The token.** `pay()` still only accepts a token issued by the gate.
- **Raw web text.** It sees numbers and names cut to 60 characters on one line. Reviews, store descriptions and Google's review summaries are never sent.

Any model failure (no SDK, no key, timeout, refusal, malformed answer) falls back to the thresholds. The receipt records which judge decided and what the thresholds said.

## Also in this PR

- A failed search now always asks the human, including at a store marked as known. Before, a known store could proceed during an outage.
- The model is shown how many reviews mention each topic, not only the negative percentage.

## Testing

- 42 offline tests pass (18 new). The new ones cover: the model overruling a soft threshold, the model being stricter, hard stops never reaching the model, an invented or excluded seller being refused, every failure mode falling back, hostile text in a store name being cleaned, and the request shape checked against the real Anthropic SDK with a fake transport.
- The rules scorecard is unchanged: 11 of 11 live cases as expected.
- **Not yet run against the live Anthropic API.** The session this was built in could not hold an Anthropic key. To run it: `pip install -e ".[llm]"`, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, then `pause scorecard cases/cases.json --judge llm`.

Flagship 6 (shift-roster-builder), item "a cheaper screen for given-up pairs". (Claimed einvoice-preflight first, yielded to #16188, which was opened a minute earlier.)

## What landed
- `coverPairRisk({ memo })` with `pairMemo()`: pair verdicts carried between walks and reused only when every list the search read is unchanged. It's exact (tests check the same verdicts, roster, moves and pairs searched). Opt-in through `coverPairMemo: true`.
- `coverPairRisk({ handOut: "fewest" | "takers" })`: measurement-only orders for handing out shifts.
- `eval/pair-memo.mjs`, `eval/pair-order.mjs` and their `.out.txt` files; README section "Remembered pair searches"; `pair-memo.test.mjs` (4 tests).

## Findings
- The memo hits 1,075 of 36,864 lookups on the 20-person week 2 and 212 of 283,507 on the 40-person week 0, where it's 23% slower. A given-up search reads 19.2 of 20 and 39.8 of 40 people's lists, so any move invalidates it. It stays off.
- Reusing given-up verdicts loosely was 10x faster but made 0 moves instead of 4. Dropped.
- Search order: no order gives up on fewer pairs on both weeks. At 200,000 checks with nothing given up, the confirmed pair hours change with the order (179 vs 187, and 313-355). So the pair check's exact answer is not order-free. That's the new flagship `next:`.
