body:
## Summary

Prepare the production image and gated release pipeline for #8. Cloud provisioning and live deployment remain pending the project, access, trial-credit and regional cost review; this PR does not close #8.

```text
Validate → test production image → transfer tested archive
         → independent production approval → GitHub OIDC
         → publish immutable digest → one migration job
         → stage candidate → HTTP smoke → promote traffic
```

The Docker image runs as a non-root user and includes the existing migration and private account-provisioning commands. CI now verifies login/current identity/logout, static assets, repeat setup and persistent sessions across application-container replacement against isolated PostgreSQL. The deployment runbook covers limited IAM, numbered secrets, connection headroom, backups and compatible application rollback.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the new image lifecycle test failed because no production image existed; this observed red run was uncommitted.
- **After:** 97 Vitest tests in 11 files, 4 Chromium journeys and 1 production-image lifecycle test passed locally. The Vitest suite includes 6 release-script tests covering successful ordering, failed migration/candidate gates and invalid deployment settings.
- `vp check`, `vp run typecheck`, Drizzle migration-history validation, application/operator builds, Docker build, Actionlint and shell syntax validation passed. The exported image's OCI revision label matches implementation commit `160e4b6`.
- Independent Standards and Spec agent reviews found no implementation findings against starting commit `0f24d8f`. Student teammate review and execution of the updated GitHub workflow remain outstanding.
- Existing deliberately failed required-check evidence is retained: PR #25 and Actions run 43592070147. Live GCP login, ingress, restart/record retrieval, backup and cost evidence remain incomplete; see `docs/deployment.md`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** delivery

Merging into `sprint-1` adds the Docker build and image test to the required Validate check. Release is manual, restricted to `main`, requires independent production-environment approval and configured GCP OIDC access. No cloud resource provisioning or deployment runs automatically on merge. A later migration can change persistent data and requires the documented compatibility and recovery review.

author: gokhanbdag-web
body:
## Problem
Admin requests are wrapped by the shared admin HTML shell in `index.php`. The wrapper was applied to POST endpoints as well, so a valid `application/json` response from `/admin/properties/locations/process` was transformed into a complete HTML admin document. The browser then received HTTP 200 with `<!doctype html>` instead of JSON.

## Fix
- Inspect the response `Content-Type` in the admin output-buffer callback.
- Return non-HTML responses unchanged; only HTML/XHTML responses pass through the admin shell.
- This protects all admin JSON endpoints, not only bulk location updates.

## Safety
- No route logic, authorization, CSRF validation, database schema, or geocoding behavior changed.
- Existing HTML admin pages continue to use the shared shell.

author: dontbyshai
body: ## Résumé SolarScan passe en **1.5.0**. Les réglages, le cache de tuiles et le modèle IA ne sont plus écrits dans le dossier du programme. Le moteur local est resserré autour de `127.0.0.1`. Trois ajouts aident le devis et la tournée. Rien n'est fusionné dans `main`. Aucune release n'est publiée. ## Corrections 1. **Dossier inscriptible.** Electron envoie `SOLARSCAN_DATA_DIR` (`app.getPath('userData')`, nom `SolarScan`). Réglages, `historique.json`, cache SQLite et `solar_detector.pt` y vivent. Un ancien `assets/settings.json` ou un modèle déjà téléchargé est recopié une fois s'il est encore sur le disque. 2. **Version 1.5.0** dans `package.json`, le lockfile (racine seulement), l'API `/health` et le README. Les commandes partent de `solar-scanner/electron` et `solar-scanner/backend`. Le README précise qu'Electron lance déjà le moteur : lancer `uvicorn` en parallèle occupe le port 8765, et l'app le signale puis quitte. 3. **Moteur local.** `webSecurity` est actif. Le CORS n'accepte que l'origine `null` (page `file://`). Les tuiles ne sont plus téléchargées depuis l'URL envoyée par l'interface : x/y/z sont reconstruits vers `data.geopf.fr` (80 tuiles max, zoom 12–22). Le SSL n'est plus désactivé. `/shutdown` et les autres routes (sauf `/health`) exigent le jeton `X-SolarScan-Token` créé au démarrage. Sans jeton (lancement manuel), `/shutdown` répond 403. L'itinéraire OSRM passe par le backend, hôte fixé. 4. **IA et CI.** `solar_backend.spec` embarque OpenCV, Ultralytics et torch (`collect_all`). Le workflow l'utilise et vérifie que ces paquets s'importent. `download_model.py` est documenté et écrit le poids dans le dossier utilisateur. Sans modèle, l'heuristique ne garde que le bleu sombre / le gris très sombre, rejette les formes trop longues, et plafonne la confiance à 70 % (le vert « haute confiance » reste réservé à YOLO). Le statut affiche `IA prête (YOLO)` ou `IA prête (heuristique)`. 5. **Ménage.** Clic droit Street View : `d.center` au lieu de `det`. Cache Nominatim borné à 256 entrées. `settings.json` (logo base64, ~266 ko) retiré du dépôt, remplacé par `settings.default.json`. Licence MIT ajoutée. Nom, adresse, SIRET, libellés et logo du PDF sont échappés ; seul un `data:image` est accepté comme logo. Les boutons Projet et CSV, déjà dans l'interface, sont branchés. La modale Street View n'est plus coincée dans la modale Tournée. ## Nouvelles fonctionnalités 1. **Historique des devis** (bouton horloge, en bas du panneau). Chaque PDF réussi ajoute une ligne locale : numéro, client, adresse, surface, HT/TTC. « Exporter en CSV » produit un fichier Excel FR. *Test :* scanner ou dessiner un panneau, générer un PDF, rouvrir l'historique, exporter le CSV. Le fichier est `historique.json` dans le dossier SolarScan. 2. **Seuil de confiance et fusion des doublons.** Le curseur retire du total (et du PDF) les panneaux sous le seuil, sans les effacer. « Fusionner les doublons » ne garde qu'une détection quand deux centres sont à moins de 15 m (la plus confiante). *Test :* scanner deux fois la même zone, monter le curseur, puis fusionner. Le compteur `retenus/total` doit baisser. 3. **Numéro de devis, validité, feuille de route.** Les paramètres ont « Validité du devis (jours) » et « Prochain n° de devis ». Le PDF affiche `DEV-année-00N` et incrémente le compteur. Dans la tournée : retirer une étape, et « Feuille de route » exporte le PDF du jour (distance et frais si l'itinéraire a été calculé). *Test :* régler le n° 12 et 15 jours, générer un devis, ajouter deux clients, calculer l'itinéraire, exporter la feuille. ## Vérifications faites ici - `python -m unittest test_v15.py` : chemins, URL de tuile ignorée, cache borné, heuristique (panneau bleu gardé, toit clair et route ignorés), jeton, `/shutdown`, version 1.5.0. - `node solar-scanner/frontend/test_v15.js` : échappement HTML du devis, numéro et validité, fusion des doublons, absence de `det.center`. ## Non vérifié ici - L'application Electron sur Mac (fenêtre, tuiles IGN, Street View, PDF réel). Le build PyInstaller avec Ultralytics/torch n'a pas été lancé dans cet environnement : il est lourd, et le workflow ne part que sur `main`. - Le téléchargement réel du modèle Hugging Face et une inférence YOLO. - Les appels réseau Nominatim, IGN et OSRM. Shaï peut lancer `cd solar-scanner/electron && npm start` sur son Mac. Le moteur Python démarre avec l'interface.

author: howardreith
body:
## What this changes

1. **Boughkeeper's buff icon.** The visible armor-class buff (`KMG.ElvenBranchedSpear.BoughkeeperArmorClassBuff`, `064feb1123cfb1ae4f541ef5e4d138a1`) was built with a null icon, which the game draws as a white square beside the portrait. `ProjectAssetIcons.Apply` now gives it the existing cached `elven-branched-spear` sprite through `BlueprintUnitFactAccess.SetIcon`, beside the spear item and proficiency assignments.
2. **Effect links on all eight named-spear buffs** (added at the owner's request). The buffs had no `FxOnStart`/`FxOnRemove` links, so the game cut their activation short: a buff showed in the portrait only after a later buff event, and its end was never scheduled. The helper that builds them now applies the empty links the project's other effect-free buffs use (`BlueprintUnitFactAccess.UseEmptyBuffEffects`). This covers Boughkeeper's buff, the Thornstep, Viper's Reach and First Branch penalties, and the four hidden once-per-round markers.

Names, descriptions, visibility, stacking, values, triggers, GUIDs and the declared one-round durations are unchanged; the links are what make those durations take effect. The hidden markers stay hidden. `assets/game/icons/elven-branched-spear.png` is unchanged (SHA-256 `5a8d3d10f95af61c6afd324c8791b37bb675d4a74d3dcd4eca7cdb4d0464109a`).

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/KingmakerGunslinger/Blueprints/ProjectAssetIcons.cs` | The one `SetIcon` call. |
| `src/KingmakerGunslinger/Blueprints/ElvenBranchedSpearNamedBlueprints.cs` | `UseEmptyBuffEffects` in the shared buff helper. |
| `assets-source/original-icons/icon-catalog.json` | Boughkeeper's buff recorded as an `intentional-family-share` consumer of a new `elven-branched-spear` concept and art source. The assignment is listed as an exact `authorizedFeatureEdits` hunk on the existing protected `ProjectAssetIcons.cs` record; it is reversed before the original baseline hash is enforced, so the baseline and every other assignment stay protected. |
| `KNOWN-ISSUES.md` | Spear buffs removed from the missing-links entry; new entry for the three icon-less penalty buffs. |
| `tools/LoaderCompatHarness/UiProbes.cs`, `HarnessRunner.cs` | Test-only ops `kmgOpportunityBuffUi` and `kmgTimedBuffs` (not in the product package). |
| `scripts/compatibility/loader-compat/sessions/boughkeeper-buff-icon.json`, `named-spear-buffs.json` | The two native sessions. |
| `reports/boughkeeper-buff-icon/NATIVE-UI-CHECK.json` | Evidence record with exact identities and limits. |

No source-text test was added.

## Validation

Focused development checkpoint, per `docs/VALIDATION-POLICY.md`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python tools/validate_icon_catalog.py --root .` | PASS |
| `python tools/test_icon_catalog.py` | 36 tests, OK |
| `Invoke-KmgGate.ps1 -Filter 'elven-branched-spear;eastern-weapons;project-icon;icon-graph;native-icon-guard;armed-presentation'` | Production compiled; 46 tests, 0 failures |
| `Build-Local.ps1 -DevelopmentPurpose boughkeeper-buff-icon` (development candidate, never a release) | Repository wrapper, 46 selected tests, exact-reference build and strict package validation passed. Package `8f4888aa…18590f`, DLL `c00f3a4e…d9c81a`, built at `d4181b1abb`. |

Deferred by policy: complete domain suite, release qualification, compatibility matrix. The frozen 0.0.190 release validator rejects this branch because product source differs from the released source, as it does for any content change; that is for the next release opening.

## Native check

Run in the disposable loader-compat game copy (owner 0.33.0 loader profile, standalone mod set, saves redirected to a per-session profile, fixture save `KMCS_AFTER_NORMAL_012_MODONLY.zks`), all on the final candidate.

**Boughkeeper** — session `20261115T153646Z-owner-0.33.0-boughkeeper-buff-icon`, PASS. The main character is armed with Boughkeeper; the game queues its own attack-of-opportunity command against a disposable hostile target and the harness runs it while paused, with the attack bonus raised so the hit is certain.

- One AoO hit; AC 17 → 18; buff in the portrait after that first hit.
- Slot draws `KMG_Icon_elven-branched-spear` at 19×19 px; tooltip "Boughkeeper", "6s", "+1 dodge bonus to Armor Class until the beginning of the wielder's next turn."
- After the fight is ended and play resumed, the buff ended by itself at 6.0 s of game time and AC returned to 17.

**All eight buffs** — session `20261115T153418Z-owner-0.33.0-named-spear-buffs`, PASS.

- The product's own `disposable-elven-branched-spear-combat` scenario passed its 24 assertions, so each named effect is still granted by its real trigger.
- Each buff was then put on the main character for one round with the game's `AddBuff`: all eight completed activation, the four visible ones showed in the portrait and the four hidden markers did not, and all eight ended by themselves at 6.0 s of game time with AC, speed and Reflex back at their earlier values.

**Comparisons**

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| Links on Boughkeeper only | Named-spear session FAIL by design: the game did not finish activating any of the other seven buffs. |
| Icon only (`6b72c8e28f`) | Boughkeeper appeared only after a second hit and was still on the character, with AC 18, after three rounds. |
| Published v0.0.190 | No icon; the slot is a white square. |

Every session reported the owner's saves and installation unchanged and the registry settings restored. Screenshots stay lab-local under `C:\Dev\KingmakerGunslingerLab\runtime-evidence\loader-compat\`; their hashes, and three discarded runs, are in the evidence record.

### For the owner to judge

- **Legibility at 19 px.** The white square is gone and the slot shows the spear, but the art is a thin diagonal shaft with a small pale blade, so at actual size it is a faint line. Enlarged it is clearly the spear. This PR does not repaint the icon.
- **Effects now end on time.** On v0.0.190 Boughkeeper's +1 AC stayed past its one round. The same construction was on the three penalties and the four once-per-round markers, so those may also have outlasted their round; that was confirmed in isolation only for Boughkeeper.
- **Three more white squares, not fixed here.** The visible Thornstep, Viper's Reach and First Branch's Reprisal penalty buffs have no icon. They sit on the enemy that was hit, so they show wherever an enemy's buffs are listed. Giving them art is a separate icon decision and needs its own authorized `ProjectAssetIcons.cs` hunk.

### Not covered

The character sheet's Buffs row, controller UI, turn-based mode, other loader profiles and mod sets, an attack of opportunity provoked by enemy movement in live play, the seven other buffs timed on an enemy after their real triggers, and reuse of a once-per-round effect in the following round of a live fight.

Accepted by the owner on 2026-11-15 and merged at their direction. Not released: no release is to be cut from this merge.

author: huacnlee
body:
Fixes #2110.

## Problem

On Windows, the GPUI backend built a web view synchronously inside `WebItem::prepaint`, which runs while GPUI holds `&mut App`. `wry`'s `build_as_child` → WebView2 `wait_with_pump` runs a nested message loop. That loop dispatches GPUI's queued foreground tasks (engine commits, the caret blink timer), they call `AsyncApp::update`, and the app panics with `RefCell already borrowed`.

## Fix

- On Windows, `prepaint` now reads the window's raw handle and schedules the build with the existing `rt::outside_app`, which runs on the main thread after the current update and outside any app borrow. The next prepaint places the view, as it already does for newly built views. A `building` flag stops a second build being scheduled. The job checks the current props and does nothing if a view already exists or the build failed.
- `build` now takes a `make` closure (Linux: `linux::build`, macOS: `build_as_child(window)`, Windows: `build_as_child(handle)`). macOS and Linux behave the same as before.
- No public API changes.

## Tests

- New `rt::tests::outside_app_runs_where_the_app_can_be_updated`: it schedules a job from inside an app update, the way a prepaint would, and checks that the job runs later and can itself call `AsyncApp::update`. This is the nested-pump case from the issue.
- `cargo test -p nsh-platform-gpui --lib` (299 passed) and `cargo clippy --all-targets` on Linux pass. `cargo xwin check` and `cargo xwin clippy --features webview --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` are clean.
- Not verified on real Windows: in our Windows VM, GPUI cannot start DirectX (`failed to initialize DirectX ... DirectWrite`), so `nsh-gpui-host` panics before opening a window, on `main` as well as on this branch. Confirming against the issue reporter's setup would help.

body:
Part of the modularity pass (#1373). `connectors/kubernetes/index.ts` and `substrate.ts` formed an import cycle: the barrel did `export * from './substrate.js'` and `substrate.ts` imported `createKubernetesConnector` back from `./index.js`.

`KubernetesConnector` / `createKubernetesConnector` depend only on the k8s submodules (client, kubeconfig, map, resolve, env-hash, objects, types), never on substrate. This moves them verbatim into a leaf module `connector.ts`:
- `substrate.ts` imports `createKubernetesConnector` from `./connector.js` (a leaf, no path back).
- `index.ts` becomes a pure barrel and re-exports `./connector.js`, so every importer of `./kubernetes` is unaffected.

Pure extraction, no logic change.

## Check
`npx madge@8 --circular --extensions ts --ts-config tsconfig.json src` from packages/core no longer lists `kubernetes/index.ts > kubernetes/substrate.ts` (the two remaining cycles, otel and ingest/policy/traverse, are pre-existing and untouched). Full core suite: 3875 passed; build + DTS pass; lint 0 errors.

Refs #1644
Refs #1373

## Motivation

Learners often want to time a study session without changing curriculum or saved progress. This adds an experimental session timer that can be started, paused, resumed, and reset, and is disabled by default.

Disabled by default. Enable with:

```bash
VITE_EXPERIMENTAL_STUDY_TIMER=true npm run dev
```

The timer keeps elapsed time across in-app navigation. A successful “save and end” pauses it. Reloading the page clears it.

The Bash pipeline propagates failure. A summary check requires **39 tests and a plain OK**, rejecting zero/partial/skipped/failed summaries. The log is retained as a 30-day Actions artifact. [Ownership/plan before implementation](https://github.com/edithatogo/paignia/commit/283da882027b87b185233bd4c7b82e9c14918bc3) and [coordinator receipt](https://github.com/edithatogo/paignia/pull/14#issuecomment-6896175943).

The exact YAML run block executed locally on CPython 3.12.14: **39 tests passed**, no failures/errors/skips, unchanged fixture hashes. YAML parsing and comparison confirm the old Rust job and top-level configuration are identical. The summary guard rejects zero, partial, skipped and failed synthetic reports. `git diff --check` passes.

[Hosted exact-head receipt](https://github.com/edithatogo/paignia/pull/17#issuecomment-6896316260) confirms CPython 3.12.14 executed all 39 tests successfully, with equal head/temporary-merge trees, retained hashes/artifact and passing existing native/privacy gates. These are harness execution checks, not independent mathematical review or production-method qualification.

## Holds

Keep draft and unmerged. PR15's independent numerical review is now [accepted for its bounded fixture scope](https://github.com/edithatogo/paignia/pull/15#issuecomment-6896316061); that reviewer has no residual assignment and is archive-ready. author: arcanis
body:
## Problem

The pnpm linker and `nmMode: hardlinks-global` / `hardlinks-local` hardlink every package file, and any `hard_link` failure aborts the install with `I/O error (Invalid cross-device link (os error 18))`. This happens whenever the global folder (`<globalFolder>/index`) and the project are on different filesystems — Docker bind mounts and volumes, CI checkouts on another disk, separate partitions, other Windows drives — and, per #389, once a store entry reaches the filesystem's link limit (1023 links per file on NTFS).

## Solution

- When linking fails with `EXDEV`/`ERROR_NOT_SAME_DEVICE` or `EMLINK`/`ERROR_TOO_MANY_LINKS`, the file is copied (with its permissions) instead. Any other error still fails the install.
- A copy that already has the right content and permissions is left alone on later linker passes, after probing whether linking works again (in which case it becomes a link). Reinstalling over a copied tree doesn't rewrite it, `yarn install --force` repairs edited copies like edited hardlinks, and fixing the setup then running `--force` once restores the links.
- Each install prints a single warning when files were copied: how many, why, the cost, and a link to a new docs page. It goes through the regular report, so `logFilters` applies (`pattern: "*copied instead of hard-linked*"`):

  ```
  1182 files were copied instead of hard-linked because the store at /root/.yarn/zpm/index and the project at /app are on different filesystems; installs are slower and use more disk space as a result (see https://yarnpkg.com/concepts/hardlinks)
  ```

- New docs page (`/concepts/hardlinks`) explaining the store, when Yarn falls back to copies, and how to fix it: `globalFolder` / `YARN_GLOBAL_FOLDER` with Docker and CI examples, or a mode that doesn't use the store. It is linked from the linkers page.

Notes for review:

- For the link limit this copies rather than porting Berry's overflow entries (yarnpkg/berry#7307): the affected files are typically tiny, and copying shares the cross-device path. The overflow scheme can be added later if the recurring copies turn out to be noisy on Windows.
- The warning links to `https://yarnpkg.com/concepts/hardlinks`, which only resolves once the v6 site is served from yarnpkg.com. It is a single constant (`COPY_FALLBACK_DOCS_URL`) if `v6.yarnpkg.com` is preferred until then.
- Unlike Berry, which downgrades the whole `hardlinks-global` run to `hardlinks-local` on `EXDEV`, the decision is made per file, and it also covers the pnpm linker and `hardlinks-local`.
- Turning an up-to-date fallback copy back into a hard link can never fail the install: if the probe link or the rename fails for another reason (on Windows, typically a process holding the file open), the copy is kept and counted in the warning as "existing copies couldn't be replaced by hard links", and the probe file is always removed, including one left by an interrupted install.

Fixes #389

## Tests

- Unit tests in `linker/helpers.rs` drive the EXDEV/EMLINK/other-error branches through an injected link function: copy, mode preservation, up-to-date copies not rewritten, edited or outdated copies replaced, relink once linking works, warning text.
- Acceptance tests in `features/contentAddressedIndex.test.ts` (pnpm, hardlinks-global, hardlinks-local), using a `YARN_INJECT_HARDLINK_ERROR` hook gated on `YARN_IS_TEST_ENV` (same pattern as the npm login injections): single warning, link-limit wording, no rewrite and no warning on reinstall, no warning when linking works, `--force` behaviour, `logFilters`, executable bit.
- Manually verified with a tmpfs global folder and with `node_modules` as its own tmpfs mount: the first install succeeds with the warning, the second is a no-op, and a same-filesystem install prints nothing.
- Not verified on Windows or macOS (the raw Windows error codes are unit-tested under `cfg(windows)`).

- Colours are written as Tailwind arbitrary values (`bg-[#1c1c1c]`, `bg-[#a0441a]`, `border-[#8a8a8a]`, …) rather than semantic tokens. - Type uses the repo's `font-primary` / `font-primary-bold` family tokens; weight is selected by family class rather than `font-bold` / `font-light`, per the repo's typography convention.

1. Start Storybook (`npm run storybook`).
2. Open the story `Components/TestCard` → `Default`.
3. Confirm the panel renders with all seven blocks in order — header and settings icon, collapsed row, "Add New Design", both labelled fields with their placeholders, the two action buttons, and "Recent Breakdowns".
4. Confirm there are no console errors.

---

## Compatibility & Notes
- No breaking changes. No new dependencies, no configuration changes, and no route or navigation changes.
- The component is not imported anywhere in the app: it exists only as the artefact of this smoke test and is reachable through its Storybook story.

body:
<!-- archon-summary -->
Risk level: high

## What changed

Leads no longer copy their own model and effort onto every worker.
Before: delegate accepted any model, and its text told leads to pass a given model straight through, so a Fable-high lead started 3 or 4 Fable-high workers.
Now: an agent can carry `config.delegation_policy` (allowed workers by model or tier with an effort cap, a default tier, a max effort, a max parallel count, and exempt roles and models). delegate refuses a child outside it and names the allowed choices.
Without a policy, a child above the lead's tier is refused, and a child on the lead's own frontier model needs a `reason`, which is recorded on its task.
The policy shows in inspect_state and in the agent's assignment. The guidance says workers default to the balanced or fast tier. An older daemon ignores the field.
<!-- /archon-summary -->

<!-- archon-evidence -->
## Evidence

**delegate on a child outside the policy: before (base) any model was accepted; after, the refusal names the allowed choices (asserted in turn::tests::delegation_policy and kernel delegation_policy)**

Before:

```text
delegate model=anthropic/claude-fable-5-2 effort=low (lead on claude-fable-5-2)
-> Delegated to agent agt_... (worker) with task tsk_...
```

After:

```text
delegate model=anthropic/claude-fable-5-2 effort=low (lead policy: balanced tier at medium, max 1 parallel)
-> delegation refused: anthropic/claude-fable-5-2 at effort low: the model is outside your delegation policy. Allowed: workers any balanced-tier model at effort medium or lower, default tier balanced, max effort high, at most 1 unfinished at once, roles reviewer unbounded by this policy but not above your tier

no policy, lead on claude-sonnet-5-5 (balanced), child claude-opus-5-5
-> delegation refused: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 is a strong-tier model, above your own balanced tier; choose a model at tier balanced or below

no policy, lead on claude-fable-5-2, child claude-fable-5-2 without reason
-> delegation refused: anthropic/claude-fable-5-2 is your own frontier-tier model. Workers default to the balanced or fast tier ...; choose one, or pass `reason` ...
with reason="the proof needs frontier depth" -> Delegated; child task.delegation_reason = "the proof needs frontier depth"
```
<!-- /archon-evidence -->

## Technical detail

## Approach
- `aether_core::delegation`: `DelegationPolicy`, `WorkerChoice` and `ModelTier`, which moved from aether-model and is re-exported there. It also holds the pure admission logic (`admits`, `admits_without_policy`, `needs_reason`, `validate`, `describe`).
- `AgentConfig.delegation_policy` is optional and omitted when unset. Children never inherit it (`child_spec` clears it). `Task.delegation_reason` records a `reason`.
- `delegate` (aether-runtime `turn/actions/delegation.rs`): after model and engine resolution, `check_delegation_policy` compares canonical models and tiers against the parent's stored policy, or applies the no-policy rules. A frontier clone needs `reason` unless the policy names that model explicitly. `max_parallel` is counted early, then checked again under the creation hold (`Preflight.parallel_limit` and `Runtime::check_parallel_limit`), so a concurrent creation cannot slip past it. Only delegate sets the flag; a person creating a child is never refused.
- The policy is validated at creation: exactly one of model/tier per entry, well-formed models (exempt_models included), no blank exempt roles, max_parallel >= 1.
- Visibility: `inspect_state.delegation` and `model_tier`, a policy line in the assignment, and updated delegate, list_models and swarm_playbook texts. Feature `delegation_policy`.

## Wire shape (for Archon)
`create_agent.config.delegation_policy`, omitted when there is none:
```json
{"workers": [{"tier": "balanced", "effort": "medium"}, {"model": {"provider": "codex", "model": "gpt-6.1-terra"}, "effort": "high"}],
 "default_tier": "balanced", "max_effort": "high", "max_parallel": 2,
 "exempt_roles": ["reviewer"], "exempt_models": [{"provider": "codex", "model": "gpt-6.1-terra"}]}
```
- A child matches an entry when its model equals `model`, or its tier equals `tier`, and its effort is at most the entry's effort. `max_effort` caps every bounded child.
- With an empty `workers` list the bound is `default_tier`; without one, the parent's tier.
- `exempt_roles` children are outside the worker list, max_effort and max_parallel. They still may not be above the lead's tier unless their model is in `exempt_models`, which holds Archon's `<stage>.review` plan.
- Unknown fields inside the policy are refused.
- AgentConfig ignores unknown fields, so an older aetherd accepts the frame and ignores the policy (protocol test). A create without a policy fingerprints exactly as before.

## Verification
- fmt and clippy (-D warnings) are clean on the touched crates.
- cargo test: core 417, tools 321, daemon 425, runtime 860, plus engine tool_surface 6/6 after the budget fix; model, context and protocol all pass.
- New tests: core delegation (13); runtime in-crate delegation_policy (3), covering refusal text, max_parallel with exempt roles, and the exempt tier bound; creation concurrency (1); kernel delegation_policy (3), covering the no-policy tier refusal, the recorded frontier reason, and a malformed policy; protocol wire and back-compat (1).

## Review scope
- Whole change eadd04891..1b346c237: failed with 4 blocking findings, all fixed in e07eed6b6.
- Fix delta 1b346c237..7c3e1563b: passed with no findings.

## Follow-ups and limits
- Tiers are bands within one provider but are compared across providers.
- A grandchild under a non-leaf worker is bound only by the no-policy rules.
- The early `max_parallel` count in delegate is advisory; the authoritative check is under the hold.
- The tool-surface budget grew by a named 420 bytes for the new delegate text.

REVIEW: pass, by codex/gpt-6.1-terra (agent agt_01M7FS3QYQSHYNKN1SVT3YG2B1), codex/gpt-6.1-terra (agent agt_01M7FTADYD93QKXCWZRNW729H8)

Archon item: qi_01M7FQ4GF45M1FN9N9WP28G9M7

<!-- archon-initiative:ini_01M7FQ4GEQXVBX9AFXFMVC4HPA -->

<!-- archon-risk -->

**Needs at least two human reviewers who read the functional code changes.**

<details>
<summary>Why this level, and the diff, checks, review and label</summary>

**Why this level.** `build` proposed `high`, and its reviewer confirmed it.

Changes what delegate accepts for every agent: a new refusal of children above the parent's tier, and the frontier-clone reason rule. Adds persisted fields to AgentConfig and Task (additive and serde-defaulted) and a limit check under the creation commit hold, which touches concurrency. author: rpegio
body:
## 这个 PR 在做什么

把「设置面板（第 19 项）」和它引出的真机问题一起收口，主线分三段：

1. **设置面板落地**：NModal 弹层五组（外观 / 运行时 / 引擎 / 时间轴与保存 / 快捷键只读表）
2. **runtime 目录可搬家**：默认仍在 `%APPDATA%`，设置里可以整体搬到别的盘，**重启生效**，旧目录保留、验证无误后一键删
3. **真机两轮反馈的修复**：搬家读不到新目录、缩放留白、tooltip 自弹、气泡撞脸、语料编辑反复全选、轨道滚不动、运行中进度行挤压、搬家后设置存不进去

---

## 一、设置面板（第 19 项）

范围由用户逐组拍板（`m04501` / `m04549`），**明确排除**的项没有做：校对区宽度、`ocr_model`、FunASR 语言/超时、OCR 与校对参数（保持 OCR 页唯一配置）、撤销深度、快捷键改键（F 组只读）。

| 组 | 条目 | 落点 |
|---|---|---|
| A 外观 | 主题、侧栏默认折叠、界面缩放 90/100/110/125% | `stores/ui.ts` + `composables/appPrefs.ts`（缩放走 WebView2 原生 `set_zoom`） |
| B 运行时 | 目录 + 可用空间、移动到…、删除旧目录、下载源三档、分段大小、启动时自动准备、重新检查、打开日志目录、清单状态 | `ai_runtime/config.rs` 五个新命令（契约 §8.10） |
| C 引擎 | OCR 设备、MOSS 线程数、MOSS 超时、MOSS 设备只读（跳打轴页）、保留中间产物 | `runtime/config.json` |
| E 时间轴与保存 | 默认吸附、分割策略、合并策略、自动保存开关 + 延迟（关闭时收起延迟项） | `stores/timeline.ts`、`stores/project.ts` |
| F 快捷键 | 只读对照表（5 组 21 行 27 键位），与 `composables/shortcuts.ts` 注册表同源 | `SettingsModal.vue` |

入口两处：项目内顶栏与欢迎页（运行时目录、下载源在开项目前就该能改）。

## 二、runtime 目录搬家

- 指针文件 `<app_data>/runtime-location.json`（`runtime_dir` / `previous` / `moved_at`），原子写
- `resolve_runtime_dir` 的入参语义改为**应用数据目录**，顺序：指针 → `GSA_RUNTIME_DIR` → exe 向上 → `<app_data>/runtime`；指针悬空时退回兜底，**不返回死路径**
- 搬家 = 复制（跳过 `.downloads` 缓存）→ 按相对路径**逐条对账** → 写指针；缺一条就报错且**不写指针**（半搬状态比不搬更糟）
- 拒绝：目标 == 当前 / 其子目录 / 其上级 / 盘符根 / 非空目录
- 旧目录保留，设置里「删除旧目录」一键清
- 只搬 runtime，`recent_projects.json` 等仍在 app_data

## 三、真机反馈的修复

### 第一轮（2026-11-04）

| 症状 | 根因 |
|---|---|
| 搬家并重启后三个运行时全未就绪，面板却显示新目录 | `lib.rs` 的 setup 先 `join("runtime")` 再传进去，函数内部又拼一次 ⇒ 指针永远读不到 |
| 指针被删/改名后界面只说"未配置" | 悬空只 `eprintln`。新增 `location_warning` + 面板警示行 |
| 打开设置面板时说明气泡自弹 | `NModal` 自动聚焦第一个可聚焦元素，命中 `InfoDot` 按钮 ⇒ `:auto-focus="false"` + 只在 `:focus-visible` 展开 |
| 缩放 90% 下方留白、125% 挤压换行 | 用 CSS `zoom`，`100vh` 不跟着缩 ⇒ 改 `WebviewWindow::set_zoom` |
| 设置图标与月亮撞脸 | `ic-gear` 画成了太阳 ⇒ 重画 8 齿齿轮 + 中心孔 |

### 第二轮（2026-11-07）

| 症状 | 根因 |
|---|---|
| 语料行内编辑每敲一个字全选一次 | 函数式 ref **每次 patch 都调用**，里面无条件 `focus()+select()` |
| 标签列滚轮完全没反应 | `.timeline-col` 缺 `min-height:0`，flex 项被内容撑高 ⇒ `.tl-tracks` 永不溢出，行被 `overflow:hidden` 裁掉 |
| 运行中进度条/长文字/按钮挤一行，长句被压成竖排 | 三样塞进同一个 `.arow` |
| 搬家后引擎组任何一项都保存失败 | `validate()` 的 python_path 存在性检查无条件执行，而默认值 `"python"` 指向目录 |

最后一条的修法值得单独看：把 `validate()` 拆成 `validate_schema()`（形状）+ `validate_paths()`（存在性），**设置面板只用 schema**；`validate_paths` 的 `python_path` 判定与运行期 `pick()` 对齐（标准布局在位即通过）；`default().python_path` 改成 `python/python.exe`。

---

## 验证

- `cargo test --lib` **368 passed**（连续 30 次全绿；顺带修掉一个因共用临时目录名导致的偶发失败）
- `cargo check --lib` 无警告
- `pnpm build`（`sync_bundle_resources` + `vue-tsc --noEmit` + `vite build`）EXIT=0
- `pnpm tauri build` EXIT=0（NSIS 57.5 MB / MSI 75.6 MB）
- headless（`temp/css-preview/`）：弹层 5 组 21 行、27 键位、宽 720、无溢出、`tooltips: 0`、`zoomTest.calls = [set_ui_zoom 1, set_ui_zoom 1.1]`、`cssZoom: ""`、无 console 错误

## Review 时建议重点看

1. **`resolve_runtime_dir` 的语义变更**（`ai_runtime/config.rs`）：入参从"runtime 兜底路径"变成"应用数据目录"，7 个调用点全部同步。这行改错的后果就是第一次真机搬家失败，请确认所有调用点都只传 `app_data_dir()`。
2. **`validate()` 一分为二**：`update_runtime_settings` 只做形状校验是有意的——存在性校验会让"运行时没装齐"时任何设置都存不进去。
3. **`.timeline-col { min-height: 0 }`**：这行是"滚不动"的真正解药，不是幂等装饰，别在后续重构里被删。
4. **`bootstrap_runtime.ps1` 是 PS 5.1 + 中文，必须 UTF-8 带 BOM**：无 BOM 会按 GBK 解析、满屏假报错。本 PR 该文件改动已核对 BOM。

## 已知未做 / 留给后续

- 搬家、删旧目录、打开日志目录、引擎参数落盘这几项**需真机手测**（headless 覆盖不到）
- 第 19 项之外还有若干杂项仍挂着，见 `docs/MISC_TODO.md`

author: zhaozhaozz
body:
Part 2 of #769 (part 1: #830). A task no longer gets a worktree while it prepares. It gets one when it first needs repository files. Without a role team, its agent may choose that worktree, or none, before then.

## When a task gets its worktree
- **Prepare** (`Workspace.plan`): the commits reach the computer's git store as before. `worktree_plans` records the commit and the mode (`read` for reviews and event work, `write` otherwise). The task context gets `workspace: {commit, mode, worktree: 'not_bound', binding}`.
- **First need** (`Workspace.ensure`): the first repository read or command binds the system's choice. This is part 1's rule: a reader takes a free, unchanged worktree of the commit made for reading, else a new one; a writer gets a new one.
  - Calls of the control plane that need the checkout bind first, in one place: `Workspace.call`. This covers finalize, restore, integration, QA's source snapshot and policy commands.
  - The Pi session's own `read_file`, `write_file` and `run_command` run in the runner. When they find no `repo`, they ask the control plane through the mailbox and run once more. The request has `kind: 'workspace'` and is not a model tool, so the model needs no extra turn.
  - Calls on the task context (`../context/`), project notes and the agent's session work without a worktree.
  - Claude Code and Codex work in the checkout with their own tools, so they get the worktree before they start.
- **New PR head**: a review that holds no worktree yet follows the head by its plan only.
- **Unchanged**: file copies (no Git cache), request tasks and integrations still bind while they prepare.

## The agent's own choice (no role team)
The executing agent gets four control-plane tools while its task holds no worktree. They are added to `basicTools`, so role policies do not filter them out:

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `list_workspaces` | This project's worktrees on this computer generation, at most 30. For each: HEAD, whether it is at the task's commit, changes as the runner sees them now (new runner op `workspace_worktree_inspect`), last handover, and the unfinished tasks holding it (read or write, running or not). It also shows what the system would give the task. |
| `use_workspace(worktree_id, mode?, on_changes?)` | Takes an existing worktree. |
| `create_workspace(mode?)` | Makes a new worktree of the task's commit. |
| `no_workspace(reason)` | Works without repository files. |

What the system still guarantees, whatever the model asks:
- **One writer.** A writer takes only a worktree nobody holds. A reader may share one with other readers, but never one a writer holds. A task that writes must take its worktree for writing.
- **The runner checks every handover** (HEAD, tree, changes). A worktree with changes, or at another commit, is handed over only with `on_changes`:
  - `reset` saves its changes as `../context/saved-changes-<worktree>-<old head>.patch`, restores it to the task's commit and keeps ignored files such as installed dependencies. A `refused` worktree becomes `ready` again.
  - `keep_changes` is only for writers, at the task's commit.
- **A refused choice changes nothing.** The worktree is not marked, and the model gets the HEAD, changed files and what it could do instead.
- **`no_workspace`** is only for tasks that do not change files. Later calls that need files answer `no_workspace` with the reason. The task may still use or create a worktree afterwards.
- **Once the task holds a worktree, it keeps it for the attempt.**
- **No race in one turn.** The system's binding and the agent's choice are serialized per task directory, so a read and a `use_workspace` in the same turn cannot both take a worktree.

The project controller of a role team does not get these tools yet. Its roles get the system's choice when they need files. Giving the tools to the controller, and binding observers and QA read-only instead of cloning, are the next PRs.

## Records and console
- `workspace_bound` in the task history now has `decided_by` (`system`, `agent` or the controller's role). `workspace_none` records the reason when there is no checkout.
- The timeline shows a "工作区" or "不用工作区" entry, with a "自选" or "系统选择" badge:

  | the agent took a changed worktree with reset | the agent chose no checkout | nobody chose: the system bound at the first file |
  |---|---|---|
  | ![workspace-own](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhaozhaozz/bot/6cf933cf0a4a967f24e40affd95047031b770e22/workspace-own.png) | ![workspace-none](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhaozhaozz/bot/6cf933cf0a4a967f24e40affd95047031b770e22/workspace-none.png) | ![workspace-system](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhaozhaozz/bot/6cf933cf0a4a967f24e40affd95047031b770e22/workspace-system.png) |

- A review that chose no checkout says so in its published coverage: `No checkout: the agent worked without the repository files (<reason>)`. Its QA verifies without a source snapshot.
- When the cleanup removes a task directory, it deletes that directory's plan. Project removal deletes all plans.

## Runner and manager
- `workspace_worktree_inspect(worktree_ids ≤ 30)` is new. `workspace_worktree_bind` takes `on_changes` (`reset`, `keep_changes`). The manager validates both (`runnerTypes`, `runnerKeys`).
- Calls that need the checkout answer `workspace_not_selected: …` when the task has none.
- The Pi session starts in the task directory when there is no `repo` yet. It still tells the model its working directory is `<task>/repo`, where the files appear once bound.
- `workspace_advance` and the new reset share one patch helper.

## Differences from the design
- `create_workspace` takes no commit or ref. The task's commit is fixed by its object, and its snapshot, candidate and publication are computed against it.
- Readers are still checked at the next handover, not when they release (as in part 1).

## Model-visible text: same-model before/after
The no-team executor now gets four more tools, one more sentence in its system prompt, and `workspace` in its task context. Nothing else in the request changed: the captured system prompts differ only by that sentence, and Pi still reports `<task>/repo` as the working directory.

I measured this on the local deployment's model (`deepseek-flash`). The provider was called directly from the bot container with the database opened read-only, the same method as #784 and #820:
- **Requests**: the first model request of a review was captured from the real engine and the real Pi SDK, on `origin/main` (before) and on this branch (after). The project was a small JS repository with a Git cache.
- **Scenarios**: "pr" is a PR that adds a function. "issue" is an Issue that only thanks for a merged fix, the kind of task that needs no repository files.
- **Tool results** were simulated. The step cap was 6: in a simulated workspace, reviews keep exploring and rarely reach `finish_review`, so none of the runs finished. The metrics are early behaviour.
- **Two simulators**: in the first, `pwd` and `ls` answered nothing. In the second, commands answer like a real checkout, and the first repository read or command binds the system's worktree, as the code does.

| prompt | scenario | runs | workspace tool calls | turns spent only on workspace tools | first repository read or command (call #) | mean tool calls in 6 turns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | pr | 8 | — | — | 1 in 8/8 | 8.8 |
| `origin/main` | issue | 8 | — | — | 1 in 7/8, 2 in 1/8 | 8.8 |
| this PR, first simulator | pr | 8 | 0 | 0 | 1 in 8/8 | 9.1 |
| this PR, first simulator | issue | 8 | 3 runs: `list_workspaces` + `use_workspace` | 3 runs, after 2–4 turns of `pwd`/`ls` probes that came back empty | 1 in 7/8, 3 in 1/8 | 8.4 |
| this PR, realistic simulator | pr | 8 | 0 | 0 | 1 in 8/8 | 8.6 |
| this PR, realistic simulator | issue | 8 | 4 runs: one `list_workspaces` each | 0 (always in the same turn as the first command) | 1 in 7/8, 2 in 1/8 | 9.0 |

body:
Before: ikam had no way to run work as a Petri net, and several kernel races only showed up with more than one writer: lost firings with `db_commit`, a second process unable to read the first's commits, puts failing when two handles dropped the same copy, and stored content lost in a crash with deferred syncing on.

After: an opt-in net module records firings, markings, outputs and checkpoints on the database log and replays them exactly, with a text format for nets, a compare-and-swap commit (`db_commit_at`), and five kernel fixes for the races above. Every optimization with a trade-off is an option, off by default.

This is one stack of experiments E269 to E308 (each on its own `exp/` branch, stacked in order), the experiment loop and its overnight run. Every experiment has an entry in `docs/experiments/log.md` and `registry.tsv`.

How: the kernel changes are in `src/net.rs` (new), `src/repo.rs`, `src/store.rs`, `src/ingest.rs` and `src/dict.rs`; the rest is examples, tests, the `net-jit` experiment crate and docs.

Kernel fixes, each with a test that fails without it:
- E292: `Repo::db_commit_at`, a commit that is refused when the ref moved, so concurrent writers stop losing firings; a NotFound race in the ledger build and `is_needed` at 8 writers.
- E296: a record always enters the shared ledger (35 transient failed reads in 600 trials before, 0 after).
- E298: `Repo::refresh_ledger` (option, off), so a process can read derivations another process recorded after its ledger was built.
- E299: a drop of a copy another handle already deleted is not an error (28% of puts failed before), and `FsStore` temporary names are unique per write.
- E300: in `open_deferred` mode a delete waits for the next sync, so a crash no longer loses the content a put replaced (all 24 seeds lost before, 0 after).

New options and APIs (off by default): the net module and its text format (E269, E270, E271), the table form, sum and lattice hashes of the marking, bounded enabling, checkpoints, color unfolding and incremental enabling (E278 to E286), `Repo::read_cache` (E294), `refresh_ledger` (E298), `FsStore::clean_temporaries` (E302). The loop's own tools: the gap list (E275, E290) and the night plan (E287). Measurements with no kernel change: E277, E282, E283, E288, E289, E293, E295, E297, E305, E307; E276 (ranking backtest) was refuted. The `net_kill` example shows worker recovery: requeue, leases, heartbeats, per-run beat refs and their cleanup (E301 to E308).

Tests: the full kernel suite passes on the last branch; the privacy scan passes over the whole range.

Notes for review:
- The hot/cold layer branches (E261 to E268, E310) also touch `store.rs`, `ingest.rs` and `repo.rs`; whichever merges second will need conflicts resolved.
- The `net-jit` crate (Cranelift) lives under `experiments/` and is not part of the kernel build.

author: lucasredjaimia
body:
## Summary

Phase 5 of the improvement plan: the detection tables that were hardcoded in C# now live in `data/detection.json`. The file is embedded in the exe as the default, and newer copies are picked up online without a new release.

## Design

- **`data/detection.json`** (`schema`, `version`, `updated`, then one section each for `nvidia`, `nvme`, `windows` and `riskyDrivers`). It holds:
  - NVIDIA problem releases (595.59, 621.01) and the minimum-release rule for RTX 50 (< 572.83), from `DetectionChecks.cs`. GPU families are matched by name, ignoring spaces (`RTX 5080` = `RTX5080`), so a downloaded file never supplies a regex.
  - DRAM-less NVMe model tokens and `hmbIssueBuild` (26100), from `NvmeDrives.cs`.
  - Windows end-of-servicing dates per build (consumer / enterprise / consumer ESU) and the date for older builds, from `WindowsRelease.cs`. The ESU, Server and LTSC logic stays in code.
  - The risky-driver catalog (file, owner key, explanation key, `recommendWhenLoaded`), from `RiskyDrivers.cs`.
  - Every user-facing explanation is a **Locales key**, never free text.
- **`DetectionData`** (`src/Core/Detection/DetectionData.cs`): loads the embedded resource `Data.detection.json`, then a cached copy if one is valid and newer. It exposes `Embedded` (never replaced) and `Current` (the snapshot in use, swapped atomically).
- **Online refresh**: `UpdateChecker.CheckAsync` is the launch-time check, and it already runs only when "check for updates at launch" is on (and never in read-only/screenshot mode). It now also starts `DetectionData.RefreshAsync()`. That refresh:
  - downloads `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasRedjaimia/DumpFinder/main/data/detection.json` using the same pattern as `UpdateChecker`: 10 s timeout, generic User-Agent, silent failure;
  - runs at most once per process;
  - refuses anything over **256 KB**, checked both on `Content-Length` and while reading the stream;
  - validates the file, and uses it only if its `version` is **strictly higher** than the tables in use;
  - writes the cache with `AtomicFile.WriteAllText` to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DumpFinder\data\detection.json`.
  
  `IsOwnUrl` also accepts this repo's raw prefix. This hook was chosen so that `src/UI/*` and `Program.cs` (owned by Phases 1 and 3) are not touched.
- Refreshed data applies the next time the checks run, and from the cache at the next launch.

## Validation (a whole file is refused on any error)

- `schema` must be 1, and `version` must be an int ≥ 1.
- Dates must be strict `yyyy-MM-dd`.
- NVIDIA versions must match `^\d{3}\.\d{2}$`.
- Model and GPU tokens must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 -]{0,31}$`, and builds must be in 10000–99999.
- Driver files must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,60}\.sys$`. This rules out paths, executables and service names.
- Each array has a size cap.
- Text keys must exist in `en.json` **and** belong to the expected section (`detection_checks.*` / `risky_drivers.*`).
- Driver entries are strict: an unknown field such as `service` or `disableable` is refused, not ignored.

## Security limits

- Downloaded data can only **add detection and warnings**. It can never name a registry key, a service or an executable to act on.
- `RiskyDrivers.IsDisableableFile` only accepts drivers of the **embedded** catalog. Fix ops (`Execute`) and undo (`IsRevertableKey`, used by `ChangeRecorder`) both go through `FindDisableable`, which applies that check.
- A driver that only a downloaded or cached copy knows shows up as a **read-only warning** under Hardware › Conflicts: no fix item, no op. Two new keys cover this, in all 14 languages.
- Embedded drivers are always kept, even if a download omits them.
- The cache sits in a user-writable folder while the app runs elevated. It goes through the same validation and is under the same embedded-only rule, so tampering with it can at worst change which warnings are shown.
- Caveat: a downloaded file that uses a Locales key the installed exe doesn't have is refused as a whole. New keys, and any new disableable driver, need an app release. This is documented in the README.

## Verification

- `dotnet build src/DumpFinder.csproj -c Release -o <temp>`: **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `--update-selftest` → **TOUT EST CONFORME**. The new cases cover:
  - embedded tables load;
  - raw URL of this repo accepted, raw URL of another repo refused;
  - valid newer file accepted, and the NVIDIA release it adds gets flagged;
  - embedded drivers are kept;
  - a downloaded driver is not disableable: op refused, undo refused, even with a forged `CanDisable`;
  - an embedded driver can still be disabled;
  - older and equal versions refused;
  - invalid JSON, free text instead of a key, a key from the wrong section, a bad date and an unknown schema are all refused;
  - drivers marked `disableable`, naming a service, given as a path or as an `.exe` are refused;
  - a payload over 256 KB is refused both as text and as a stream;
  - the tables in use are unchanged after the refusals and restored at the end.
  
  The live fetch currently reports "not published on main yet". That is expected until this PR is merged.
- `--detect-selftest` → **TOUT EST CONFORME** on a real PC:
  - the existing 595.59 / 621.01 / RTX 50 rules still pass;
  - the risky drivers really installed here (inpoutx64, RTCore64) are still detected, offered as fixes and revertable.
- README: new "Detection data" section (what the file is, that it only holds data, how to update it).

## Summary
Follow-up to #3075 and #3079 (#3029). It closes the gaps between the merged heavy read gate and the orchestrator's go conditions:

- **One named list next to the route table** (condition 1): `HEAVY_READ_ROUTES` in `backend/http_api/route_table.py`, the five view reads over the history. `Route.__post_init__` refuses any mismatch: `heavy=True` on a route outside the list, a listed GET route without it, or `heavy` on a non-GET method. So a route joins only by a decision in that list. Writes, auth, sync status, health and static files cannot take the gate.
- **A named wait** (condition 2): `HEAVY_READ_WAIT_S = 5.0` in `backend/runtime/heavy_reads.py`. A waiter holds no reader slot and no writer: the gate is taken before the handler opens a lease, as in #3075.
- **A waits count** (condition 3): `runtime.heavy_read_gate` now has `waits` next to `waits_over_1s`, `timeouts` and `longest_wait_s`. `scripts/prod_diagnostics.py` already allows `heavy_read_gate.*`.
- **A disconnect while waiting** (condition 4): the disconnect test now holds the gate in another thread first, so the request waits before its send fails with `BrokenPipeError` or `ConnectionResetError`. Afterwards the gate is free and no wait timed out. While it waits, a request does no socket I/O, so a hang-up shows only when it sends, and that path releases the gate in a `finally`.

Part of #3029

author: natbediee
body:
Closes #206

**Ce que fait la PR (seconde et dernière PR de l'issue)**
La PR #250 a ajouté `MySQLUtils.open_cursor` et y a passé les routers. Celle-ci passe dessus tout le reste du backend : `utils/`, `services/`, `etl/` et `agents/`. Il ne reste plus aucune connexion MySQL qui puisse rester ouverte après une erreur.

- `open_cursor` :
  - Nouvelle option `buffered=True` : le curseur lit tout le résultat d'un coup, pour qu'une ligne non lue ne bloque pas la requête suivante (« Unread result found »). Le chargement des spots en a besoin.
  - Elle ne passe à MySQL que les options demandées, et passe par `MySQLUtils.get_cursor`, comme elle passe déjà par `connect` et `disconnect`. Les tests existants gardent ainsi leurs faux curseurs sans changement.
- Les 31 connexions qui n'étaient pas protégées passent sur `with`, dans 17 fichiers :
  - `services/` : `plan_service` (`insert_or_update_plan`, `set_day_city`, appelés à chaque étape du voyage) et `service_store`.
  - `utils/` : les 5 anciennes fonctions de `db_utils`, et `get_city_center` de `geo_utils`.
  - `etl/load/` : `load_p4n`, `load_gpx`, `load_meteo`, `load_poi`, `load_poi_checks`, `load_carburants.known_stations`.
  - `etl/` : `etl_pipeline`, `etl_poi_check`, `etl_rattrapage`, `fill_communes`.
  - `agents/` : `dedupe_spots`, `find_service_links`, `harmonize_spots`.
- `load_gpx` garde un `try/finally` plutôt qu'`open_cursor`, parce qu'il ouvre lui-même plusieurs curseurs successifs sur sa connexion. La fonction est coupée en deux : l'une ouvre et ferme la connexion, l'autre fait le chargement.
- Les 51 connexions qui avaient déjà leur `try/finally` restent telles quelles : elles se ferment déjà même en cas d'erreur.

Pour relire : beaucoup de lignes ne sont qu'un décalage de 4 espaces (le corps entre dans le bloc `with`). Dans « Files changed », cliquer sur la roue dentée, puis cocher « Hide whitespace ».

**Critères d'acceptation et preuves**
- [x] Une fonction de `utils/db_utils.py` s'utilise avec `with` et ferme le curseur et la connexion dans tous les cas.
  `MySQLUtils.open_cursor` (PR #250), complétée ici par l'option `buffered`. Tests : `tests/unit/utils/test_db_utils.py`.
- [x] Première PR : les routers ; seconde PR : `utils/db_utils.py`, `services/`, `etl/`, `agents/`.
  Les routers sont passés dans la PR #250, et tout le reste dans celle-ci. Recomptage fait sur le code : les 53 `MySQLUtils.connect()` restants (hors `db_init`, qui a sa propre connexion de démarrage) ont tous une fermeture garantie, par `with` ou par `try/finally`.
- [x] Un test montre qu'une erreur dans le bloc ferme quand même la connexion.
  Dans la PR #250 : `test_open_cursor_closes_everything_when_block_raises` et `/hikes`. Ici : `test_failed_choice_still_closes_the_connection`, où un choix du jour dont l'écriture échoue (« Lock wait timeout ») ferme quand même le curseur et la connexion.
- [x] Aucun changement de comportement : les tests existants passent sans modification de leurs attentes.
  1420 tests passent : les 1415 d'avant et 5 nouveaux. Ruff est vert. Deux fichiers de test existants sont touchés sans changer leurs attentes :
  - le faux de `test_db_utils.py` accepte maintenant toutes les options du curseur ;
  - `test_plan_service.py` reçoit `import pytest` pour son nouveau test.

  Sur la pile de branche, avec les agents coupés :
  - Un voyage de 2 jours à Plougonvelin. Jour 1 : rando, spot et un point d'eau. Jour 2 : « Rester à Plougonvelin », pas de rando, autre hébergement. Puis le carnet. Toutes les routes répondent 200.
  - Le rafraîchissement météo de Plougonvelin, qui passe par `load_weather_data`.
  - Une lecture de chaque fonction convertie qui ne fait que lire (villes, centre d'une ville, stations, lieux à vérifier…).
  - À la fin, **0 connexion MySQL** reste ouverte par le backend de branche.

**Découvert pendant le travail**
- `etl/load/load_p4n.py` ouvrait **deux** connexions et ne fermait jamais la première, même sans erreur. Ses `return` anticipés (ville absente) laissaient aussi la seconde ouverte. Cette fonction tourne aussi dans l'API, à l'envoi d'un GPX. Elle n'ouvre plus qu'une connexion, dans un `with`. Test : `tests/unit/etl/load/test_load_p4n.py`, qui échoue sur l'ancien code (2 connexions ouvertes au lieu d'une).
- `load_gpx` ouvre une connexion MongoDB qu'il ne ferme jamais. C'est hors du périmètre (l'issue parle de MySQL) : une issue est proposée.

author: koeppben23
body:
## Safety issue
`emitAuditBodyWithEvidence` advances `ctx.prevHash` before `appendAndTrack` resolves, despite the append being fallible. Its pre-finalized event hash is also provisional because the canonical writer stamps sequence/timestamp/hash under the write lock. Subsequent operations in the same drain must use the **committed** hash, not a speculative one.

## Atomic change
- Keep `ctx.prevHash` unchanged if durable append fails.
- After successful `appendAndTrack`, resolve the existing writer-tracked tip via `initChain(sessDir, sessionId)`; this is an already-initialized in-memory chain-state lookup in production.
- If the committed tip cannot be resolved, fail closed and leave the context unchanged.
- No public API, schema or data-layout changes; durable audit writer remains atomic.

## Tests
`src/integration/plugin-audit-committed-tip.test.ts`: failed append leaves cursor unchanged, successful append observes committed hash (not provisional), and unavailable chain tip fails closed.

## Verification
`npx vitest run src/integration/plugin-audit-committed-tip.test.ts`, full CI, Security, contract smoke. This PR addresses correctness, **not** the full rewrite-performance issue; performance claims remain reserved for a measured redesign.

Draft until all checks pass. It is independent of #1231 and may need its Unreleased changelog reconciled when #1231 merges.

ovn.rs had grown to 2857 lines. It is now a folder with one file per
function, each starting with the usual two licence lines, and mod.rs
carries nothing but the module doc comment, the module declarations and
the re-exports. Paths other files use are unchanged.

Names are lowercase snake_case and equal to the module name, so a case
sensitive filesystem builds the same tree this one does. Types get a
file of their own with their derives and trait impls, and each inherent
method is its own impl block in its own file. A private helper used by
only one function stayed with that function.

The shared constants are in consts.rs and the public ones in pub_consts.rs,

Unit tests left the tests module and sit beside the function they cover as
<function>_tests.rs under cfg(test). The helpers they share are in
test_support.rs; none of them had a Drop guard to keep.

NetBackend is an async_trait, so Rust wants the whole implementation in one
block. Each method body therefore lives in its own file as a body function
and trait_net_backend.rs is the single impl block that calls them; that is
the only place a name changed, and no body was edited.

author: parsabee
body:
Fixes #33

**Stacked on #55** (#32). The diff shows only #33.

## Problem
The windowed runner exited the event loop whenever Escape was pressed, before the game saw the key. A game therefore couldn't use Escape for a pause menu, for closing a dialog, or for "press Escape again to quit".

## Fix
- **`RunConfig::quit_on_escape`** defaults to `true`, today's behaviour. With it off, Escape reaches `ctx.input()` like any other key.
- **`EngineCtx::request_exit()`**, with `exit_requested()` to read it back, is how such a game quits. It sets `Loop::exit_requested`:
  - the windowed runner exits after that frame;
  - `Headless::run` stops early, and later calls run no frames.
- The close button and Cmd-Q always quit.
- `RunConfig` and `Loop` each gain a public field. That's a breaking change only for struct literals without `..Default::default()`; nothing in the workspace builds them that way.

## Docs
- The `RunConfig`, `request_exit` and `Headless::run` docs cover the new behaviour.
- The `stickshift-core` README and `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` §5 explain how to take over Escape.
- `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry.
- The `drive_frame` anchor in `docs/PLAYABLE_DEMO.md` was repointed (`#L218` → `#L226`); #32 shifted it.

## Tests
- **`a_game_can_ask_to_exit`:** a game that calls `request_exit` on its third update stops a 10-frame headless run at 3 frames, and a second `run` adds none.
- **`escape_quits_by_default`:** the default `RunConfig` still quits on Escape.

The winit key path itself has no test harness, but the change there is the single `&& self.config.quit_on_escape` condition, plus the `exit_requested` check after each frame.

## Checks run locally
- `cargo fmt --check` and clippy with CI's flags are clean.
- All 470 workspace tests pass.
- `cargo doc` builds with CI's rustdoc flags.
- `scripts/test-c-api.sh`, `playable-demo --smoke`, `check-renamed.sh` and `check-doc-anchors.py` pass.

author: sisshiki1969
body:
## Summary

`Encoding::classify` decided its SevenBit fast path with `bytes.iter().all(|b| *b < 0x80)`. LLVM does not vectorize a loop with an early exit, so that walked one byte at a time. Core's `<[u8]>::is_ascii()` is SIMD on x86-64 (word-at-a-time elsewhere) and does exactly the same test.

| 1 MiB ASCII, pinned nightly, opt-level 3 | throughput |
|---|---|
| `iter().all(\|b\| *b < 0x80)` | 2.9 GB/s |
| `<[u8]>::is_ascii()` | 104 GB/s |
| `str::from_utf8` | 55 GB/s |

Every `code_range()` miss goes through `classify`, and `String#gsub` reaches one per call (`check_match_encoding` asks `is_valid_encoding()`; the result is built with an Unknown range), so optcarrot's `--opt` code generator — a chain of `gsub`s over a few hundred KB of generated Ruby — spent 7–8.5% of its CPU samples in `classify`.

The same loop, as `all(|b| b < 0x80)` or its negation `any(|b| b >= 0x80)`, was spelled out in 26 other places (string building and appends, transcoding, regexp encoding resolution, `Regexp.union`, `tr` / `delete` / `count` sets, `scrub`, `unicode_normalized?`, Marshal symbols). All of them become `is_ascii()` / `!is_ascii()`. No behaviour change: `is_ascii` is precisely "no byte is >= 0x80".

## Measurement

`MONORUBY_PROF=cpu target/release/monoruby ../optcarrot/bin/optcarrot -b --opt ../optcarrot/examples/Lan_Master.nes`, three runs each way, release build with `--features prof`:

| | `classify` self samples | builtins / runtime tier | total samples |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 43–48 (7.1–8.5%) | 209–227 | 562–607 |
| after | 0 (not in the table) | 166–176 | 526–565 |

Checksum is 59662 in every run.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p monoruby --lib`: 2970 passed, 1 failed — `fork_block_child_runs_the_exit_sequence`, which fails identically on `master` in this WSL2 environment (`[false, true, 1] != [true, false, 1]`) and is unrelated.
- `cargo test -p monoruby --test integration -- string regexp marshal encoding transcode`: 146 passed.

## Not in this PR

With the scan itself now cheap, the remaining duplicate work on the `gsub` path is minor (~10 µs per MB) but still there: `EncBuf::finish` discards the `seven_bit` it tracked and returns `CodeRange::Unknown`; `Subject::text` recomputes `is_ascii()` although the receiver's code range was just cached; `Subject::to_inner` re-classifies on a no-match return. Setting `SevenBit` in `EncBuf::finish` would be the one worth doing.

author: generalpawz
body:
In a melee the musketeers' ramrods hung in the air and the muskets lay level on the shoulder between blows (#512, seen in the unit inspector). Neither is in a clip: a man posed by the hit-reaction ragdoll got every carried slot from the model's rest pose, and his weapon followed the physics arm, which leaves the clip's arm with the first step.

- **What a ragdoll carries** (`carried`, `carry`): slots that are not a body bone's own (sockets, held gear, fingers) keep the clip's matrix relative to their carrying bone, for a survivor refreshed every frame, for a dying man frozen at takeover. A part lying along a longer part held by another bone goes with that part: the stowed rod stays on the musket.
- **A survivor keeps his grip** (`held_arms`): the arms that hold a weapon in the clip pose keep the clip's pose relative to the chest for the reaction; trunk, head, legs and an empty arm stay physics. A dying man's fall is unchanged.

Render only; nothing writes to the world.

author: uxsmedjan
dhairya-007
body:
## Problem

The operation header names its enum by simple name only:

```java
javaType = "WatsonxAiOperations")
public static final String OPERATION = "CamelIBMWatsonxAiOperation";
```

`WatsonxAiOperations` is `org.apache.camel.component.ibm.watsonx.ai.WatsonxAiOperations`, the component's own enum.

Because the short name does not resolve, the header loses its value list: the generator derives an `enum` from a resolved enum class, so the catalog published no accepted values for the one header that decides what the producer does.

```json
"CamelIBMWatsonxAiOperation": { ..., "javaType": "WatsonxAiOperations", ... }
```

The matching `operation` URI option has always listed all 33, because its field is typed. After qualifying the header's `javaType` the two agree:

```
operation option : 33 values
operation header : 33 values   (was none)
```

This is the worst case of the gap I have found: 33 operations, with names like `textExtractionUploadAndFetch`, `textClassificationDeleteRequest` and `processToolCalls` that nobody will guess, and the header is the only way to vary the operation per exchange. A wrong value is not reported either - the conversion yields `null` and the producer falls back to the configured operation.

Fully qualified is the convention by a wide margin across the catalog: 3692 header `javaType` values are fully qualified or a built-in type, and 151 are not.

## Fix

Qualify it to `org.apache.camel.component.ibm.watsonx.ai.WatsonxAiOperations`, the FQN the component's own sources import. The header name is untouched.

Metadata only - no behaviour change. I diffed the regenerated catalog file against `main`: the only differences are this `javaType` and the `enum` list appearing beside it.

author: darknesskiller
body:
## Problem

A Claude Code session through the proxy re-bills most of its prompt cache. Rebuilt the cache chain from raw client JSONL (`cache_read(n)` vs `cache_read(n-1) + write(n-1)`):

| backend session | turns | cache writes | re-written | churn |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| direct (native) | 25 | 137,037 | 0 | **0.0%** |
| fixed CPA | 41 | 104,705 | 8,307 | 7.9% |
| this proxy | 58 | 417,495 | 291,065 | **69.7%** |

Native's total writes equal its final context exactly — every token written once. Through the proxy, reads plateau for several turns while writes keep accruing, so the previous turn's write is never re-read. Same model, same effort, same client version, single OAuth account.

## Cause

`buildClaudePassthroughBody` trusts the client body, but two steps still rewrote a marker set the client manages itself:

1. `normalizeCacheControlTtl` (`open-sse/executors/base.ts`) added an explicit `ttl:"5m"` to every marker even when the body carried no `ttl` anywhere.
2. `ensureCacheControlOnLastUserMessage` appended a breakpoint on the last user turn — the exact position `ensurePassthroughCacheBreakpoints` documents as "stays unmarked — it is the working set and would invalidate on every turn".

## Change

- `hasExplicitCacheTtl()` (`claudeCodeConstraints.ts`): true when any marker states a `ttl`. `normalizeCacheControlTtl` now runs only then.
- `claudePassthroughBody.ts`: inject a breakpoint only when the body carries none.
- `bodyHasAnyCacheControl` exported from `claudeHelper.ts`.

## Behavior preserved

- Marker-less bodies (Cursor and friends) still get the rescue from `ensurePassthroughCacheBreakpoints`.
- A connection cache opt-out still wins.
- A client-supplied `ttl:"1h"` still normalizes and pulls earlier breakpoints up. `hasExplicitCacheTtl` only skips the 5m default when *no* marker stated a ttl, so #30's "never bill 1h by omission" guarantee holds: absent ttl stays absent, which Anthropic prices as 5m.
- Max-4-breakpoint and tool_result-nesting rules are untouched.

## Verification

Test added to `tests/unit/claude-passthrough-cache-wiring.test.ts`: a Claude Code body with 3 markers must reach upstream with 3, `ttl` still implicit.

```
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/claude-passthrough-cache-wiring.test.ts
```

Not yet executed here — this workspace has no `node_modules`, so CI is the first run.

Open risk: the marker rewrite is the strongest remaining suspect, not a proven root cause. If churn survives this, the next step is logging a digest of the outbound body per request rather than another body mutation.
