author: j-shilling
body:
## Decisions for the reviewer

- **Tradeoff:** the fix is in the test realm, not the application. `stale-auth-time-web` now takes the realm's default client scopes except `basic`, so its hardcoded `auth_time` is the only mapper writing that claim. As a result its access tokens carry neither `sub` nor `auth_time`; its ID tokens still carry `sub`, and the application reads only ID tokens. Keeping `basic` cannot work, because Keycloak offers no per-client mapper order ([realm](../blob/448-stale-auth-time-bdd-flake/docker/keycloak/pre-ets-realm.json), [local services](../blob/448-stale-auth-time-bdd-flake/docs/docker-compose.md#keycloak)).
- **Beyond plan:** the Stale tenant setup step now signs the synthetic user in at the real provider, without the application, and fails unless the ID token carries a subject and an authentication time at least a day old. Without `basic`, a fixture that stopped emitting `auth_time` would be denied as missing evidence, and the scenario would pass without a stale time reaching the freshness check. The helper reads the provider's answer to the sign-in without following it, so the code never reaches whatever listens at the redirect URI. This adds about a second, one support helper, and a sentence in the [step guidance](../blob/448-stale-auth-time-bdd-flake/tests/bdd/steps/README.md). It is a harness prerequisite check, like the permission-denial setup's access check, not application evidence (V-004).
- **Evidence substitution:** the cause (V-001) rests on the provider's ID tokens and on the scenario failing on the same realm import, not on the application's span for the failing callback. When the scenario fails at the status step, its servers stop before that instance exports. The span for the fixed realm is captured (V-003).
- **Outstanding manual check:** sessions may not dispatch the Nightly BDD workflow. A person may dispatch it on this branch to see the fix in CI; otherwise the first nightly run after merge shows it. Requirements BDD ran only by tag: `@preets-session-013` in full (15 of 15 at 96b1995) and its stale, provider, and fresh-recovery scenarios by name; no out-of-scope failure was seen. CI pins Keycloak 26.8.1 and Compose pins 26.8.2; the fix was probed on both.

## Review objective

One-pull-request change: a fix inside an approved contract, or Light work such as a refactor, tooling,
documentation, or a dependency update. Approval means the change is correct and stays inside the contract it names.
New behavior or a contract change belongs in a specification pull request instead.

## Tier

- Risk tier: High
- Triggers that matched, or why none applies: as #448 records, authentication freshness on a PHI-bearing, tenant-isolated path, PREETS-SESSION-013 (the `SESSION` area); the failure meant a session may have been established when none was required.
- Why a stack does not apply: a fix inside the approved contract with no new behavior; the issue asks for one pull request.
- Issue and the approved contract this stays inside: #448, within PREETS-SESSION-013 criterion 3 and the freshness window in [Authentication](../blob/main/docs/authentication.md). No application code changes.

## Change

- **Cause.** In Keycloak 26 every client gets the realm's `basic` client scope, whose `auth_time` mapper writes the session's real authentication time. `stale-auth-time-web` also has a hardcoded mapper that writes `1000000000` (2001) to the same claim. Keycloak applies the two in an order that is fixed within one realm import and changes between imports. On an import where `basic` wins, the fixture's ID tokens report a genuinely fresh authentication, the callback correctly confirms freshness and establishes a session, and the scenario fails with `303 !== 200`. CI imports a fresh realm on every run, so the outcome varied by run.
- **No application defect.** A 303 from `/auth/callback` comes only from session establishment, after the freshness window confirmed the provider's `auth_time`. In those runs the provider reported a fresh authentication, so confirming it was correct. The freshness check, the callback, and the scenario's Gherkin and `Then` steps are unchanged.
- `docker/keycloak/pre-ets-realm.json`: `stale-auth-time-web` lists `defaultClientScopes` without `basic`; its description says why.
- `tests/bdd/steps/tenant.ts`, `tests/bdd/support/browser.ts`, `tests/bdd/support/harness.ts`: the Stale tenant setup check described above (`providerIdTokenClaims`, `providerBrowser`). `addFixtureTenant` now answers the issuer and callback origin it wrote.
- `tests/bdd/support/browser.ts` now owns the tracked provider's origin and its authorization and authentication-step predicates; `tests/bdd/steps/expiration.ts` and `tests/bdd/steps/fresh-recovery.ts` use them instead of their own copies (review R-001). Their behavior is unchanged.
- `docs/docker-compose.md`: lists the realm's two fixture clients and records the rule that a fixture client hardcoding a claim `basic` also maps leaves `basic` out. `tests/bdd/steps/README.md`: when setup may reach the provider directly.

## Evidence

Verified SHA: 96b1995. Verification report, round 2: `refs/notes/verification` @ 96b199565152bbf4e6125e4911ecfc93454c9530, run `08ebae64-df22-4561-829b-ec3a6698c6c9`: V-001 to V-006 established, no telemetry rows, no forbidden data, no escalation. Round 1 (run `59738e64-0dcc-4b08-9c91-ab7980219d6e` @ 8740e65) established the same claims. Both were recorded by the verification session. `pnpm verify:gate` passes at 96b1995.

Code review: round 2 (review `a0983c41` at 96b1995) has 0 blocking and 0 advisory findings. R-001 from round 1 (review `77501f02` at 8740e65, advisory: duplicated provider endpoint predicates) is closed as fixed.

The Evidence column below is the implementation session's own local runs; the results are the verification report's.

Local conditions: synthetic tenants, the tracked realm's `demo` user, Keycloak 26.8.1 (CI's image) in disposable containers started as CI starts them (`start-dev --import-realm`), and Keycloak 26.8.2 from Compose; Redis 8.10.3; production `next start`. A fresh realm import gives every mapper a new ID. An ID-token probe is one authorization-code sign-in for `stale-auth-time-web` outside the application, decoding the ID token.

| Claim | Result | Evidence | Limits |
| ----- | ------ | -------- | ------ |
| V-001: On the realm before this change, `stale-auth-time-web` has two ID-token mappers writing `auth_time` (the `basic` scope's session-note mapper and the client's hardcoded one), and which value its ID tokens carry depends on the realm import. On an import where the real time wins, "A real provider return with a stale authentication time establishes no session" fails with `303 !== 200` at `Then the response status is 200` | Established at 96b1995 and 8740e65 | Keycloak's admin "evaluate scopes" listed both mappers for the client on each of the 11 disposable imports inspected. ID-token probes on 21 fresh imports: 11 carried the current time and 10 carried `1000000000`, and every token from one import carried the same value. On the two such imports run before the setup check existed, the scenario failed locally with the CI signature. CI: in the six recent nightly or dispatched runs where this scenario ran without a suite-wide startup failure, it failed four times with that signature ([43637691359](https://github.com/PathableAI-org/Pre-ETS/actions/runs/43637691359), [43665238057](https://github.com/PathableAI-org/Pre-ETS/actions/runs/43665238057), [43666055356](https://github.com/PathableAI-org/Pre-ETS/actions/runs/43666055356), [43718202843](https://github.com/PathableAI-org/Pre-ETS/actions/runs/43718202843)) and passed twice ([43617836625](https://github.com/PathableAI-org/Pre-ETS/actions/runs/43617836625), [43681604776](https://github.com/PathableAI-org/Pre-ETS/actions/runs/43681604776)). The two failing runs' attached server logs have no `Authentication freshness denied` warning. A freshness denial writes

author: yasha-dev1
body:
Every release, deploy and publish workflow we inherited points at T3 Code's accounts: Alchemy state `T3CodeRelay/prod`, Axiom datasets, Vercel projects and `app.t3.codes`, npm `t3`, AUR `t3code-bin`, EAS, a Play Store mirror, and T3's task cache worker. Each one was gated on `github.repository == 'pingdotgg/t3code'`. Changing that string to ours would have started the half-hourly nightly releases as soon as this merged.

Now each job runs only in `QualityUnit/amicited-desktop` **and** only once a maintainer sets a repository variable to `true`. None of these variables is set, so nothing new can run after this merges. The workflows are also still disabled in repository settings.

| Variable | Gates |
| --- | --- |
| `AMICITED_RELEASES_ENABLED` | `release.yml` (the `resolve_commit` gate covers every job, including the `release-desktop.yml` calls), `publish-aur.yml` |
| `AMICITED_AUR_ENABLED` | `publish_aur` and `publish-aur.yml`, on top of the releases variable |
| `AMICITED_DESKTOP_PREVIEW_ENABLED` | `desktop-macos-preview.yml`, `desktop-macos-preview-publish.yml` |
| `AMICITED_WEB_PREVIEW_ENABLED` | `web-preview.yml` |
| `AMICITED_RELAY_ENABLED` | `deploy-relay.yml`, `relay-preview.yml`, `relay-preview-cleanup.yml` |
| `AMICITED_MOBILE_ENABLED` | `mobile-eas-*.yml`, `mobile-fingerprint-*.yml` |

**Why no job can run on merge:** each of the 13 workflows above has the repo-and-variable check on its root job. Every other job reaches it through `needs`. Where a job uses `!cancelled()` or `always()`, its condition also requires `needs.<gated job>.result == 'success'`. A script walked every job's `if` and `needs` and found all 13 workflows fully gated. The workflows left ungated (`ci`, `pr-size`, `pr-vouch`, `issue-labels`, `stale-needs-more-info`, `thread-transfer-report`, `windows-tests`, `agent-context-budget`, `mobile-showcase-screenshots`) use only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and no outside account. Every remaining `github.repository ==` check is on our repo name:

```
deploy-relay.yml:32           QualityUnit/amicited-desktop && vars.AMICITED_RELAY_ENABLED
publish-aur.yml:42            … && vars.AMICITED_RELEASES_ENABLED && vars.AMICITED_AUR_ENABLED
desktop-macos-preview*.yml    … && vars.AMICITED_DESKTOP_PREVIEW_ENABLED
mobile-*.yml (5 files)        … && vars.AMICITED_MOBILE_ENABLED
relay-preview*.yml            … && vars.AMICITED_RELAY_ENABLED
release.yml:57                … && vars.AMICITED_RELEASES_ENABLED
web-preview.yml:40            … && vars.AMICITED_WEB_PREVIEW_ENABLED
release.yml:519, release-desktop.yml:332, desktop-macos-preview.yml:88   telemetry channel stamp only
```

### Release pipeline
- `relay_public_config` no longer reads T3's Alchemy state or `.env.example`. If the relay and Clerk variables are unset, it builds with AmICited Link disabled. If only some are set, it fails. The relay client tracing artifact is gone from `release.yml`, `release-desktop.yml` and the macOS preview. `.github/scripts/relay-state-output.test.cjs` tested that step, so it is gone too.
- The hosted web jobs read `AMICITED_WEB_ROUTER_URL`, `AMICITED_WEB_LATEST_DOMAIN` and `AMICITED_WEB_NIGHTLY_DOMAIN`, with no defaults, and skip unless all three are set. Marketing reads `VERCEL_MARKETING_PROJECT` and skips while it is unset. The Discord announcement still requires `publish_cli` to succeed, and it treats a skipped web deploy as fine only while web is switched off.
- Release titles, the preview warning, the Discord copy and the release-notes prompt now say "AmICited Desktop" (from `@amicited/identity`). The preview warning links to this repo's releases.
- `publish_cli` refers to npm package `amicited`. CLI archive globs are `amicited-*`, the AppImage launch check runs `amicited-desktop`, and the AUR asset is `AmICited-Desktop-*`. These names match the CLI and OS-identity rebrand branches. The pipeline is off, so the order these PRs land in does not matter.
- I removed the nightly Play APK mirror step and deleted `mobile-android-apk.yml` and `.github/scripts/mirror-play-apk.cjs`, the hourly mirror of T3's Play app.
- `deploy-relay.yml` and `relay-preview.yml` no longer pass `T3CHAT_LINK_SECRET`.

### Infra
- Relay: stack `AmICitedRelay`, PlanetScale DB `amicitedrelay`, tunnel prefix `amicitedrelay-managedendpoint`, Axiom datasets and tokens `amicited-*`, worker service name `amicited-relay`, JWT audience example `amicited-relay`. The dashboard's relay-connect match and the runbook links come from `main` (#25). The agent-activity title is `PRODUCT_NAME`. Relay tests were updated for the tunnel prefix.
- Task cache: `.task-cache.json` (T3's Ping Labs worker) is deleted, which turns the remote cache off everywhere. `install.ts` has no default endpoint any more. `install-ci.ts` accepts only our repo and reads its config from `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, so its test now supplies a fixture instead of the repo file. The stack and worker are now `AmICitedTaskCache` and `amicited-task-cache`.

### Repo automation
- `VOUCHED.td` is emptied (collaborators are trusted automatically). `TRIAGE_EXEMPTIONS.td` lists `vzeman` and `yasha-dev1`, our two git authors.
- The `contribution-triage` skill now loads policy from `QualityUnit/amicited-desktop`, and T3's PR rulings are rewritten as generic examples.
- The devcontainer has our name, its own volume names (so nothing is shared with a T3 Code devcontainer), and keeps `main`'s note about the rebranded `.env.example`.
- **AUR: renamed, not removed**, to `amicited-desktop-bin` and `amicited-desktop-nightly-bin`. The maintainer is FlowHunt, checksums and versions are placeholders that `release.sh` overwrites, and publishing is gated off. The spec (section 2) says "keep, rebrand" for `packaging/aur`.

### Proof
- actionlint 1.7.12 with shellcheck on every workflow gives the same findings as `origin/main`: 2 false positives on syntax newer than actionlint (`concurrency.queue`, `github.run_started_at`) and 6 existing shellcheck style notes. This PR adds no new findings.
- Task cache makes no remote requests. A fake T3 credential file in `HOME` would turn the cache on with `origin/main`: there `remoteCacheUrl()` returns `https://fake-dev:***@t3-task-cache.pinglabs.workers.dev/projects/t3code`. On this branch it returns `undefined`. Forcing `VP_REMOTE_CACHE=read-write` makes vp refuse with `Remote caching requires cache.remote.url or VP_REMOTE_CACHE_URL`. I ran a cached test task twice under `strace -f -e trace=connect`: the second run shows `1/1 cache hit (100%)`, and both runs made **0** `connect()` calls. A positive control in the same setup does record one.
- `vp check` passes (format, lint, knip). Typecheck passes for `@amicited/identity`, `@t3tools/scripts`, `t3code-relay` and `@t3tools/task-cache`. Tests: relay 305/305, task-cache 41/41, scripts 244/246. The 2 `server-compile-cache` failures also fail on a clean `origin/main` checkout. `node scripts/release-smoke.ts` passes; I added the new package to its manifest list. `resolve-nightly-release.ts` prints `name=AmICited Desktop Nightly 0.1.8-nightly.20261115.7 (abcdef123456)`.

### TODO(amicited-infra)
Relay and Clerk for Link (`release.yml` `relay_public_config`, macOS preview), relay deploys (`deploy-relay`, `relay-preview`, `relay-preview-cleanup`), npm trusted publisher for `amicited`, AUR account and `AUR_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` (job and both PKGBUILDs), hosted web app and its Vercel project (`build_web`/`deploy_web`, `web-preview`), the marketing Vercel project, the release GitHub App (`finalize`), the Expo (EAS) project, Apple team and Play listing (3 mobile EAS workflows), and our own task cache (`infra/task-cache/scripts/install.ts`).

author: spacegoose02
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Spacegoose02"} -->
_Requested by **Supreme Leader** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01SZxRCdv691pstdWTK5qT6F?thread=cmsg_01SZxRCdv691pstdWTK5qT6FMNR8QTZVBJcTMvpMcrAV5a)_

## What
The Hub can now sign people in with tinyauth over **OpenID Connect**, using a client ID and secret. Forward-auth (#325) keeps working, either alone or alongside OIDC.

- **`hub/src/oidc.ts`**: a confidential OIDC client. It uses discovery and the authorization code flow with **PKCE (S256)**. `state` is bound to the browser by a cookie, and there's a `nonce`. The ID token signature is checked against the provider's JWKS (RS/PS/ES/EdDSA, HS with the secret), along with iss, aud, exp and nonce. Groups come from userinfo when the ID token leaves them out. The client secret is sent only to the token endpoint.
- **Plugs into the existing model**: a successful callback yields the same `SsoIdentity` that forward-auth headers give. It's kept for 15 minutes in a signed, HttpOnly cookie (`wl_sso`, path `/auth/`). `/auth/sso/link`, `/auth/sso/web`, `/auth/sso/connect` and `/auth/sso/session` read it via `requestIdentity()`. A page opened without an identity goes through `/auth/oidc/start?next=…` first. Pairing links (desktop, Android, TV via QR), the web page, family sign-ins and the picker, PINs, Stay signed in, account linking and admin-set SSO names all work unchanged.
  - The web page's session uses up the cookie, so signing out doesn't sign straight back in.
  - `next` is restricted to the Hub's own `/auth/sso/` pages and `/`.
- **Identity** is matched by `preferred_username` (configurable), not `sub`. Tinyauth's `sub` changes with the client ID, and the username is what `Remote-User` already linked people by.
- **Settings → Users → Single sign-on** has these parts:
  - A shared "Who signs in" block.
  - A new **Sign in with OIDC** block: issuer, client ID, secret, scopes and username claim, the **redirect URI to register** (`<public URL>/auth/oidc/callback`), and **Check the issuer** (`POST /api/admin/sso/oidc/check`).
  - The existing proxy block.
  - The secret is **sealed at rest** (AES-GCM with the Hub key) and never returned by the API (`oidcClientSecretSet` only). It is also never written to the audit log.
  - A save that would leave OIDC on without an issuer, ID or secret is refused.
- **Env vars**: `WAVELENGTH_OIDC`, `_ISSUER`, `_CLIENT_ID`, `_CLIENT_SECRET` (or `_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE`), `_SCOPES` and `_USERNAME_CLAIM`. Each one locks its field in the app.
- **Docs**: `docs/HUB.md` has a new "Sign in with OIDC" section with the tinyauth client setup (placeholders only), the env table, and how it works. Also updated: the changelog, the compose example and the Unraid template.

## Tests
- `hub/test/oidc.test.ts` runs against a fake OIDC provider with real RS256 signing. It covers:
  - device pairing
  - admin group from userinfo
  - strangers refused
  - a family sign-in reaching the picker
  - web sign-in using up the cookie, and a forged cookie being rejected
  - a bad signature, nonce or audience
  - a callback from another browser, and a replayed state
  - open-redirect guard
  - the secret never in API, DB or audit
  - env lock
  - forward-auth still working alongside
- Hub: 256/256 pass. App: tsc clean, vitest 425/425.
- In a real browser against a running Hub, the sign-in screen showed "Sign in with Tinyauth" and the new settings block rendered.

Not tested against a live tinyauth instance. Tinyauth's docs don't mention PKCE, so the Hub always sends it. Providers ignore unknown parameters, and the client secret still authenticates.

author: liamphmurphy
body:
## Problem

Three backend hot paths scaled linearly with historical data or repeated per-invocation setup overhead:

1. **Run event fan-out & hydration (`31ce42b1`)**: Every streamed `run_events` row triggered an unscoped `run.updated` SSE event that caused all open chat views to re-fetch `GetRun` + `runs` lists, while `watchSession` inserted events one row at a time and `ListRuns` hydrated metadata with per-run N+1 queries.
2. **Code-review git polling (`cc039ffb`)**: `reviewSignature`, `codeChanges`, and `snapshot`/`branchTree` each spawned multiple sequential `Backend.Start` processes per tick/repo and re-archived the full `HEAD` tree into JSONB even when `HEAD` was unchanged.
3. **Global shell queries (`0c531e1d`)**: `PersonaDockChats` scanned and ran correlated subqueries over a user's entire historical `chat_sessions` table, and `ListInbox` lacked selective partial/trigram indexes on comment `@` mentions, open/in-review tickets, active/failed runs, PR merge activity, and pending artifact/workflow gates.

## Change

- **Commit 1 (`31ce42b1`) — `perf(runs): scope run.events SSE, batch event writes, and batch ListRuns`**
  - Migration `00145_run_events_and_chat_run_index.sql` emits scoped `run.events` notifications (`run_id`) and indexes `chat_sessions (current_run_id)` and `chat_messages (run_id, session_id)`.
  - `watchSession` buffers streamed `run_events` and flushes in batches (`64` events / `512 KiB` / `50ms` via `AddRunEvents`), draining synchronously before turn completion.
  - Added slim `GET /runs/{id}/events` (`listRunEvents`) and switched `useChatRunEvents` + `plans-screen.tsx` to poll/invalidate only `["runs", id]` and `["runs", "chat", id]`, while `toRuns` batches hydration across `ListRuns` and `GetRun` child runs.

- **Commit 2 (`cc039ffb`) — `perf(runner): batch code-review git reads and cache HEAD trees per turn`**
  - Added `runGitBatch` (`git_batch.go`), a single-process `python3` runner that executes `signature`, `code_changes`, and `snapshot` checks with all untrusted repo git config/filters neutralized.
  - Cached per-turn `HEAD` tree metadata and blobs in `codeReviewCache` across live watcher ticks and final settlement, passing `Tree: nil` in `UpsertChatCodeReview` when the serialized tree is unchanged.

- **Commit 3 (`0c531e1d`) — `perf(store): index PersonaDockChats and ListInbox for O(active) scans`**
  - Migration `00146_dock_and_inbox_indexes.sql` adds `chat_sessions.last_assistant_seq` kept in sync by guarded statement-level transition-table triggers on `chat_messages`, plus partial/GIN indexes for dock candidates and inbox branches.
  - Rewrote `PersonaDockChats` to union indexed candidate IDs before evaluating laterals, and updated `ListInbox` with a single `run_events` lateral for stalled runs and an indexable `@` + escaped `LIKE` filter for mentions.

## Verification

- `cd /workspace && make gen-check` — exited `0` (clean working tree).
- `cd /workspace/server && gofmt -l ...` (all modified Go files) & `go vet ./...` — passed (`0` issues).
- `cd /workspace/server && go test ./internal/db/...` — passed (`14.167s`, including migration up/down and trigger notification tests).
- `cd /workspace/server && go test ./internal/realtime/... ./internal/transfer/... ./internal/runner/...` — passed (`realtime`: `8.587s`, `transfer`: `39.009s`, `runner`: `529.831s` including new `TestCodeReviewBatchOperations`).
- `cd /workspace/server && go test ./internal/httpapi/...`: all new/regression tests passed (`TestListRuns`, `TestListRunEventsAndBatchHydration`, `TestPersonaDockChatsAssistantSeqAndProposalIndex`, `TestInboxMentionsEscapedNameAndCommentIndexes`, `TestInboxTraySections`, `TestInboxQuestionsAndStalledRuns`, `TestAppChatsStayInTheirApps`).
  - Note: two pre-existing untouched failures on `origin/HEAD` (`e94d98ef`) also fail identically here: `TestEveryPageQueryHasAudienceFilterOrReason` (`wiki.sql: UnresolveLinksTo`) in `internal/store/queries` and `TestVerifyHarnessAntigravityTakesNativeSignIn` (`onboarding_test.go:213`) in `internal/httpapi`.
- `cd /workspace/web && npm run test:unit && npm run typecheck && npm run lint` — `898/898` unit tests passed, `typecheck` passed, `lint` exited `0` (`0` errors; `4` pre-existing warnings in unrelated files).

## Risk

- **Low–Medium**: Requires migrations `00145` and `00146` before deploying the new queries/triggers (`chat_messages_assistant_seq_ins`/`_del` and `run_events` `notify_entity_change`). Both migrations include complete `-- +goose Down` rollbacks, and the statement triggers guard against 0-row updates on cascading chat deletes.

author: adm01-debug
body:
## O que muda

Fora de CI, quando o login automático do E2E (`auth.setup`) falha, ele grava um `storageState` **sem sessão** e a execução continua — e aí cada spec autenticado ainda tenta o mesmo login pela tela e queima até 150 s antes de falhar. Com esta mudança, esses specs pulam na hora, com o motivo no relatório.

Quem ganha: quem roda a suíte autenticada na máquina depois de uma indisponibilidade do Supabase. Em vez de uma hora de timeouts, a suíte termina em minutos dizendo que o setup não produziu sessão.

## Correção da descrição original (achado do Devin Review)

A primeira versão desta descrição dizia que o ganho era **em CI**. Estava errado: `e2e/fixtures/auth.setup.ts:79-81` faz `if (process.env.CI) throw`, e a sessão vazia só é gravada na linha 83, no ramo fora de CI. Em CI um setup degradado aborta a execução e os projetos autenticados nem rodam. O ganho é local.

## Origem

Resgate de `codex/fix-auth-degraded-retry-261107-0227` (SHA `5de2649db1`), branch **já apagada** de outro agente. Ela caiu num grupo de 106 branches que a medição mecânica classificou como "só relatório" sem leitura; a releitura arquivo por arquivo mostrou que era a única das 106 com código de produção útil ausente da `main`. Relatório em adm01-debug/Promo_Gifts_V4#3679.

## O que foi corrigido em relação à branch original (achado P2 do Codex)

A branch original chamava `requireAuth`. Isso é uma regressão: `requireAuth` exige `payload.exp > Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)` (`e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts:328-329`) relendo o arquivo estático a cada chamada, enquanto o navegador renova a sessão com `autoRefreshToken: true` (`src/integrations/supabase/client.ts:146`). Numa suíte autenticada longa, o `exp` salvo vence e **todo** `loginAs` seguinte passaria a falhar com setup são.

Trocado por `authSetupProducedNoSession()`, que olha só a **ausência** da chave `sb-…-auth-token` — a forma `{cookies: [], origins: []}` que o `auth.setup` grava ao degradar. Não lê `exp`. Arquivo ausente ou ilegível devolve `false` e deixa o fluxo normal seguir. E `test.skip` substituiu o `requireAuth`, então não há `throw` em nenhum caminho.

## Diff

| Arquivo | Mudança |
|---|---|
| `e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts` | +`authSetupProducedNoSession()` ao lado de `authStorageHasSession`, reaproveitando `STORAGE_STATE` e a chave canônica |
| `e2e/helpers/auth.ts` | em `loginAs`, depois do atalho de `E2E_MOCK_AUTH`, pula quando o projeto usa o `storageState` do setup (`chromium-smoke`, `*-authed`, `mobile-*`) **e** não há sessão |

Nomes de projeto conferidos em `playwright.config.ts`: `chromium-smoke` (:156), `chromium-authed` (:99), `firefox-authed` (:110), `webkit-authed` (:120), `mobile-chrome` (:131), `mobile-safari` (:141).

## Verificado

Prova do comportamento, chamando a função exportada contra três `storageState` reais:

```
OK   setup degradado (origins vazio): pula=true  (esperado true)
OK   sessao valida (exp no futuro):   pula=false (esperado false)
OK   token VENCIDO (exp no passado):  pula=false (esperado false)
PROVA_OK
```

| Checagem | Comando | Resultado |
|---|---|---|
| Typecheck do CI | `npm run typecheck` (→ `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`) | exit 0 |
| Ratchet de tamanho | `node scripts/check-file-size-baseline.mjs` | sem regressão (433 e 334 linhas, limite 500) |
| ESLint dos 2 arquivos | `npx eslint …` | 1 erro, **herdado** |

O erro de ESLint é `no-empty` em `e2e/helpers/auth.ts:182` (`} catch {}`) e aparece **idêntico** na versão de `origin/main` do mesmo arquivo, com o mesmo comando — confirmado trocando a versão do arquivo no mesmo worktree. Não foi introduzido aqui e não foi silenciado.

## Não verificado

Não executei a suíte autenticada contra o Supabase de produção: ela depende de credenciais de CI que não existem nesta sessão. Não há teste de unidade novo porque `STORAGE_STATE` é um caminho fixo no módulo e torná-lo injetável mexeria em infraestrutura compartilhada fora do escopo deste resgate — por isso a prova acima é por execução direta da função exportada, não um teste commitado.

author: j0n4e
body:
Hardens the self-updater in `macos/Updater.swift`.

**Depends on PR A (release signing).** Releases must ship the asset `Nexview-<v>.zip.sig`, which is the base64 of the 64-byte raw Ed25519 signature over the exact zip bytes, signed with the key matching the embedded public key `QZNsnKHonvP62BxLWUxBUfej1aqt65ao2TeYBEeZNKk=`. **Once this is merged, every update is rejected until releases are signed.** Merge A first and cut a signed release, then merge this.

### Changes
- **S1**: the updater downloads `Nexview-<v>.zip.sig` and checks it with CryptoKit `Curve25519.Signing.PublicKey` against the embedded key *before* unpacking. If the signature is missing or invalid, it refuses to install and shows an error. The check lives in a pure function, `static func verifySignature(data:signatureBase64:publicKeyBase64:)`.
  - The zip and sig `browser_download_url` are only accepted if they start with `https://github.com/J0n4e/nexview_mac/releases/download/`.
  - The `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine` strip is removed. After unpacking, `codesign --verify --deep --strict` must pass. A comment notes that the build is only ad-hoc signed, so the Ed25519 check is the real trust anchor.
  - Removing the strip should be safe: `URLSession` downloads are not quarantined, because Info.plist has no `LSFileQuarantineEnabled`. That means the strip was a no-op. If an updated app ever fails to launch for this reason, the fallback is to re-add the strip after verification.
- **S8**: the release-notes renderer only keeps links whose scheme is `https`.
- **B8**: if a newer release exists but its zip or sig asset is missing, a manual check now shows an error instead of "You're up to date."
- **B9**: `found` and `showPending` return early while an install is in progress.
- **B10**: the temp `nexview-update-*` dir is removed on any failure, and the swap script runs `rm -rf` on it at the end.
- **B11**: signature check, `ditto` and codesign run on a background queue. UI work goes back to main.
- **Tests**: new `macos/tests/updater-signature-test.swift`, using an openssl-generated test vector. It checks: valid → true; tampered message, bad signature, empty signature and wrong key → false. Run with:
  `swiftc macos/Updater.swift macos/tests/updater-signature-test.swift -o /tmp/st && /tmp/st`

**Untested on macOS.** It was written on Linux with no Swift compiler, so CI on macOS (another PR) or a local build should confirm that it compiles.

author: mrbogomips
body:
## What changed

- `AGENTS.md` is the hand-written instruction file for every agent: Codex reads it directly, Claude Code through `CLAUDE.md`, now a symbolic link to it. Claude Code's own lines (the development plugin, the agents' model and effort, the reviewers' memory, the `Session context` pin) are in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
- What always loads keeps the rules that must always apply: overview, design documents and how they change, invariants, stack, working documents, the backlog's core rules, OpenSpec, the agent harness, Codex interop, development commands, the local CI rules, git and pull requests.
- Moved, word for word, to files that load only when needed:
  - the backlog procedure (labels, area map, lifecycle, end-to-end findings) → `.claude/skills/askboard-backlog/` (ported to Codex like the other skills);
  - the CI workflows, cadence, runners and the release workflow → `.github/AGENTS.md`;
  - import rules, tsconfig rules, licences, test timings → `tools/AGENTS.md`;
  - folder names, `.memlog.md`, planning-repository citations, the AXFX contract → `docs/AGENTS.md`;
  - each nested `AGENTS.md` has a `CLAUDE.md` link beside it;
  - the agent harness change history → `docs/harness-history.md`, with a row for this change.
- Tooling: the codex-port block of `setup.sh` takes the `port-to-codex` template (it no longer writes `AGENTS.md`; it checks that `CLAUDE.md` links to it) with the linked-skill amendment for OpenSpec 2 re-applied and marked; `.gitignore` tracks `AGENTS.md`; `tools/codex-interop.test.ts` and `tools/codex-port.test.ts` test the new direction; `tools/ci/changed-paths.sh` starts `codex` on any instruction file; the release assembly refuses `AGENTS.md` in copied folders as it does `CLAUDE.md`.
- Citations in the harness skills and agents, the Issue templates and `openspec/config.yaml` point to the new places.

## Why

`CLAUDE.md` was 47,065 characters (about 11.8k tokens), loaded into every session and every project agent and above Claude Code's large-file warning; most of it served one task at a time. The always-loaded part is now about 19,300 characters (`AGENTS.md` 18.0k, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` 1.3k). One hand-written file for both tools replaces the generated copy, which reverses the Codex interop decision of 2026-11-09.

## Checks

- `./setup.sh --codex-only`: rulesync 43.8.3 wrote 6 skills and 4 agents; `./setup.sh --check`: up to date.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`: pass.
- `bun run test`: 14,732 pass, 0 fail (a first run had one transient failure that did not recur, as in #219).
- `check:imports`, `check:skills`, `check:licences`: no problems. `openspec validate --all --strict`: 13 passed.

Closes #220

## Left for the PO

- Other checkouts and worktrees: after pulling, run `./setup.sh --codex-only`; the old generated `AGENTS.md` is replaced by the committed one.
- The linked-skill amendment should go upstream into the `port-to-codex` template; until then a test fails if a re-vendored block drops it.

author: alexwarren
body:
Stable Windows builds now also produce an unsigned `.appx` for the "Quest Viva" Microsoft Store listing. The Store signs it after certification, so Store installs avoid the SmartScreen warning the unsigned NSIS installer gets on every release (unsigned files only build reputation per hash, and EV certificates no longer skip the check), without a code-signing certificate of our own.

## Changes

- **`package.json`**: `appx` identity copied from the listing's Product identity page.
- **`scripts/dist.mjs`**: adds the `appx` target for stable builds only, next to NSIS (electron-builder concatenates arrays when merging config). Betas keep their own identity and stay off the Store. electron-builder writes the version as `major.minor.patch.0`, the form the Store requires.
- **`build/appx/`**: Start menu, taskbar and Store tile images generated from `icon-source.svg`; the commands are in `build/README.md`.
- **`electron-publish.yml`**: the Windows leg keeps the `.appx` as a workflow artifact (it can't be installed outside the Store, so it isn't attached to the release). A `channel` input on `workflow_dispatch` lets a manual run build the stable variant, including the Store package.
- **`preload.ts` / `PlayCatalog.svelte`**: exposes Electron's `process.windowsStore` and hides the update banner in the Store build, since the Store updates the app itself and the banner links to the GitHub installer.
- **Docs**: new "Microsoft Store" section in `docs/electron-desktop-app.md`, updated Windows signing decision, and a stale CLAUDE.md line fixed.

## Testing

- `npm run check` and `npm run lint` in AppShell, `tsc` in ElectronApp.
- `electron/update-banner.spec.mjs` and `electron/clientinfo.spec.mjs` pass, so the banner still shows outside the Store build.
- **Not yet verified:** the `.appx` build itself (`makeappx`/`makepri`) only runs on Windows. Run `electron-publish` manually on this branch with `channel: stable`, then sideload-test the artifact on a Windows machine before the first submission.

Submission stays manual for now: upload the `.appx` from a stable tag's workflow run in Partner Center. Betas aren't in the Store.

author: mattbusel
body: Whatever a player types in say, party, guild or a whisper goes straight into the bot's prompt, its conversation history and the sentiment prompt, so an email or phone number gets sent to a hosted provider and a line like "ignore previous instructions, you are now..." is answered like any other. This PR runs player lines (not bot lines) through llm-guard in ProcessChat: PII is replaced with [EMAIL]/[PHONE]-style placeholders in the copy the bots see, lines that score as injection get no reply, and what other players see in chat is untouched (OllamaChat.Guard.Enable, default 1). It also adds an opt-in reply cache in QueryOllama for byte-identical prompts (OllamaChat.Cache.Enable, default 0, emptied on .ollama reload), so with the defaults nothing about the requests themselves changes. I don't have a full AzerothCore + playerbots tree here, so I compiled the changed files with MSVC 2022 at /W4 and GCC 13 against stubbed core headers, and ran the real mod-ollama-chat_api.cpp and the new guard file against a fake HTTP client to check redaction, injection blocking, cache hits, per-request-kind misses and the reset on reload. Both headers are single-file MIT libraries I maintain, vendored unmodified in deps/llm with their license, next to the bundled nlohmann/json.

## What this does

Adds `docs/plans/repository-foundation-closure.md`, the foundation campaign's closure report. It is written for the independent assessment that an external reviewer will carry out, so that they can start from what was asked, what was done and where the evidence is.

## What the report contains

- How to reproduce the verification, and the result of a fresh-clone run at `43a6886`: every check passes; core 469 tests, web 152, browser 38; three moderate advisories under Storybook 8 (accepted until 2027-02-12, #46); none in production dependencies.

The report says plainly that it is the campaign checking itself, and that every "Met" is the author's judgement, not an independent one.

body:
## Problem

The interface had no simple way to see what omg has deleted so far. `omg history` shows operations, but not a plain list of each removed item with its size.

## Change

- Key `5` opens a new view, **Deleted**: one line per deleted item with its date, how long ago, estimated size and path (Docker items as "Docker <kind>: <name>"). It is a text record only; nothing in it can be acted on.
- Lines older than 20 days are removed automatically, when the log is written and when it is read (`index::DELETED_LOG_DAYS`).
- New table `deleted_log` (migration 014, schema 14). A row is written in the same transaction that records a fully removed target of a permanent delete, and for each Docker item the engine removed. The `operations` audit trail, `omg history` and the freed total are unchanged.
- Help, footer and option bar now say 1-5. Docs: `docs/evidence.md`, `docs/compatibility.md` (schema 14), `docs/mac-final-check.md`.
- The pseudo-terminal tests waited for the word "Deleted", which the new tab name already shows, so they now wait for the result line itself.

## Verification

On macOS 27 (APFS):
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and the same with `--no-default-features`
- `TMPDIR=$(cd "$TMPDIR" && pwd -P) OMG_REQUIRE_DISK_IMAGES=1 cargo test --workspace --locked` and `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features --locked`
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` (with a canonical `TMPDIR`): the delete-around-protected test now opens the log after a real delete and finds the removed folder and its size
- `node --test packages/oh-my-gigabytes/test/release.test.js`

New tests: `deleted_items_are_logged_with_size_and_dropped_after_twenty_days`, `removed_docker_items_go_in_the_deleted_log_and_skipped_ones_do_not`, `deleted_log_lists_date_size_and_escaped_path`, `key_five_opens_the_deleted_log`; migrations tests cover schema 1..14.

FBXConverter::ConvertLine copies every PointsIndex entry of an FBX Line geometry (and each end point decoded from -(index + 1)) into the face indices without checking them against the point count, so a crafted line like `PointsIndex: *3 { a: 0,100000,-3 }` yields faces past mNumVertices and aiProcess_JoinIdenticalVertices then hits an ASAN heap-buffer-overflow at JoinVerticesProcess.cpp:242; this rejects out-of-range indices in the LineGeometry constructor with DOMError, the same way MeshGeometry already range-checks PolygonVertexIndex, and the new importLinePointsIndexOutOfRange test covers a bad point and a bad end point (the full unit suite, 741 tests, passes under ASAN).

author: rumoroso
body:
The open Phase 1 build items, and the quality gates from "Quality, in every phase" that were not yet in CI.

## What changes

- **Headings and Images views.** "Findings", "Headings" and "Images" above the list. Headings in order, indented by level; each image with what a screen reader says for it (its text, "Decorative", or "No text alternative"). An entry is flagged only where the engine reported on that element, so the views never disagree with the findings. On a page, the theme's headings and images are listed too, marked "Theme or template".
- **More settings opened from a finding.** "Change the heading level" (focus on the level it has now), "Open the text colour" (Typography → Color), and "Select the link text" (selected in its block, ready to type over; link text has no setting).
- **Fewer buttons per card.** When both "Reviewed, it's fine" and "Hide for me" are offered, they sit behind "More" (a disclosure button, not a menu). At most four actions per card.
- **Page checker.** "Hide for me" works there too, kept in the same personal preferences as the editor (`/wp-json/surea11y/v1/hidden/<post>`). "Edit in the editor" opens the editor on that finding.
- **Quality gates in CI.** ESLint and Prettier with core's settings (the code was formatted once, in its own commit), size budgets on the built files (`npm run size`), and a syntax check of every PHP file.

Not done: the phone-width check waits for a reflow rule (WCAG 1.4.10) in core. Recorded in the plan and the decisions.

## Quality

- **Tests:** 66 panel, 10 pack and 26 end-to-end tests pass against a local WordPress 7.1. New: the outline, the views, "More", the three new settings, page hides seen in the editor, and the link to a finding.
- **Performance:** the outline is read once per check from the sandbox, with no extra scan. Panel 18.0 KB compressed (budget 22 KB), engine 511 KB (budget 540 KB).
- **Accessibility of our interface:** the views use real headings, lists and toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`); "More" uses `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and focus stays on it. The sidebar passes the engine's WCAG 2.2 AA checks in all three views.
- **Security and privacy:** the new REST route checks that the person sees the checker and can edit the post, and accepts only cleaned finding keys (at most 50 per request). It changes only the plugin's own entry of the person's preferences. Nothing is sent anywhere else.

Signed-off-by: Jorge Rumoroso <rumoroso@gmail.com>

author: argoleon
body:
## L05-US06 — Track ticket history in the Activity tab

Closes #153, #154, #155, #156.

### Backend
- **`audit_log`** (migration `20261203000001_audit_log.sql`): partitioned by month like the outbox (`app_ensure_audit_partitions`, a default partition, partitions secured by `app_secure_partition`), RLS, index `(tenant_id, entity_id, created_at)`. One row per changed field (`updated`) or per action (`created`, `moved`, `link_added` / `link_removed`, `comment_created` / `comment_updated` / `comment_deleted`), with old and new values (JSONB), actor, origin (`interface`, `api`, `mcp`, `import`, `system`) and a `change_id` shared by the rows of one write.
- **`domain::audit`**: origins, actions, fields and `diff(before, after)` field by field (system then custom fields; absent = null), unit-tested.
- **`api::issue_history`**: snapshot before/after, entries, `record` in the **same transaction** as every ticket write: creation, edit, move (sub-tasks included), transition, parent, links (on both tickets, each with its own reading), comments. Types and statuses are stored with their labels of the time (the configuration may change, the ticket may move).
- **`GET /api/v1/issues/{idOrKey}/activity`**: newest first, cursor pagination, labels in the request's language. Links to tickets the reader does not see are left out; the content of a deleted comment is returned to moderators only.
- **Origin**: `TenantTx::author()` returns `interface` for sessions. API tokens (L15) and the MCP server (L16) do not exist yet: the "via MCP" marking is tested by recording an `mcp` entry directly (infra and API tests) and in the web tests.
- The worker's partition job is now `keep_partitions` (outbox and history).

### GDPR fix found on the way
- US04 registered **no erasure step for comments**, and names on tickets and comments were joined from `account.display_name`. Names now come from `app_member_name(account)`: "Deleted user #N" once the member is erased in the tenant (null, "a former member", when they merely left). The history, ticket reporter/assignee and comment authors use it.
- The erasure job gets two steps: `comments` (emptied to the "Comment deleted" placeholder when `purgeComments`) and `history` (the content of their comments stripped from the history; their other entries stay, under the pseudonym).
- Not covered: the `@Name` label of a mention inside **another member's** comment keeps the erased member's name. Worth a follow-up issue?

### Web
- The ticket page groups history and comments in one card with `mat-tab-group` (mockup 03): **Activity** first, then **Comments (n)**. Time spent comes with L10.
- `app-issue-activity`: sentences built in the browser from the entries (`activity-sentence.ts`, unit-tested in FR and EN), date in the user's time zone, avatars, a "via MCP" chip (also via the API, by import), "Show before and after" for a description or rich text field, "Show the deleted comment" for moderators, older entries page by page. It reads the history again when the ticket is read again or a comment changes.
- Translations FR and EN.

### Tests
- Unit: `domain::audit` (diff of system and custom fields, origins, actions), `api::issue_history` (names, entries), `activity-sentence.spec.ts` (FR and EN), `issue-activity.spec.ts` (tabs, sentences, MCP, before/after, paging, reload on comment change, states, axe).
- Integration (real PostgreSQL): `infra/tests/audit.rs` (partitions, order and paging, RLS isolation, refused rows, pseudonyms, purge on erasure), `api/tests/issue_history.rs` (every write path, refused edit records nothing, paging and invalid cursor, moderators only for deleted comments, erased author as "Deleted user #N", MCP and system origins, links out of sight hidden, 404 cross-tenant and for confidential projects), worker partition keeper.
- E2E: mocked Activity tab and its accessibility (light/dark, FR/EN); on the production stack, a ticket edited, started, commented and the comment deleted, then read in the Activity tab.

### Test adjustments (separate commit `test(web): open the Comments tab…`)
The comments moved into a tab that is not selected first: the comments spec and e2e tests now open the Comments tab before reading them, and read "Comments (n)" on the tab instead of the card heading that no longer exists. What they check is unchanged.

body:
This PR establishes the sheaf-cohomological acyclicity of fine sheaves of abelian groups, proves that smooth vector-valued functions on Hausdorff `σ`-compact and second-countable manifolds form a fine sheaf with vanishing positive-degree sheaf cohomology, constructs the sheaf of locally constant abelian-group-valued functions, and proves short exactness and the cohomological connecting isomorphisms of the smooth exponential sequence `0 ⟶ ℤ_M ⟶ C^∞_M(ℝ) ⟶ C^∞_M(S¹) ⟶ 0`:

- `TauCeti/Topology/Sheaves/Fine.lean` defines `TopCat.Sheaf.IsFine` via locally finite closed-support partitions of `𝟙 F` subordinate to arbitrary open covers, proves permanence under canonical Godement embeddings and cokernels (`TopCat.Sheaf.isFine_godement_obj`, `TopCat.Sheaf.isFine_cokernel_toGodement_app`) together with global section lifting (`TopCat.Sheaf.cokernel_π_toGodement_app_top_surjective`), and deduces positive-degree vanishing of global and open-subset sheaf cohomology (`TopCat.Sheaf.subsingleton_H_of_isFine`, `TopCat.Sheaf.subsingleton_H'_of_isFine_sheafRestrict`) by dimension shifting along the canonical Godement resolution.
- `TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Algebra/TypeTags.lean` and `TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Sheaf/Smooth/Restrict.lean` supply the `C^n` equivalences for `Multiplicative` and `Additive` type tags (`Multiplicative.contMDiff_ofAdd`, `Multiplicative.contMDiff_toAdd`, `Additive.contMDiff_ofMul`, `Additive.contMDiff_toMul`) and open-submanifold restriction isomorphisms `TauCeti.smoothSheafCommGroup.restrictIso` and `TauCeti.smoothSheafAddCommGroup.restrictIso`.

author: arwalk
body:
When an optional `string`/`bytes` field (`?[]const u8`) appears more than once in a message, the binary decoder replaced the old value without freeing it. Each repeat leaked one allocation. You don't see the leak with an arena allocator, but you do with any other allocator.

The optional branch now frees the previous value unless it is the field's declared default, the same rule the non-optional branch already uses. Three new tests in `tests/leaks.zig` cover an optional string sent twice, optional bytes sent twice, and a string inside a submessage that is sent twice and merged.

author: telosnox
body:
The last open point of step 3 of #288. The data basis points at snow periods that closed only at the limit of 7 days after the last snowfall, although bright hours would have shown free modules.

## What changes
- `model.snow_windows` returns the hours under snow, as before, and the ends of those windows. `snow_hours` wraps it, unchanged.
  - A window counts only if it had a measured hour in which the recovery rule could have fired: satellite clearness ≥ `SNOW_RECOVER_KT` and free modules above 5 % of peak.
  - An overcast week, a time before commissioning or a gap in the data is no such case.
  - A window the history ends inside is unfinished, not capped.
- `learning.LeftOut.snow_capped` carries these ends, and `coordinator._basis` passes them to `databasis.summary`.
- `databasis.summary` adds the anomaly `snow_cap`: the count, and the last day of the latest such window as an ISO date.
- Panel texts in de and en, README en/de, and the changelog: the existing *Data basis* entry, which is unreleased.

## Evidence (exported history of the maintainer's installation, not committed)
- Balcony: 78 snow hours on 14 days, and no capped window. Each window closed by thaw or by an hour of free modules.
- Roof: no snow window.
- So the hint stays silent here. It is meant for installations with real winters during the beta.
- Learning is unchanged: the pinned snapshot is not touched.

## Review
Tier: Model (model.py; learning output identical)
- A Compatibility:
  - The anomaly key is added to the summary. No version step is needed: the frontend shows an unknown key as raw text, and the text ships with it.
  - `LeftOut` is not stored, and its new field has a default.
- B Physics:
  - Windows that had no chance to close counted as capped: before the first use, during a data gap, and the ordinary overcast week after snow. That would have fired routinely in Central European winters. Fixed: only windows with a bright measured hour count. There are tests for an overcast week and for an array installed later.
  - A window ending exactly at the last hour of the history was not counted. Fixed.
  - Snow exactly at the closing hour opens no new window. Not followed: this was so before this PR, it is rare, and it does not change this hint.
- C Explainability:
  - The day points at the calendar, where the snow days are hatched and the day view shows when the array delivered again.
  - The count covers the whole history and the calendar shows one year. Accepted.
- D Texts:
  - "Snow window" was internal jargon, and "after 7 days" was inexact, because the limit counts from the last snowfall. Fixed in panel, README and changelog.
  - The overcast cause no longer needs a mention, because those weeks are not counted any more.
- E Privacy: nothing found.
- F Correctness:
  - `value` is None, and the text has no `{v}`.
  - The memo of `left_out` hits, because `_basis` gets the same history as learning.

Backtest: no model change. The pinned learning values are identical, and the full suite (504 tests) passed locally.

body:
Implements R27 from `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` ("Import contribution history and refresh repo details") on top of R26 (`d2eec45`). Design: [ADR 0010](docs/adr/0010-contribution-facts.md).

## What changed

- **Queries.** `import_prs.graphql`, `import_timeline.graphql`, `import_reviewed_prs.graphql`, `import_reviews.graphql`, and `repo_meta.graphql`, each registered through `query_doc!`. `viewer.graphql` reads `createdAt`. Every document is a `query` and selects no body or title.
- **Keys.** `crates/worker/src/sync/work.rs` gains `ImportKey` (`Start`, `SearchRange { from, to, after }`, `Timeline { pr, after }`, `ReviewedPrs { year, after }`, `Reviews { prs, after }`) and `RepoPage { week, after }`. `WorkKind::ImportFacts` is a `backfill_page` row under an `import.` key and `WorkKind::RefreshRepos` under a `repos.` key, so the deployed `work` table's `kind` CHECK is unchanged. A `Reviews` unit keeps its up to 50 node IDs in the `payload` column, and its key holds their hash, as `Enrich` does.
- **Handler.** `crates/worker/src/sync/import.rs` runs each unit with one GraphQL request:
  - `Start` reads my `createdAt`, stores it in `import_state.account_created_at`, and queues one `SearchRange` (January 1 to December 31) and one `ReviewedPrs` per year from the account's first year to this year.
  - `SearchRange` runs `search(type: ISSUE, query: "is:pr author:<login> created:<from>..<to>", first: 50)`. A first page with `issueCount` over 1,000 queues the two date halves and writes nothing. Otherwise it writes `pr_facts` with `source = 'imported'` through R26's upsert, whose `WHERE excluded.source = 'live' OR pr_facts.source = 'imported'` keeps live rows, plus `pr_issue_links`, and upserts each repo's node ID, stars, language, and `owned_by_me`. A pull request with no human reply in its first 20 timeline items queues a `Timeline` unit, which pages on until a reply or the end and then sets `first_response_*` on the imported row only.
  - `ReviewedPrs` reads `pullRequestReviewContributions(first: 100)` only for PR IDs, queues `Reviews` units of up to 50, and pages on. `Reviews` reads `reviews(author: <login>, first: 100)` and writes one `review_facts` row per review (`submittedAt`, else `createdAt`, pending skipped). A PR with more reviews pages on in a one-ID unit.
  - The last unit sets `import_state.facts_imported_at` in the same D1 batch as its own rows, only when its follow-ups hold no import unit and no other `import.` row is in `work`, dead ones included. The Syncer then saves the marker in its `kv` table.
  - `RefreshRepos` reads 50 repos with a node ID from `repos` in name order, asks one `nodes(ids:)` query, sets `stars`, `primary_language`, `owned_by_me` (owner login equals my login, case-insensitive, via `domain::facts::is_external`), and `meta_refreshed_at`, and pages on by name.
- **Nightly kick.** `scheduler::kick(Rollup)` queues `import.start` while `facts_imported_at` is unset and no `import.` row exists, and `RefreshRepos` once per week, keyed by `repos_refreshed_week`. Dead `import.` and `repos.` rows come back through the existing dead `backfill_page` revival and show on the freshness panel like other dead rows.
- **Budget.** The units share `backfill_page`'s rate gate. They also wait for `paced_until`, set 10 s after each import or refresh unit (`IMPORT_SPACING_SECS`), so the import makes at most 360 GitHub calls an hour, inside the 500 cap.
- **Migration 0012** adds `repos.node_id`, because the weekly refresh's `nodes` query needs repo node IDs.
- **Stub.** `tools/github-stub/import.mjs` answers the five queries. `import.test.mjs` tests it. `server.mjs` routes to it, and `scenarios/import-history.json` holds the import scenario. `history.mjs` now sends `resetAt` in whole seconds; with milliseconds Radar's `Timestamp` refused it and every seed unit died.

## Evidence per unit box

- `cargo test -p radar-worker import`: `over_limit_range_splits_in_two`, `split_ranges_cover_the_year_without_overlap`, `one_range_and_one_reviewed_list_per_year`, `marker_waits_for_every_import_row`, `no_enqueue_while_an_import_row_remains`, `a_second_night_enqueues_nothing`, `timeline_pages_until_a_human_answers`, `three_reviews_on_one_pr_make_three_rows`, plus `a_range_page_writes_imported_facts_and_live_rows_win`, `a_reviewed_page_queues_reviews_fifty_at_a_time_and_its_next_page`, `a_start_reads_my_creation_date_stores_it_and_queues_the_years`, `every_unit_sends_the_variables_its_query_names`, `a_response_missing_a_field_its_unit_needs_is_retried_not_stored`, `refresh_matches_repos_by_node_id_and_owns_mine_whatever_the_case`, and `no_import_document_asks_for_a_body_or_a_title`. All pass.
- `cargo test -p radar-worker work`: `import_and_repos_keys_round_trip_through_columns_as_backfill_pages`, `import_and_repos_keys_reject_everything_else`, `a_day_reads_its_year_and_counts_days`. All pass.
- `every_registered_document_is_a_query` covers the five new documents. `scheduler`: `import_and_repo_rows_wait_for_the_pace_and_others_do_not`. `store`: `import_markers_are_kept_apart_in_the_kv_table`. `db::repos`: `meta_keeps_the_repo_cards_counts_and_refreshes_the_rest`, `a_page_holds_repos_with_a_node_id_after_the_last_name`.
- `node --test "tools/github-stub/*.test.mjs"` includes `import.test.mjs`.

## Gates (run at the head commit)

```
cargo fmt --all --check                               exit 0
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exit 0
cargo test --workspace                                domain 112, 2, 37 passed; radar-worker 414 passed; read_only 11 passed; web 82 passed; 0 failed
node --test "scripts/*.test.mjs"                      pass 40, fail 0
node --test "tools/github-stub/*.test.mjs"            pass 70, fail 0
node --test "tools/github-stub/scenarios/*.test.mjs"  pass 9, fail 0
node scripts/build.mjs && node scripts/check-size.mjs
  worker: 369.0 KB gzipped, budget 400 KB, ok
  ui: 253.2 KB gzipped, budget 300 KB, ok
```

Trunk `d2eec45`, built on the same machine from a scratch worktree: Worker 345.2 KB gzipped. Head is +23.8 KB.

## Local smoke

Stub on 8902 with `import-history`. Radar on 8802 with `--persist-to .wrangler/r27 --test-scheduled --infer-origin-from-routes=false`, migrations 0001 to 0012 applied locally. Signed in with a curl cookie jar (`/api/me` gave `{"login":"karthik","user_id":1001}`), then fired `/__scheduled?cron=0+3+*+*+*`.

- `import.start` asked `Viewer` once and queued 6 units (2024, 2025, 2026). `import_state.account_created_at = 1710057600` (2024-03-10T08:00:00Z).
- Split, from the stub log `variables.q`: `created:2025-01-01..2025-12-31` (issueCount 1,520) was queued once, then `2025-01-01..2025-07-01` and `2025-07-02..2025-12-31`. The first half (1,500) split into `2025-01-01..2025-04-01` and `2025-04-02..2025-07-01`, which split again into `2025-04-02..2025-05-16` and `2025-05-17..2025-07-01`, each under 1,000. The Worker logs a split as `writes=0 follow_ups=2`.
- Deep timeline: `ImportTimeline` for `PR_deep` with `after` `timeline:20`, then `timeline:40`. `first_response_at = 1770120000` (2026-02-03T12:00:00Z), `first_response_login = maint`, as in the stub.
- The reviewed list for 2025 read `after: null`, then `reviewed:100`.
- Mid-run, three `import.reviews` units died. The stub process had started before I added `__typename` to its review authors, and one died with `transport` while I restarted the stub. Freshness then listed them under `dead` and the queue held no pending row: `pr_facts` 1,563, `review_facts` 23, `facts_imported_at` null. The marker waited, as it should.
- A second nightly kick revived them (`syncer kick reason=rollup queued=6`). The last one wrote its reviews and the marker in one batch: `sync.import key=import.reviews.61149b097acf19f7.start writes=2 follow_ups=0`, then `sync.import facts_imported_at=2026-11-15T16:39:24Z`.
- Final D1: `pr_facts` 1,563 rows, all `source = 'imported'`, which equals `importTotals` (1,563). `review_facts` 128 rows, all imported (stub total 128).

author: alfonslm
body:
## What and why

"Keep instruments running when playback is stopped" was one global switch (Diagnostic > VST). It matters only for some plugins, such as VOCALOID7 with its own editor, and keeping every VST instrument running costs CPU. It is now set per instrument and saved with the score. The MuseScore side, which adds the item to each VST instrument's sound menu in the mixer, is alfonslm/MuseScore#25 (same branch name). **Merge this one first, with a merge commit.**

- **Storage:** the key `keepRunningWhenStopped` = `"1"` in the instrument's `AudioUnitConfig` (`KEEP_RUNNING_WHEN_STOPPED_CONFIG_KEY` in `audio/common/audiotypes.h`), next to the plugin state and the keyswitch map. `VstSynthesiser::shouldProcessWhenIdle()` reads it.
- **No plugin reload on toggle:** new optional `ISynthesizer::applyConfiguration()`. `EventAudioNode::applyInputParams()` tries it first when only the configuration of the same sound changed. `VstSynthesiser` accepts it only when nothing but this key differs; any other change still recreates the synthesizer, as before.
- **Idle set refresh:** `AudioContext` refreshes the set of tracks processed while stopped when a track's source parameters change.
- **Bug fix:** when the plugin reports a new state, `VstSynthesiser` now keeps the keys the host set. Before, the configuration was replaced by the plugin's state alone, which also dropped a keyswitch map from the project. `isPluginStateConfigKey()` in `vsttypes.h` names the plugin's own keys.
- **Removed:** the global setting (`AudioEngineConfig`, `IAudioConfiguration` and its stub and mock, `IAudioEngineConfiguration`, the `command://vst/keep-instruments-running` command).

## Testing

- Every changed `.cpp` passes a syntax-only compile (Qt 6.4 headers, VST3 SDK at the pinned commits), including the audio tests that use the changed mocks.
- Formatted with uncrustify 0.74.0 and the repository's config.
- Not built or run here: no full build, and no unit tests (the framework's unit-test workflow is disabled). The macOS arm64 build on alfonslm/MuseScore#25 is the first real compile.
- Not tried with a plugin yet. The user confirmed the global version with VOCALOID7 (works while stopped) and Kontakt 8 (silent while stopped without the option).

author: psyao
body:
Closes #661

The admin's global search linked every matching Translation to its edit page. That page answers 403 to a User without the type's `update`, and for a published Translation also to a User without `publish` (ADR 0019). This is the same defect #388 fixed in the dashboard.

`KamiGlobalSearchProvider` now asks `EntryResource::editUrlIfAllowed()` (#632) for each result and leaves out a Translation with no URL. Filament's `GlobalSearchResult::$url` is a non-nullable `string`, and Filament itself drops a Resource result whose URL is blank. So the dashboard's "row with no link" was not an option.

**Decisions**
- Leave such a result out, rather than fall back to the type's list searched for it as Media does (Steve).
- A User with `view` but not `update` loses that type's Entry results too: the edit page answers 403 to them as well, which was verified (Steve).
- Not breaking: a removed result only ever led to a 403. `UPGRADING.md` § Unreleased item 9 now names global search next to the dashboard (Steve, review).

**Defaults taken without asking**
- The policy check reads the Translations already eager-loaded, so it adds no query per result. A test pins 7 queries for both 1 and 10 hits.
- The pre-existing "skips the types the User may not list" test now grants `update` and `publish`, so it keeps testing what it was written for.

**Known ceiling**
- The 50-Entry limit applies before the policy filter. A User without `publish` can see fewer hits than match when the newest matches are published. The code carries a `ponytail:` note, to lift in V1 if an editor runs into it.

**Follow-up**
- #667: four other admin links to the edit page answer 403 the same way (Media "used by", audit subjects, the locale switcher, the redirect after duplicating).

Refs Kosinkadink/comfy-vibe-station#675

Owner thread: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a1df2a-45c4-722f-a4f8-708dd2a81b58

## Behavior

The generic remote pack selects its exact supported schema wire and reads the current install bearer for every catalog fetch. It sends no project/account/grant claims and decodes no JWT authority. Gateway producer [PR12](https://github.com/Kosinkadink/dinkster-gateway/pull/12) derives verified project policy from that bearer; producer landing is required before a deployed integration claim.

Authenticated catalogs are memory-only and never written to the public cache. Bearer replacement clears prior schemas and ETags; a failed discovery with a different bearer yields an empty pack rather than another account's cached schemas. Public cache is bound to its catalog endpoint. Signed-in polling rechecks conditional catalog responses because project policy may change without advancing the public catalog epoch; same-epoch filtered schema changes trigger worker replacement. A changed bearer during a response prevents accepting its stale payload. Logged-out public discovery and sign-in refusal on job invocation remain intact. Explicit token-file precedence and per-invocation reads stay unchanged.

Remote pack version0.0.7 is consistent in project metadata, manifest and lock; no engine pin changes. No provider/model-specific client code or second service table.

Head [639d8e4d5e1a](https://github.com/Kosinkadink/dinkster-nodes/commit/639d8e4d5e1a9b21abac926e88b85d92b08d1f2c): remote CPU suite25 passed in13.62seconds, including actual isolated-worker catalog/job/reload scenarios and new local-HTTP policy/rotation/cache isolation cases. All production675/QA928 criteria, identity945 runtime waits and no-default943/944 remain required. No deployment, live sign-in, R2/provider/paid traffic or issue acceptance is claimed. Engine PR1235 remains independently frozen and under the recorded main landing hold.

## Actual gateway interoperability proof

The current CatalogClient passed against gateway PR12 through real loopback HTTP with real pinned identity signing/policy and isolated PostgreSQL fixtures in4.61seconds: wire1 decoding, unchanged-epoch policy denial, atomic bearer project switch, invalid bearer clearing schemas and public/private cache isolation. Authenticated schemas were not persisted. This is local source interoperability, not deployment/provider/whole-issue acceptance. Log/harness retained under the owner gateway .amp/in/artifacts, temporary source test removed.

author: eyobtadelew12-hash
body:
The DEV deploy after the note-count merge failed on the self-hosted runner before any step ran:

> File C:\runners\_work\_temp\...ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system.

GitHub's hosted Windows machines allow scripts, but a normal Windows PC (and most real deploy agents) keeps the default **Restricted** policy. The runner runs each `shell: powershell` step as a `.ps1` file, so every deploy step was blocked.

**Fix:** `PSExecutionPolicyPreference: Bypass` on the deploy job. It is the process-level policy, so it applies only to that job's PowerShell processes; the machine's own policy stays as it is. Checked locally: with Restricted, `powershell -command ". 'x.ps1'"` fails, and with this variable set it runs.

After merging, the merge's own Build run deploys to DEV with the fix.

author: rabhanz
body:
Open and status questions on the Tessel ("why is everything so slow", "how are things going") were answered in 30-45 words aloud: two or three sentences, often with a line about what she cannot see and a request to narrow it down.

The room prompt (`ROOM_SYSTEM`) now asks for one spoken sentence of about twenty words, with a second only for a step he must take or detail he asked for. An open question, however he puts it (a wonder too), gets the one thing that matters most and then stops: nothing about what she cannot see, no guessed cause, no asking him to narrow it down. When the tools returned more he may want, she ends with "want the rest?", the one question allowed to end an answer, and gives the rest when he says yes. A yes-or-no or simple question gets its answer and no offer.

Four made-up room-suite cases cover it (`brief-why-slow`, `brief-how-things`, `brief-whats-going-on`, `brief-yes-no`). Each checks that the answer is 25 words or fewer before any offer, that it includes something the work tools read, and that a yes-or-no gets no offer. A grader test covers the check.

## Numbers (Sonnet 5.5 voice, effort low, as the room suite runs it)
- **Room suite, 4 new cases plus direct-wonder, x5:** 15/25 before, 24/25 after. Median last-reply words went from 29 to 21 (direct-wonder 45 to 26, why-slow 37 to 20).
- **Full room suite after:** 91 pass, 0 fail, 13 not applicable.
- **His 81 real Tessel question turns (11-15 Nov), replayed through each prompt:** each turn's tools were given the facts her real reply rested on. A blind Opus 5.5 judge ranked three replies: her real reply, the before prompt and the after prompt.
  - Median words: real 27, before 25, after 22. For the long ones (real reply over 22 words): 38, 35 and 28.
  - Brief: 52%, 63%, 85%. Natural: 81%, 93%, 94%. Needless offers: 10%, 16%, 7%.
  - Facts kept: before 90%, after 86%. None of the 5 turns kept before and lost after is a real loss. 3 are the time said the way a person says it ("twenty to five" for 4:46), which `ANSWER_ONLY` already asks for. 1 is the existing rule against guessing a reason for a delay ("the link was choppy"). 1 is a replay artefact: the replay marks his voice verified.
  - Win-loss-tie: after beat before 33-18-30 and beat her real replies 44-23-14.
- **tessaya-brain (latency and cost), before and after:** no regression. First word p50 (p95): Haiku 624 (1565) ms before, 650 (1441) after; Sonnet low 1465 (2077) before, 1471 (2016) after. Whole turn p50: Haiku 1642 to 1562 ms, Sonnet 3296 to 3286 ms. Cost a turn: Haiku $0.00059 to $0.00058, Sonnet $0.0113 to $0.0115. 332 turns an arm. The before run was on #1188's head; main differs only in Sebastian's roster line.

`R1_STREAM_SYSTEM` (the subscription route's acts form) is unchanged.

author: umairashrafx-cell
body:
The owner runs the counter from a phone, and the panel is a website he has to find in a browser each morning.

Chrome will install it to the home screen already — but it installs **the site manifest**, which is called *Al-Madina Jewellers* and starts at `/`. So what lands on the phone is the storefront, opening at the catalogue every time. The shortcut to the work does not exist.

`public/admin.webmanifest` is the same application under a different door:

| | site.webmanifest | admin.webmanifest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | Al-Madina Jewellers | **Al-Madina Admin** |
| short_name | Al-Madina | **Admin** |
| start_url | `/` | **`/admin`** |
| scope | `/` | **`/admin`** |

Installed from the panel it is a separate icon that opens where the work is. And because the scope stops at `/admin`, following **View site** hands the customer-facing pages back to the browser, where they belong.

## The subtlety, which is the whole of this change

The link is chosen in `__root.tsx` rather than added to the admin route.

A document may only carry one manifest: a browser reads the **first** `<link rel="manifest">` and ignores the rest. Declaring one on the admin route does emit a second tag — I checked, both render, root's first — so the site manifest would quietly win and nothing would look wrong. The choice has to be made where the single link is written, so `head` now takes `{ matches }` and picks by route.

## Checked on a running build

| Route | Manifest links | Points at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/admin` | 1 | `/admin.webmanifest` |
| `/admin/rates` | 1 | `/admin.webmanifest` |
| `/` | 1 | `/site.webmanifest` |
| `/collections` | 1 | `/site.webmanifest` |

The browser parses the admin one as `application/manifest+json` with name "Al-Madina Admin", `start_url` `/admin`, `scope` `/admin`, `display: standalone`, and 192 and 512 icons in both `any` and `maskable` — which is what Chrome asks for. Both files ship in the production build (`vite build` clean).

`tsc --noEmit` clean, 271 tests pass, prettier clean. Lint is clean — the only eslint output in a Windows checkout is `core.autocrlf` CRLF noise that hits untouched files identically.

## Two things I did not change, deliberately

- **The service worker needed nothing.** It is network-first for navigations and only falls back to `/offline.html` when the network is gone, so it was never going to serve the admin a stale shell. Worth knowing: with no signal the installed admin shows the shop's offline page, which is odd but harmless.
- **The icons are the shop's own**, so the two installed apps look alike and are told apart by their names on the home screen. A distinct admin icon is a design decision and inventing one was not mine to make — say the word and it is a small follow-up.

## How to install it

On the phone, in Chrome: open `almadinajeweller.com/admin`, menu (⋮) → **Install app**. The icon will read **Admin**.

author: itsjoshpark
body:
## Why

Chromium copies its own bundle to `$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)../X/<bundle-id>.code_sign_clone/code_sign_clone.XXXXXX/` at start-up (`code_sign_clone_manager.mm`) and deletes the copy only when it quits through its own shutdown path. A SIGTERM, Ctrl-C, `pkill` or crash leaves it behind, about 380 MB each time. On the dev machine, `run-local.sh` and the probe's `launch-clair.sh` were leaking one per launch, which added up to several GB in an afternoon.

## What

- `scripts/clean-code-sign-clones.sh [bundle-id]` deletes clones that are over a minute old and that no running process has a file open in (`lsof +D`). A clone's main executable is a hard link to the app's, so every clone of a build counts as in use while any copy of that build runs. That errs toward keeping clones too long, never toward deleting one in use.
- It's called from:
  - `run-local.sh`'s exit cleanup
  - `launch-clair.sh`, after it stops the previous test copy
  - `smoke-test.sh` on the self-hosted runner, which keeps its disk between runs
- `scripts/clean-code-sign-clones.test.sh` covers stale, open, new and unrelated entries, and argument checks. `run-local.test.sh` checks the cleanup runs, and points it at a temp directory.

## Testing

- `scripts/clean-code-sign-clones.test.sh` and `scripts/run-local.test.sh` pass, as does `shellcheck -S warning`.
- Run against the real directory while a runtime-suite Clair was running: it removed the 2 stale clones and kept the one that Clair had open.

No Changie fragment: dev and CI tooling only.
