### Picomatch: Method Injection in POSIX Character Classes causes incorrect Glob Matching
[CVE-2026-33672](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-33672) / [GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact
picomatch is vulnerable to a **method injection vulnerability (CWE-1321)** affecting the `POSIX_REGEX_SOURCE` object. Because the object inherits from `Object.prototype`, specially crafted POSIX bracket expressions (e.g., `[[:constructor:]]`) can reference inherited method names. These methods are implicitly converted to strings and injected into the generated regular expression.

This leads to **incorrect glob matching behavior (integrity impact)**, where patterns may match unintended filenames. The issue does **not enable remote code execution**, but it can cause security-relevant logic errors in applications that rely on glob matching for filtering, validation, or access control.

All users of affected `picomatch` versions that process untrusted or user-controlled glob patterns are potentially impacted.

##### Patches

This issue is fixed in picomatch 4.0.4, 3.0.2 and 2.3.2.

Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later, depending on their supported release line.

##### Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, avoid passing untrusted glob patterns to picomatch.

Possible mitigations include:
- Sanitizing or rejecting untrusted glob patterns, especially those containing POSIX character classes like `[[:...:]]`.
- Avoiding the use of POSIX bracket expressions if user input is involved.
- Manually patching the library by modifying `POSIX_REGEX_SOURCE` to use a null prototype:

  ```js
  const POSIX_REGEX_SOURCE = {
    __proto__: null,
    alnum: 'a-zA-Z0-9',
    alpha: 'a-zA-Z',
    // ... rest unchanged
  };
  

##### Resources

- fix for similar issue: [https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch/pull/144](https://redirect.github.com/micromatch/picomatch/pull/144)
- picomatch repository https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 5.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N`

#### References
- [https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch/security/advisories/GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p](https://redirect.github.com/micromatch/picomatch/security/advisories/GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p)
- [https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-33672](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-33672)
- [https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch/commit/4516eb521f13a46b2fe1a1d2c9ef6b20ddc0e903](https://redirect.github.com/micromatch/picomatch/commit/4516eb521f13a46b2fe1a1d2c9ef6b20ddc0e903)
- [https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch](https://redirect.github.com/micromatch/picomatch)

This data is provided by [OSV](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p) and the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).
</details>

---

### Picomatch has a ReDoS vulnerability via extglob quantifiers
[CVE-2026-33671](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-33671) / [GHSA-c2c7-rcm5-vvqj](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2c7-rcm5-vvqj)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact
`picomatch` is vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) when processing crafted extglob patterns. Certain patterns using extglob quantifiers such as `+()` and `*()`, especially when combined with overlapping alternatives or nested extglobs, are compiled into regular expressions that can exhibit catastrophic backtracking on non-matching input.

Examples of problematic patterns include `+(a|aa)`, `+(*|?)`, `+(+(a))`, `*(+(a))`, and `+(+(+(a)))`. In local reproduction, these patterns caused multi-second event-loop blocking with relatively short inputs. For example, `+(a|aa)` compiled to `^(?:(?=.)(?:a|aa)+)$` and took about 2 seconds to reject a 41-character non-matching input, while nested patterns such as `+(+(a))` and `*(+(a))` took around 29 seconds to reject a 33-character input on a modern M1 MacBook.

Applications are impacted when they allow untrusted users to supply glob patterns that are passed to `picomatch` for compilation or matching. In those cases, an attacker can cause excessive CPU consumption and block the Node.js event loop, resulting in a denial of service. Applications that only use trusted, developer-controlled glob patterns are much less likely to be exposed in a security-relevant way.

##### Patches
This issue is fixed in picomatch 4.0.4, 3.0.2 and 2.3.2.

Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later, depending on their supported release line.

##### Workarounds
If upgrading is not immediately possible, avoid passing untrusted glob patterns to `picomatch`.

Possible mitigations include:
- disable extglob support for untrusted patterns by using `noextglob: true`
- reject or sanitize patterns containing nested extglobs or extglob quantifiers such as `+()` and `*()`
- enforce strict allowlists for accepted pattern syntax
- run matching in an isolated worker or separate process with time and resource limits
- apply application-level request throttling and input validation for any endpoint that accepts glob patterns

##### Resources
- Picomatch repository: https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch
- `lib/parse.js` and `lib/constants.js` are involved in generating the vulnerable regex forms
- Comparable ReDoS precedent: CVE-2024-4067 (`micromatch`)
- Comparable generated-regex precedent: CVE-2024-45296 (`path-to-regexp`)

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

author: ehfazrezwan
body:
## What

Deleting one extracted fact of a conversation used to expire the graph edges of all its sibling facts, and a partition migration of one fact did the same. A conversation writes ONE Graphiti episode for N facts and stamps its uuid/name on every row, and the cascade expires and deletes that whole episode. The siblings kept their vectors, with a dangling episode ref and nothing re-ingesting them.

Refs #176

## Design

Privacy comes first: episode recall is on by default and an episode body holds the deleted fact verbatim, so the most-restrictive cascade is **unchanged** (expire the episode's edges, clear/remove its entities, delete the episode node). On top of it:

- `memory/provenance.py::_cascade_rows_once` cascades each distinct episode once per call and repairs every live sibling in the same owner: stale `graph_episode_uuid`/`graph_episode_name` cleared with an atomic nested `set_payload(key="metadata")`, plus one single-fact re-enrichment job per sibling (the `patch_memory` `graph_job` shape that `enqueue_graph_enrichment` / `process_graph_enrichment` consume). Rows deleted in the same call are never re-enriched. Siblings that cannot be repaired (clear failed, empty content, workspace-partitioned since the job shape carries no workspace, sibling lookup failed) are reported in `graph_sibling_unrepaired_ids` / `graph_sibling_repair_failed`.
- `delete_memory` / `delete_memories` return the jobs additively (`graph_jobs`, `graph_jobs_count`); `patch_memory` returns `sibling_graph_jobs`. REST (`DELETE /v1/memories/{id}`, `DELETE /v1/memories`, `PATCH`) and MCP (`delete_memories`, `edit_memory`) enqueue them through the new `TaskManager.enqueue_graph_jobs` and replace the payloads with counts (`graph_jobs_enqueued`, `graph_jobs_not_enqueued_ids`). Redis down never fails the delete.
- Episode lookup now returns the episode name in the same Cypher round trip (no extra round trips).

## Issue 176 (unfiltered bulk private delete)

The per-row try/except was already on dev, but the issue's root cause was not fixed: `_expire_graph_edges_for_groups` still did one serial `edge.save()` per edge capped at 1000 (edges past the cap stayed live), and the graph ran before the vector deletes. Now: group edges expire in ONE Cypher statement; vectors are deleted first, so a failing or slow graph step can never leave a half-deleted store; the cascade runs once per distinct episode. Previously every row after the first of a conversation re-resolved an already-deleted episode, was reported unresolved and ran the lossy substring fallback.

This also fixes atlas bug `fork.graphiti.bitemporal` (bulk edge expiry capped at 1000 edges): `test_bulk_group_expiry_is_one_statement_not_per_edge` expires 1500 edges in one statement and the #176 regression test expires 2500, asserting none stay live.

Also: `DELETE /v1/memories/{id}` with a malformed id returns 404 instead of 500 (the GET side is read-04's).

## Tests

`tests/test_episode_cascade_siblings.py` (41 tests) drives the real `MemoryService`, REST routes and MCP handlers against a fake Qdrant (real Filter evaluation) and a fake graph that interprets the cascade's Cypher. Covered: 1-of-N delete (siblings repaired, N-1 jobs, REST and MCP enqueue), bulk all (no jobs, one cascade), bulk subset (jobs only for survivors), null-category and include_shared paths, partition migration of 1-of-N, the #176 regression (300 rows / 100 episodes / 2500 edges, failing cascades, graph fully down: every vector row gone, failures reported, bounded work), Redis down, cross-user rows untouched, malformed id.

Asserted at the mock/Cypher level (not against real Neo4j): the fact is gone from the vector store AND from the graph, meaning all of the episode's edges get `expired_at` set (what the live-edge filter excludes) and the episode node is deleted so `search_episodes_fulltext` returns nothing. The Cypher text itself is not executed against Neo4j here.

Reality check: with the production changes reverted and the tests kept, the new tests fail (34 of 41 for the first commit, 7 more for the widened scope).

One existing test was updated, not weakened: `tests/test_memory_service.py::TestPatchMemory::test_content_edit_passes_merged_metadata_to_mem0` encoded the old behaviour (a content edit never touches the graph). It now stubs the cascade as resolved and asserts the cascade runs on the OLD content.

## Widened scope (same root cause)

- `retag_memories` partition migration: cascades once per episode after the scroll; sibling re-ingests are appended to the existing `graph_jobs` list (so the worker and callers enqueue them unchanged), counted in `sibling_graph_jobs_count`. The REST sync-fallback now reports `graph_jobs_not_enqueued_ids` instead of silently dropping jobs.
- Dedup (`dedup_memories`, both phases): returns `graph_jobs`. The graph-worker cron `dedup_all_memories` enqueues them via the existing `_enqueue_graph_jobs`; the conversation-compiler post-compile dedup enqueues through a short-lived `TaskManager` and reports `dedup_graph_jobs_enqueued` / `dedup_graph_jobs_not_enqueued` on `CompileResult`. Dedup policy itself is unchanged. - `tests/test_delete_edit_helpers.py`: direct coverage of the module-level helpers and pure methods in `memory/delete.py` and `memory/edit.py`.

Compared against `refs/import/X10/heads/codex/graph-wave` (commits `df2b121b`, `6ab0e0e4`, `31083336` touch the cascade).

body:
Phase H2 of the hydrology plan (`Documentation/HYDROLOGY_PLAN.md` in the parent, section 5.4): a lake or a river reach holds flagged water to its own level in the voxels of both generators. No world has a body: a chunk no body's footprint may reach generates from the request's one level as before and builds nothing new.

## What changed

- **A chunk's water columns** (`FVoxelChunkWaterColumns`, VoxelGeneration): the level over each XY column on a heightmap world, or over each down-line on a planet, with a value for no water. One function builds the list from the water levels the request carries (`FVoxelNoiseGenerationRequest::WaterBodies`, set by the chunk manager only where the chunk's range is not uniform); the CPU generator reads it and the GPU uploads the same float4s.
- **CPU generator:** the underwater materials and the caves' underwater depth per column, the fill's seed per column and its flood at or under the level over the voxel's own column, on heightmap worlds and planets.
- **GPU:** the density pass reads the list (`WaterColumnData`; a planet voxel finds its line from the shift rows), and four column kernels run the fill for a chunk with a list. The kernels of a chunk with one level are unchanged.
- **A lake's minimum cave depth** (`FVoxelWaterBody::MinCaveDepth`, on the sample too): over its footprint no cave opens above it, in both generators and in `FVoxelSurfaceQuery`'s cave test.
- **The pull and the edit-driven flood** test a voxel against the level over its own column (`UVoxelChunkManager::IsVoxelUnderWater`, `FVoxelChunkWaterReader`). The flood is made for a world with a lake or a river reach and the sea off too.
- `FVoxelDownLines` moves to the module's public headers. `voxel.Water.Stats` reports two more counters.

## Tests

`Generation.WaterColumns.Fill`, `.Planet`, `.OneLevel`; `Generation.GPUvsCPUWaterBodiesParity` (in the editor); `Streaming.Water.PullOrder.LakePlane`, `.LakePlanet`; `Streaming.WaterPropagation.Lake.Plane`, `.Planet`.

## Gates against the base (`dev` 3ff4970 under parent `dev` 02d7600, same worktree, same day)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Build | no new warning; non-unity build of VoxelCore, VoxelGeneration, VoxelStreaming: no error |
| Headless suite | 1,009 of 1,009 (base 1,001; eight new tests); mesh digests identical (209 lines); no new warning kind |
| `editor_gate.py` | 30 of 30; the 186 recorded parity lines identical; 24 new lines from the new parity test (material, biome and metadata agree in every voxel; density differs in 0 to 3 of 32,768 voxels by no more than 2 steps) |
| `map_gate.py` | `VoxelDemo` and `PlanetTest` byte-identical |
| `digest_gate.py` | `VoxelDemo` 188 of 188 and `Review_Planet` 195 of 195 chunks identical |
| `startup_order.py`, alone and `--net` | no source registered late |
| `check_docs.py` | no unknown name the base lacks |
| `bench_gate.py` | disturbed, see below |

**The bench is not a clean comparison.** Another session's editor ran PIE gates on the same GPU through most runs, which also raised costs this change does not touch (the far field's P95). Undisturbed runs, frame P95: the chord 29.9 and 28.7 ms on the base against 32.9 and 31.6 on the change, with equal medians (frame P50 19.6 and 19.3 against 20.0 and 18.8); the great circle 46.6 against 46.5. Disturbed runs read 38 to 53 ms (chord) and 52 to 87 (great circle) on the base, 40 to 54 and 52 to 91 on the change. No difference beyond the spread shows, but it is not three quiet runs a side; the combined gate should repeat it on a quiet machine.

## Documents

`WATER_SYSTEM.md` ("A chunk's water columns"), `GPU_PIPELINE.md` ("The water over a column", stage 2), `TESTING_STRATEGY.md` (30 results, 210 parity lines). The parent PR carries the plan's result, the new parity record and the gitlink.

author: screaminghawk
body:
Aligns the prototyp Hash validators with the decoders whose input they gate, found while reviewing trails-api#1231: `IsValidAddress` accepted any 42-character `0x`-prefixed string, and `ToAddress` (via `hex.DecodeString`'s partial decode) silently truncated at the first non-hex character and right-aligned the remainder — so a passing value could decode to a different address than the user typed.

## Changes

- `IsValidAddress` (Hash and HashText) now requires a valid hex body via `common.IsHexAddress`, on top of the existing lowercase-`0x` + length-42 checks. Everything that passes now decodes losslessly through `ToAddress`.
- `IsValidTxnHash` (Hash and HashText) gets the same treatment via `hex.DecodeString` on the body, aligning it with `ToHash`.
- All four validators short-circuit on inputs shorter than the `0x` prefix they slice, where they previously panicked (`IsValidTxnHash("")` panicked on both variants; `HashText.IsValidAddress` did too).
- `IsValidHex` rejects odd-length bodies: the hex decoder left-pads a leading nibble for them, shifting the decoded value, so an odd-length body never round-trips through `Bytes()`. All Hash values produced by `HashFromBytes` have even-length bodies, so no legitimate value is rejected.

Deliberately unchanged: `IsValidHex` stays lowercase-only (it checks the package's normalized form, and its only caller lowercases first), and the validators keep rejecting the uppercase `0X` prefix that the decoders accept — a stricter predicate than its decoder is safe; the pre-fix bug was the reverse.

## Behavior changes worth noting

- 42/66-character strings containing non-hex characters now fail validation instead of passing and being silently re-encoded to a different value at decode time.
- Zero-padded 32-byte words and short values were already rejected by the length checks; no change there.

## Known decode quirks (out of scope, unchanged)

`Bytes()` truncates at the first invalid hex character without padding or aligning, and `ByteSize()` counts characters rather than decoded bytes, so the two disagree on non-hex or odd-length input. These operate on data expected to be pre-validated by the validators above.

## Testing

`go test ./lib/prototyp/` passes with new table tests for `IsValidAddress` and `IsValidTxnHash` covering valid, mixed-case, non-hex, wrong-length, short, empty, and uppercase-prefix inputs. `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./lib/...` green except `lib/deployer`, which requires a live test chain and fails identically on master.

## Downstream

Downstream call sites (indexer, builder, stack, chainsight) use these validators as input-validation gates, so the stricter check only rejects values that were never real addresses or transaction hashes. Consumers pick this up via their go-sequence version bump.

author: acs
body:
The project has been carrying two things in its head, and this writes both down.

## `GLOSSARY.md` — the words

The base of the ubiquitous language. What a **take** is (one press of Record — not a mark), what a **clip** is (the takes in order, with the keep range and what was trimmed away), and the words in between:

| word | and what it is *not* |
|---|---|
| **mark** | a position on the clip; two of them bound a **section**, which is only a proposal |
| **cut** | a section that was approved — it has left the timeline |
| **keep range** | the IN/OUT you keep; a *cut* is what you dropped inside it |
| **segment** | a kept stretch of **one take**: what an export is made of |
| **kept time** | where a moment *appears*; **recording time** is where it *is* |

It also records the words we no longer use and why: **`part`** for a take — which cost a rename across nine modules — and **`region`** for a removed area, when a region is the *crop*.

The file ends with how to keep it alive: a new concept starts there in a sentence before it starts in the code, and a changed meaning changes the words and the code **together**.

## Three skills — how work is done here

`.agents/skills/` — the directory the coding harnesses **share**, rather than any one tool's private one — so an agent picks them up from the repository rather than from a session's memory:

- **`verification`** — what counts as proving a change: a unit test for a rule in the domain, a browser harness for anything drawn or played, a real session for the recorder. With the sandbox's traps written down (a WebM recorded here has `duration = 0`; the panel is backgrounded and never gets animation frames; assert what a person would *see*, not only the model) and the rule that a pull request says what was **not** verified.
- **`domain-model`** — the layers, who owns which rule (a range → the value object; the clip made consistent → the aggregate; the browser → an adapter), ports for collaborators, and that the view **listens** to `clip.onChange` rather than being called by whoever changed it.
- **`project-workflow`** — one change per pull request, how branches and commit messages are written, what a pull request body carries, what CI owns (the version), and what to ask about rather than decide.

## Verified

Nothing in `src/` changed, so the build, lint and the 51 tests are untouched.

The one thing that *is* checkable is whether the skills are **found**, and that was checked rather than assumed, twice over:

- All three were advertised to the agent on the next step, from their descriptions, before anything was restarted.
- After the move to `.agents/skills`, loading one by ID reports its own base directory: `/Users/alvaro.delcastillo/devel/orbit-capture/.agents/skills/verification` — so it is being discovered from the shared directory, not from a leftover copy. `.opencode/` is gone, and git recorded the move as renames.
- `.agents/skills` is a documented discovery source for OpenCode (a *project compatibility* source, like `.claude/skills`), so this costs nothing and is readable by the other harnesses too.

## Caveats

These are a first cut and meant to be edited. Two things will want adding as the refactor finishes: the session/view split (step 5) will have a rule about objects with a lifetime, and the recorder's flow will want a line about the one thing a harness cannot reach.

author: dmccoystephenson
body:
## What changes for the player

- **The photon ring is a smooth, continuous line.** It is the thin, higher-order image of the disk that hugs the shadow. At the low sky scales the owner's Intel UHD 630 runs (0.23–0.36), every playtest saw it as a broken, dotted line. Now it is drawn as a faint, unbroken line, and the lower arc of it under the disk is unbroken too.
- **The sky's resolution can rise again once the game holds 30 fps.** Before, a start-up hitch could push the scale down, and it never came back up on a 30 fps machine.
- **The bridge windows and the full-screen views (dream, epilogue) each keep their own resolution**, so moving from one to the other no longer carries a scale across that suits only one of them.

## Photon ring: why the result is still faithful

Each pixel used to trace one ray through its centre. The n = 1 image of the disk is about 0.045 M wide in impact parameter b. That was measured with the JS reference integrator from the ship's position: b − 3√3 ∈ [0.05, 0.095] above the shadow. One sky pixel at scale 0.23 spans about 0.13 M. So a pixel caught the line only when the line crossed its centre, and that is where the dots came from.

Each ray's impact parameter b = L/E is conserved, so it can be computed from the camera before any tracing. The shader evaluates it at the pixel and at two neighbouring pixels.
- **Which pixels:** those whose b-footprint overlaps the band [3√3 − 0.01, 3√3 + 0.13] are traced with `ceil(Δb / 0.04)` rays (2 to 5). This band holds all the thin images: n = 1 above the shadow, and n ≥ 2.
- **How:** the rays are spread evenly across the pixel along the direction b changes. That is the ring's radial direction; along the ring the image changes slowly.
- **Averaging:** their light is averaged **before** tone mapping.
- **Rays that go outward** from a camera outside r = 3.5 are skipped. They never come near the photon sphere.

This is a box filter over the pixel's width, so the pixel records the mean light across its footprint, as a camera pixel of that size would. Nothing is widened or brightened, and no coverage weight is invented. The ring is fainter than its rare old dots, because its true light is spread across a pixel 3× wider than the ring. Neighbouring rays are at most 0.04 M apart in b, which is closer than the n = 1 image is wide, so that image can no longer slip between samples. The n = 2 image (about 0.005 M wide) can still show the odd faint speck, at most 1/ns of its old brightness.

Every pixel outside the band is **bit-identical** to before. In `tools/render-bench.cjs`, `window_hole` changed 0.45% of pixels, all of them on the ring. `helm_r6` and `fall_r3` showed a max difference of 0. Physics, the integrator, step sizes and termination are all unchanged, and the GLSL rules still hold: no `pow()` of a negative base, ordered `smoothstep` edges, and the NaN guard.

Other options considered:
- **A coverage weight from the closest approach to the photon sphere.** Rejected: the weight would be invented rather than measured.
- **Temporal jitter.** Rejected: it needs a history buffer and reprojection while the player looks around, which adds per-frame cost.

**Cost:** only ring pixels pay. On swiftshader the hole-on view took about +20% (noisy: the machine was at load ~100, and unrelated views moved ±30% between runs). Views without the ring pay three extra impact-parameter evaluations per pixel, or one when far from the band. The adaptive scale absorbs this.

Before/after (scale 0.23, the owner's bridge view at 1584×861): the dotted ring and the dotted lower arc become continuous lines. The images were made with a local harness that loads `BlackHoleView` at a fixed scale. `tools/render-test.html` now takes `ring=0` to switch the new sampling off for A/B checks.

## Adaptive resolution (`AdaptiveScale` in raytracer.js; used by game.js and view3d.js)

The old rule shrank the scale above 36 ms per frame and grew it below 22 ms. With vsync, any GPU load between 16.7 and 33.3 ms shows as a 33.3 ms frame, so on a 30 fps machine the scale never grew. Start-up hitches pushed it down, and it stayed down. That is the likely reason for 0.23 on the bridge. The new controller works like this:
- **GPU timer path** (`EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2`; Chromium exposes it, and even swiftshader has it): the ray trace's own GPU time is measured, and the scale is steered so the sky takes a budget per frame (Auto 12 ms, Sharp 22 ms, Fast 5 ms). Cost grows as scale². If the whole frame still drops below ~28 fps, the budget shrinks to as little as 0.3×, and it recovers above 30 fps.
- **No-timer path:** while the frame holds 30 fps, the scale steps up 6% every 2 s, or 10% every 0.5 s when frames take under 22 ms. A step that drops the frame rate is undone, and that scale becomes a ceiling for 60 s.
- **One-off hitches are ignored**: a frame over 60 ms and over 2.5× the average. Three in a row count as real. The first second after a reset or mode switch is also ignored. The ship DPR controller now skips hitches too.
- **Separate controllers** for the window rectangles and the full-screen sky.
- `test/adaptive-scale.test.js` (6 tests; `npm test` 32/32) simulates a vsync'd UHD-630-like cost curve. Without a timer, the scale climbs from 0.23 to just under the 30 fps limit (~0.34) and backs off from steps that cost frames. With a timer, it settles within 10% of the budget. Hitches don't ratchet it down, a lasting slowdown is still seen as real, and a starved machine falls to the floor.

It cannot be promised that the scale will be higher on the UHD 630. That depends on how the frame splits between the sky and the ship, which only the real GPU shows. The new smoke fields report exactly that.

## Desktop smoke mode

The existing `ready, errors, info, fps, scale, electron` keys are unchanged. Two new keys are added:
- `gpu: { vendor, renderer }` (unmasked, via `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info`)
- `perf: { fps, frameMs, frameP95Ms, skyScaleAvg, skyGpuMs, gpuTimer }`, measured over the same 3 s window as `fps`

## What to look for on the real GPU

1. `gpu.renderer` should name the UHD 630 (ANGLE D3D11). Check `perf.gpuTimer`. If it is false, the no-timer path is in use.
2. `perf.skyGpuMs` should be near 12 on the bridge. Compare `perf.skyScaleAvg` with the earlier 0.23 (bridge), 0.36 (dream) and 0.29 (epilogue), and `fps` with 31/37/31. If fps drops below ~28 while `skyGpuMs` is about 12, the ship render is the bottleneck, and the controller should have lowered the budget by itself.
3. In the PNGs: the thin ring around the shadow should read as one continuous line, with no dashes.
4. Not touched (not this lane's files): the title screen's own adaptive loop in `src/main.js` still uses the old 22/36 ms rule. It could switch to `AdaptiveScale` in a one-line follow-up.

author: cocofhu
body:
## Problem

Switching away from a Solo session with a very long running reply and back replays the whole reply as a streaming animation, stutters, and takes a long time.

`SoloView` remounts `SoloSessionPane` per session, so switching back resubscribes and the server replays every frame of the running turn. The client held frames only until the history read returned; later replay frames were applied one WebSocket message at a time. Each one re-rendered the timeline, and the timeline typed the replayed text out again. #1229 only covered text already present when the timeline mounts.

## Fix

- `useSoloChat`: after a busy subscribe snapshot, frames up to its seq are buffered and applied together when the replay ends, meaning a frame at or past the snapshot seq arrives. When the replay stops short of it (the last published frame was a non-replayed KeepNone frame, or the network pauses), a 120ms quiet pause shows what has arrived, and later replay frames keep batching until the first live frame. On close, buffered frames are applied first so the reconnect cursor still advances.
- Each batch bumps the turn's `replayBatches`. `SoloSessionPane` passes it to `AgentTimeline`, which shows that update whole, including a short new step created inside the batch. Live chunks still animate.

## Verification

- New `useSoloChat` tests: a replay arriving after the history read applies in one batch; a replay stopping short of the snapshot seq applies after the quiet pause, and delayed replay frames still batch. New `AgentTimeline` test: a replay batch shows whole, and live chunks after it animate. All three fail without the source change.
- `npm run lint`, `npx vue-tsc --noEmit`, `npm test -- --coverage` (6261 passed, lines 91.76%), `npm run build`.
- Standalone simulation with the same rules, replaying about 30,000 characters: per-frame handling took ~3000 renders, 31s and dropped to 8 fps; batched handling showed everything in 0.3s at 54 fps or better (0.7s with a 0.4s network pause).

body:
## Что

Лимит запросов на клиентский IP для обоих транспортов узла — REST `/v0` и MCP `/mcp`.

- `src/adapters/inbound/rate-limit.ts` — скользящее окно в одну минуту на IP: N+1-й запрос получает `429`, `Retry-After` в секундах и каноническое тело `RATE_LIMITED` из `spec/v0/schemas/error.json`. Окно скользящее (не счётчик со сбросом на границе минуты), ключи с истёкшим окном вычищаются.
- `src/adapters/inbound/rest/handler.ts`, `src/adapters/inbound/mcp/http.ts` — проверка перед обработкой запроса; `GET /health` (`/v0/health`) и CORS-preflight окно не расходуют.
- `src/adapters/inbound/gateway.ts` — один лимитер на оба транспорта: переключение между REST и MCP не удваивает лимит.
- `src/core/errors.ts`, `spec/v0/schemas/error.json`, `spec/v0/README.md`, `llms.txt`, `website/llms.txt` — код `RATE_LIMITED` (HTTP 429) в каноническом списке ошибок.
- `OPENSMM_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN` (по умолчанию 120, `0` — выключено) и `OPENSMM_TRUST_PROXY` (1 — брать IP из `x-forwarded-for`, для узла за своим reverse-proxy) — в `gateway --help`, `.env.example`, `docs/DEPLOY.md` (раздел «Rate limit» + таблица Environment).

`OPENSMM_TRUST_PROXY` вне скоупа карточки, но без него документированный деплой за Caddy (все запросы приходят с IP прокси) упирается в общий лимит: по умолчанию выключено, поведение не меняется.

## Как проверить

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "rate limit"
```

Ручная проверка живого узла (лимит 3/мин, `/health` при исчерпанном окне, `0` отключает):

```bash

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:18081/v0/capabilities  # 4-й раз → 429 + retry-after
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:18081/health            # 200
```

## What changes

The schema a direct title call sends to the provider now describes only the answer's shape (an object with a string `title` and a string `summary`). The length limits stay where they were already enforced: on the answer, before anything is stored. The retry message names the limits.

## Why

On the owner's Deployment, every direct title call after #2269 deployed ended as `completion_timeout` at 25 seconds: 14 of 14 in the first three minutes. Reproduced against `@cf/openai/gpt-oss-20b` through the Workers AI binding with about 9,000 characters of material:

| Schema sent | Result |
|---|---|
| `title` and `summary` as plain strings | answered in 3 to 8 seconds |
| the same with `minLength` and `maxLength` on each string | no answer in 90 seconds |

String bounds stall the provider's schema-constrained output. Each timeout also spends one of a session's three title attempts.

Titling and completion tests (27 pass); server type check. The repository's fake provider cannot show this defect; it was confirmed against the real one from a scratch Worker and will be confirmed on the Deployment after deploy.

author: waeter-alt
body:
## Quoi

Le tracé des routes entre deux Postes commerciaux (bloc de test) est réécrit de zéro. Les versions précédentes décidaient pont ou tunnel case par case et ratent toujours les mêmes cas : ponts au ras de l'eau, tunnels là où une route suffisait, pentes impraticables, « cible trop loin ».

## Comment ça marche

- **Planificateur en Java pur** (`routes/plan/`, aucune classe Minecraft, donc testable hors jeu) en deux passes : recherche sur treillis qui suit le sol ou file droit à niveau (tablier au-dessus d'un creux, déblai ou tunnel à travers une bosse) en payant le vrai travail de chaque case, puis profil optimal bloc par bloc. Un pont ou un tunnel n'est jamais « décidé » : c'est ce que la ligne la moins chère donne, et son tablier est de niveau par construction.
- **Arpentage sans bloquer le serveur** (`RouteSurvey`) : les chunks déjà sauvés sont lus directement dans leurs fichiers de région sur des threads de travail (1 400 chunks en moins d'une seconde au lieu de 39 s) ; seuls les chunks jamais générés passent par le vrai chargement.
- **Pose au fil du chantier** (`RouteBuilder` + `RouteSite`) : chaque case est calculée au moment de la poser, depuis les deux extrémités ; le chantier ne garde chargés que ses deux fronts. Distance maximale : 2 600 blocs à vol d'oiseau.
- **Rendu** : chaussée 7 de large, volées pavées, ponts sur chevalets avec culées et lanternes, tunnels voûtés à portail, arbres abattus entiers sans feuilles en l'air (`TreeFelling.orphans`).
- **Réseau** : une route déjà construite est réutilisée par les suivantes (tronc commun, pont partagé).

## Vérification

- `./gradlew build` + 7 tests JUnit (`RoutePlannerTest` : canyon, rivière, crête, lac, diagonale, terrain inconnu, pont partagé).
- Serveur dédié : démarrage propre.
- En jeu, sur du vrai relief généré (seed 20262027), avec captures automatiques (`RouteShot`) : 5 tracés construits (ponts de gorge de 56 à 138 blocs, ponts de rivière, tunnels de 76 et 183 blocs), dont deux par le chantier animé, et un parcours joueur simulé (clic droit / sneak + clic droit sur les postes).
- Monde prêt à jouer en local : `mod/run/client/saves/Routes test` (non versionné, `run/` est ignoré).

## À savoir

- Le Poste commercial reste un bloc de test : rien n'est encore branché aux colonies, contrats ou caravanes.
- Pas encore vérifié : route à travers du terrain jamais généré (arpentage lent, ~80 s pour 2 000 chunks) ; un nouveau tunnel ne connaît pas un ancien tunnel qu'il croiserait.
- Outils de dev ajoutés (inactifs en production) : `dev/TerrainDump`, `dev/RouteDev`, `client/dev/RouteShot`, `RouteBench` ; pièges documentés dans `mod/docs/GOTCHA.md`.
- `RoutePath.java` est supprimé (remplacé).

author: tannevaled
body:
The tool asked for was one that deduplicates downloads by **sound, image and
video** similarity. It did pictures. This adds the other two — and in doing so
had to fix the gate that would have made them useless.

## Classify by reading, not by naming

The walk filtered on an extension list. That was wrong in a way worth naming:
an extension is a claim by whoever named the file, and the copy a
deduplicator exists to find is often *precisely the one that was renamed*. A
film saved as `backup.dat`, a photograph renamed `.thumb`, an MP3 with no
extension at all were all invisible — and **in a deduplicator an invisible
file reads as "no duplicates found"**, which is indistinguishable from a clean
tree.

Every file is now opened and its header read. Images and the audio-only
containers are settled by the header alone; only a container that could hold
either gets opened properly, and that open **streams** rather than slurping,
which matters when the candidate is a 4 GB film. The cost is one open and one
64 KiB read per file; what it buys is an answer about the tree rather than
about its naming conventions.

Measured on a tree holding four encodings of one melody and three scales of
one clip, two of them deliberately misnamed:

```
walked 11 file(s) under 1 root(s)
classified by content: 2 image(s), 5 recording(s), 4 video(s); 0 not media

SAME RECORDING, DIFFERENT BYTES — 1 group(s)
  133.6 KB recoverable, weakest pair 1.0000
    keep  song.flac (66.0 KB)
      dup renamed-audio.dat (48.3 KB)      ← an M4A called .dat
      dup sub/song-copy.mp3 (47.8 KB)
      dup song.opus (37.5 KB)

SAME VIDEO, DIFFERENT BYTES — 1 group(s)
  21.6 KB recoverable, weakest pair 0.9745
    keep  film.mp4 (56.3 KB)
      dup sub/film-small.mp4 (14.7 KB)
      dup no-extension (6.8 KB)            ← an MP4 with no extension
```

A file holding **both** audio and video is video. Its pictures are the
stronger evidence: two different films can share a soundtrack, and one film in
two languages shares its pictures.

## The audio threshold is 0.9, and the number was measured

Not the 0.7 that reads naturally beside TMK's video threshold. A chroma
feature is a profile of which pitch classes are present, so two recordings
built from the same notes agree substantially even when they are not the same
piece. The same eight-chord melody played **backwards** scores **0.7064**;
with only **four** chords it scores **0.8176**, because fewer distinct chords
means more of the piece overlaps itself. The real margin above 0.9 is 0.08, so
0.85 would be wrong too.

## The video pass stays within a kilobyte a video

TMK's level-2 features are 262 KB a video against 1 KB for level 1, so holding
them for a tree is what would make this unusable on a real download folder —
five hundred videos is 131 MB before any comparison starts. TMK's own
documentation calls the level-1 feature *"what a large index stores"*, so that
design is used as intended: sweep on level 1, release `Cos`/`Sin`, and pay for
level 2 only on pairs that survive. The cost is decoding a candidate twice.

The prefilter gate is **0.5**, far below the 0.7 decision, because a prefilter
sitting at the decision threshold starts *making* the decision. It is a recall
risk rather than a free optimisation, so it is measured rather than asserted
safe:

| level-1 score | |
|---|---|
| a clip vs its half-scale copy | 0.9851 |
| a clip vs its quarter-scale copy | 0.9881 |
| a clip vs an unrelated clip | −0.0829 |

`TestLevel1GateDoesNotRejectATrueMatch` fails if a true match's margin
disappears **and** if the gate stops rejecting unrelated material — a
prefilter that rejects nothing has saved nothing.

## Bounds, and what they cost

`--audio-seconds` and `--video-seconds` default to 180. Chroma features run at
roughly 97 float64 a second, so two thousand tracks would be 460 MB held at
once; video is bounded for **time** rather than memory, since every frame is
resampled to 15 fps and put through PDQ. Stated rather than hidden: two files
that differ only *after* the window are reported as the same, and a clip taken
from beyond the window does not match its source.

## One copy of the clustering

Single-linkage union-find was about to become three copies, one per pass,
which is how passes drift apart: a fix to the image clustering that never
reaches the audio one leaves two tools inside one binary. It is one type now,
with the warning in one place, and every pass reports its **worst** pair so a
stretched chain stays visible.

## A regression this caught in its own tests

Classifying by content made an existing test stop testing anything.
`TestAFileItCannotDecodeMakesTheReportSayIncomplete` staged a file called
`broken.png` holding no PNG, which worked while the walk trusted names: the
name got it in and the decoder found out. By content that file is genuinely
not media — correctly — so the `INCOMPLETE` warning went untested **while the
test still passed**.

It is now a *truncated but valid* PNG: real header, missing pixel data, which
is what a half-finished download is. It checks its own premise (`classify`
says image, `perceptual` fails) so it cannot pass for the wrong reason.

A new bucket needed its own guard for the same reason: "not media" now absorbs
most of the tree, and a classifier that broke and called everything other
would print an empty report that reads as a clean tree. The count is printed
and `TestFilesThatAreNotMediaAreCountedNotSwallowed` keeps it printed.

One more test stopped skipping rather than being left green: the corrupt-video
case turned out to fail at **classification**, not at hashing — a truncated
MP4 is refused by the container because the declared box outruns the file — so
it now asserts that path instead of skipping.

## Found upstream while doing this

A VP9 file is reported as unreadable rather than skipped, which is the wanted
behaviour — but the message is wrong:

```
decode: invalid sample: NAL unit of 2185855810 bytes with 2939 left
```

That is an H.264 NAL-unit parser handed VP9 data. `go-avkit/decode` does not
check the codec before parsing, so it reads VP9 bytes as a length prefix and
calls the file **corrupt** instead of saying the codec is unsupported, sending
a user to inspect a file that is fine. The length is bounds-checked, so this is
a wrong diagnosis and not an unbounded allocation. The fixture is committed and
a test pins the **reporting**, not the wording.

## Checks

- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing; `go mod tidy -diff` clean; `go vet` clean.
- Full suite green, and green under `-race`.
- Coverage **91.3%** against the existing **90% floor, which was not lowered**
  to accommodate the new code. `pcmMono` and `pcmValue` were at 0% because
  dedupe had no WAV fixture at all — the PCM passthrough had never run in its
  own suite.
- `js/wasm`, `linux/386` and `linux/s390x` build locally; the full matrix is
  in CI.
- Fixtures committed so no runner needs ffmpeg; README records the command
  that produced each one, including why `clip-180p.mp4` is *derived from*
  `clip-360p.mp4` rather than rendered at that size.

### Known duplication, not hidden

`pcm.go`, `toMono`, `resampleToFeatureRate` and `frameImage` are now in both
this repository and `go-perceptual/perceptual`. That plumbing — decode to
mono PCM at the feature rate, wrap a frame for hashing — belongs in a shared
package rather than copied. I would rather land the working passes and extract
it as its own reviewable change than bundle a new module into this one; filing
it as an issue.

body:
Refs #595, #596, #597

Task T3 of fixes batch 10 (docs/EPIC-fixes-10.md, rulings 1-6, 8, 9). Serves SPEC 9.1, 9.2, 9.14 and 17.10 as the plan's "SPEC changes" section words them; SPEC 3.4 for the delete cleanup.

## What changed

- **Results** (Mods tab and `/mods/search`): the "Mods matching" panel is always there, a list (not a table) of ten rows, named by its count line. Paging sits above and below: Previous page, a "Page [n] of N" box with Go (a plain GET form), Next page. With script only the panel is replaced and focus goes to its heading; without script they are plain links and forms. On the tab, Enter now searches in place too.
- **Rows**: the title links to the mod's portal page in a new tab (says so in its name), summary (two lines), Latest, Downloads, Updated (from `Hit.ReleasedAt`; nothing when zero; `time.js` writes the date in the reader's language through a new `data-day` mode). The control is "+" ("Add *mod* to the plan", 44 px on touch), "Installed", "In plan" with a tick and "−", or "Needed by *mod*" with no button. "+" shows "Adding…" until the panel is back.
- **Plan panel** (new `internal/web/modplanpanel.go`): reads the saved picks (T1's store), works the plan out with the existing resolver, and shows each pick with a cross and its changing required dependencies nested under it, "Needed by *mod*" on each; a shared dependency under each pick; built-in and already-fitting installed mods hidden; "Will update to *x.y.z*"; a warning triangle and short reason for a dependency that cannot be had or conflicts. "Review and install N mods" (distinct mods) opens today's plan page (`kind=install&name=…`). Started time and "Clear plan". Empty and portal-down states. Phone: follows the results and holds to the bottom as a bar once it has a mod.
- **Routes**: `POST /worlds/{id}/mods/plan/mods` (add or remove one name) and `POST …/plan/clear`, behind `modsWorld` and the site's cross-origin protection. Without script they go back to the page and row they came from (the return address must be one of this world's mods pages); with htmx they send the panel plus each result row on the page out of band, with the words to announce and where focus goes. Picks past `store.MaxModPlanNames` are refused with a message.
- `store.MaxModPlanNames` replaces the web package's `maxPlanNames` everywhere.
- `internal/mods`: `Plan.Requires` (each enabled mod's required dependencies), not hashed, with a unit test; nothing else in the resolver changed.
- World delete clears the world's saved plan (`worlds.go`, that call only).
- Strings in all eight languages, with `make i18n-hash`. The tick-box strings are gone.
- DESIGN 8.11: the search section is rewritten for the list, paging and panel.

## Files outside the brief's list

- `internal/web/modgone.go`: one line, `maxPlanNames` to `store.MaxModPlanNames`.
- `internal/world/modupload.go`: `validModName` exported as `ValidModName`, so the add route checks a name before it is saved.
- `internal/web/static/time.js`: a `data-day` mode (date only) for the Updated date.
- `internal/web/modlink_test.go`, `modplan_add_test.go`: assertions that read the old search table.
- e2e `mods-failures`, `mods-inactive`, `mods-install`, `mods-version`, `mods-ui`, `mods-plan` specs: they reached the plan page through the search page's "Add to plan" link, which is gone; they now use "+" and Review, or open the plan page directly. `mods-plan.spec.ts` is T4's file; only its first search step changed.

## Review fixes (second commit)

- "+" checks the name with `world.ValidModName` before the store; a bad name gets 400 (an error page without script, the panel's error with htmx). Removing needs no check.
- While a plan change runs, Review is `aria-disabled` and described by "Review is ready once the plan is updated.", shown under it, so it never opens without the last change. "Adding…" is no longer `aria-hidden` and is read out through the announcer.
- Phone bar (WCAG 2.4.11): `scroll-padding-block-end: 9rem` while the bar has a mod (below 64rem only, where the bar is at the foot), and the open list folds when focus leaves the panel. An e2e tabs through the rows at 320 px and checks no focused button sits under the bar; it fails without the padding.
- Titles: `modportal.Client.Mod` keeps each mod 15 minutes in a client-wide cache, and the planner uses the same client, so the panel's title lookups hit what the resolver just fetched; no extra portal request per row.
- World ids are never reused: `newID` skips any id with a world or a snapshot folder, and delete keeps `snapshots/<id>` (`keepID`). Create, clone and import always get a fresh id; restoring a deleted world brings back its own id, whose picks were cleared at delete. So no clearing at create is needed.
- Cleanups: the no-script anchor is worked out in `planChanged`; the dead branch in `PlanPanel.Names` is gone. Strings: ru "Нужен моду {mod}", pl impersonal "Należy wpisać…", two new strings in all eight languages, `make i18n-hash`.

## Left for T4

The plan page's "Add another mod" still uses the old `mod-hits` and `mod-pager` templates, now kept in `modportal.html` for that page alone (the tick-box branches are gone). T4 removes them with "Add another mod".

## How it was verified

- `make check-go fmt-check vet lint typecheck`: clean (0 lint issues).
- `go test ./internal/web` in four chunks under 3 minutes each: all pass. `go test ./internal/mods ./internal/store ./internal/i18n`: pass.
- New unit tests: add, remove, clear, bad requests and return addresses, cross-site refused, limit, tree content (nesting, shared dependency, hidden built-in and fitting installed, update line, warning line, count), installed pick, portal down, htmx reply (out-of-band rows, focus, announcement, row cap), world delete clears the plan, tree builder (lifting through a hidden dependency, cycles).
- e2e, all four projects (desktop and 320 px, dark and light): `mods-search.spec.ts` (19 tests, every state, with and without script, axe on each), `mods-tab.spec.ts`, the mods rows of `click-budgets.spec.ts` (4 and 5 clicks); the other changed mods specs on desktop-dark and phone-light; the remaining Mods-page specs (`mods-files`, `mods-updates`, `mods-prestart`, `mods-save`, `mods-sync`, `mods-settings`, `mods-undo`, `ui-fixes`, `account`, `fakeportal`, `times`) on desktop-dark, most on phone-dark. All passed. The full suite was not run here (foreman.css changed, so the orchestrator runs it).

## Click and screen counts

- Search for a mod and install it: Mods, +, Review and install 1 mod, Install 1 mod = 4 clicks, 2 screens (Mods tab, plan page). Typing is not a click and needs no Search.
- A second mod in the same change: one more + = 5 clicks, same 2 screens.

## Proposed STATUS line

Fixes batch 10, T3: the Mods tab and search page show results as a list with paging above and below and a page box; each row has "+" (or In plan with "−", Installed, or Needed by), and the world's saved plan sits beside the results as a tree of each pick and the dependencies that change, with updates and warnings, Review and install N mods, Clear plan, and a bottom bar on phones. Gaps: the plan page still has "Add another mod" until T4.

author: emilwareus
body:
Speeds up JS/TS analysis while preserving the measured JS benchmark accuracy. The original AX102 run reduced the refined zod fact dump from **81.5 s to 37.9 s**. The timing and RSS table below describes those samples; it does not establish unchanged peak memory for other inputs.

## Equivalence evidence and limits

- The original author reported byte-identical output for all 82 sorted JS bench dumps (41 cases × base and refined plans) against v0.5.1 (`e0d4199f`), and identical refined zod provider output digests. The raw `/home/dev/polint-perf/` comparison artifacts were unavailable in this review workspace, so those historical comparisons have not been independently reproduced here.
- Sorted JSON dumps omit fact metadata and some internal families. Equality of these dumps does not prove unchanged internal ordering, metadata, or every cache digest.
- `make js-bench`: only the Cost section and the version line changed. Recall, unresolved and wrong-complete rows are untouched.
- The benchmark reports zero false-complete results over four labelled hidden lines and 83 labelled call lines. Package observations cover exercised paths only; these results do not prove universal soundness. Source inspection found the first-match and key-equality semantics preserved.

## Changes, ranked by refined-zod time won

| Commit | Change | Won |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `abe8a601` | JS/TS call refinement indexes call sites, places and solver-resolved sites once per run instead of scanning all of them per unresolved call | ~37.6 s |
| `6837a20b` | Unknown collection looks up nodes and call sites through maps instead of a linear scan per edge | ~6 s |
| `222c9e96` | Four provider output digests write packed parts in parallel row-count batches instead of one heap string per row. Row counts do not bound payload bytes or guarantee an allocator threshold; the review identified a large-payload memory regression in indexed evidence emission | 8.7 → 4.1 s |
| `9680264f` | Evidence and data-flow fact metadata is built in parallel and recorded in row order, through `record_family_metadata` like the call families. The builders only resolve keys, never intern | 5.4 → 2.4 s |
| `c43a0d70` | Narrowing groups places by function | ~0.5 s |
| `f5559d1b` | Normalization sorts and reference validation resolve keys under one interner read view | noise |
| `347e7c32` | Test-only: provider stage timings from the bench dump under `RUST_LOG=polint::kernel::stage` | — |

## Before / after: fact dump, from `make js-bench`

The dump runs with no cache, one tree per process, and peak RSS from `wait4`.

| tree | base ms | base RSS MB | refined ms | refined RSS MB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| axios | 618 → 627 | 117 → 117 | 2158 → 1913 | 279 → 295 |
| zod | 10898 → 10861 | 1333 → 1333 | **81463 → 37860** | 3811 → 3784 |
| commander | 235 → 236 | 59 → 60 | 1691 → 1591 | 146 → 154 |
| async | 410 → 409 | 93 → 92 | 1924 → 1748 | 262 → 296 |
| chalk | 42 → 56 | 32 → 32 | 93 → 91 | 40 → 42 |
| dayjs | 41 → 40 | 32 → 32 | 93 → 110 | 37 → 37 |
| underscore | 191 → 192 | 53 → 54 | 674 → 599 | 122 → 133 |

These are historical samples from the original AX102 run. Small-tree timing differences can include run-to-run noise; RSS increases in this table are not evidence of unchanged peak memory.

## Targets not met

| Target | Result | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Refined zod under 2× base | 3.5× (was 7.5×) | Profile and analysis below |
| Refined memory near base | 3.8 GB vs 1.3 GB | Long-lived fact rows and 4.9 M interned keys |
| Base zod reduced | No | `symbol_graph` and `semantic_mir` per-node work |

- **Remaining refined time:** the largest single step is `ts_direct_bindings` (4.2 s). Its callable-flow walk reads the oxc `Program`, which is `!Sync`, so per-file parallelism would need re-parsing per thread or unsafe code.
- **Memory:** the sampled zod peak includes long-lived facts. Transient payload buffers also matter: row-count batching can retain hundreds of MiB on large stable-key payloads. Indexed evidence emission needs one-row streaming or a byte bound.
- **Base:** neither provider has an algorithmic hotspot. A speedup needs per-file interner overlays.

The profile, numbers and ranking are in `.planning/quick/261115-p8s-js-callgraph-speed/261115-p8s-FINDINGS.md`.

## Original author validation (before review fixes)

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- Clippy `-D warnings`, five sets:
  - workspace `--all-features`
  - `-p polint` default
  - `--no-default-features`
  - `--features lang-go`
  - `--features lang-typescript`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked`: debug build, Go 1.25, `POLINT_REQUIRE_TS_TYPESCRIPT=1`

- `make js-bench`

author: kusts
body:
## Summary

Corrige as duas causas das 20 falhas de E2E que o merge do V2 introduziu em `main`.

### Causa 1 — nomes acessíveis colidentes
O V2 renomeou o FAB do BottomNav para `Novo lançamento`, o mesmo nome que o popup de ações já usava. `getByLabel("Novo lançamento")` passou a casar com 2 elementos (strict mode) e o grupo ficou indistinguivel do botao.

- FAB mantem `Novo lançamento` (a acao).
- Popup passa a se chamar **"Acoes de novo lancamento"** (o menu).
- Specs/helpers que miravam o grupo foram atualizados para `getByRole("group", { name: "Acoes de novo lancamento" })`.

### Causa 2 — deteccao de viewport no helper
`e2e/support/new-transaction.ts` usava um fallback generico `getByRole("button", { name: "Novo lancamento" })` como sinal de "estamos no desktop". Com o FAB renomeado, esse lookup casou com o **FAB mobile**, entao testes mobile entravam no ramo desktop: clicavam o FAB uma vez e esperavam um `dialog` que nunca abre.

- Deteccao agora usa apenas o rail (`complementary`) visivel ou viewport >= 1024.
- Sinais de shell em outros specs foram escopados por viewport/rail; nenhum lookup generico restante pode confundir FAB com CTA.

## Evidence

- `playwright --project=functional-mobile -g "TX-0|TRF-0|UI-0|G3-0|NOAPI-01|NAV-0|HOME-1"` -> **36/36 PASS** (base: 19-20 falhas)
- `playwright --project=functional-desktop -g "TX-01|TRF-01"` -> **2/2 PASS**
- `vitest BottomNav + AppShell` -> **39 PASS**
- `typecheck` PASS · `lint` 0 erros (34 warnings pre-existentes) · `build:next:cloudflare` PASS

## Notes

- O job `e2e` roda apenas em `main` (nao em PR), por isso o CI de PR ficou verde com a regressao presente. Fica registrado como lacuna de gate: vale habilitar um subconjunto de E2E em PR para pegar essa classe de falha antes do merge.
- Nenhuma mudanca de comportamento financeiro; a correcao de acessibilidade melhora a distincao acao/menu para leitores de tela.

author: maxfindel
body:
## Summary

In-app purchase of **Fix one domain** ($149 USD, one time, paid in advance) for the hosted service, the way fly.io does it: the workspace **owner** is redirected to Stripe to save a card, comes back, and confirms with one click. One card (one Stripe Customer) per workspace, so an agency can have its client own a workspace and pay directly. No subscription, no hosted plan, no Stripe SDK, no analytics.

Hosted only (`MODE=saas` + `SAAS_ENABLED=1`) and only when `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` (restricted key) and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` are set. Otherwise there is no offer, no Billing section and every billing route is a `404` (self-host included).

Server: migration `0016`, `src/billing/*`, query module, operator orders API, preflight, export, retention, daily reconcile, an in-repo fake Stripe. Dashboard: Settings → Billing, the offer and confirm step on a domain page, order state, the instance owner's Orders page. Docs: `docs/billing.md` and the usual retention/schema/upgrade/changelog entries. `src/api/router.ts` gets one import and one mount block, nothing else; none of PR 172's or PR 174's files are touched.

## The flow step by step

1. **Add a card.** Owner clicks *Add a card*. `POST /api/billing/card-session` lazily creates the workspace's Stripe Customer (idempotency key `rsm-cust-<workspace id>`, then `UPDATE … WHERE stripe_customer_id IS NULL` and a re-read, metadata `workspace_id`), inserts a binding row (workspace, user, purpose, validated return path) **before** calling Stripe, then creates a Checkout session (`mode=setup`, `payment_method_types[]=card`, `customer`, `client_reference_id`, `metadata`). The browser goes to Stripe.
2. **Return.** `GET /api/billing/checkout/return?session_id=…` looks the session up in *our* table, requires the signed-in person to be (still) owner of that row's workspace, re-fetches the session from Stripe and checks `status=complete`, customer, metadata and a succeeded setup intent, sets the card as the customer's default, completes the row, and `303`s to the stored return path. The `checkout.session.completed` webhook does the same; whichever is first wins and one audit entry is written. It can never mark an order paid.
3. **Offer.** On a domain page that has something to fix (the page's own "Do this next" list is the source of truth), below "Do this next", a quiet secondary button: "Have us fix this domain: $149 USD" (amount and currency from the Stripe price). Hidden on a fine, unproven or non-resolving domain, and while an order is open.
4. **Confirm.** A dialog states what is bought, the domain (shown, never typed), the price, the refund rule, what happens next, links to the terms and refund policy, the card to be charged and the billing email. No card: the one primary action is *Add a card to continue* (Stripe, then back to the **same** confirm step via `?order=fix-one-domain`). Card: the one brand-filled *Pay $149 USD*, disabled while in flight. Members and admins are told only the owner can buy.
5. **Charge.** `POST /api/billing/orders` re-checks everything server-side, inserts the order `pending` **first** (unique open slot), then Stripe Invoice → item → finalize → pay with `Idempotency-Key: rsm-<order>-<step>`. The answer is `processing`; the signed `invoice.paid` webhook (re-reading the invoice) marks it paid. 3-D Secure: the hosted invoice page opens in a new tab and the dialog polls ("Waiting for your bank's confirmation"). Declined: invoice voided, order `failed` with Stripe's own words, the buyer can change the card and try again.
6. **Paid.** Exactly once: an audit entry and an email to `OWNER_EMAIL` (workspace, domain, buyer, amount, order id, Stripe invoice id).
7. **The work.** The instance owner marks the order *started* and later *done* in the Orders page; both audited. Nothing is sent automatically on done. Refunds are made in the Stripe dashboard and arrive via `charge.refunded`.

States: `pending → paid → started → done`, plus `refunded` (from paid/started/done), `failed`, `canceled`. Transitions are monotonic and validated in one place (`src/billing/orders.ts`), each a single conditional `UPDATE`.

## Charge mechanism and why (Invoice vs PaymentIntent)

Server-side: re-check owner role, hosted, billing on, domain belongs to the workspace and is live and proven, no open order; resolve the price by `lookup_key` (active, one-time, USD, fixed amount; cached in D1 with a 10-minute TTL, always fresh when someone pays; misconfigured prices are refused); insert the order; then **Invoice** (`collection_method=charge_automatically`, `auto_advance=false`, `pending_invoice_items_behavior=exclude`, metadata `order_id|workspace_id|domain|offer`) → one invoice item with the price → finalize → pay (`off_session=true`, the default card).

Why an Invoice and not a bare PaymentIntent:
* Stripe emails the buyer a proper invoice and receipt, so we send the buyer nothing.
* The customer portal lists it.
* Refunds and credit notes attach to it.
* A future subscription invoices the same way.

Every Stripe POST carries `Idempotency-Key: rsm-<order id>-<step>`, so a retry or a double click repeats the same objects. A pending order that stalls (older than a minute) is resumed with the same keys; one older than an hour with an unpaid invoice is reconciled (paid if the webhook was lost, otherwise voided and `canceled`) on view and in the daily job. A draft invoice that never finalized is deleted (Stripe cannot void drafts).

Pinned `Stripe-Version: 2025-09-30.clover`: payments are read with `expand[]=payments`, charge events are matched by stored charge/payment-intent ids (falling back to `GET /v1/invoice_payments`) because `Charge.invoice` no longer exists.

## No SDK, why

`StripeClient` is ~150 lines of `fetch` with form encoding for 14 fixed calls. The SDK is a large dependency for that, would put the Stripe key through third-party code, and we need exact control of `Idempotency-Key` and the pinned version. The key lives in a private field and never appears in errors, JSON, `inspect` output or logs (as `CfClient`). `STRIPE_API_BASE` is honoured only for `http://127.0.0.1` / `localhost` (the e2e fake); anything else is ignored.

## Security

| Attack | Answer | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| Admin/member buys, adds a card or opens the portal | Owner only, `403 owner_required`, no Stripe call | `test/billing/card.test.ts` (roles) |
| API key or agent credential spends money | Browser session only, `403` | `test/billing/card.test.ts` |
| CSRF on a state-changing route | Resolver's same-origin check for cookie sessions on every POST (card, portal, order, operator) | `test/billing/card.test.ts` (CSRF) |
| Cross-workspace order, session or domain id | Behaves as missing: `404`, identical body | `test/billing/card.test.ts` (isolation), `orders.test.ts` |
| Forged checkout return: unknown, another workspace's, incomplete, mismatched customer or metadata, not the owner | No effect; verified against our table and Stripe | `test/billing/card.test.ts` (return URL) |
| Open redirect via return path | Allow-list of the app's own routes; the server builds the URL from the stored workspace id | `test/billing/unit.test.ts` (paths), `card.test.ts` |
| Return marks an order paid / attaches another customer | Cannot; it never touches orders and re-checks the customer | `test/billing/card.test.ts` |
| Forged webhook: bad signature, stale or future timestamp, tampered body, other key mode, oversized | `400`/`413`, nothing recorded | `test/billing/webhook.test.ts` |
| Replay or duplicate event | Insert-first event ledger; one effect, one owner email | `test/billing/webhook.test.ts` |
| Handler crash swallowed by dedupe | Ledger has status; failure answers `500` and is re-run | `test/billing/webhook.test.ts` |
| Out-of-order events (`invoice.paid` after `charge.refunded`, `payment_failed` after paid) | No legal predecessor, no change | `test/billing/orders.test.ts`, `webhook.test.ts` |

author: jtn0123
body:
## What

Step 6 of the typing plan: `app_setup`, `display` and `services` now run with mypy's `disallow_any_explicit`, so writing `Any` in those packages is an error.
- The new last section of `mypy.ini` turns it on.
- `tests/unit/test_mypy_config.py` checks the package list never shrinks.
- `docs/typing.md` explains what to write instead.

## How the 67 uses were replaced

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `device_config: Any`, `playlist_manager: Any` in the service workflows | `Config`, `PlaylistManager` (imported under `TYPE_CHECKING`) |
| `plugin: Any` in the save workflow | a `SettingsValidator` protocol (`validate_settings`), which `BasePlugin` and the tests' fakes both satisfy |
| `dict[str, Any]` for decoded JSON | `utils.json_types.JsonObject`, a named alias |
| bare `np.ndarray` in `display/crisp.py` | `NDArray[np.uint8]` pixels and indexes, `NDArray[np.int32]` packed colours, `NDArray[np.intp]` counts. I checked each one against a real frame at runtime. |
| `cast(Any, fn)(...)` ×4 in `display_manager.py` | direct calls |
| the imported Waveshare driver, its SPI libraries, GPIO modules | `ModuleType`, `CDLL`, and plain inference (those libraries have no types) |

## What removing the casts found

- **`apply_image_enhancement`** declared `dict[str, float]`, but the device's `image_settings` also hold `screen_rendering`, a string. It now takes a `Mapping[str, object]` and treats any factor that isn't a number as 1.0. Before, such a value reached `ImageEnhance` and raised. Load-time schema validation keeps the four factors numeric today, so this changes nothing for a valid `device.json`.
- **`resize_image`** declared `list[str]`, but a plugin's hints can include objects (see `plugin-info.schema.json`). It only tests `"keep-width" in ...`, so it now takes any collection.
- **Waveshare `epdconfig.py`** built `RuntimeError("Cannot find DEV_Config.so")` without `raise`. A missing library therefore failed one line later with `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'DEV_Module_Init'`. It now raises the intended message.
  - A `DEV_SPI_*` call before the library is loaded now says so, instead of raising `AttributeError`.
  - The two tests that pinned the old `AttributeError`s now expect the clear errors.

## Tests

- **New and updated:**
  - non-numeric enhancement factors are ignored; this fails on main with `TypeError` from `ImageEnhance`;
  - the `mypy.ini` contract;
  - a non-callable driver `init`;
  - a journal entry without `MESSAGE`.
- **Test fixes found by the new types:**
  - `test_crisp.py` built its packed arrays as int64; it now uses `Frame(img).packed`, which is what the code passes;
  - the always-raising `fail()` helpers return `NoReturn`;
  - the timezone test checks for `ZoneInfo` before reading `.key`.
- **Runs:** 2404 tests across the 111 files that touch these modules pass. `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- **mypy:** `src/` is clean with the flag. The tests count drops from 487 to 485, measured against main locally, with no new errors.

author: andjalis
body:
Fixes #443.

The main case of #443 (Invasion of Innistrad: "target creature an opponent controls gets -13/-13") was already fixed on main by #452 (`tests/test_debuff_opponent_filter.py`). This PR fixes the two related quirks the issue lists, both in `cards/patterns.py`:

1. **"Up to one target creature gets -N/-N until end of turn"** had `filter="opp"` and no `optional_target`. Now any creature is a legal target, and choosing none is allowed. The AI still aims at the opponent: the `debuff_one` chooser picks only from opposing creatures, and returns none when it has no good target.
2. **"Another target creature gets -N/-N"** (Leeching Bite and the like: "Target creature gets +1/+1 ... Another target creature gets -1/-1 ...") dropped "another", so one creature could take both targets. The new effect flag `not_earlier` (read in `Game.legal_targets` through the new helper `Game._earlier_targets`) excludes objects that an earlier target of the same spell or ability took. The check runs while targets are chosen (`auto_targets`), when a whole list is validated (`valid_action_targets`, using the effect's index, which avoids the #393-style anchor bug) and on resolution (through the `StackItem`).

## Parse-diff (whole database): 22 cards, all intended
- `not_earlier`: leeching bite, consume strength, steal strength, rites of reaping, schismotivate, drooling groodion.
- Opponent filter dropped and `optional_target` added: rat out, bleeding edge, dissection practice, dubious delicacy, zulaport duelist, ant-man's air force, gumdrop poisoner, and the planeswalker "+1: (until your next turn,) up to one target creature gets -N/-0" lines of garruk veiled butcher, jace the perfected mind, jace telepath unbound, liliana the last hope and mu yanling celestial wind.
- The bounce cards in the full-database diff belong to #551, not this PR.

No full-card count change: these were counted full but targeted wrong.

## Tests
`tests/test_debuff_another_upto.py`, six of whose eight tests fail on main:
- parse;
- with "up to one", any creature or none is legal, and the AI picks none when it has only its own X/1 and picks the opposing creature when there is one;
- with "another", the same creature twice is rejected by `valid_action_targets` and by `cast`;
- a game test that casts and resolves Leeching Bite on two creatures;
- the AI picks two different creatures;
- the real cards from the database.

Checks run: the related debuff and exchange modules, planeswalker and loyalty test modules, lint, and `scripts/fast_check.py` (PASS, run through `heavy`).

author: conahmorgan2304
body:
## Purpose
Address all seven reliability and intelligence-consistency improvements without a second service or changed autonomous permissions.

## Changes
1. Guarded API: preserve selected existing read-only investigation tools while keeping scripts/scenes and arbitrary actions restricted.
2. Reliability: classify unrecognised successful tool results as unverified rather than incorrectly treating them as confirmed or failed.
3. Voice deduplication: only collapse likely relays with compatible room/device scope.
4. Evidence checks: unrelated or unavailable tool results cannot satisfy historical evidence requirements.
5. Focused tools: fall back to the complete tool set for cross-domain investigations.
6. Optional unified evidence tool (setting off by default): reuse timeline, ledger, camera records, root-cause and bounded authorised Recorder queries. Raw system logs are deliberately excluded.
7. Expand dynamic read-only heating/energy questions, plus offline deterministic multi-step planning benchmark with partial failure cases.

## Validation
Earlier HACS and Hassfest checks passed; an earlier full test run had 2,228 passes and one focus-test failure corrected in later commits.
Full pytest and other checks on the latest head remain required before the draft is ready.
Live physical device, microphone, Frigate and Home Assistant testing remains necessary.

## Review priorities
- Existing historical tools must enforce exposure, guest privacy and per-user read permissions.
- External tool results cannot be treated as physically verified changes.
- Voice relay matching remains heuristic until a durable request identifier is available.
- Evidence is not proof of identity or causation.

body:
## Intent

Captain's request: "the Overview should be a metrics area or showing what research is still being done". Overview is the app's HOME page: the default view and the target of the logo/brand link; existing routes and deep links (#Home and #Research open Research, #Overview, #Overview/example/<kind>/<id>) must keep working. Layout top to bottom, calm and aligned, no big hero copy: (1) a compact one-line question box that starts research and hands off to the Research thread (keeps #25's behaviour: the answer becomes Research's conversation; Deep and an engine without direct answers use the existing setAsk hand-off; refusals shown inline); (2) research in progress: every running answer, team review and benchmark run with question, agents taking part, current step, elapsed time, spend so far vs its cap, live updates (polling plus each run's event stream, capped at a few streams) and click-through to Research/Team review/Compare and the Agent Log; (3) metrics from REAL recorded data only, never invented: done/running/failed counts (failed stays), today's spend vs the /api/paid daily cap, recent (7-day) recorded spend, the per-run cap and Exa ceiling, average time and cost per answer, sources searched/kept/cited, checks passed/failed/not checked; empty states say "No data"/"Not recorded"; research and practice (scripted/Demo) are never mixed (a Research/Practice switch); examples are never counted; (4) recent research; (5) a compact Agent Lab showing one running run (or the example from the deep link).

Deliberate decisions: the app no longer restores the last-used view from localStorage — it opens on Overview unless the hash names a view (home-page requirement). The Hero ("Let's research together!", starter questions) is removed from the Overview; Research keeps Try asking. Credits.tsx is intentionally left in place but unused by Overview, because the parallel branch fm/ui-layout-review moves it to Settings; avoid conflicting with that lane. Benchmark (swarm) runs show spend as "Not recorded" because the engine records no dollars for them. To feed the page, the engine list replies gained fields (additive only, no answer/source text): GET /api/research?all=1 via shortLine in engine/src/research/store.ts (effort, workStartedAt, seconds, maxUsd, running step, agents, searches, sources kept/cited, checks by verdict), and GET /api/runs via engine/src/board/listline.ts boardExtras (usd, mock, members, checks by verdict) with a one-line spread in shared engine/src/app.ts; board.ts summarize was left untouched. Use shadcn components/design tokens; tests use fakes only; no paid calls. README and docs/status.md updated; docs/images/overview.png replaced with a Demo-mode screenshot labelled as practice.

## What Changed

- The Overview is now the home page. It shows a one-line question box that hands off to Research, then every running answer, team review and benchmark run with live updates. After that come metrics taken only from recorded data, with a Research/Practice switch: counts, spend against the caps, average time and cost, sources, and checks. Recent research and a compact Agent Lab come last. The Hero and its starter questions are removed. The app no longer reopens the last view saved in localStorage. ✅ Low: The change adds a dashboard page and a few extra fields to read-only engine list replies, with no answer or source text. The last fix round (the restored status row and the removed unused prop) is correct, and only a stale screenshot remains.

## Testing

I ran the real engine and dashboard on separate ports, isolated from the operator's engine and data, with paid calls off and locked. Using headless Chrome, I drove the Overview home page end to end and captured screenshots for each scenario. The page opens by default and from the logo link, and the old deep links still work. Scripted benchmark, team-review and answer runs appear in In progress with live time and spend against their caps, and their links open Compare, the Agent Log and Research. author: kcco543
body:
Stacked on the gifts PR (`claude/project-thread-7c059h`).

## What changes for players
- Relationships grow slowly and believably. Twenty friendly chats between strangers make them acquaintances, not friends. Friendship, deep trust and admiration need real milestones (help in a hard moment, kept promises, shared experiences, respected boundaries).
- Characters keep **hard** and **soft** boundaries, edited in Character Studio. Asking again never wears them down: the answer gets firmer, then they change the subject or say they're uncomfortable, then they end the conversation. Pushing costs trust.
- Trust is not obedience. A close friend still disagrees with an opinion against their values, and a disliked rival with a good argument earns agreement and respect, not affection.
- Mood & bonds tab shows how the character sees each other person (label, stages, meters, clearest impression).

## How it's enforced (code, not prompts)
- New `src/lib/relationships/`: one validated writer (`recordInteraction`) for every source (AI talk, built-in topics, behavior engine, story events, gifts, photos). Significance scoring, per-axis and total caps, repetition and lifetime diminishing returns, stage ladders with hysteresis and milestone doors, impressions backed by evidence, conflicts and promises. All numbers in `config.ts`.
- `decideRequest()` runs the 8-step decision before any reply. The AI must return a stance the game allowed; otherwise the reply is rejected and a built-in line is used. AI relationship numbers are proposals, taken only when colder than the rule.
- Emotions stay a separate layer and never write long-term values.

## Developer tools
- Relationship Inspector (Settings, developers only): values, stages, what the next stage needs, impressions, milestones, refused requests and every validated change with reasons; seeded scenarios and a 20-interaction simulation.

## Saves
Additive optional fields only (`story.progress`, `Character.boundaries`, `Relation.dependence`); old worlds load as-is with stages read from current values. Also fixes conversation history and relationship log being dropped on reload.

## Checks
- `npm test`: 366 passed (new `tests/relationships.test.ts` runs all 16 scenarios on 5 seeds in English and Chinese, the 20-step simulation, repeated refusals at several trust levels, AI rejection rules, hysteresis)
- typecheck, lint, build: clean
- Played in the browser with test replies: repeated sensitive question → refuse, refuse firmly, change subject, conversation ended (desktop English and iPhone Chinese)

Docs: `docs/RELATIONSHIPS.md`.
