author: namastex888
body:
Chat backfills always attempt media downloads, including media inside WhatsApp envelopes, with no request option to disable them. Cancellation stops the round driver while pending media callbacks drain; those callbacks cannot store messages after cancellation. Progress counts downloaded and missing files once per file, and reruns can repair missing media paths on existing rows. Missing media remains identifiable by the stored media row and coverage's mediaMissing count.

Old media WhatsApp no longer serves stays missing. Backfill does not call updateMediaMessage: that helper emits a live messages.update event and waits without a timeout. Normal download failures are counted without introducing live message events.

Stacked on O3 (#1763); O5 follows this PR. Do not merge independently.

Validation: all required static gates pass; 16 targeted round/worker/media tests and 15 direct core guards pass. Full unit suite passes outside four sandbox CLI teardown failures caused by ps EPERM. Host full-suite and PostgreSQL gates remain pending; O1 coverage is integrated through O3.

body:
## Summary

Lets the owner allow specific people to DM the bot even though they share no admitted group with it, granted the same way as trusted group invitations: owner-only, confirmed, audited and revocable.

- `/admin dmgrant tg:ID [DURATION]`, `/admin dmrevoke tg:ID`, `/admin dmgrants`: owner-only, owner-DM-only, through the existing PendingAction flow (requester-bound, single use, revision-checked). The optional expiry can be 1m to 365d and is re-validated under the lock at commit.
- `manage_dm_access`: an owner-only natural-language batch of up to 20 people in the existing invitation-management skill. It accepts known names, plus explicit `tg:` IDs the owner typed, which the preview shows as `unknown name [tg:…]`. Nothing is written until the owner confirms.
- Additive core migration **`0013_owner_dm_grants.sql`**. `AccessSnapshot.dm_grants` defaults to empty.
- Optional `BotApp(dm_request_notice=False)`. When on, a denied DM gets one fixed reply with the sender's ID, at most once per user per 24h and 30 per hour bot-wide, with no model call, message logging or plugin hooks.
- **Neutral by default:** with no grants and the notice off, access behaves as before.

Plan: [docs/plans/2026-11-16-owner-dm-grants.md](docs/plans/2026-11-16-owner-dm-grants.md), approved by the owner on 2026-11-16. Execution brief: [docs/plans/2026-11-16-owner-dm-grants-execution.md](docs/plans/2026-11-16-owner-dm-grants-execution.md).

## ⚠️ Permission change (maintenance review)

- `AccessPolicy.can_dm` now also allows users with an active owner grant (last clause). A grant gives them the same DM features a group member gets, which is the owner's decision. It gives no group admission, setup, moderation, admin or invite rights, and `member_groups` stays empty. A global block or pause still wins.
- `administration/gates.py` adds the `manage_dm_access` owner-DM gate. `permissions.py` is reused unchanged.
- Protected files touched: core, the core migration, and `administration/__init__.py` (exports `DmGrant`).

## Interactions and limits

- Bridge transport: the protected bridge's independent relay allowlist is unchanged, so grants take effect only where the transport actually delivers the DM. Check which transport each downstream bot uses.
- Grantee usage counts toward the shared daily budget, and every per-user and plugin cap still applies.
- **Known pre-existing limit (follow-up, not changed here):** for any globally blocked or paused DM user, the app logs the message and runs plugin `on_message` hooks before it sends the restriction notice. The responder is never called. Grantees inherit this ordering.

## Execution and review

Codex (`gpt-6-luna`) executed. Codex (`gpt-6.1-sol`) reviewed twice, with two fix rounds:
- Round 1: memory-store audit atomicity, identity spoofing in the preview through display names, commit-time expiry checks, notice lock order, and much fuller app-path tests.
- Round 2: hollow target-rejection tests (tests only).

Claude did the final review.

Karakeep's chrome container image moves from `gcr.io/zenika-hub/alpine-chrome:124` to `docker.io/zenika/alpine-chrome:124`.

`gcr.io/zenika-hub` is unpullable: its token endpoint returns `DENIED: This API method requires billing to be enabled`. The Scan Containers (Trivy) CI job fails on any PR touching karakeep's helmrelease, and any node without the image cached would hit ImagePullBackOff. The live pod only works off its cached copy on k8s-0.

Default namespace, karakeep chrome pod only; it restarts on reconcile. No storage, networking or RBAC changes. The Docker Hub tag is multi-arch (amd64+arm64), last pushed 2026-09-03 (sha256:eb3378c1ed...), and differs from the cached gcr digest (sha256:1a0046448e...), so the pod pulls a newer build of the same Chromium 124 tag.

author: rubentxu
body:
## Qué cambia

La deuda OpenAPI que HSP-129 dejó sin ejecución, cerrada: el contrato modular valida limpio y su validación vive en la puerta local, con gate de deriva.

### El contrato (17 errores + 14 avisos → 0 + 0)

Baseline medido con el validador real (`npx @redocly/cli lint`) antes de tocar nada:

- `webhooks:` en un spec **3.0.3** (llegaron en 3.1) → fuera, con su fichero huérfano.
- 13 referencias internas rotas en `users.yaml` y `policies.yaml` (`'#/components/...'` se resuelve contra el propio fichero en un contrato modular) → refs de fichero relativas. La clave del 500 es `InternalError`, que es como la llama el fichero de respuestas.
- `components/schemas/policies.yaml` **vacío (0 bytes)** mientras el contrato declaraba `POST /v1/policies` → escrito con `CreatePolicyCommand`/`CreatePolicyResponse`, la superficie que el contrato ya declaraba.
- `/simple/{packageName}/` con slash final (PEP 503 lo pide en la URL; un path template no puede llevarlo).
- 11 `operationId` ausentes (maven, npm, pypi, auth); el GET de lista sin respuesta 4xx; y el patrón del tarball npm exigía una barra invertida literal (`'\\.tgz'` en YAML simple cita dos backslashes) — su propio ejemplo no lo cumplía.
- `redocly.yaml` versionado con la única excepción escrita y con motivo: el server de desarrollo es documentación intencional.

### El gate (AC#2 y #3)

`scripts/check-openapi.sh` + etapa `contract (openapi)` en `pipeline.kts`: lint con las reglas de `redocly.yaml`, bundle, y **deriva** contra `docs/openapi/bundled.yaml` versionado — el gate que el workflow muerto prometía y nunca tuvo (su script no existía).

### La publicación (AC#4), decidida y escrita

La publicación **no vive en la CI**: la CI es local y no publica nada. El entregable es `bundled.yaml`, versionado y en sincronía por el gate; publicarlo fuera (explorador, portal) es decisión de la persona por el canal que se decida. Escrito en `docs/openapi/README.md` y en la tarea.

## Evidencia medida

- Baseline RED: 17 errores + 14 avisos. GREEN: `Woohoo! Your API description is valid` — 0 y 0.
- **Negativos discriminantes del script**: ref rota reintroducida → exit 1 nombrando el sitio; bundle alterado → exit 3 con el diff.
- **Negativo discriminante de la pipeline**: bundle alterado → falla **exactamente** en `contract-openapi/sh-0` con el mensaje de deriva, exit 1.
- **PipelineK completa** → exit 0, 19/19 pasos.
- Suite completa del workspace → **1593 pasados, 0 fallidos**. `ci_suites` 11/11.

Fixes #96

author: chitik1011-tech
body:
## Scope

Extends the poll foundation merged by #91. This PR does **not** replace or duplicate the existing poll model/state.

## End-to-end flow

- Telegram poll media/results -> existing `PollSummary` / `PollOption`
- `updateMessagePoll` -> `CoreEvent::PollUpdated` -> persisted `CoreState`
- Android -> existing JSON/JNI command bridge -> `CoreCommand::VotePoll`
- `CoreCommand::VotePoll` -> `messages.sendVote`
- server update -> `PollUpdated` -> Android Compose

## Telegram protocol support

- regular polls
- public/anonymous via `public_voters`
- single choice
- multiple choice
- quiz
- closed polls
- question/options
- per-option voter counts
- total voters
- current user's chosen option(s)
- quiz correct option when Telegram reveals it
- quiz solution/explanation when Telegram reveals it
- opaque Telegram option bytes preserved for `messages.sendVote`

Polls are mapped both from message history/media and from live `UpdateMessagePoll` updates.

A small bounded protocol-side registry exists only to resolve partial `UpdateMessagePoll` updates that omit peer/message identity. `CoreState` remains the canonical application state.

## Voting behavior

`CoreCommand::VotePoll { poll_id, chat_id, message_id, option_ids }` uses the existing poll/message/chat identity.

Validation covers:
- unknown poll
- mismatched poll/message/chat identity
- closed poll
- empty selection
- duplicate option id
- unknown option id
- single-choice with multiple selections
- missing legacy Telegram option bytes

Successful RPC emits a transient `poll_vote_submitted`, but Android keeps the loading state until an authoritative `PollUpdated` arrives. RPC/validation failure emits poll-correlated `poll_vote_failed` and preserves the last server-confirmed poll snapshot.

## Android

Poll UI is embedded in the existing message bubble and renders:
- question and options
- radio controls for single choice
- checkboxes + submit button for multiple choice
- voter counts and percentages when results are available
- total voters
- current user's selected answer(s)
- quiz correct/wrong marking when known
- closed state
- quiz explanation when known
- loading and poll-local error state

The Android state parser consumes the existing Rust `CoreState.polls`; no fake/local production poll model is used.

## Tests

Added deterministic coverage for:
- Telegram poll/result mapping
- regular / multiple-choice / closed / quiz mapping
- duplicate partial update stability
- vote validation for single/multiple choice
- invalid option / closed poll
- legacy poll JSON compatibility
- `vote_poll` serde round-trip
- JNI command decode round-trip
- vote RPC failure preserving server-confirmed poll state
- Android poll percentage presentation

Existing #91 reducer/persistence/delete-with-message coverage remains in place.

## Coordination / overlap

body:
Updates and "Program Finished" alerts could silently stop until Homebridge was restarted. This makes the plugin recover on its own and log when it can't.

## Changes
- **Token refresh:** `Session` now records expiry (it never did), so tokens refresh a minute before they expire instead of only after LG rejects a request. A refresh reply without an access token throws instead of storing an empty token, which used to leave the plugin unable to reach LG at all. Concurrent requests share one refresh; with username/password, a failed refresh signs in again.
- **Startup:** login and device discovery retry with backoff (30s up to 10 min) instead of giving up after an LG or network outage; a retried discovery doesn't wire accessories twice.
- **MQTT:** startup retries with backoff (5s up to 5 min) instead of giving up after 5 tries, and no longer blocks ThinQ1 polling. A watchdog reconnects MQTT when 3 polls in a row see device changes MQTT never delivered (at most every 30 min).
- **Logging:** failed polls and token refreshes are warnings/errors (once per outage, with a recovery message) instead of debug-only. `getListDevices` throws on failure instead of reporting an empty account.
- Version 2.2.6, CHANGELOG, README note on the backup poll.

## Testing
- `npm run check`: lint (0 errors), build, 115 tests (16 new: token refresh, watchdog, backoff, startup retry, forced reconnect), coverage thresholds met.
- Running on a live Homebridge since 14:14: connects to the ThinQ API and MQTT, sets up all devices, and reads current state for the washer, dryer, dishwasher and oven.

body:
**Stacked on PR 50 (History, `feat/m3-history`)**: this branch starts at its head 1f85d99 and adds its own commits on top; review those (`git log 1f85d99..feat/m3-pets`). Merge PR 50 first; this one then shows only its own changes.

## What

SPEC.md §5.5.

- **Pets list** (Home's "See all"): each pet with its avatar, weight, today's visits (counted from the day's cards as Home counts them, so live updates move both alike) and how it is recognised; a card opens the pet.
- **Pet page** (Home's pet chip, a list card):
  - switcher to the other pets at the top, in place (the chosen pet survives recreation);
  - avatar from `GET /pets/{id}/photo` through the app's Coil loader on its OkHttp client (bearer in the header only), over the pet's initial on its colour;
  - name and how it is recognised: "face and weight" when the server has reference photos (it serves a photo only then), "weight" otherwise, and the reference weight, learned from visits or entered in petkit-local;
  - tiles: weight (the server's `median_weight_g`, median of the last weighed visits), visits today (the server's count, shown only if it was read today: another day's count is no count), last visit (time, day, device);
  - weight chart, 30 days / 6 months;
  - recent visits (`recent_visits`, up to 20 of the last 7 days; 6 shown), each opening History narrowed to the pet **on that visit's day**; "See all in History" opens it on today.
  - A visit of the pet landing in the day's cards over `/ws` reads its statistics again.
- History: `HistoryDestination` gains an optional `day`; History opens on it, in the strip its arrows would reach it in.

## Design choices

- **Weight series source.** The API serves no weight series: `/pets/{id}` has only the median and 7 days of visits. The chart therefore reads the pet's visits from `GET /timeline?pet={id}&kind=toileting&limit=100`, page after page (no `day`: the cursor walks back through all history) until the start of the range, at most 24 pages (2,400 visits). Weighed visits (`kind == visit`, `weight_g` set, that pet) go into their own Room table (`pet_weights`) and replace the cached ones over the time the pages covered (ADR 0002). Nothing is invented: a bucket without a weighed visit has no point, the line joins only adjacent buckets, and a caption says what a point is ("the median of a day's / a week's weighed visits") and, when the data starts later than the range, "No weighed visit before 9 November". The server only serves what its event retention keeps, so the chart cannot tell a pruned history from a pet that did not visit; it says neither.
- **Chart.** Compose Canvas in feature:pets (`WeightChart.kt`), in the style of `DayScatterChart` (dashed guides, ringed dots, muted axis labels) but a line chart: x is the range's buckets (30 days, or 26 weeks ending today), y kilograms rounded out to 100 g with at least 400 g of span so a steady weight draws a flat line; TalkBack reads the number of points and the lightest and heaviest.
- **Cache.** Schema 4 (`PetkitDatabase.VERSION` and `OLDEST_SUPPORTED_VERSION` raised, only 4.json exported, no migration): `pet_activity` (stats, recent visits as the server sent them, when they were read) and `pet_weights`. A pet the server answers `pet_not_found` for leaves the cache with everything held of it; a refreshed list drops what it held of pets it no longer has.
- Home: a pet chip now opens that pet (it opened the placeholder list), "See all" opens the list. The pet avatar is a copy of Home's in feature:pets: moving it to core:ui needs Coil there, which resolves older transitive `.module` files strict verification has no entries for.
- At 130 % font the last-visit tile takes a row of its own rather than breaking "Aujourd'hui" mid-word.

## How to run

`cd mock-server && ./gradlew run --args="--port=<port>"`, sign in at `http://10.0.2.2:<port>` (password `demo`), Home → a pet chip, or "See all".

## Tests

All run locally on the last commit (2d0c48f), JDK 25 (JBR), strict dependency verification:

- `./gradlew assembleDebug assembleRelease check :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Host tests: 1,135 run, 0 failures (20 skipped, as before). Goldens: the 24 new pet ones recorded (`feature/pets/src/test/screenshots`: content light/dark x EN/FR at 100 % and 130 %, six months, never weighed, unreachable, list), then every module's goldens verified by `check` (Home and History unchanged).
- New tests: `PetRulesTest` (7: median, day/week buckets, gaps, local days across the zone, stale "today", page, visit ids), `PetRepositoryTest` (7, MockWebServer + Room: stats cached with their read time, list order kept, `pet_not_found` drops everything, failed read keeps the cache, weights follow the cursor and stop at the range start, removed visits drop, failed page keeps weights), `PetDaoTest` (4), `PetViewModelTest` (8), `PetsViewModelTest` (2), `PetScreenTest` (9, Compose UI), `HistoryRulesTest` +1 and `HistoryViewModelTest` +2 (the day argument), `HomeScreenTest` updated (a chip opens its pet).
- `:app:pixel6Api37DebugAndroidTest` against my own mock (port 18297): 20 tests, 0 failures, including the new `PetsFlowTest` (2).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` on the release APK (headless API 37 emulator): passed.
- Looked at on the emulator against the mock: EN light (pet page, recent visit opening History on Mochi and that day), FR dark (pet page live-updated by a new visit, Tigrou in 6 months, the list).

## Unverified

- The 6-month chart against a real petkit-local: the mock seeds 7 days, so on it the chart shows one week (and says "No weighed visit before ..."). Paging back six months of a real household's timeline (up to 24 pages of 100) was tested only with scripted pages; how long it takes on a large server is not measured.
- Whether a real server still has six months of events depends on its event retention; the chart cannot tell a pruned history from a pet that did not visit, and says neither.
- "Recognition: face and weight" is inferred from the server serving a photo (it does only when the pet has reference faces); whether a given litter box actually matches by face is not in the API.
- API 29 managed device not run (nightly in CI).
- Seen in passing, not touched (PR 50's): History's time column wraps "10:20 AM" as "10:20 A / M" on the emulator.

Closes #20

author: shaunpatterson
body:
Fixes #12049.

### Problem

`RDFImporterFormat.load()` read N-Triples as delimited text (univocity CSV parser, the terms as cells) and keyed the subject and object vertices by the cell text. That changed or corrupted literal objects with `result: OK`:

1. the empty literal `""` was an empty cell, skipped, so the terminator `.` became the object;
2. a plain literal lost its quotes, so `"http://ex.org/o1"` became the same vertex as `<http://ex.org/o1>`;
3. a tagged or typed literal kept its quotes and suffix, so the same string was stored two ways;
4. no N-Triples escape was decoded (`\u00E9`, `\n`).

And an import into a database without the `Node` type failed with `Type with name 'Node' was not found`.

### Change

- Each line is read as one N-Triples statement by a small term reader (`NTriplesStatement`) instead of the CSV parser. With a space or tab delimiter (canonical N-Triples) terms are separated by runs of whitespace (#8159); with any other delimiter (a comma-separated triple file, or `-delimiter` set by the user) by that delimiter, whitespace around it ignored, so an explicit delimiter still overrides the detected one (#7315). A delimiter of more than one character (`;;`) separates terms whole. Blank lines and `#` comment lines are skipped as before; what follows the third term (the `.`, or an N-Quads graph) is ignored as before. A blank-node label ends before a final `.` (`_:b1.` is `_:b1` and the terminator), a `.` inside it is kept.
- `maxPropertySize` bounds a term as it bounded a cell, with the same default (4,096, univocity's `maxCharsPerColumn`): the row is refused with an `ImportException` (it was univocity's `TextParsingException`), so `-onRowError skip` now reaches it. Lines are read keeping at most `4 * maxPropertySize + 4096` characters (four terms, an N-Quads graph being the fourth, plus room for separators): a longer line is counted, not kept, and refused as a row error. [INFERENCE] A legal line can exceed that only with more than 4,096 characters of whitespace or a trailing comment that long.
- Identity (the key property, `id` by default, which `newEdgeByKeys` looks terms up by): an IRI is its text with `\u`/`\U` escapes decoded (as before, without `<>`); a blank node is its label (`_:b1`, as before); a literal is its canonical N-Triples form: lexical form decoded and re-escaped the canonical way (only `"`, `\`, LF, CR), between quotes, then its language tag or `^^<datatype>` (`xsd:string` left out, so `"a"` and `"a"^^xsd:string` are one vertex). A literal can no longer be the vertex of an IRI.
- Value (what a user reads): the vertex of a literal object also carries `value`, its lexical form with the escapes decoded and no quotes (`hello world`, `café` + LF + `line2`, `say "hi"`, the empty string), plus `lang` for a tagged literal and `datatype` for a typed one. They are written when the literal's vertex is created; a property named like the key property is never written over it. IRI and blank-node vertices are unchanged.
- **Behaviour change:** the key of a plain literal object now has its quotes (`"hello world"`, was `hello world`), the form tagged and typed literals already had; its unquoted text is in `value`. The key has to tell a literal from an IRI because the key property carries a unique index (the importer's own tests and `ensureVertexType` create one), so a literal and an IRI with the same text cannot share it.
- `load()` creates the vertex type with its key property (STRING) and a unique index when the database does not have it; an existing type is left as it is.
- `CSVImporterFormat.delimiterFor()` becomes `protected` so the RDF format reads the same resolved delimiter.

### Tests

`RDFImporterFormatStatementBoundariesTest`: a blank-node label before the terminator and with an inner `.`, a `;;` delimiter, an overlong line refused (and skipped under `-onRowError skip`), the reader keeping no more than the line limit of a 1,000,000-character line, and a 5,000-character term refused under the default limit.

`Issue12049RdfLiteralTermsTest` imports into an empty database (no `Node` type) a file with an IRI object, a literal spelling the same IRI, plain, `xsd:string`, tagged and typed literals, `\u` and `\n` escapes, an escaped quote, the empty literal, a blank-node subject, an escaped IRI, a comment line and a blank line, and checks every object key and the `value`, `lang` and `datatype` of every literal object. Without the fix it fails on the missing type. `RDFImporterFormatTransactionLeakTest` and `RDFImporterFormatCommitCadenceTest` force a failing row with `maxPropertySize`: they now expect `ImportException` instead of `TextParsingException`, and `eachSourceRowIsCountedExactlyOnce` counts the refused seventh row as read (7, was 6: the CSV parser threw before the row reached the loop). The other RDF tests (`Issue7345`, `Issue7346`, `Issue7347`, `Issue7482`, `Issue7487`, `Issue7488`, `Issue7891`, `RDFImporterFormatDelimiterDetectionTest`, `ImporterRefusedCommitTest`) and the rest of the integration importer test package pass unchanged.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * RDF imports now parse N-Triples statements, including IRIs, blank nodes, and plain, language-tagged, or typed literals.
  * Literal values, language tags, and datatypes are stored separately. Equivalent plain and `xsd:string` literals share an identity, while literals remain distinct from IRIs with the same text.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Blank lines and comments are skipped, and malformed or oversized terms are rejected with an import error.

body:
## Summary

Implements #568: the two Monte Carlo runners still carried the last duplicated
batch-helper pair — `batch_measurements()` and `build_batch_groups()`. This PR
collapses them into one shared helper, `batch_sim.build_mc_batch_groups()`,
placed beside `build_mc_group` as the issue's step 1 specified, with the
per-bench parts injected as parameters:

- `netlist_for(point)` returns that point's complete pre-`.lib` netlist text,
  which absorbs the one legitimate divergence (amp-offset hoists one netlist
  because it does not vary per point; untrimmed builds `batch_netlist(p, body)`
  per point because the `config` axis rides in as `.param` overrides).
- `measurements` is the bench's `[{"name", "expr"}]` list, absorbing
  `batch_measurements()` outright (the symbol no longer exists anywhere — the
  per-bench part was the `VECTOR_EXPRS` constant, not the code).
- `max_concurrent_jobs` / `resume` are forwarded unconditionally via
  `getattr(args, …)`; per the issue's traced defaults they reproduce today's
  values for benches whose argparse lacks the flags, so amp-offset's
  `request.json` is unchanged (verified, not assumed — see Test Plan).

Each runner keeps a thin `build_batch_groups(pin, body, points, spiceinit_text,
out_dir, args)` wrapper with today's exact signature, so the #536 shared
fixture (`sim/tests/mc_batch_shared.py`) and both bench test files are the
regression test for this refactor and needed **no edits**. The #528
timeout-refusal paragraph now appears once, in the shared helper; the refusal
still surfaces as each bench's own `HarnessError` (the wrapper does the
`BatchError` translation, matching `batch_sim`'s existing convention of leaving
the harness error type to the caller).

**Deviation from the issue's step-1 signature sketch**: `supply_v` is an extra
positional parameter (`build_mc_batch_groups(pin, supply_v, points, …)`).
`build_mc_group` requires it, both benches pass their own `SUPPLY_V`, and
`batch_sim` is bench-independent so it cannot be hardcoded. Everything else in
the sketch is as written.

## Changes

- `sim/bin/batch_sim.py` — new `build_mc_batch_groups()` (one request per
  Monte Carlo point; merged docstring incl. the once-written #528 refusal
  paragraph; unconditional flag forwarding).
- `sim/error-amp-offset-mc/run_amp_offset_mc.py` — `batch_measurements()`

body:
## Problem

In `auto` mode with the git store, a change's pull request should merge itself once tests pass, but only if it changes nothing but valid content. The site trial does this for one site only.

## Solution

- `.github/workflows/content-merge.yml` (`workflow_call`): a site calls it from `workflow_run` after `ci`. It runs from the site's default branch and never checks out the PR; it reads the PR through the API.
- `src/merge/decide.ts` (pure) and `src/merge/cli.ts`: squash-merge the tested commit only if every changed file is under `content/` and is the texts file or an item of a declared list, every value passes the site's declaration again, list sizes fit, and the `test` check passed. Otherwise label `status:needs-human-review` and comment why. `review` mode does nothing.
- README: the few lines a site adds.
- `content-merge-selftest.yml`: manual run of the workflow on this repo, for a test PR.
- `dist/` rebuilt.

## Validation

- Unit tests (ported from the site's, adapted to content files): decisions, script with a fake `gh`, workflow properties. `npm run check`, build and 285 unit tests pass.
- Browser tests not run locally: Playwright browsers cannot be downloaded here. CI runs them.
- Test-PR run: see the comment below.
- Deploy risk: low (no site changes until a site calls it; no release or version bump).

Closes #11

author: slashnephy
body:
## 概要

保存先プールのディレクトリに置いた TS（`.ts`、`.m2ts`）を、録画として取り込む `kotatsu import files プールID:ディレクトリ` を足します。#1734 の検討の案 A のうち、決めてもらう事柄に触れない範囲です。

- 番組名、局、放送時刻は、ファイルの頭と終わりにある PAT、PMT、SDT、EIT[p/f]、TOT から読みます。
- Kotatsu にない局のファイルは取り込まず、理由を出します（`recordings.service_id` は必須のままです）。
- Blu-ray（BDAV）の 192 バイトの `.m2ts` は見分けて断ります。

## 変更

- `kotatsu import files POOL:DIR`（`--dry-run`、`--user`、`--min-age`。最後に書いてから 10 分たっていないファイルは、書いている途中かもしれないので飛ばします）
  - プールの外を指すディレクトリは拒みます。
  - 録った範囲は、頭で最初に読んだ TOT から、終わりで最後に読んだ TOT までにします。
  - 番組は、頭と終わりの EIT[p/f] の放送中と次の番組のうち、録った範囲に最も長く重なるものにします。録画はマージンを取って始まるので、頭で放送中の番組は前の番組であることが多いためです。
  - EIT が読めなければファイル名を番組名にします。TOT も読めなければ、ファイルの更新日時を使います。
  - 取り込んだことは `import_sources`（取り込み元は `files`）に記録します。ID は、プール、パス、大きさ、更新日時から作ります。もう録画のファイルとして記録されているファイル（Kotatsu が録った録画など）も取り込みません。
  - 取り込んだら、EPGStation から取り込んだときと同じく、解析のジョブ（索引、ドロップの集計、画像）を入れます。監査ログには `recording.imported` を残します。アニメの作品との結びつきも、EPGStation から取り込んだ録画と同じく対象にします。
- `recording_files.external` を足しました（マイグレーションあり。既定値は false）。取り込んだファイルには、この印を付けます。
  - 録画を消しても、ファイルは残します。索引や画像などの生成物は消します。
  - 容量の管理では、ほかにファイルを持たない取り込んだ録画を、消す対象にしません。
  - ファイル名の付け直しの対象にもしません。
- `lib/ts`: EIT[p/f] の番組の開始と長さを読む `Analyzer.EventTime` を足しました。TOT と同じ時刻の読み方を、1 つの関数にまとめました。
- 設計書: 6.5 を足し、2 章、4.7、5.6、6.1、付録 A を直しました。`docs/setup.md` にも使い方を書きました。

## 確かめたこと

- `golangci-lint run ./...` は 0 件でした。次のテストは通りました（DB は開発用の PostgreSQL）。
  - `lib/ts`、`usecase/fileimport`、`library`、`capacity`、`cli`、`epgstation`、`analysis`、`recording`、`segjoin`、`transcode`、`web/graph`、`infra/database`
  - 足したテストは、頭の読み取り（`test.ts`）、BDAV と TS でないファイルの拒否、番組の選び方、Kotatsu にない局の飛ばし、二重に取り込まないこと、dry run で何も書かないこと、プールの外の拒否、消しても external のファイルが残ること、容量の管理と付け直しの対象外です。
- 開発用のスタックで、ビルドしたバイナリを動かして確かめました（コンテナの中で実行）。プールに一時ディレクトリ `tmp-1734/` を作り、次の 3 つを置きました。
  - 開発用のプールにあった短い録画の写し
  - `test.ts` の SDT の original_network_id を書き換えた、Kotatsu にない局の TS
  - `test.ts` を 192 バイトにした BDAV

置いた直後の dry run です。すべて飛ばしました。

```
$ kotatsu import files main:tmp-1734 --dry-run
Would import             0
Skipped                  3
  tmp-1734/bluray.m2ts      modified within the last 10m0s; it may still be being written
  （ほか 2 つも同じ）
```

更新日時を 1 時間前にしてから、dry run、取り込み、もう一度の取り込みを実行しました。DB の件数は、dry run の前後で変わりませんでした。

```
$ kotatsu import files main:tmp-1734 --dry-run
Would import             1
Skipped                  2
  tmp-1734/drama-copy.m2ts     ＮＨＫ総合１・東京  2026-11-09T23:45:00+09:00  ドラマ１０「会社員」毎週火曜夜１０時、放送中！🈑
  tmp-1734/bluray.m2ts         the file is a 192-byte-packet BDAV stream (Blu-ray .m2ts); only 188-byte-packet TS is supported
  tmp-1734/unknown-service.ts  the service is not in Kotatsu (network 32752, service 1024 "こたつテスト１")
 recordings | files | sources | analyze_jobs | audits
          5 |     5 |       0 |            5 |      0      ← dry run の後も変わらない

$ kotatsu import files main:tmp-1734 --user admin
Imported                 1   （同じ 1 件）
 recordings | files | sources | analyze_jobs | audits
          6 |     6 |       1 |            6 |      1

$ kotatsu import files main:tmp-1734 --user admin   （2 回目）
Imported                 0
Already imported         1
```

- 番組は、頭で放送中だった前の番組ではありませんでした。録った範囲（23:44:49〜23:47:14）に最も長く重なる 23:45 の番組を選びました。
- `recording_analyze` と `thumbnail_generate` のジョブは終わりました。
- 画面で、録画の詳細と再生を確かめました。録画した時刻、画質の情報、代表画像が出ます。再生では、終わりの近くへシークでき（2:22 / 2:25）、字幕と実況の過去ログも時刻に合って出ました（放送の映像と実況の書き込みはぼかしています）。

![録画の詳細](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/169d685f-c4c5-4d1f-8989-2fcf62966e92)
![再生して終わりの近くへシークしたところ](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f157bd1e-c8e0-41a0-a4e5-ceee094c9959)

- 画面から録画を消しても、`tmp-1734/drama-copy.m2ts` はプールに残りました。監査ログには `recording.imported` と `recording.deleted` が残りました。もう一度 dry run すると `Already imported 1` で、取り込み直しませんでした。
- 確かめた後に、一時ディレクトリと、取り込みの記録（`import_sources` の行）を消しました。

## 確かめていないこと

- 生成物（データディレクトリの索引と画像）が、消したときに消えることは、テストでだけ確かめました。開発用のスタックでは確かめていません。
- 頭が 32 MiB を超える実際のファイルで、終わりの EIT と頭の EIT が食い違う場合は、テストの合成ファイルでだけ確かめました。
- SDT のない TS（サービス ID だけで引く場合）は、テストを書いていません。

## 残り（決めてもらう事柄）

- 画面から取り込む方法（案 B。保存先の画面での一覧と、見回りのジョブ）
- Kotatsu にない局の録画を取り込むか（`recordings.service_id` を任意にする変更が要ります）
- Blu-ray（BDAV）の 192 バイトの `.m2ts` を対象にするか
- 取り込んだ録画を消すときに、ファイルも消す選択肢を画面に出すか（今は常に残します）

Refs #1734

# 📋 Portfolio Obrigatório - Feature

## 📝 Descrição

Esta PR implementa a funcionalidade de **portfólio opcional** para prestadores de serviços no Procuro Quem Faça.

### Problema
Atualmente, fotos no portfólio são obrigatórias no início e fim de todos os serviços. Porém, alguns tipos de serviço (como massagem, quiropraxia) valorizam mais as **avaliações** do que o portfólio visual.

### Solução
Permitir que cada prestador **ative/desative** a obrigatoriedade de fotos de forma global, com:
- ✅ **Aceite do cliente** sempre obrigatório no início e fim
- ⚡ **Fotos** opcionais se desativado pelo prestador
- 🎯 **Aba de portfólio** oculta no perfil público se desativado
- 🔄 **Validação dinâmica** no fluxo de registro de serviço

---

## 🔧 Alterações Técnicas

### 1. **Banco de Dados**
- ✅ Migration: Adiciona coluna `portfolio_obrigatorio` (BOOLEAN, DEFAULT true) na tabela `prestadores`
- ✅ Index criado para performance

**Migration:**
```sql
ALTER TABLE public.prestadores ADD COLUMN portfolio_obrigatorio BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true;
CREATE INDEX idx_prestadores_portfolio_obrigatorio ON public.prestadores(portfolio_obrigatorio);
```

### 2. **Backend - Services**
- `lib/services/prestadorPerfil.service.ts` (NOVO)
  - `updatePortfolioObrigatorio()` — atualiza configuração
  - `atualizarPerfilPrestador()` — atualiza múltiplos campos
  - `getPrestador()` — busca dados

- `lib/services/uploadWizard.service.ts` (MODIFICADO)
  - `validarRequisitosFinalizacao()` — valida obrigatoriedade de fotos

### 3. **Frontend - Componentes**
- `components/dashboard/PortfolioToggle.tsx` (NOVO)
  - Toggle UI para ativar/desativar portfólio obrigatório
  - Estados de carregamento e erro

- `components/dashboard/EditarPerfilTab.tsx` (MODIFICADO)
  - Integra `PortfolioToggle` em "Dados Profissionais"
  - Permite prestador gerenciar configuração

- `components/profile/PerfilTabs.tsx` (MODIFICADO)
  - Renderiza aba de portfólio condicionalmente
  - Se `portfolio_obrigatorio = false`, oculta aba
  - Começa em "Avaliações" se portfólio desativado

- `app/(perfil)/[slug]/page.tsx` (MODIFICADO)
  - Passa `portfolioObrigatorio` para `PerfilTabs`

### 4. **Frontend - Hooks**
- `hooks/useEditarPerfilPrestador.ts` (NOVO)
  - Gerencia estado de edição de perfil
  - `handleTogglePortfolio()` — toggle da configuração
  - `handleAtualizarPerfil()` — atualização geral

### 5. **TypeScript Types**
- `types/prestador.ts` (MODIFICADO)
  - Adicionado campo `portfolio_obrigatorio: boolean`

---

## 📊 Fluxo de Integração

```
Dashboard Prestador
  ↓
[Dados Profissionais]
  ↓
PortfolioToggle ON/OFF
  ↓
updatePortfolioObrigatorio()
  ↓
Perfil Público
  ↓
PerfilTabs (condicional)
  ├─ Se ON → mostra "Portfólio"
  └─ Se OFF → mostra só "Avaliações"
  ↓
Upload Wizard (novo serviço)
  ↓
validarRequisitosFinalizacao()
  ├─ Se ON → exige fotos
  └─ Se OFF → fotos opcionais
```

---

## ✅ Próximas Etapas (Após Merge)

1. **Executar migration** no Supabase
2. **Integrar validação** em `UploadWizardContainer.tsx`
   - Usar `validarRequisitosFinalizacao()` em handleIniciarServico/handleFinalizarServico
3. **Testar fluxo completo:**
   - Toggle em "Dados Profissionais" ✓
   - Perfil público mostra/oculta portfólio ✓
   - Serviço bloqueia/permite sem foto ✓
4. **Deploy** em produção

---

## 🎨 Design/UX

- **Toggle color scheme:**
  - ON (Ativado): Verde 🟢
  - OFF (Desativado): Laranja 🟠

- **Mensagens claras:**
  - ON: "Fotos são obrigatórias no início e fim do serviço"
  - OFF: "Fotos são opcionais — aceite do cliente ainda é obrigatório"

---

- [x] Frontend (components + hooks)
- [x] Database (migration)
- [ ] Integração no Upload Wizard (próxima PR ou commit)
- [ ] Testes

body:
## Purpose
Measure the status-check path from #53 against the original fixed L1 path on the same independent loopback fixture, and preserve the evidence. This PR is stacked on #53.

## Local measurement
Run `VULNIX_NO_ENV_LOCAL=1 python3 -m scripts.bench_status_exposure_after`. The recorded artifact is `docs/STATUS_EXPOSURE_COMPARISON_STANDIN.json` and the interpretation is `docs/STATUS_EXPOSURE_INTEGRATION.md`.

Across vulnerable, patched, and generic-200 modes, the before path scored TP0/FP0/FN1/TN2; the after path scored TP1/FP0/FN0/TN2. Recall moved from 0/1 to 1/1; precision after is 1/1 and false-positive rate remains 0/2. Safety denials for expired scope and revoked ownership remained 2/2 in both runs. This **local after run uses the Python ARTEX stand-in** and makes zero model calls. It measures Gateway/Worker/verdict behavior, not real ARTEX latency or tokens.

The added check costs one extra target GET, Gateway call, and Worker launch. In these short local samples completion time rose from 0.074–0.096 s to 0.656–0.669 s, state saves from 15 to 17, and signed-ledger commits from 17 to 21. These are file persistence calls, not SQL DB counts. No speed or cost improvement is claimed.

## Real ARTEX evidence gate
The Linux real-ARTEX CI job passed the same three-mode benchmark with the actual overlay and loopback mock LLM: https://github.com/FORIFOR/Vulnix/actions/runs/43771848321 . Its `status-exposure-comparison.json` is preserved in `docs/STATUS_EXPOSURE_COMPARISON_REAL_ARTEX.json`. TP1/FP0/FN0/TN2, precision 1/1, recall 1/1, FPR 0/2 on this small fixed lab. Per diagnosis the local model received 2 requests and Planner LLM Gateway counted 8,328 estimated tokens; actual paid API cost was US$0. Real-overlay completion time was 1.220–1.368 s versus 0.107–0.204 s for fixed L1. The token count is a gateway estimate, not measured provider usage; commercial model cost is not calculated. No paid API or real service is contacted.

body:
## Summary

The game details dialog has a new **Scoring summary** section above the game leaders. It lists both teams' scoring plays in one list, in the order they happened.

**Data (`parseScoringPlays`, `espnGameSummary.ts`)**
- Reads `scoringPlays` from the ESPN game summary the dialog already loads, so there is no extra request.
- Each play records:
  - the scoring team (away or home)
  - the quarter and clock
  - the short type (TD / FG)
  - ESPN's description
  - both teams' scores after the play
- A play by a team that isn't in the game is skipped.
- `GameSummary` gains `scoringPlays`.

**UI**
- **`ScoringPlays`:**
  - One list, grouped under a heading per quarter ("1st Quarter" … "Overtime").
  - Each heading shows the away and home score columns.
  - Shows "No scoring plays yet." for a started game with no scores.
- **`ScoringPlayRow`:**
  - Shows the scoring team's logo, then the type and clock above the description, then the two scores.
  - The scoring team's score is in bold.
  - Screen readers hear the score as "CAN 28, LAK 31".
- **`ScoringPlaysSkeleton`:** a placeholder shown on first load. The real list's length varies by game, so this one can't match its height exactly the way the other placeholders do.
- **Live games:** a live refresh keeps the list on screen instead of flashing the placeholder.
- **Upcoming and soccer games:** they load no summary, so the section doesn't appear.
- **`visuallyHidden`:** moved from `ResponsiveDialog` to `shared/visuallyHidden.ts` so both components can use it.

**Test data**
- The e2e summary fixture gains scoring plays for the live game (17–24) and the final game (28–31), matching the scoreboard fixture's scores.
- The unit-test summary mocks are now typed as `GameSummarySource["load"]`, so a missing summary field is a type error.

    - `parseScoringPlays`: order, fields, unknown team, no plays.

Owner 2026-11-16 (TASK_no_die_banner): the banner after another session's API import was a wall of text with four buttons.

## What changes
- One line, e.g. `No die attached: <die> was detached by <who> at <time>. Nothing to save.`; the reason is in the tooltip. EN + full zh-CN mirror (`releasedStrip.*` in common.json).
- Screen identical to the stored configuration -> only `Reload <config>` (nothing that creates a copy).
- Real differences -> `Save as new configuration` (same lamination) or `Save as new die` (new lamination; blue only there) plus `Discard changes and reload`. Unknown comparison never says "nothing to save".
- Backend (additive, no stored result touched): `/deactivate` records `by` (caller account) in the context file; `/context` serves `by` and `live_matches_config` (every stored geometry value of the released configuration equals the screen's; null = unknown).

## Why the import detached his die (item 3, proposal, not coded)
`POST /api/family/die` takes the geometry from the workspace's single LIVE machine, so an agent creating a new die must first PUT the geometry into the live machine; with a die active that PUT syncs into the active die, so the agent calls `/deactivate` first. The agent session works in the owner's own workspace (same identity), so it released HIS context. Fix proposed: an optional `geometry` body on `POST /api/family/die` (validated by the geometry PUT validators) that builds the die without touching the live machine or the context. Opt-in; absent = old behaviour. Needs the owner's yes before I code it.

## Tests
- `node --test web/src/lib/__tests__/releasedContext.test.mjs`: 10 pass (banner states: identical, edited, other lamination, no duty, die gone).
- `tests/test_family_released_context.py`: 3 new tests pass in a job container; the 10 failures there also fail on the base (stand-in runner has no autouse fixtures). Real pytest, TSX build and the live page not run.

Stop rendering ignored `runner_security`, while retaining its decoder for the configuration rollout. Preserve the Sessions client certificate, Dispatcher listener, Environments proxy credential and Controller observer credential. Wrong-issuer and Firecracker certificate-rotation acceptance now use the actual Environments proxy client SVID.

Rendered manifests deliberately change only these credentials/mounts, `runner_security` and Flux's readiness entry for the removed Certificate. Flux prunes the Certificate resources. This PR performs no manual cluster deletion and changes no retained Sandbox, volume, Identity, Session or History data.

Deliberately left out: obsolete proxy grant settings, direct-Runtime network access, Runtime's legacy Gateway peer admission and obsolete RBAC. Those removals are the separate final permission step after their last caller. Strict decoder deletion waits until the manifest omissions roll; the Sessions directory move follows the cutover exit. body:
사용자 결정 3가지 (11/16) — ADR-060 '남긴 것'에 대한 답.

## 1. 랭킹 점수 하루 상한 1,000점

- **문제**: 답 1장 = 1점에 상한이 없어, 큰 덱을 되풀이하거나 일괄 제출(요청 하나에 답 1000개)을 거듭 보내면 점수가 끝없이 올랐다.
- **방법**: 랭킹을 **읽을 때만** `least(study_count, 1000)`으로 자른다. `daily_user_stats`에는 답한 수가 그대로 쌓여 통계 화면은 깎이지 않고, 마이그레이션도 없다.
- 전체 탭은 **날마다 자른 뒤 합계** (합계를 한 번 자르면 꾸준히 한 사람과 하루 몰아서 한 사람이 같아진다).
- 상한에 닿은 사람끼리는 같은 순위, 줄 순서는 가입 순 — 정렬도 자른 값으로 한다.
- 목록 밖일 때 따로 세는 내 순위도 같은 규칙. 내 전체 점수는 통계용 `aggregate`(자르지 않음) 대신 전용 쿼리 `cappedTotal`.
- **값의 근거**: 운영 실측 — 하루에 가장 많이 답한 날이 568장, 1,000장을 넘긴 날은 없다. 지금까지의 학습은 한 점도 깎이지 않는다.
- 화면: 규칙 문구에 '하루 최대 1,000점'(4개 언어). 숫자는 화면에 적어 두지 않고 응답의 `dailyCap`을 쓴다.

## 2. 듣기·시험지는 점수 없음

코드는 그대로다(화면에서만 채점 → 서버 기록 없음 → 0점). 결정이 된 만큼 E2E로 박아 둔다.

## 3. README 화면 캡처

8월 캡처 4장(카드 1장짜리 덱)을 8장으로 — 홈·통계·덱·시험지·퀴즈·랭킹 + 폰 화면(일본어·영어).
로컬 빌드에 예시 계정·덱 3개·28일 학습 기록·랭킹 사용자 7명을 넣고 Playwright로 찍었다. 운영 데이터와 실제 닉네임은 쓰지 않았다.
README의 낡은 숫자(테스트 180개)도 정정.

## 검사

- 서버 **336** 통과 (+2: 오늘 탭 상한·동점 순서 / 전체 탭 날마다 자르기)
- 화면 단위 검사(`npm test`), `tsc`, `oxlint` 통과
- E2E **73** 통과 (+1: 듣기·시험지 점수 없음, 기존 랭킹 테스트에 상한 문구 ↔ 서버 값 대조)

Second of three stacked PRs for #241 and #349 (on top of #492). It adds the builder UI for the new cross-type field conditions.

## What changes

- **"Per-item fields" becomes "Any item type".** It lists one row per key and kind that is on two or more item types or on items' own fields, labelled by the most common title and sorted by it. A field on one type only stays in that type's group, to avoid listing everything twice. For a choice field, a type field's options are offered, so values are picked rather than typed.
- **New "Saved fields" group**: each saved single field and its table columns (e.g. "Acquisition › Date"). Choosing one writes `{kind: 'field', origin, sub_key?}`.
- **Chips** read `Any item type › Status: is Wanted` and `Saved field › Acquisition › Date: in the last 30 days`.
- A saved field that is no longer listed is flagged as removed. While the listing is unread or at its cap, it isn't.
- The items, collections and collection pages load saved fields (`fetchSavedFields`, first 100) alongside the per-item listing.

The e2e test that pinned the old rule ("never match a type field with the same key") now asserts the new meaning: own fields and type fields with that key and kind both match.

## Tests

- New `tests/query-cross-type.test.ts`, with existing builder and component tests updated for the label and order.

body:
## What

- **Auto-merge** (`.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`): on Dependabot PRs whose highest change is a minor or patch update, the workflow enables auto-merge (squash), so they merge once the required checks pass. Major updates and PRs whose update type can't be determined still wait for a review. Separate `apca-w3` minor and patch PRs auto-merge too. That keeps it current, as its license requires, and the contrast tests in CI still guard against changed results.
- **`@types/node` majors are ignored** in `.github/dependabot.yml`. The types follow the Node major the site runs on (24, `ci.yml`), so a types major comes with a deliberate Node upgrade.
- README: one sentence on how dependency updates arrive.

## Why `pull_request_target`

Workflows that Dependabot triggers on `pull_request` only get a read-only token, which can't enable auto-merge. The [`dependabot/fetch-metadata` docs](https://github.com/dependabot/fetch-metadata#enabling-auto-merge) use `pull_request_target` for this reason. It is safe here because the job never checks out or runs code from the PR. It only reads Dependabot's metadata. The job also runs only for `dependabot[bot]` PRs in this repository.

## Needed before merging (repository settings)

1. **Settings → General → Pull Requests → Allow auto-merge.** Without it, `gh pr merge --auto` fails on every Dependabot PR.
2. **A ruleset or branch protection on `main` that requires the CI `check` job.** Without a required check, auto-merge merges right away instead of waiting for CI.

## Not verified

`pull_request_target` runs the workflow from `main`, so it can't run in this PR. It takes effect for Dependabot PRs opened or rebased after the merge. Comment `@dependabot rebase` on an open PR to pick it up. The open `@types/node` 24 → 26 PR is not closed by the new ignore rule. Close it by hand.

author: isaacasamoah
body:
Closes #166

## Why

Isaac wants a clean refactor of VoyagerShell, with the native verification environment as the safety net. A journey must never pass a broken product, never fail a working one under ordinary load, and blame the right side. The Core reply relay from "Delay chosen Core replies in the sandbox" had three places where it would blame the wrong side. This change closes them. It touches only `tests/native/`.

## What changes

- **Independent audit.** The ledger audit looks up each requested delay in the parsed flag itself, and no longer calls the relay's `CoreDelay::hold`. A relay that holds every method fails with verifier blame.
- **A release means a write.** The relay writes a `held` line when a reply arrives from Core. It writes a `released` line only after the reply is written to the app's socket. A failed write writes an `undelivered` line with the error kind. An `undelivered` line whose error is not `BrokenPipe` fails the run with verifier blame. A broken pipe means the app closed its end.
- **Relay instances.** The app starts a new relay on each launch and kills it when it closes its Core connection, and request identities restart with each launch. Each ledger line carries the pid and start time of its relay, and the audit keys a hold by relay and identity. A relay writes an `alive` line every 250 ms. A `held` line with no later `released` or `undelivered` line is a lost reply only when its relay was still alive more than 1000 ms after the hold was due. A relay killed mid-hold did not lose the reply.
- **Lateness.** A `released` line more than 1000 ms after the hold ended fails with verifier blame. A relay that waits several times its delay fails here.
- **Typed ledger.** The ledger events are one serde enum shared by the writer and the audit. A line that does not parse, or a ledger that cannot be read, fails with verifier blame. A missing ledger is empty.
- **Named timeouts.** When Core stops reading or answering the verifier's own connection, the error reads "Core did not accept METHOD" or "Core did not answer METHOD", then "within 5000 ms on the verifier's own connection", with the OS error after it.
- `slow-save` and `outcomes` read the same `released` lines as before. `tests/native/README.md` documents the ledger lines, the audit rules and the gaps.

The two app findings in the issue are left for the plan steps that own them.

## Proof

Journeys ran inside the battery lock on Linux X11 with one release candidate built from main. Planted mutants changed `tests/native/src/core_relay.rs` only and were reverted.

| Plant | On main | On this head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none, `workspace --core-delay doc.set=500` | passed | passed |
| `CoreDelay::hold` ignores the method | passed (gap 1) | `inconclusive`, fixture blame: "held events.subscribe for 500 ms, which the delay did not ask for" |
| relay returns before writing a held reply | `failed`, product blame (gap 2) | `inconclusive`, fixture blame: "held a doc.set reply and never wrote it to the app" |
| relay waits 4 times the delay | passed | `inconclusive`, fixture blame: "released doc.set 1500 ms after its hold ended, past the 1000 ms bound" |
| ledger keyed by id alone (unit) | not applicable | `two_relays_that_reuse_one_request_id_are_audited_apart` fails |
| every unreleased hold counts as lost (unit) | not applicable | `a_relay_that_stopped_mid_hold_did_not_lose_the_reply` fails |
| the audit drops the delay comparison (unit) | not applicable | `the_ledger_audit_catches_a_hold_nobody_asked_for` fails |
| the audit drops the lateness check (unit) | not applicable | `a_release_later_than_the_bound_fails` fails |
| malformed lines skipped (unit) | not applicable | `a_malformed_ledger_line_is_refused` fails |
| write error left unnamed (unit) | not applicable | `a_core_that_stops_reading_is_named_in_the_error` fails |
| release recorded when the write fails (unit) | not applicable | `a_failed_write_is_recorded_as_undelivered_and_not_as_a_release` fails |
| timeout message reverted to the bare error (unit) | not applicable | `a_core_that_stops_answering_is_named_in_the_error` fails |

Each unit plant passes once removed. The review of the first head found that `quit-restore --core-delay terminal.list=2000` passed on main and ended `inconclusive` with verifier blame at that head, 3 of 3, because the app kills the relay while a reply is held. At this head it passes 3 of 3, and `quit-restore` without a delay passes once. Its ledger shows a hold left unreleased by a killed relay, and request identities reused across relays.

Journeys that use the relay, at this head. `slow-save` passed 10 of 10 and `outcomes` passed 10 of 10. The independent verdict repeated both on a quiet machine, 10 of 10 each.

CI steps from the workflow, run locally: hook tests, `prepare-sdk`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `format:check`, `npm test`, `contract:check`, `architecture:check`, `vocabulary:check`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, workspace clippy, native fmt, native clippy and native `cargo test --locked` (175 tests). All passed.

## Not covered

- A relay that overruns its delay by less than 1000 ms is not caught. In the saved runs, the worst release was 87 ms late while other builds ran, and at most 4 ms late across 436 quiet releases. One heartbeat gap of 1059 ms was seen with swap exhausted, so the margin under memory pressure is thin.
- A reply lost in the last 1000 ms of a relay's life is not caught.
- A relay that writes a `released` line without writing the reply is not caught. The ledger cannot see the app's socket from outside the relay.
- `slow-save` and `outcomes` select `released` lines, `slow-save` by `releasedAtMs` and `outcomes` by `event`. Neither journey fails when its filter is removed, so those two filters are unproved.
- The timeout messages are proved by unit tests on a silent and a non-reading listener. A real Core stall was not reproduced.

author: alan-schramm
body:
## Summary
Independent fix for the revenue double allocation (CTO 252-P P3, CTO 254). Separate from #652 by CTO decision; #652 is not changed.

**Economic unit that must not be allocated twice:** the collected fee of one `FeeObligation` (C). Each confirmation generation is a claim on that same C, not new revenue. At most one generation of an obligation may be net-allocated at a time.

**Why it duplicated:** `allocate()` was idempotent only per generation: `@@unique([confirmationEvidenceId, recipientId, kind])` (`entitlement-allocation.service.ts`, G9/G10). A second CONFIRMED row of the same obligation opened a new key. Two ways this happens:
1. A reorg was recorded and the obligation reconfirmed, but `reverseGeneration()` was not run before the next `allocate()`.
2. A historical `recordedAt` tie whose "latest" row changes. #652's `seq` ordering can do exactly this; see its STOP characterization test.

## Change
- `allocate()` refuses (`EscrowError`, "still allocated") while any ALLOCATION of another generation of the same obligation has no REVERSAL.
  - The guard is per obligation and does not depend on which confirmation row the reader picks.
  - After `reverseGeneration()`, the next generation allocates normally.
  - Multi-recipient allocations and sequential reorg/reconfirm cycles keep working (existing T1-T6 tests pass unchanged).
- `allocate()` first takes `SELECT … FROM fee_obligations … FOR NO KEY UPDATE`.
  - This is the lock the collection-status UPDATE already takes, so no reorg revert or reconfirmation commits between the checks and the inserts.
  - It does not block FK inserts (FOR KEY SHARE).
  - This is a **new lock** in `allocate()`, which previously took none. No existing path changes its order. The lock is held only for allocate's own reads and inserts, with no external call inside.
- No schema change and no migration.

## Tests (`tests/integration/distributionEntitlementFoundation.test.ts`, real Postgres)
| Test | On main a530fdc1 | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| reorg recorded, not reversed → second allocate refused; allocates after reversal; balance = C | **fails** (second allocation succeeds → 2C) | passes |
| second CONFIRMED row becomes latest (order-independent), retry refused the same way | **fails** | passes |
| allocate waits on a second connection holding the obligation row, then sees the reverted status | **fails** (no wait) | passes |

- Related suites run locally on PG 18: 4 suites, 63/63 (`entitlementAllocationService`, `atomicCollectionRecognition`, `collectedTimeDistributionFreeze`, `distributionEntitlementFoundation`).
- Full suite: CI.
- Mutants, each killed:
  - lock line removed: 1 test fails;
  - guard limited to the same generation: 3 tests fail;
  - reversal filter removed: 4 tests fail, because legitimate reallocation after reversal is refused.

## Risk and history
- `allocate()`, `reverseGeneration()` and `findCollectedNotYetAllocated()` have **no caller** in `src/` or `scripts/`, so nothing triggers allocation automatically today.
- Existing ledgers should be inventoried read-only before any real migration or activation: obligations with more than one generation that has an unreversed ALLOCATION. The query is in the Principal's report. Rows are reviewed, never rewritten.

## Update: HEAD `bdcd44f2` (CTO 268)
History: `e29e57e6` (guard) → `7bd32cbf` (reverseGeneration skips reversed entries) → `bdcd44f2` (atomic, serialized reverseGeneration).

**H1, CI red at `e29e57e6` (`eventProjectionClaims.test.ts:256`): pre-existing, not caused by this diff.**
- Cause: `event_projection_claims."appliedAt"` is `timestamp(3)`, filled by Prisma from the app clock. `reconcileIncompleteProjections(report, 0)` selects `"appliedAt" < Date.now() - 0`, a strict comparison.
- When the claim insert and the recovery call fall in the same millisecond (one fast write in between on CI), the row is excluded and `projectionsRecovered` is `[]`.
- Proof (disposable PG 18, temporary probe copy of the test, not committed): pinning `Date.now()` to the claim's `appliedAt` reproduces the exact CI diff (`Expected -7 / Received +1`, `Array []`) with this branch's `src/` **and with `main` `a530fdc1` `src/`**. Control without the pin passes.
- Normal runs: 6/6 green on this HEAD and 6/6 on main code. The same job of the other workflow passed the test at `e29e57e6`.
- Fix belongs in a separate PR (test grace or `<=`); not widened here.

**H2: idempotent recovery of a partial reversal (multi-recipient).**
- `reverseGeneration()` is one transaction under the obligation row lock (the lock `allocate()` takes, same order: obligation row → ledger inserts). It reverses every not-yet-reversed ALLOCATION of the generation, or none.
- No nested transaction or second pool connection under the lock.
- `reverseEntry()` takes no lock: a reversal in flight can only make `allocate()` refuse.

| Case | Test |
|---|---|
| interruption after the first recipient's reversal (inside `reverseGeneration()`, DB trigger fails the 2nd insert) | nothing kept (0 REVERSAL); `allocate()` still refused |
| retry completes the remaining recipients | retry reverses both; a further retry returns `[]` |
| obligation released only after full reversal | next generation allocates once; a 2nd `allocate()` is refused |
| no duplication / no undue reversal | per-recipient balance equals one allocation; exactly 2 REVERSAL rows |
| committed partial state (manual `reverseEntry()` on one recipient) | blocked; retry reverses only the other; then allocates; total = C |
| two concurrent `reverseGeneration()` | results `[0, 2]`, 2 REVERSAL rows |
| `reverseGeneration()` waits on a second connection holding the obligation row; entry reversed meanwhile is not reversed again | deterministic |
| `allocate()` racing `allocate()` + `reverseGeneration()` | exactly C allocated |

**Mutants at `bdcd44f2` (all killed):**

| Mutant | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| lock removed from `reverseGeneration()` | 1 |
| non-atomic loop (per-entry transactions) | 1 |
| reversed filter removed | 3 |
| `allocate()` lock removed | 1 |
| guard scoped to the same generation | 5 |
| guard ignoring reversals | 7 |

Local: `distributionEntitlementFoundation` 39/39 (×3 runs); related suites 83/83 incl. `eventProjectionClaims`; `tsc` clean.

author: lbstrydom
body:
## Summary

This fixes four operator-UX defects in the consumer sync and setup tooling, reported by the wine (WCA) coordinator after the 2026-11-15 sync. Each was checked against the source before being fixed. Each lands with a test that fails on the pre-fix source and passes after (Tier 3: consumer sync contract).

1. **Merge policy in the consumer registry.** `consumer-repos.mjs` entries now take `merge: 'auto' | 'manual'`, and wine is `manual`. The value is validated and fails closed. A local repoint inherits the base entry's policy through one identity resolution that refuses an ambiguous registry. `sync:pr` follows the registry by default, and `--merge` / `--no-merge` override it. Every consumer's output says which source decided: `merge: manual — no auto-merge (decided by consumer registry (merge: "manual"))`. The PR body no longer claims auto-merge is armed when it isn't. This is the gap that let wine#1380 auto-merge.
2. **Backend and its source.** check-setup's *Environment provenance* section now prints one line: the backend in effect, the layer that set it, and any lower layer it overrides. Example: `Claude backend: cli — from .env; overrides ~/.audit-loop.env (sdk)`. Only backend names are printed, and an invalid value is withheld with a WARN. `parseBackendName` in the new dependency-free `claude-backend-name.mjs` is the one reading of the value; `resolveBackend` uses it too.
3. **Dry-run apply verdict.** Each UNMEASURED target now gets a line such as `safe to apply (base lag): yes — a real sync fast-forwards N commit(s) first …`, or `NO … remedy` / `UNKNOWN`. It comes from the same `planBaseLag` result the real run executes. It is printed in dry runs only; a real run reports what actually happened.
4. **Run artifacts are not orphans.** `patchManifestWithExtraHashes` records `scripts/.sync-owned.json` and `.sync-receipt.json` in the manifest after the payload. Garbage collection then read both as "no longer synced, likely renamed upstream". The GC signal was the wrong one. `SYNC_RUN_ARTIFACTS` is now the one list that both the manifest patch and GC read.

Plan: `docs/plans/consumer-sync-operator-ux-fixes.md`. Audit trail: `docs/plans/consumer-sync-operator-ux-fixes-audit-summary.md`.

## Audit

- `/audit-code`, 6 GPT rounds. The round cap was hit without 2/2 stability. Every R6 finding was fixed after the round, and the structural card shows 0 structural and 30 polish clusters. The STOP / CONTINUE call is the operator's.
- **Gemini final gate: APPROVE, round 1** (`gateDisposition: approve`, 0 blocking, code read FULL).
- R1 also raised 17 findings against pre-existing `sync-to-repos.mjs` code this change does not depend on. They were dismissed as out of scope and independent. They are unverified, and not captured as debt.

## Test plan

- [x] New and changed suites: sync-pr, sync-pr-git, env-provenance, sync-base-lag, and the new `sync-run-artifacts-not-orphans-e2e`. All pass, and each was shown failing on HEAD's source.
- [x] Touched-area suites (`sync*`, `anthropic*`, `consumer-repos*`, `check-setup*`, `env-*`, `relocation*`, `cli-entry*`, `bundle*`): 1,402 pass, 0 fail.
- [x] `npm run guards:preflight` PASS. The `npm run check` gates pass, but its local test tier failed 3 files (`prepush-hook-bounded-steps`, `prepush-installed-tree-identity`, `test-tier-gate`). The last two fail on unmodified `main` in the same environment (15 failures there).
- [ ] `full-suite` on Actions.
- No real sync was run against any consumer. Do not merge without the coordinator.

author: franciscoep
body:
Esta entrega necesita reunir el monitoreo de drift y la comparación de modelos con código que permita reproducir la tabla y sus intervalos. Este PR integra el trabajo de las ramas de Kim y añade la ejecución del A/B y una conversión explícita de coordenadas: con `--coordenadas sin_fma`, los paneles regenerados y los resultados de v1 frente a v3 coinciden con el reporte dentro de la tolerancia documentada.

Se abre **en borrador para revisión del equipo**. La recomendación permanece en conservar v1; las mejoras puntuales de v3 no excluyen cero en los intervalos exploratorios.

## Trabajo integrado y atribución

- Monitoreo con Evidently, evaluación del modelo original, challenger v2 y bootstrap pareado, comparación y paquete portable de v3. Se conservan sus commits `a89b1ea`, `63f7955`, `2b65a7c` y `03db371`, procedentes de `feat/evidently-drift-p1` y `feat/week9-drift-model-comparison-20261111`.
- Revisión e interpretación del reporte y señalamiento de los pendientes de integración y reproducción de intervalos. Esto reconoce su aporte al documento y a la revisión; no le atribuye la implementación del código de este PR.
- Integración de ramas, módulo ejecutable del A/B, diagnóstico y conversión explícita de coordenadas, pruebas y evidencia de reproducción.

Abrir este PR reúne las contribuciones del equipo; no sustituye su autoría. Se solicita revisar la integración y el procedimiento antes de pasar el borrador a listo para fusionar.

## Cambios

- `mibici/ab_testing.py`: predicciones pareadas, MAE, RMSE, WAPE, sesgo, tabla y JSON; reutiliza `paired_intervals` de Kim sin modificar el método (bloques de siete días, todas las estaciones del día juntas, 2,000 réplicas, semilla 42, percentiles 2.5/97.5 para v3 − v1).
- `mibici/coordenadas.py` y preparación de datos: modos explícitos `sin_fma` y `con_fma`, reconstruidos desde el CSV del catálogo verificado por SHA-256. El valor predeterminado sigue siendo `pandas`; para reproducir el reporte debe indicarse `sin_fma`.
- Documentación, pruebas y evidencia en `docs/week9-evidence/ab-v1-v3-20261115/` y `docs/week9-evidence/coordenadas-20261115/`. Las cifras históricas se conservan.
- Integración del challenger y resolución de dependencias con MLflow, mlflow-skinny y mlflow-tracing 3.17.2.
- Incluye los cambios de **#26**, todavía abierto: descarga alternativa verificada del catálogo histórico y diagnóstico previo de Windows/macOS. Coordinar su integración para evitar dos revisiones independientes del mismo cambio; este PR no lo cierra automáticamente.

No se añaden datasets ni predicciones por fila. El paquete portable de v3 y el ZIP de reportes Evidently ya procedían de las ramas de Kim. No se cambian los modelos existentes ni los aliases del registro. Los workflows incluidos son manuales.

## Validación

- Revisión independiente de Codex sobre este estado: **75 pruebas relacionadas aprobadas**; `git diff --check` sin errores.
- Codex regeneró los paneles desde los datos locales verificados y el CSV del catálogo, usando `sin_fma`: valores de referencia y actual iguales a los Parquet compartidos (normalizando la unidad temporal de `fecha`). Los Parquet compartidos se usaron solo para comprobar los resultados.
- Con la exportación oficial v1 (`2cac5ef2…`) y el portable v3 (`278b7a9e…`), Codex reprodujo las métricas y los tres intervalos del reporte. V1: MAE 8.0544, RMSE 15.8910 y WAPE 18.5263%; v3: MAE 7.7664, RMSE 13.8618 y WAPE 17.8638%.
- La evidencia de Claude en `cadena-limpia.json` registra una ejecución en un clon limpio con descarga y procesamiento, diferencia máxima de 1.8e-15 frente al reporte. Su ejecución reportó 296 pruebas aprobadas y tres omitidas.

body:
## ELI5

Allows Windows users to run Antigravity in Orca's Chat window using their locally installed `agy` CLI (`agy acp`).

## What Changed

- In `src/main/acp/session/acp-structured-location-support.ts`, updated `supportsAcpStructuredLocation` so that when a spec defines a `hostBackend` (`Boolean(spec.hostBackend)`), the location is accepted even if the managed runtime does not have a pinned archive for that platform.
- In `src/shared/agent-session/structured-chat-platform-support.ts`, relaxed `structuredChatUnavailableOnPlatform` so it returns `false`, allowing Windows hosts to offer Antigravity Native Chat when `agy acp` is available and compatible.
- Added regression unit tests in `src/main/acp/session/acp-structured-location-support.test.ts`.

## Why

On Windows, Antigravity previously fell back to opening in a terminal because Google does not publish a pre-packaged Windows archive for Orca's managed ACP server runtime. However, the host's installed Antigravity CLI (`agy.exe acp`) natively implements the ACP protocol and meets all server requirements (`isCompatibleAntigravityHostAcp`). Enabling the host backend on Windows lets users use Antigravity in the Native Chat UI without waiting for a managed runtime package.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #40321

N/A: Logic and backend capability check changes that enable the existing Native Chat surface for Antigravity on Windows.

The change only allows structured location support when `hostBackend` is configured and passes `isCompatibleAntigravityHostAcp` and `hasAgyCredential`. If uninstalled or unauthenticated, it safely falls back as before.

author: polylane[bot]
body:
Large find-refs jobs were failing and taking the NER service down with them. The linker sent every paragraph of a job in one request to the GPU NER server, and when that inference ran past the server's 30-second worker timeout the server killed its only worker, so find-refs returned errors and NER was unavailable for about a minute while the models reloaded. The linker now sends bounded batches, so each request finishes inside the worker timeout. The gpu-server logs put the kill 30.4s after the failing request started, matching gunicorn's unset 30s worker timeout, and container memory stayed near 1.32 GB of its 3.8 GiB limit, so the `Perhaps out of memory?` text was not the cause. Bounding the POST keeps each request inside the timeout. **Production impact** at `25a99bb`: Bounded NER requests keep the GPU server's single worker alive at current load ### Fix walkthrough [![Watch the fix walkthrough](https://badges.polylane.com/poster/autofix/ws_1d0fe0646001396oajcx781f08rjytku/fix_1e16989cb0016koz6d2qxz4w/25a99bbff89eb6d6329965ecefcc6a0d268d5f15.png)](https://console.polylane.com/sefaria/deliverables/p/dlv_1e16b0125001x90v93zfdmfq?video=25a99bbff89eb6d6329965ecefcc6a0d268d5f15#video) [Watch the fix explained (1:30)](https://console.polylane.com/sefaria/deliverables/p/dlv_1e16b0125001x90v93zfdmfq?video=25a99bbff89eb6d6329965ecefcc6a0d268d5f15#video). Recorded for commit `25a99bbff89eb6d6329965ecefcc6a0d268d5f15`.
Full analysis ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Linker bulk_recognize
(production-tasks pod)"] --> B["POST /bulk-recognize-entities"] B --> C["gpu-server
one sync gunicorn worker"] C --> D{"inference longer
than 30s?"} D -->|"before: yes, one unbounded POST"| E["WORKER TIMEOUT + SIGKILL
HTTP 500, no NER for ~100s"] D -->|"after: no, batches of 150"| F["200 with results"] F --> G["results concatenated
in input order"] ```
Detection evidence **Affected:** Gcp account `production-deployment`
## Production impact I checked the linker NER call path on the production-tasks pods and the gpu-server deployment it calls. The change only splits one unbounded HTTP POST into requests of at most 150 texts and concatenates the responses in input order, so it reduces load on the gpu-server instead of adding any. Sampled production calls in the last 22 hours carried 3 to 391 inputs and finished in at most 3.4s, well inside the server's 30s worker timeout; gpu-server memory held about 1.32 GB against its 3.8Gi limit across the kill, so the kill was the worker timeout, not memory pressure. **Affected resources** - `production-tasks-6bfcf99546-24j4v` - `production-tasks-6bfcf99546-2hkbx` - `production-tasks-6bfcf99546-2xjqr` - `production-tasks-6bfcf99546-6rvc6`
Checked and not affected (1) - `gpu-server`
**Observability** - `bulk_recognize GPU server post completed` records `num_inputs` and `elapsed_time` for each linker call. - `Linker NER server error from bulk-recognize-entities: HTTP 500` reports a rejected request. - gpu-server container log `[CRITICAL] WORKER TIMEOUT` and `Booting worker with pid:` show worker kills and reloads. _Polylane assessed this pull request at `25a99bb`._
Causal chain - **Signal** (log template): [CRITICAL] WORKER TIMEOUT (pid:) - **Surfacing site**: gpu-server container, Deployment gpu-server, namespace gpu-server, GKE cluster-1, GCP project production-deployment at Sefaria/gpu-server app/Dockerfile#gunicorn master worker timeout - **Mechanism**: A single POST /bulk-recognize-entities whose transformers inference ran 30.4s exceeded gunicorn's default 30s worker timeout, so the master aborted the in-flight request with handle_abort/SystemExit and SIGKILLed the only worker, returning HTTP 500 and leaving the single-replica NER service without a worker until the models reloaded. - **Producer**: linker bulk NER request, instance Celery task linker.find_refs_api on a production-tasks pod, at Sefaria/Sefaria-Project:sefaria/model/linker/linker_entity_recognizer.py#bulk_recognize - **Trigger**: a find-refs job whose paragraph list made one bulk inference outlast the 30s worker timeout - **What happens to the failed unit today**: gpu-server runs gunicorn --workers 1 --threads 1 --worker-class sync with no --timeout, so the 30s default applies and any over-timeout request takes the only worker down; the caller's find_refs_api_task runs under a 60s soft time limit. - **Cadence check**: 36 WORKER TIMEOUT events from 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-15 (1, 14, 3, 10, 8 per day); newest at 2026-11-15T20:47:08.896Z, none after that through 2026-11-15T22:55Z. - **Last observed**: 2026-11-15T20:47:08.896Z - **Blast radius**: 1 other resource(s), unknown other tenant(s); data at risk: none named - **Producer evidence**: - The failing POST started at 2026-11-15T20:46:38.497Z (gpu-server log Starting bulk_recognize_entities, no matching Completed) and WORKER TIMEOUT fired at 2026-11-15T20:47:08.896Z, 30.4s later. - bulk_recognize posted every normalized input in one request with no bound, so the request duration scaled with the size of the find-refs job. - Sampled successful requests in the last 22 hours carried 3..391 inputs and completed in <=3.4s, so the failing request was a large outlier that outlasted the 30s timeout. - gpu-server container memory held about 1.32 GB against the 3.8Gi limit across the kill, so the SIGKILL was the timeout abort and not an OOM.
2 files changed (+41/-3) - `sefaria/model/linker/linker_entity_recognizer.py`: modified, +16/-2 - `sefaria/model/linker/tests/linker_test.py`: modified, +25/-1

author: dadukhankevin
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to AQU-2117 (#1567), which turned **Suggest next words** off by default.

The problem was how the ghost text was wired into the editor, not the BIA guesses themselves:
- A suggestion was requested on every focus and caret move, so one appeared as soon as you landed in a cell, and **Tab (cell navigation) pasted it in**.
- A plain **→ at the end of a line accepted a word** for people who were only moving the caret.
- It showed **mid-sentence**, pushing the rest of the line along.
- With no real guess it fell back to the project's **most frequent word** that fit the letters typed.
- Each Tab put in **two words**, so a wrong guess cost two words to delete.

This PR fixes all five, turns the default back on, and adds PostHog events for the acceptance rate.

## Changes
- `src/lib/richtext/ghost-text-plugin.ts`
  - Asks only after a doc change (typing). Focus and caret moves ask nothing and cancel a pending ask.
  - Only when the caret is at the end of the line (nothing but whitespace to its right).
  - Drops the `frequency` fallback. BIA and bigram (`markov`) guesses still show.
  - One word at a time. After an accept, the next word is offered.
  - Tab or **Ctrl/Cmd + →** (← in RTL) accepts. A plain arrow only moves the caret. Esc dismisses.
  - Debounce 120 → 250 ms.
  - New `onEvent` option: `shown` / `accepted` (`how: tab | word`, `source`).
- `src/components/TranslatedEditor.tsx`: sends those events to PostHog as `next word suggestion shown` and `next word suggestion accepted`. **No text is sent.** Acceptance rate = accepted ÷ shown.
- `src/lib/store/ghost-text-pref.ts`: **on by default.** The key is now `aq.ghost-text.v3`: absent means on, and only an opt-out is stored. The v1/v2 keys are ignored and dropped on the next write, so anyone who switched it off before gets it back, deliberately, since the behavior they turned off is gone.

**Root cause.** The recurring refusal text Rai reported has two periods ("…so photos are not sent to it.."). Only code from before #94 produces that. `78d97d6`, the reported live commit, is the #94 merge, and it cannot produce that text for any model id. Failed turns keep their error text on the message, so the report is either an old stored refusal still on display or a process not actually running `78d97d6`. This PR does not fix deployment lag. It makes the next report unambiguous: new wording, a `check: "capability-resolver/1"` marker, and `/status` `photos`.

**Changes**
- `src/model-capability.ts`: photo capability keyed by backend (ChatGPT token sharing / OpenAI API) and canonical model id. Precedence: explicit provider metadata, then a validated trusted operator file (`ORBIT_MODEL_CAPABILITIES`, with explicit aliases), then a bundled registry of exact ids with cited evidence, then unknown. Explicit unsupported always wins, and conflicts are reported. No name patterns.
- Provider metadata matches what each route actually offers. The ChatGPT token-sharing route has no documented metadata contract, so nothing is called. The OpenAI API uses `GET /v1/models/{id}`, whose documented object only shows the model exists; `input_modalities` is used only if present. The fetch runs in the background with a timeout, body cap, TTL, retry, staleness rules and invalidation. It never runs during a reply and never carries a photo.

**Testing.** `tsc` passes. `node --test test/*.test.ts`: 1256 pass, 0 fail. New `test/model-capability.test.ts` (14 tests) drives the real adapters and server with provider HTTP mocked and synthetic photos. It covers the reported block, the backend differences, unavailable, malformed and no-capability metadata, explicit unsupported, operator overrides and conflicts, TTL, staleness and invalidation, aliases, fallback, 1 and 10 photos, text-only turns, stored-photo retry, and provider rejection versus local block. author: cameronraysmith
body:
A manual suspend on pyrite often looked like a machine that would not wake. Boot-clock (`trace_clock=boot`) traces of `power:suspend_resume` over 39 self-waking cycles localise it:

- Suspend reaches S3 in about 0.7 s, and the RTC alarm wakes it on time (S3 lasts 58.6 s for a 60 s alarm).
- On resume, `thaw_secondary_cpus()` onlines **core 1** (CPUs 1 and 3) slowly: 0.5–6 s on every resume, and up to **761 s** on some (`CPU_ON[1]`; also 652.9 s for `CPU_ON[3]`). Displays, network and userspace stay down until it finishes. CPU 2 (core 0's sibling) takes 2–5 ms.
- Ruled out by trace: lid wake sources, the d3cold sweep, the VT switch, PM notifiers, efivarfs, the filesystem sync, and the preemption model (`preempt=voluntary` still stalled 653 s).

`mem_sleep_default=s2idle` takes no CPU offline: 8 of 8 s2idle cycles resumed in exactly 63 s. The cost is standby drain: this platform reaches neither S0ix nor PC10 (`slp_s0_residency_usec` stays 0). The stale comment claiming s2idle \"also hung\" is removed; that single failure in the archived design (D22) predates the NVMe d3cold fix.

Root cause and drain follow-up: CAM-104.

Verification: pyrite builds on magnetite and is deployed. The default boot entry (generation 90) carries `mem_sleep_default=s2idle`, and `/sys/power/mem_sleep` reads `[s2idle] deep` at runtime (set live until the next reboot).

Refs CAM-99, CAM-104.
